The use case therefore involves archivists, cultural-heritage institutions and information-management stakeholders seeking to create a richer and more machine-readable description model for archival material. Its objective is to support the semi-automatic creation of metadata, improve the quality and consistency of archival descriptions and connect national archives to the wider network of semantic linked data. The implementation uses natural language processing, named-entity recognition and machine-learning methods to analyse archival descriptions and, where available, the digital documents themselves. Conceptually, the system extracts entities, relationships and relevant properties from texts and uses them to populate a semantic description model that is more expressive and more suitable for automated processing than conventional archival structures. The impact is improved discoverability, stronger interoperability and reduced manual effort in metadata creation. More broadly, the project increases the accessibility and long-term value of archival collections, supports digital transformation in the cultural sector and enables more scalable management of documentary heritage.

title: Data2Help - Optimizing the allocation of resources for a faster response to medical emergencies
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Data2Help was created to help Portugal’s National Institute for Medical Emergency (INEM) improve operational performance by allocating emergency resources more effectively and reducing response times. Emergency demand varies across locations and over time, making it difficult to position vehicles and teams optimally using static planning alone. The use case therefore involves emergency-service operators, dispatch teams and planning stakeholders who need better forecasting and decision support to ensure that limited resources are directed where they are most needed. The objective is to strengthen emergency preparedness and improve the speed and quality of response by combining operational, geographic and contextual information in a more systematic way. The implementation integrates INEM’s internal information systems with external datasets such as meteorology, epidemic indicators, demography and forest-fire information, and uses historical records to build predictive models for emergency vehicle demand in each geographic area. These forecasts then inform optimisation models that support resource allocation and deployment decisions. At a conceptual level, the solution combines data integration, demand prediction and operational optimisation within emergency-management workflows. The expected impact is faster response to medical emergencies, more efficient use of vehicles and personnel, and improved scalability in managing fluctuating demand. In public-value terms, it supports more reliable emergency coverage, better service outcomes and stronger resilience in critical healthcare operations.

title: CCM-SNS - Verification of medical prescriptions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Portuguese Public National Health Service (Centro de Controlo e Monitorização do Sistema Nacional de Saúde)
source_description: Portugal’s National Health Service needed a stronger way to detect irregular prescribing patterns and possible fraud after introducing paperless prescriptions and mandatory electronic medical prescriptions across the public sector in 2016. The operational challenge was to monitor very large volumes of prescription and invoicing data across multiple databases in order to identify suspicious claims without relying on slower, fragmented manual checks. The use case therefore involves the Control and Monitoring Centre of the Portuguese Public National Health Service, healthcare-finance authorities and prosecutors, with the objective of protecting public funds, improving oversight of prescription activity and supporting the investigation of fraud within the health system. The solution is implemented through data integration and analytical controls applied to several health and billing databases. At a conceptual level, the system cross-checks prescription, invoicing and related administrative records to identify anomalies and inconsistencies that may indicate fraudulent or improper activity. These flagged cases can then be escalated for further review or prosecution. The results reported are substantial: during the first seven years, irregularities amounting to hundreds of millions of euros were detected, and in the first half of 2017 alone the Invoice Control Centre processed EUR 356.2 million in prescriptions and flagged EUR 21.1 million to the State Prosecutor. The impact includes major financial-control benefits, improved fraud detection and stronger accountability in public healthcare spending.

title: Derm.AI - Tele Dermatological Screening
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Shared Services of the Ministry of Health
source_description: This use case aims to improve teledermatology processes within the National Health Service by strengthening collaboration between Primary Care Units and Hospital Dermatology Departments in the assessment of skin lesions. In the existing pathway, general practitioners must capture and refer cases efficiently, while dermatologists need to review large numbers of referrals and prioritise those requiring urgent attention. The operational challenge lies in improving referral quality, reducing delays and supporting more consistent triage across different points of care. The stakeholders include general practitioners, dermatologists, hospital teams and healthcare administrators, all of whom require a more effective screening and prioritisation process. The objective is to streamline dermatology referral workflows, improve early assessment and support faster, more appropriate specialist intervention. The implementation combines computer-vision capabilities in a mobile application used by general practitioners with a risk-prioritisation and decision-support platform for dermatologists, both integrated into the SIGA-VAI eReferral system. At a conceptual level, the service uses image analysis, classification models and workflow integration to support case submission, prioritisation and review. The expected impact includes improved referral consistency, better prioritisation of higher-risk lesions, reduced pressure on specialist services and a smoother user experience for clinicians. Overall, the use case supports more timely care, better use of specialist capacity and greater efficiency in teledermatology services.

title: ModEst - Student Flow Modeling
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Directorate-General for Education and Science Statistics
source_description: ModEst addresses the need for better planning and policy support in the Portuguese education system by producing reliable estimates of student movements across the system at NUTS 3 regional level. Education authorities must understand how learners progress through different stages of education, where dropouts occur and how admission patterns evolve over time in order to design effective policies and corrective measures. The use case therefore involves education planners, public administrators and policy stakeholders who need robust forecasting to support decision-making across the six stages of education. Its objective is to model student flows more accurately and provide a structured evidence base for planning interventions, resource allocation and policy design. The implementation decomposes forecasting into segment-specific models corresponding to each education stage and estimates variables such as admissions, progressions and dropouts on an annual basis. These models are enriched with contextual socio-economic data from sources including the National Statistics Institute and Pordata, enabling regional patterns and external influences to be incorporated into the analysis. At a conceptual level, the solution combines predictive modelling, segmentation and contextual data enrichment. The impact is improved planning precision, stronger policy insight and a more scalable way to monitor educational dynamics over time. In practical terms, it supports earlier identification of risk areas, better-targeted interventions and more informed use of public education resources.

title: IPSTERS - Remote Sense Data
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: IPSTERS focuses on the challenge of processing very large volumes of remotely sensed data for land applications with minimal manual intervention. Public-sector and research stakeholders increasingly depend on satellite and other remote-sensing data, yet the scale and complexity of these datasets make traditional processing workflows slow and resource-intensive. The use case brings together stakeholders interested in environmental monitoring and land-information products, with the objective of improving the efficiency and autonomy of data digestion and generating level-3 products suitable for operational use. It also explores the practical boundaries of advanced analytical methods when combined with accelerated hardware. The implementation uses accelerated processing hardware within the IPSentinel framework and investigates two complementary approaches: one based on active learning and another based on fuzzy logic. At a conceptual level, the system is designed to automate the interpretation and transformation of large remote-sensing datasets into higher-level analytical products while reducing the need for continuous human intervention. The expected impact is faster processing, improved scalability and greater consistency in producing land-related outputs from remote-sensing data. More broadly, the project supports better exploitation of Earth-observation information, enhances operational efficiency for data-intensive workflows and provides a foundation for more responsive environmental and territorial analysis in the public sector.

title: GADgET - Online Gambling Addiction Detection
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: GADgET was designed to help the gambling control authority identify problematic patterns of online gambling behaviour more effectively by making better use of the large volumes of behavioural data generated every day on digital gambling platforms. The operational challenge is that harmful gambling behaviour can be difficult to detect early through manual review alone, especially at scale, despite the importance of timely intervention for consumer protection and regulatory oversight. The use case therefore involves the gambling regulator and associated supervisory stakeholders, with the objective of modelling user behaviour, detecting patterns associated with addiction risk and enabling proportionate follow-up actions where necessary. The implementation uses behavioural data captured from online gambling activity to build detection models capable of identifying behavioural signals associated with addiction. At a conceptual level, the solution combines user-behaviour analysis, pattern-modelling and integration with the authority’s existing operational system so that flagged cases can be reviewed and acted upon within current supervisory processes. The impact is improved detection capability, more efficient monitoring of large user populations and stronger support for targeted regulatory intervention. In qualitative terms, the project enhances scalability, improves the consistency of oversight and contributes to better protection of vulnerable users, while also increasing the effectiveness and responsiveness of the authority’s control mechanisms.

title: WISDom - Water Intelligence Data
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: WISDom addresses a core operational challenge for water utilities: how to turn large volumes of network and consumption data into practical insight that improves service continuity, reduces losses and supports reliable water supply in both quantity and quality. The use case involves water-network operators, planners and technical decision-makers who need stronger visibility over consumption patterns, infrastructure failures and abnormal events in order to manage increasingly complex systems more effectively. Its objective is to improve network management by enabling earlier detection of problems, more accurate forecasting and better-informed operational decisions across the water cycle. The implementation combines exploratory data analysis with predictive and spatial modelling techniques applied to Water Intelligence System data. At a conceptual level, the solution covers five analytical capabilities: understanding historical patterns, forecasting water consumption, locating pipe breaks spatially, identifying and anticipating anomalous events, and delivering a prototype recommendation and decision-support system for end users. These components are integrated into a unified analytical framework that supports both monitoring and planning activities. The expected impact is lower water loss, faster identification of incidents, more efficient network management and improved service reliability. In practical terms, the project supports better resource use, greater scalability in operational control and stronger decision-making for maintaining resilient water services.

title: Bucharest airport Face recognition - Detection of wanted persons and unsafe situations
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Bucharest Henri Coandă Airport sought to strengthen its security operations in a context where major transport hubs must identify wanted individuals, respond to terrorism-related risks and detect suspicious behaviour across fast-moving passenger flows. Conventional airport surveillance can struggle to process the scale and pace of activity effectively, particularly when security teams need to distinguish priority threats from routine movement in real time. This use case therefore involves airport authorities, security services and intelligence-linked stakeholders, with the objective of improving threat detection, supporting faster intervention and enhancing overall passenger and infrastructure safety. The solution is implemented through a facial-recognition-based security system designed both to identify persons on wanted or intelligence-service lists and to detect suspicious behaviour patterns. At a conceptual level, the platform combines live camera feeds with biometric matching and behavioural-analysis functions so that visual information from the airport environment can be screened automatically against relevant watchlists and risk indicators. This creates a dual-layer security capability focused on both person identification and situational anomaly detection. The expected impact is stronger surveillance coverage, faster recognition of high-risk individuals and improved capacity to spot unsafe situations before they escalate. More broadly, the system creates value by enhancing airport-security efficiency, supporting more targeted use of human security resources and contributing to a more proactive and technology-enabled approach to protecting a critical transport hub.

title: Metrici LPR cameras - Better license plate detection
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Authorities managing one of Romania’s busiest traffic corridors needed more reliable vehicle-identification capabilities in order to support traffic monitoring and related enforcement or operational functions. Heavy traffic volumes can make manual identification impractical and can also reduce the effectiveness of conventional camera systems when conditions are complex or fast-moving. The operational problem was therefore to improve the accuracy and usability of licence-plate capture in a demanding transport environment. The stakeholders include road authorities, traffic-management teams and organisations relying on vehicle-recognition data, with the objective of improving detection quality, supporting more effective monitoring and making camera-based traffic analysis more dependable at scale. The solution is implemented through an LPR camera system enhanced with image-analysis technology for licence-plate recognition. At a conceptual level, the platform analyses video or image streams captured along the route, isolates vehicle plates and improves character extraction so that registration numbers can be read more accurately under heavy-traffic conditions. This creates a stronger basis for downstream traffic-management, control or investigative processes than standard visual review alone. While the source does not provide quantitative performance figures, the expected impact is better plate-detection accuracy, reduced manual effort and more reliable road-monitoring outputs. More broadly, the use case creates value by improving the operational performance of camera infrastructure on high-traffic routes and by supporting scalable vehicle identification where traffic intensity makes conventional methods less effective.

title: Antonia - Automatic processing of requests of public services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Cluj-Napoca City Hall introduced Antonia to address a common municipal challenge: handling large volumes of standard service requests quickly, consistently and without creating unnecessary queues for residents. Public administrations often spend substantial time on repetitive form processing and on answering routine questions about how applications should be completed, which can slow service delivery and increase frustration for citizens. The use case therefore involves city-hall staff, local residents and applicants for municipal services, with the objective of simplifying access to public services, reducing administrative bottlenecks and ensuring that requests can be handled efficiently at any time of day. The solution is implemented through a digital system that automatically processes 64 types of forms for public-service requests and includes a chatbot component that answers questions about how to complete them. At a conceptual level, the platform combines form-recognition, workflow automation and conversational support to guide users through administrative procedures and route applications into the city hall’s operational processes. Antonia has operated around the clock since its launch in April 2018, creating a continuous digital access point for residents. A second development stage is intended to extend the system into a hologram-based interface, with completion of the wider project estimated over a 30-month period, subject to technical progress. The impact includes faster processing, reduced waiting, improved user guidance and a more scalable model for municipal service delivery.

title: Taxana - Chatbot for financial administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The Slovak Financial Administration introduced Taxana to improve communication with taxpayers and to reduce the burden on traditional support channels in a context of ongoing digitalisation of public finance services. Taxpayers frequently need answers to routine procedural questions, and when these enquiries are handled only through call centres or manual support, staff capacity is quickly absorbed by repetitive issues that do not require specialist judgement. The use case therefore involves taxpayers, financial-administration staff and customer-support teams, with the objective of making tax-related processes easier to navigate, improving service accessibility and allowing staff to focus on more complex matters. The solution is implemented through an automated chatbot available 24/7, making the Slovak Financial Administration the first state institution in the country to launch this type of tool for client communication. At a conceptual level, the system uses conversational language processing and structured tax-service knowledge to interpret user questions and provide relevant answers through a digital interface. This creates an always-available first line of support that complements existing channels and fits within the broader shift towards electronic processes in financial administration. The impact includes faster responses to common enquiries, lower pressure on call-centre staff and a more convenient user experience for taxpayers. More broadly, Taxana creates value by supporting public-sector digital transformation, improving service efficiency and enabling financial-administration teams to devote more time to higher-value and more complex client issues.

title: OverSi - Chatbot to faster burocracy
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: The Office of the Deputy Prime Minister of the Slovak Republic for Investments and Informatization (ODPMII)
source_description: Slovakia’s wider effort to reduce bureaucracy and apply the once-only principle in digital form created a need for simpler ways for citizens to obtain clear answers to common administrative questions. Public procedures are often difficult to navigate, particularly when people are uncertain which rule applies, which document is needed or which process should be followed. The OverSi chatbot was introduced as part of a government initiative to tackle that friction by helping the general public identify the most relevant information and solutions more quickly. The stakeholders include citizens, public-service users and administrative bodies involved in simplification efforts, with the objective of reducing confusion, speeding up access to guidance and supporting a less burdensome relationship between people and the state. The solution is implemented through a chatbot designed to respond to routine public questions and direct users towards the most appropriate information or procedure. At a conceptual level, the system combines conversational query handling with structured administrative knowledge so that users can ask questions in natural language and receive practical guidance without needing to search through multiple websites or documents manually. This supports the broader digital application of the once-only principle by helping people navigate services more efficiently. The impact includes quicker access to answers, less wasted effort for users and a more scalable way of handling recurring public enquiries. More broadly, OverSi creates value by supporting administrative simplification and improving the usability of public services in a digital environment.

title: PCA - AI algorithms in audit methodology detecting potential fraud when prescribing medicines
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: AI algorithms in audit methodology detecting potential fraud when prescribing medicines. Between 2014–2018, big data analysis was used to examine prescribing of two expensive ophthalmology drugs, Eylea and Lucentis, in Slovakia. The study found that 15.5% of patients were treated atypically, with high concentrations of irregular prescribing in three centres. These anomalies could stem from medical decisions, patient non-compliance, or potential fraud, with estimated savings of €1.8M if practices matched national norms. Following the analysis, health insurers tightened monitoring and restrictions for these treatments. The case highlights how big data can uncover inefficiencies and protect public resources, while final judgments must rest with medical experts.

title: Case Fiva (RPA) - Support the Financial supervisory Authority
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: This use case was developed to support the Financial Supervisory Authority in carrying out time-consuming administrative tasks more efficiently in a context of limited resources and high accuracy requirements. One of the authority’s operational challenges involved manually entering information on investment services offered by European companies into a database, based on notifications exchanged between authorities. The task required significant staff effort, was repetitive in nature and presented substantial scope for human error. The objective was therefore to reduce manual workload, improve processing accuracy and allow supervisory staff to focus on higher-value activities while maintaining the reliability of regulatory information handling. The implementation combined robotic process automation with rule-based processing to capture, validate and enter structured information into the relevant database. At a conceptual level, the solution replicated a clearly defined administrative workflow that could be standardised and executed consistently by software, with appropriate integration into the authority’s existing data-management processes. The impact was improved operational efficiency, a marked reduction in human error and better use of constrained supervisory resources. Qualitatively, the solution increased reliability, reduced the burden of repetitive work and demonstrated a scalable approach for automating similar back-office tasks in financial supervision.

title: Semantic analyser - Document analyser for the public administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: This use case was initiated by the Ministry of Public Administration, in cooperation with the Faculty of Computer Science and Informatics of the University of Ljubljana, to improve how public administration bodies compare and analyse unstructured textual documents. The operational problem was that conventional text comparison methods tended to rely heavily on statistical similarity or keyword overlap, which limited their ability to identify documents expressing the same ideas in different wording. The use case therefore involved public-sector organisations handling large volumes of documents and seeking more accurate ways to identify similarities, overlaps or related content across texts. Its objective was to enable comparison based on meaning and context rather than surface-level word matching alone. The implementation used semantic text-analysis techniques to compare unstructured documents according to their content and intended meaning. At a conceptual level, the solution relied on language-processing methods capable of recognising contextual similarity, semantically related expressions and documents containing equivalent or closely aligned concepts even where vocabulary differed. The impact was improved document analysis, more effective retrieval of related texts and stronger support for knowledge-intensive administrative work. In practical terms, the tool increases efficiency in handling unstructured information, improves consistency in text comparison and provides a more scalable basis for document management within public administration.

title: Optimum - decision making for efficient integration of transport modes
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: OPTIMUM was created to support urban authorities in making better decisions about the integration of transport modes across interconnected mobility systems. In complex city environments, travellers depend on a combination of transport options, yet fragmented information and rapidly changing traffic conditions can make it difficult for operators and planners to maintain quality, accessibility and efficient system use. The use case involved urban mobility stakeholders participating in pilot studies, with the objective of facilitating proactive decision-making through a smart multimodal transit concept that would improve the coordination and utilisation of different transport modes. The implementation combined multiple transport information sources with advanced real-time predictive analytics to create a complex model of current traffic conditions and a short-term forecast of how those conditions were likely to evolve. At a conceptual level, the system integrated multimodal data streams, predictive models and decision-support capabilities to provide a dynamic view of network conditions and support more effective operational and planning choices. The impact was improved integration of transport services, better accessibility and more efficient use of interconnected mobility networks. More broadly, the use case supports higher service quality, stronger responsiveness to changing conditions and a more scalable approach to managing multimodal urban transport.

title: 060 Service - Answer FAQ from citizens and burocratic terms into informal language
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Territorial Policy and Public Function
source_description: Spain’s 060 Service was created as a central contact point to help citizens navigate the complexity of central government services through one short number and a unified access channel. A key operational challenge for public administrations is that official terminology is often formal, technical and difficult for citizens to understand, while large volumes of routine questions can create pressure on service teams. This use case focused on improving clarity and accessibility by helping citizens obtain answers to frequently asked questions and by translating bureaucratic language into more informal, user-friendly terms. The stakeholders included Spanish citizens, central-administration service teams and public-service providers connected through the 060 channel, with the objective of making public information easier to access, easier to understand and more consistent across services. The solution was implemented using natural language processing to interpret citizen queries and match them to relevant answers, while also recognising formal administrative expressions and converting them into plainer language. At a conceptual level, the system combined FAQ retrieval, conversational query handling and terminology simplification so that citizens could interact more naturally with government information. The expected impact was faster access to answers, reduced friction in understanding public services and improved efficiency in handling common enquiries. More broadly, the 060 Service created value by simplifying interaction with central administration, improving the user experience and supporting a more citizen-centred model of public information delivery.

title: Robots - Automating Covid-19 tests
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: During the COVID-19 emergency, Spanish authorities faced the urgent challenge of scaling up testing capacity quickly enough to support public-health management and identify infections at a much larger volume than manual processes could comfortably handle. Traditional laboratory and sample-processing workflows risked becoming a bottleneck at a time when testing speed and throughput were critical to the national response. The use case therefore focused on increasing testing capacity in order to improve operational efficiency and strengthen the response to the spread of the virus. The stakeholders included health authorities, laboratory operators and the wider public, with the objective of processing far more tests per day while reducing dependence on slower, labour-intensive routines. The solution was implemented through the planned acquisition and testing of four robots designed to automate parts of the COVID-19 testing process. At a conceptual level, the system was intended to use robotic automation to handle repetitive steps within the testing workflow, allowing higher throughput and more consistent execution than purely manual operations. The target capacity reported was up to 80,000 tests per day, highlighting the scale of the ambition behind the project. The expected impact was significantly increased testing throughput, reduced operational pressure on staff and stronger capacity to manage pandemic surveillance. More broadly, the initiative illustrated how robotic automation could support rapid scaling in high-demand public-health operations, with value in speed, consistency and resilience during a crisis.

title: Fuengirola Town Hall - measuring beach attendance
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Fuengirola Town Hall needed a practical way to manage crowding on beaches and in public spaces so that residents and visitors could use these areas more safely while reducing the risk of infection. The operational challenge was that beach attendance changes constantly, and manual supervision alone could not provide timely, area-wide visibility of occupancy levels. The use case therefore focused on helping the municipality monitor capacity in real time and communicate crowding information clearly to the public. The stakeholders included town-hall representatives, local residents, visitors and public-space managers, with the objective of avoiding overcrowding, supporting safer use of public areas and improving situational awareness during the health emergency. The solution was implemented through a system developed by a local company using sensors installed in streetlights and virtual occupancy grids with defined maximum capacities. At a conceptual level, the system measured the three-dimensional movement of people entering and leaving monitored spaces and counted how many individuals were present in each measurement grid, producing real-time occupancy calculations. These results were then translated into public warnings using percentages and colour-coded alerts. The expected impact was better crowd management, improved public information and faster response to unsafe density levels. More broadly, the initiative created value by improving public-space management, supporting safer tourism and demonstrating a scalable model for real-time occupancy monitoring in high-footfall environments.

title: Chatbot - Boost relations with citizens
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Sant Just Desvern City Council launched its chatbot initiative to improve how citizens interact with municipal services and to streamline routine administrative processes in a town of around 17,200 inhabitants. Local authorities often face pressure to reduce waiting times and make services more accessible, yet appointment scheduling and registration management can still generate delays and administrative overhead when handled through conventional channels alone. The use case therefore involved the city council, residents and frontline administrative teams, with the objective of speeding up access to services, improving communication with citizens and strengthening day-to-day relations between the administration and the local community. The solution is implemented through two initial chatbot services focused on arranging prior appointments with the City Council and supporting management of registration flyers. At a conceptual level, the system uses conversational interaction to guide users through these processes, capture their requests and route them into the relevant municipal workflow, reducing reliance on slower manual exchanges. This creates a more immediate digital access point for common tasks and helps the administration organise routine demand more efficiently. The impact includes shorter waits, smoother appointment handling and a more convenient experience for residents seeking municipal services. More broadly, the project creates value by improving responsiveness, supporting a more citizen-friendly local administration and demonstrating how targeted chatbot deployment can strengthen both efficiency and public engagement at municipal level.

title: VioGen - Forecast gender violence
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Spain introduced VioGen to support one of the most sensitive and high-stakes areas of public protection: assessing the risk faced by victims of gender-based violence and determining the level of police protection required. The operational challenge is that risk can change across time and across judicial stages, and authorities need a more consistent basis for deciding how to prioritise resources before trial, after sentencing or even in situations where a trial does not take place. The stakeholders include victims, police forces and protection services, with the objective of improving risk assessment, tailoring police protection more effectively and reducing repeat violence. The solution is implemented through an algorithmic system that uses two assessment tests to evaluate the risk level associated with complainants or already sentenced offenders. At a conceptual level, the system processes case-related information and translates it into a graded risk classification, which then determines the level of police monitoring and protection to be applied. This embeds the tool directly into protection workflows rather than treating it as a separate analytical exercise. The reported results are significant: according to the source, recurrence of attacks has fallen by 25% since implementation, and whereas recidivism in comparable neighbouring countries reaches around 35%, in Spain it is reported at 15%. The impact therefore includes measurable reductions in repeat violence, more targeted protection and stronger operational consistency in safeguarding victims of gender violence.

title: VeriPol - Detect false police reports
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: False police reports, especially for low-level offences, consume investigative resources, distort crime recording and can be linked to wider fraudulent behaviour, making them a costly problem for law-enforcement agencies. In Spain, the National Police adopted VeriPol to help identify reports that may be fabricated and to improve the efficiency of case handling within existing policing workflows. The stakeholders include police officers, investigators and administrative staff, with the objective of reducing wasted effort, improving the quality of recorded complaints and supporting earlier detection of potentially fraudulent claims. The solution is implemented as a system integrated into SIDENPOL, the existing information system of the Spanish National Police, so that it can be used directly within standard reporting practices. At a conceptual level, VeriPol was trained on a dataset of 1,122 police reports, including 534 genuine and 588 false reports, and applies natural language processing together with classification models to estimate the probability that a report is false. In addition to producing a risk score, the system also provides insight into linguistic and structural differences between false and true reports, which can support professional understanding and review. The impact includes more efficient screening of complaints, better targeting of police attention and stronger integration into established operational systems. More broadly, VeriPol creates value by reducing misuse of police resources, improving investigative efficiency and supporting a more evidence-based response to fraudulent reporting.

title: Madrid - AI for saving lives of Psychiatric patients
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: This use case focused on supporting clinicians in identifying suicide risk and other serious health threats among psychiatric patients more rapidly and consistently. Conducted through field trials involving San Carlos Hospital in Madrid, Fujitsu Laboratories of Europe and Fujitsu Spain, the project addressed a high-stakes clinical context in which doctors must make fast decisions based on complex and often fragmented medical information. The stakeholders included psychiatrists, hospital teams and clinical researchers, with the objective of improving diagnostic support and helping professionals recognise relevant risks earlier in the care pathway. The implementation led to the development of the Advanced Clinical Research Information System, which combined anonymised medical histories from more than 36,000 patients with a large body of external knowledge, including over one million medical papers. At a conceptual level, the system used analytical models to examine this integrated knowledge base and present possible health risks relevant to an individual patient. The impact was improved clinical decision support, faster access to relevant evidence and stronger capacity to identify patients requiring urgent attention. In qualitative terms, the solution enhanced the usefulness of available data, improved the consistency of risk assessment and delivered significant potential value in protecting vulnerable psychiatric patients.

title: SIMPATICO Platform for PS iN Spain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The SIMPATICO Platform was developed to simplify how citizens and companies interact with public services by improving the usability and relevance of digital administrative systems. In many cases, public e-services remain difficult to navigate, creating barriers to adoption and reducing the efficiency gains that digital transformation is meant to achieve. The use case, deployed in Galicia, involved public administrations, service managers and end users, with the objective of making existing systems more understandable, more personalised and more responsive to citizen needs. It sought not only to improve individual service interactions but also to enable the continuous optimisation of services and administrative processes over time. The implementation used advanced technical components layered onto existing public administration systems to adapt content, support personalised interactions and improve the delivery of customer-centric services. At a conceptual level, the platform combined service integration, user-oriented adaptation and process-improvement mechanisms to reduce complexity and strengthen engagement with digital public services. The impact was better user experience for citizens and businesses, higher accessibility and improved uptake of e-services. More broadly, the platform supports efficiency in service delivery, enables continuous improvement of administrative processes and strengthens the public sector’s ability to provide scalable, user-centred digital services.

title: ARSI – Aerial Robot for Sewer Inspection
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: ARSI addresses a difficult operational challenge for urban infrastructure management: inspecting sewer networks safely, efficiently and in sufficient detail to detect blockages, sediment build-up and structural defects before they compromise system performance. Sewer environments are hazardous, constrained and costly to inspect manually, which limits the frequency and breadth of conventional inspections. The use case therefore involves infrastructure operators and maintenance teams seeking more effective ways to assess sewer condition, monitor system performance and collect environmental samples from hard-to-reach locations. Its objective is to support earlier identification of compromised sewer segments and improve maintenance planning through more capable and less intrusive inspection methods. The implementation uses an aerial robotic solution designed to operate within sewer environments and assess infrastructure condition while carrying out additional monitoring functions. At a conceptual level, the platform combines onboard sensing, navigation and inspection capabilities to identify sediments, detect structural defects, monitor sewer conditions and collect samples of water, air and sediments for further analysis. The impact is improved inspection coverage, reduced reliance on labour-intensive manual procedures and stronger support for preventive maintenance. In operational terms, the solution offers better scalability, improved safety for inspection activities and greater reliability in monitoring critical underground infrastructure.

title: SCRIPT Project - Supervised Care & Rehabilitation Involving Personal Tele-robotics
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The SCRIPT project was created to address a major challenge in stroke rehabilitation: how to ensure that patients, particularly those in the chronic phase of recovery, can continue to receive intensive and repetitive therapy beyond the clinical setting. Conventional rehabilitation often depends on in-person sessions, which can limit the volume and frequency of exercise that patients are able to complete once they return home. The use case therefore involved stroke patients, clinicians, rehabilitation specialists and carers, with the objective of extending supervised rehabilitation into the home environment in a way that supports better long-term management of recovery. By enabling a higher number of repetitions and more frequent exercise, the project aimed to improve functional and motor outcomes while reducing dependence on hospital-based delivery alone. The implementation used robot-mediated rehabilitation technologies adapted for home use, combining tele-robotic devices with remote supervision and monitoring capabilities. At a conceptual level, the solution enabled structured exercise delivery, capture of performance data and integration with professional oversight so that therapy could be administered safely and consistently outside traditional care settings. The impact was expected to include greater continuity of care, improved rehabilitation intensity and a better user experience for patients managing recovery at home. More broadly, the project supports scalable long-term rehabilitation, more efficient use of clinical resources and stronger recovery potential for stroke patients.

title: Robotic System Da Vinci
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Hospitals and surgical teams continually seek ways to perform delicate and complex operations with greater precision, less trauma to the patient and shorter recovery times, particularly in procedures where conventional open surgery may involve larger incisions and longer rehabilitation. The da Vinci Surgical System addresses this challenge by supporting minimally invasive surgery in situations where high dexterity and fine control are especially important. The stakeholders include surgeons, hospital teams and patients undergoing complex procedures, with the objective of improving surgical performance, reducing the physical burden of operations on patients and expanding the range of procedures that can be carried out through small incisions. The solution is implemented as a robotic-assisted surgical platform that enables surgeons to operate through a limited number of small entry points while controlling instruments with enhanced precision. At a conceptual level, the system combines robotic arms, surgeon-controlled interfaces and high-definition visualisation to translate the surgeon’s movements into highly controlled instrument actions inside the body. This allows intricate procedures to be performed with a level of stability and manoeuvrability that can exceed conventional laparoscopy in certain contexts. The impact includes more precise surgical intervention, reduced invasiveness and potential improvements in patient recovery and hospital efficiency. More broadly, the da Vinci system creates value by modernising the surgical theatre, improving the quality of complex operations and supporting a more advanced model of minimally invasive care.

title: VI-DAS – Vision Inspired Driver Assistance Systems
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: VI-DAS addressed the need for safer, more adaptive driver-assistance systems by focusing on contextual understanding of driver behaviour and road situations using non-invasive sensing. Many road incidents are linked to human error, yet traditional vehicle systems do not always interpret behaviour, environment and risk in a sufficiently integrated way. The use case therefore involved vehicle manufacturers, drivers, road-safety stakeholders and system designers seeking to improve safety, comfort and efficiency through better situational awareness and more personalised driver support. Its objective was to understand scene dynamics and driver behaviour in real time, and to provide the most appropriate response through vehicle interfaces that guide safer decisions. The implementation combined computer vision and machine-learning methods with inexpensive and widely available sensors, primarily cameras, to monitor the driving context and model driver behaviour. At a conceptual level, the system generated predictions about likely outcomes in a scene and used these to drive a personalised human-machine interface that recommended appropriate actions. A cloud platform supported large-scale storage and analysis of data, improved the design of sensors and algorithms, and enabled the use of connected and cooperative vehicle systems. The impact was improved safety support, more effective anticipation of risk and stronger potential to reduce incidents linked to human error. It also offered benefits in comfort, efficiency and scalability, while recognising important legal, liability and ethical considerations associated with advanced driver-assistance technologies.

title: Corpus Viewer: NLP and ML-based Platform for Public Policy Making and Implementation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Corpus Viewer was developed to help public administrations make better-informed policy decisions by analysing large and complex bodies of textual information that would be difficult to process manually. Policy design and implementation increasingly require evidence drawn from diverse sources such as patents, scientific publications and public-aid records, yet these datasets often combine structured metadata with large volumes of unstructured text. The use case therefore involved decision-makers and policy implementers who needed a clearer, more navigable view of the research and innovation landscape in order to support evidence-based action. Its objective was to enable the analysis of this information space in a way that reveals themes, relationships and patterns relevant to public policy. The implementation used natural language processing, machine learning and machine translation techniques to process multilingual textual corpora and associated metadata. At a conceptual level, the platform combined topic modelling, graph analysis and large-scale text exploration to support the discovery of connections across documents and sources. It was developed through collaboration between research groups and companies, and is used by several public administrations, including SEAD, FECYT and SEUIDI. The impact includes improved analytical capacity for policy teams, more robust evidence for decision-making and a more scalable way to explore large knowledge domains. In practical terms, it strengthens policy design, supports implementation oversight and improves the usability of complex R&D information.

title: Tengai - Robot in recruitment processes
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Upplands-Bro Municipality began using Tengai in June 2019 to address a persistent challenge in recruitment: reducing bias in candidate selection while maintaining a structured and efficient hiring process. Traditional interviews can be influenced by subjective impressions, inconsistent questioning and uneven evaluation practices, which may affect fairness and the quality of shortlist decisions. The use case therefore involved the municipality’s recruitment and staffing agency, hiring managers and job candidates, with the objective of making recruitment more impartial, standardised and evidence-based while preserving a final human assessment of motivation and fit. The solution was implemented through Tengai, one of the first social interview robots, developed in collaboration between municipal staff and Furhat Robotics. At a conceptual level, the system first identifies candidates with the highest general performance scores to create a shortlist, then conducts structured interviews in which it assesses behaviour, problem-solving ability and other competencies, including the ability to ask follow-up questions where needed. These interview outputs are combined with competency scores and passed on to recruiters, who then carry out the final interview stage. The first results were regarded as successful, and the service was adopted permanently within a week of release. The impact included a more standardised interview process, reduced exposure to bias in early screening and significant reputational value through national and international media attention to the municipality’s innovative recruitment approach.

title: AIDA - Interpreting detailed plan provisions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Sweden’s planning system has long relied on a large stock of existing detailed plans that must be digitised before they can be integrated into a coherent national plan database. The operational problem is that interpreting and standardising plan provisions is labour-intensive, technically complex and slow, especially when older planning documents must be translated into a common format aligned with the standards of the National Board of Housing, Building and Planning. The use case therefore involved planning authorities, digitisation teams and national actors working towards a shared planning-data infrastructure, with the objective of accelerating the conversion of existing plans into standardised digital form while reducing manual effort and improving consistency. The solution was implemented through a system designed to interpret detailed-plan regulations according to the relevant national standard. At a conceptual level, the platform applies document interpretation and classification techniques to extract and structure provisions from existing plans, converting them into standardised digital representations that can feed into the wider national planning database. This allows the digitisation process to move beyond fully manual interpretation and supports a more uniform treatment of plan content. The expected impact was a 20% reduction in the time required for digitisation, which, when applied across the full stock of plans still to be processed, would save years of work. More broadly, the project promised gains in efficiency, consistency and interoperability, supporting wider Smart Built Environment goals through faster, more scalable planning-data modernisation.

title: SKOSA - Interpreting medical information
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Administrators handling health-related casework often need to review large volumes of medical information and translate complex clinical material into structured assessments that support benefit or needs-related decisions. This is a demanding process because medical records can be detailed, inconsistent in format and difficult for non-clinical staff to interpret without support. SKOSA was developed to address this challenge by helping administrators analyse, structure and understand medical information more effectively when conducting needs assessments. The stakeholders include public administrators, medical experts and case-handling organisations responsible for decisions influenced by health information, with the objective of improving consistency, reducing interpretative burden and strengthening the quality of assessment processes. The solution is implemented as a general platform with a digital knowledge base built in collaboration with doctors and other subject-matter experts. At a conceptual level, the system combines expert-curated knowledge structures with analytical support tools that help caseworkers organise medical data, identify relevant information and interpret it within a decision-support context. Rather than replacing professional judgement, the platform is designed to make medical evidence more accessible and usable in administrative workflows. The expected impact is more efficient case handling, better-structured use of health information and improved consistency in needs assessments. More broadly, SKOSA creates value by reducing the cognitive load on administrators, supporting more reliable decisions and building a reusable infrastructure for interpreting complex medical evidence in public administration.

title: SCAPIS - Prevention of heart- and lung-diseases
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Uppsala, Umeå, Linköping, Malmö/Lund, Gothenburg and Stockholm Hospitals
source_description: SCAPIS was established to strengthen prevention and risk assessment for cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases through a large-scale population study capable of generating deeper insight into how these conditions develop and how they might be prevented or delayed. Heart and lung diseases place a major burden on health systems, yet earlier and more individualised risk identification requires data on a scale and depth that routine care alone cannot easily provide. The use case brought together all six Swedish healthcare regions, university hospitals and a broad group of scientific stakeholders, with the objective of building a national evidence base to improve understanding of cardiovascular, pulmonary, epidemiological and genetic risk factors. The implementation was centred on the Swedish CardioPulmonary bioImage Study, a population-based initiative involving 30,000 participants. At a conceptual level, the programme integrated imaging, clinical, epidemiological and genetic data in order to support the development of more individualised risk assessments and preventive strategies. The study began with a pilot in 2012 to confirm feasibility, followed by the major study launch in 2014, building on work initiated in 2007. The impact lies in creating a world-leading research resource that supports earlier prevention, more precise risk stratification and stronger scientific understanding of heart and lung disease. In broader terms, SCAPIS improves the foundation for long-term public-health planning, supports clinical innovation and strengthens the ability of the health system to move from reactive treatment towards prevention.

title: Norwegian Tax Administration chat service
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The Norwegian Tax Administration introduced its chat service to address a familiar public-service challenge: large numbers of taxpayers need timely answers to general questions, particularly when they are trying to understand obligations, complete filings correctly or resolve routine issues without delay. Relying only on traditional contact channels can create unnecessary waiting times and increase pressure on service staff, especially during peak tax periods. The use case therefore involves taxpayers and tax-administration support teams, with the objective of improving access to general information, simplifying communication and making it easier for users to get their taxes right. The solution is implemented as a digital chat service that handles general enquiries through an online interface. At a conceptual level, the service uses conversational interaction and structured service knowledge to interpret routine questions and return relevant tax information quickly, creating a more immediate support layer than static web pages alone. By focusing on general enquiries, the service can respond at scale while leaving more complex or case-specific matters to other channels. The expected impact is faster access to guidance, reduced pressure on manual support functions and a more convenient experience for taxpayers seeking straightforward information. More broadly, the chat service creates value by improving digital service delivery, supporting greater self-service in tax administration and helping the organisation allocate human support capacity more effectively.

title: Stockholm3 - Diagnosing prostate cancer with OncoWatch
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: This use case focuses on improving the diagnosis of prostate cancer by strengthening the consistency, accuracy and scalability of pathology assessment across laboratories and clinical settings. Diagnosing prostate cancer can be complex, and variability in interpretation may affect both efficiency and quality of care. The use case therefore involved pathology laboratories, clinicians, diagnostic innovators and health-system stakeholders seeking to improve diagnostic support and broaden access to reliable assessment tools. Its objective was to accelerate the development and implementation of Stockholm3 together with OncoWatch, so that diagnostic workflows could benefit from more standardised and scalable support. The implementation involved the development and validation of OncoWatch as a diagnostic system for use in pathology contexts, supported by EIT Health through funding and network access. At a conceptual level, the solution was tested in a nine-country multicentre study to assess performance across different laboratories and a wider range of digital pathology scanners, ensuring that the system could operate effectively in heterogeneous real-world environments. This emphasis on cross-site validation supported readiness for broader deployment, with a first CE-marked product expected to launch by the end of the year referenced. The impact includes improved confidence in diagnostic consistency, stronger interoperability across lab settings and better scalability of prostate-cancer diagnostics. More broadly, the use case supports faster translation of innovation into clinical practice and creates business value through improved efficiency, standardisation and potential expansion across multiple healthcare markets.

title: Plausibility check on quality and reliability of administrative data
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: This use case addresses the substantial effort required by statistical offices to validate the quality and reliability of administrative and survey data before it can be used confidently. Existing plausibility checks have typically relied either on manual review or on rule-based validation using thresholds and logical tests, both of which can be labour-intensive, incomplete or insufficiently precise. The use case therefore involved statistical offices and data suppliers seeking to improve validation processes, reduce repeated back-and-forth corrections and strengthen the consistency of data quality assurance. Its objective was to identify questionable or incorrect records more quickly and accurately, while also improving communication with data suppliers about detected issues. The implementation used machine-learning methods trained initially on historical data, with a target variable defined through prior analysis and then predicted by the algorithm. At a conceptual level, the solution compared predicted and actual values to evaluate accuracy, used these results to support plausibility checks and incorporated a feedback mechanism to generate automatic explanations for data suppliers. This moved validation beyond fixed rules towards a more adaptive and evidence-based approach. The expected impact was faster and more accurate checks, reduced manual workload and more efficient handling of correction cycles. In operational terms, the use case improves data reliability, enhances scalability in statistical production and strengthens the overall quality of administrative information used in the public sector.

title: NOGAuto - Assign or control codes to companies for economic activities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Federal Statistical Office depends on accurate and stable NOGA coding in the Business and Enterprise Register because these economic-activity classifications directly influence the quality of structural, economic and synthetic business statistics. The operational challenge is that coding enterprises on the basis of survey responses, commercial-register descriptions and other available information requires human interpretation, which can introduce subjectivity and make standardisation difficult. At the same time, manual coding is resource-intensive and can increase the burden associated with maintaining high-quality classifications across the register. NOGAuto was therefore developed to support staff responsible for assigning or checking economic-activity codes, with the objective of automating part of the coding process, improving consistency and reducing administrative burden on both the statistical office and enterprises. The solution is implemented through an automated coding approach that initially relies on information already available within the Federal Statistical Office. At a conceptual level, the system analyses existing textual and administrative data, identifies patterns associated with NOGA classifications and generates proposed codes or control suggestions for review. This creates a more standardised and reproducible coding workflow while still allowing staff to validate or adjust outcomes where needed. The expected impact is improved coding quality, greater consistency across enterprises and reduced manual effort in maintaining the register. More broadly, the project creates value by strengthening the statistical production chain, enhancing reliability in enterprise-based statistics and supporting more efficient and scalable classification management.

title: Chatbot - Offer residents and tourism information and services from the administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The City of St. Gallen tested this chatbot to improve how residents and tourists access municipal information and services, particularly in situations where users need quick, practical answers without navigating multiple systems. City administrations often hold a broad range of service information, but users may find it difficult to locate the right detail at the right moment, whether they are looking for parking, event information or digital administrative services. The use case therefore involved residents, visitors and municipal service teams, with the objective of simplifying access, improving convenience and testing public acceptance of conversational service delivery. The solution was implemented through a prototype chatbot integrated into both the city’s website and its urban app, mobileSG. At a conceptual level, the system combined conversational query handling with access to multiple municipal information domains, including the event calendar, parking information, mobility data, disposal guidance, eUmzugCH functionality and user feedback collection. The roadmap also included integration into the city’s own software environment and extension to services such as residence confirmation, debt-enforcement register extracts and tax-deadline extensions. Public testing and subsequent revision were built into the implementation approach. The impact included broader access to municipal and tourism information, a more user-friendly service experience and a scalable foundation for expanding digital interaction across urban administration.

title: Maxi - Chatbot answering questions on insurance
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Social Insurance Institute of Canton of Aargau
source_description: Social Insurance Aargau introduced the Maxi chatbot to deal with a high volume of routine enquiries and to reduce the operational burden created by daily incoming questions. Many requests to social-insurance institutions concern general matters that do not involve sensitive personal data, yet handling them manually consumes time that staff could otherwise spend on more complex and case-specific work. The use case therefore involved the social-insurance institution, its customer-service teams and citizens seeking information, with the objective of improving responsiveness, reducing repetitive workload and creating a pathway towards more automated handling of incoming communication. The solution was implemented through a chatbot capable of answering general questions that do not require access to sensitive personal information. At a conceptual level, Maxi uses conversational query handling and structured service knowledge to respond to standard requests, while the broader plan is for future emails to pass through automated, intelligent triage and further processing. In that next stage, requests containing personal data would be classified correctly and, depending on the issue, could trigger processes directly within specialist applications. The impact has already been measurable: the introduction of Maxi reduced mail enquiries by around 30%. More broadly, the use case creates value by improving service efficiency, reducing pressure on support teams and laying the groundwork for a more integrated and scalable model of automated request management in social insurance.

title: Chatbot - Security institution information, find the ones entitled to premium reductions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: In the Canton of St. Gallen, the social security institution needed a more accessible way to provide citizens with information about its services, particularly where people may be unsure about entitlements or may not know how to navigate the institution’s offerings. Access barriers of this kind can reduce uptake of available support and increase administrative pressure when routine questions must be handled manually. The use case therefore involved the cantonal social security organisation and citizens seeking guidance, with the objective of improving access to service information and helping people identify support, including potential entitlement to premium reductions. The solution was implemented through a chatbot developed within the SVA organisation to provide answers about the institution’s services. At a conceptual level, the system uses conversational interaction and structured benefit-related information to interpret user questions and return relevant guidance through a digital interface. This allows citizens to obtain first-line support more quickly and more independently than through traditional channels alone. While the available description is brief, the intended value lies in making social-security information easier to understand and more readily available, particularly for users who may otherwise struggle to identify the right service path. The expected impact includes improved accessibility of service information, greater convenience for citizens and reduced demand on manual enquiry handling.
