The objective is to simplify workflows, ensure authenticity and irrevocability of guarantees, and reduce processing times and disputes for all stakeholders. The solution implements a distributed ledger infrastructure where each surety policy is issued, certified and recorded as a unique digital record. Guarantees are registered once and become tamper-proof, with authorised issuers writing validated data to the ledger and the municipality accessing a single, trusted source of truth. Integration with existing administrative systems enables end-to-end digital handling without duplicating data. The pilot delivers faster issuance and verification, reduced administrative overhead, improved auditability and legal certainty, and lower fraud risk. It represents the first Italian public-sector experimentation of this kind and provides a scalable model for other municipalities seeking trusted digital guarantee management.

title: Ensuring the validity and integrity of European degree certificates
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Italian universities faced increasing challenges with diploma verification requests and credential fraud, whilst graduates required faster proof of qualifications for job applications and further study. The University of Cagliari became the first Italian university to issue blockchain-validated academic degrees, storing cryptographic hashes of diploma data on the public Ethereum network. This approach enables independent verification by employers or other institutions without requiring contact with the university, reducing administrative burden whilst providing tamper-proof evidence of qualification authenticity. The system supports European Higher Education Area mobility objectives by facilitating cross-border credential recognition. The initiative established a model subsequently adopted by other Italian institutions seeking to modernise their credential issuance processes.

title: Payments on Madrid's buses with blockchain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Madrid’s public transport system involves multiple operators and services, leading to fragmented onboarding, duplicated user accounts and inconsistent payment experiences. In partnership with Banco Santander and Vottun, the city sought to simplify access to public mobility while strengthening data security and interoperability across services. The objective of this pilot is to provide citizens with a single registration and payment interface covering buses, taxis and electric vehicle charging, reducing friction for users and operational complexity for providers. The solution is built around a blockchain-enabled certification layer that securely records user credentials and transactions, allowing a single digital identity and payment profile to be reused across transport services. Transaction records are cryptographically secured, while backend systems integrate with existing ticketing and payment infrastructures. The result is a unified mobility app that enables seamless payments and service access with enhanced data protection. Expected impacts include improved user experience, reduced onboarding costs, better interoperability between transport services and increased trust in digital payments, supporting Madrid’s transition towards integrated smart mobility services.

title: Enabling the transparent exchange of medical records
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: This use case addresses the fragmentation and limited patient control of medical records within healthcare systems. Patients and healthcare providers often struggle with data silos, delayed access to records, and unclear consent management. The Proof of Concept, conducted with Groves Medical Group in London, involves patients, doctors, and healthcare administrators. Its objective is to enable patients to securely manage, share, and monetise access to their medical records, while supporting flexible care delivery such as remote consultations. The solution is delivered through a blockchain-based health data platform where patients create digital wallets to manage permissions to their medical records. Health data references and access rights are recorded immutably, while clinical data remains securely stored off-chain. The platform integrates video consultation services and enables payments using digital tokens, incentivising the use of telemedicine services. The Proof of Concept enhances patient empowerment, data transparency, and trust between patients and clinicians. It improves access to care, supports new service models, and provides a scalable foundation for secure health data exchange, with positive implications for efficiency, user experience, and continuity of care.

title: Validation of judicial expenses incurred during investigations
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Law enforcement agencies face complex administrative requirements when validating operational expenses, particularly in sensitive investigations where transparency must be balanced with confidentiality. The French Gendarmerie’s cybercrime division (C3N), together with defence and judicial authorities, launched this pilot to improve traceability and auditability of judicial expenses without exposing operational details. The objective is to simplify expense validation, ensure compliance, and enable secure oversight of funds used during investigations. The system uses smart contracts deployed on a public blockchain to manage authorised expense validation workflows. Only approved actors can interact with the contracts, which record transactions immutably and enable auditing of fund usage while abstracting sensitive operational information. Integration with internal financial systems allows expenses to be justified and reviewed efficiently. The pilot has reduced administrative burden, improved financial traceability, and strengthened accountability while preserving operational secrecy. It demonstrates how distributed ledger systems can support trusted financial governance in high-security public sector contexts.

title: Blockchain-Based Training Certificates
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: The Chamber of Industry and Commerce of Munich and Upper Bavaria
source_description: Employers and institutions often struggle to verify the authenticity of training certificates, while issuing bodies face increasing administrative workloads and fraud risks. The Chamber of Industry and Commerce of Munich and Upper Bavaria, in cooperation with the Bavarian Digital Ministry, launched this pilot to modernise vocational certificate issuance and verification. The objective is to enable instant, reliable validation of qualifications while simplifying processes for graduates, employers and certifying authorities. Certificates are issued digitally, with cryptographic hash values anchored on a blockchain. Graduates share a PDF certificate and a verification key, which employers can upload to a web application to instantly confirm authenticity against the ledger. The solution integrates with existing certification workflows without exposing personal data. The pilot improves trust in credentials, reduces verification time from days to seconds, lowers administrative costs, and enhances labour market efficiency. It provides a scalable foundation for broader adoption of digital credentials across education and training systems.

title: Copyright Management
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Italian Society of Authors and Publishers (SIAE)
source_description: Copyright management requires handling vast volumes of metadata, rights information and transactions, often across fragmented systems that lack transparency and efficiency. The Italian Society of Authors and Publishers (SIAE), together with Algorand, launched this pilot to modernise copyright registration, rights tracking and remuneration processes. The objective is to create a transparent, secure and scalable ecosystem that better serves creators, publishers and rights holders while reducing disputes and administrative costs. The platform uses a public blockchain based on a pure Proof-of-Stake protocol to record rights metadata and transactions immutably. Smart contracts manage ownership, licensing events and revenue distribution, while system integrations connect existing rights management databases to the ledger. The pilot enhances traceability, improves data integrity and supports high transaction throughput. Expected impacts include faster rights registration, improved transparency for creators, reduced reconciliation costs, and a future-proof infrastructure for digital copyright management at national scale.

title: Finding Waste Heat Spots
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Austrian Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation, and Technology
source_description: Large amounts of industrial waste heat remain unused in cities, despite growing demand for sustainable district heating solutions. The HotCity’s pilot, backed by the Austrian government and deployed in Vienna and Graz, addresses this inefficiency by engaging citizens in identifying waste heat sources. Stakeholders include municipalities, energy providers, industrial operators and residents. The objective is to crowdsource reliable data on waste heat availability and integrate it into district heating planning, improving energy efficiency and reducing emissions. The pilot combines a digital platform with a blockchain-based incentive mechanism that records submissions and rewards contributors with tokens for validated data. Submitted location data is verified and aggregated to support urban energy planning. The approach improves data coverage at low cost while ensuring transparency and trust in contributions. The pilot demonstrates increased citizen engagement, better identification of usable waste heat, and potential reductions in CO₂ emissions by integrating industrial surplus heat into existing heating networks.

title: Health Certificates To Address Lockdowns
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, governments, employers and event organisers required reliable ways to verify individuals’ health status in order to manage access to workplaces, transport and public spaces while limiting lockdowns. Existing paper-based certificates were difficult to verify at scale, easy to falsify and slow to distribute. Health n Go, developed by Swiss company TIXnGO, repurposed an existing digital ticketing infrastructure to address this challenge by enabling the secure issuance and presentation of health certificates. Stakeholders included healthcare providers, public authorities, organisations managing access control, and citizens needing proof of health status. The objective was to provide a scalable, secure and privacy-preserving mechanism for distributing trusted health certificates. The solution uses distributed ledger technology to issue each certificate with a unique, encrypted and traceable digital identity anchored on a blockchain. Certificates are stored in a mobile wallet on the user’s smartphone and can be presented via a QR code, which is scanned and verified against the ledger without revealing unnecessary personal data. The pilot enabled rapid deployment of digital health passes, reduced fraud risk, improved verification speed, and supported safer reopening strategies. It demonstrated the feasibility of decentralised digital certification in crisis response contexts.

title: Medical Data Management
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Healthcare providers face challenges in securely managing and sharing patient medical records while ensuring data integrity, privacy and accessibility. Fragmented systems and limited interoperability can delay treatment and reduce patient control over personal health information. To improve transparency and empower patients, VeChain and I-Dante co-developed a distributed ledger-based medical data management platform, deployed at the Mediterranean Hospital of Cyprus. The objective is to provide secure, patient-centred record management while improving traceability and reliability of clinical data. The platform records encrypted medical data references on a blockchain infrastructure, ensuring tamper-resistant logging of transactions and access events. Patients access their records through mobile interfaces, while backend systems integrate with hospital information systems via secure APIs. Cryptographic validation mechanisms ensure that data integrity can be verified without exposing sensitive content on-chain. The first deployment phase in the emergency department enables identity verification, queue management and direct patient interaction with medical records. The solution has been implemented in pilot deployment within the hospital environment. It enhances transparency, strengthens data integrity, improves patient engagement and streamlines administrative processes while maintaining compliance with healthcare data protection standards.

title: Tax Payments with bitcoins in the City of Zermatt
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Switzerland's canton system allows municipalities flexibility in payment methods, enabling innovative approaches to public finance that could position localities as attractive destinations for cryptocurrency businesses and residents. Zermatt became the second Swiss municipality after Zug to accept Bitcoin for tax payments, allowing residents to settle obligations up to CHF 250 (approximately €230) using cryptocurrency. The system operates through partnership with Bitcoin Suisse AG, which provides instant conversion to Swiss Francs, eliminating volatility risk for the municipal treasury whilst offering convenience for crypto-holding residents. All transactions maintain full regulatory compliance including anti-money laundering requirements. The initiative reflects Switzerland's broader approach of integrating cryptocurrency into mainstream financial services whilst maintaining regulatory oversight.

title: Blockchain-based union card
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The blockchain-based union card initiative aims to address challenges related to membership verification, data integrity, and secure communication between trade unions and their members. Traditional membership systems are vulnerable to duplication, outdated records, and privacy risks. The Italian trade union Fim Cisl, its members, and union administrators are the primary stakeholders. The objective is to ensure unique, tamper-proof membership registration while enabling trusted, ongoing digital engagement between the union and its members. The solution consists of a tokenised digital union card built on the Ethereum blockchain. Membership credentials are issued as digital tokens managed through mobile applications and wallets. Transactions and updates are recorded immutably, ensuring that each membership is uniquely registered and verifiable, while personal data is protected through cryptographic mechanisms. The initiative provides certified and transparent membership records, reduces the risk of fraud or data manipulation, and strengthens privacy protection. It also creates a secure digital channel for sharing information, announcements, and services, improving member engagement and enabling scalable, trusted union operations.

title: Traceability of meat and milk
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Regione Lombardia per la trasformazione digitale
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: Consumers increasingly demand transparency regarding the origin, safety and quality of agri-food products, while producers and public authorities require reliable mechanisms to demonstrate compliance with health and animal welfare standards. In Lombardy, the regional administration sought to strengthen trust across the agri-food supply chain by providing verifiable information on meat and milk products available in supermarkets. Stakeholders include consumers, farmers, processing plants, regional health inspectors, third-party certification bodies and food retailers. The objective is to enhance transparency, improve communication between companies and citizens, and reinforce food safety oversight through a trusted traceability framework. The solution is based on a blockchain infrastructure that records key supply chain events and inspection results in an immutable ledger. Each product package includes a QR code that consumers can scan to access structured information pages containing official data from public authorities and companies, including inspection outcomes on animal health, drug use, hygiene conditions and third-party animal welfare controls. The system integrates supply chain data inputs with public administration databases to ensure data integrity and accessibility. Expected impacts include increased consumer confidence, improved brand value for compliant producers, enhanced regulatory transparency and more efficient information sharing across the agri-food ecosystem.

title: Digital baccalaureate diplomas
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: This use case addresses the need for secure, verifiable, and easily shareable educational credentials. Paper-based diplomas are vulnerable to loss, forgery, and costly verification processes. The project involves Villa Flaminia International High Schools, students, and external stakeholders such as universities and employers. Its objective is to issue tamper-proof digital baccalaureate diplomas that certify both the final qualification and the student’s broader educational pathway. The solution issues digital diplomas certified on the public Ethereum platform. Key milestones of the student’s training process, including courses and subjects completed, are notarised and anchored to the ledger. Credentials can be shared digitally, with third parties able to verify authenticity without relying on intermediaries. The initiative improves trust and efficiency in credential verification, reduces administrative costs, and enhances student mobility. It delivers a better user experience for graduates and institutions while providing a scalable, reliable foundation for lifelong digital education records.

title: Kickstarting the Financial Lives of Refugees in Finland
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Asylum seekers in Finland faced significant barriers accessing financial services, as traditional banking requires identity documentation that refugees often cannot provide, forcing reliance on cash and excluding them from the formal economy. The Finnish Immigration Service partnered with MONI, a Finnish fintech startup, to provide asylum seekers with prepaid Mastercards linked to blockchain-based digital identities, replacing cash-based support systems. Several thousand participants received cards enabling participation in the formal economy whilst building transaction histories that could support future creditworthiness assessments. The blockchain component provides identity verification without requiring traditional documentation, enabling financial inclusion for individuals whose identity records may be incomplete or inaccessible. MIT Technology Review recognised the initiative as a pioneering example of blockchain technology addressing humanitarian challenges.

title: Online services for managing personnel salary accounts
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Transfers of a general character between different levels of government.
source_description: Managing personnel salary accounts across public administrations requires the secure handling and exchange of highly sensitive personal and financial data, while complying with strict legal, privacy, and sovereignty constraints. In Italy, the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Ministry of Interior must cooperate to process salary information, yet fragmented private cloud infrastructures and rigid data-sharing mechanisms limit efficiency and transparency. The aim of this use case is to enable seamless inter-ministerial collaboration, optimise the use of existing IT resources, and ensure that sensitive data remains protected and under institutional control throughout its lifecycle. The solution is delivered through the SUNFISH platform, which provides Federation-as-a-Service capabilities to securely interconnect heterogeneous private cloud environments. A blockchain-empowered service ledger governs service registration, access control, and accountability across the federation, while sensitive data processing is executed within authorised cloud domains. This approach enables secure resource sharing without centralising data. The demonstrator confirms improved infrastructure utilisation, reduced operational complexity, and secure cross-ministry data exchange, offering a scalable and compliant model for handling sensitive public sector information.

title: Use of Public Cloud PaaS to host SaaS and/or to integrate with commercial SaaS solutions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Modernising fiscal services requires public administrations to exploit the scalability of public cloud platforms while preserving strict compliance with secrecy, privacy, and data protection regulations. In Malta, the Ministry for Finance and the Taxation Department must collect, validate, and process data from taxpayers, employers, banks, and SMEs, yet traditional systems constrain integration and responsiveness. The objective of this use case is to simplify interactions between citizens and government, improve service agility, and securely integrate governmental applications with external service providers. The solution relies on the SUNFISH platform to federate public cloud Platform-as-a-Service environments hosting government applications with commercial Software-as-a-Service solutions, such as payroll systems. Secure federation mechanisms enforce policies, control data flows, and ensure regulatory compliance across environments. The results include enhanced scalability, improved interoperability, reduced operational overhead, and faster deployment of digital services, demonstrating how public cloud adoption can strengthen efficiency and service quality in the public sector.

title: Organised Crime Unit: Secure Cloud Storage for Data
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: South East Regional Cyber Crime Unit (SEROCU)
source_description: Handling cybercrime evidence demands strict control over data locality, access rights, and confidentiality, while enabling effective collaboration across law enforcement agencies. The South East Regional Cyber Crime Unit must store sensitive investigation data on its own premises but also grant regulated access to other Regional Cyber Crime Units and national bodies during active cases. Conventional sharing models risk exposing sensitive information or breaching jurisdictional constraints. The goal of this use case is to support secure, privacy-preserving cooperation without centralising or duplicating data. The SUNFISH platform provides Secure Multiparty Computation services based on advanced cryptographic techniques, allowing authorised searches and operations to be performed on encrypted data without revealing its content. Data remains local, while access policies are enforced across federated cloud environments. The Proof of Concept demonstrates privacy-preserving cross-cloud data sharing, improved investigative collaboration, and stronger protection of sensitive evidence, establishing a robust and scalable framework for secure law enforcement operations.

title: Corporate Registry in commercial court
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: French commercial court clerks faced delays and limited transparency when recording changes to companies’ legal status, including name changes, branch establishments and dissolutions. Multiple stakeholders – the National Council of Clerks (NCC), local court offices and regulatory bodies – required reliable, synchronised access to registry data to ensure legal certainty and efficient processing. The objective was to streamline updates to the corporate registry and improve data integrity across jurisdictions. A distributed ledger platform jointly developed by IBM and the NCC was implemented using Hyperledger Fabric. The permissioned blockchain records and shares regulatory information related to companies’ lifecycle events, ensuring tamper-evident entries, controlled access and real-time synchronisation between authorised participants through integrated registry systems. In proof-of-concept testing, registry update times were reduced from several days to one day, improving operational efficiency, transparency and trust while strengthening data reliability across the national registry ecosystem.

title: Verifiable and tamper-proof university degree
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Private universities in Italy sought differentiation through technological innovation in credential management, recognising that blockchain verification could provide competitive advantages in demonstrating institutional credibility to employers. Link Campus University in Rome implemented blockchain-certified academic degrees, storing cryptographic hashes on a distributed ledger to enable instant verification by employers and other institutions worldwide. The system allows graduates to share their credentials digitally with verifiable proof of authenticity, eliminating requirements for physical document copies or institutional confirmation letters. This digital sharing mechanism accelerates hiring processes whilst reducing administrative costs for both the university and credential verifiers. The initiative demonstrates private sector leadership in educational technology adoption within the Italian higher education system.

title: Smart Working management with blockchain in the Municipality of Bari
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public administrations faced organisational and accountability challenges when adopting remote and flexible working arrangements, particularly in tracking activities, authorisations and compliance with internal rules. The Municipality of Bari launched this pilot within the H2020 CITADEL project to explore new ways of managing smart working for municipal employees. Stakeholders included municipal managers, employees participating in agile working, and IT service providers. The objective was to test a transparent and trustworthy digital system to manage work authorisations, activities and reporting while supporting organisational flexibility. The solution involved developing a prototype based on distributed ledger technology to record work agreements, task assignments and activity logs in a tamper-resistant manner. Smart contracts formalised working arrangements and ensured that records could not be altered unilaterally. The system integrated with existing administrative tools while providing a shared, auditable record of smart working activities. The pilot improved transparency, reduced administrative disputes, and increased trust between employees and management. It also demonstrated how public administrations can adopt flexible working models while maintaining accountability, offering a replicable approach for digital transformation in public sector workforce management.

title: Verification of the authenticity of university degrees
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Universities and employers face growing challenges in verifying academic qualifications due to increasing diploma fraud and time-consuming manual validation processes. The University of St. Gallen introduced a pilot to enable near-instant verification of degree authenticity, benefiting graduates, employers and academic institutions. The objective was to reduce verification times from days to seconds while strengthening trust in academic credentials. The solution was developed with Swiss startup BlockFactory and relies on issuing digital diplomas whose cryptographic fingerprints are anchored on a public blockchain. Graduates receive a digital certificate that can be shared electronically, while verifiers upload the certificate to a validation interface that checks its integrity against the blockchain record. The system integrates with the university’s degree management processes without exposing sensitive personal data on-chain. The pilot significantly reduced administrative workload, accelerated recruitment and admissions processes, and enhanced protection against fraudulent diplomas. It demonstrated a scalable and cost-effective approach to digital credential verification that supports international mobility and trust in higher education qualifications.

title: Flexible energy demand through blockchain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Agency for Energy and Sustainable Development (AESS)
source_description: Creating more efficient and sustainable energy systems requires mechanisms that align consumption with local production while rewarding flexible demand. In Bologna, citizens and companies participating in a local energy community face limited incentives to adapt energy usage patterns, despite growing pressure to reduce costs and emissions. The GECO project brings together public bodies, research institutions, and local partners with the objective of enabling flexible energy demand and strengthening community-based energy models. The solution uses a blockchain-based infrastructure to record and validate energy production, consumption, and exchanges among participants, ensuring transparency and trust in shared data. Reduced tariffs and incentives are managed through trusted digital records accessible to community members. The pilot demonstrates improved coordination between producers and consumers, greater transparency in energy flows, lower energy costs, and a replicable model for smart, decentralised energy communities supporting sustainability objectives.

title: Enhancing intermodal freight movements in Marseille
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Intermodal freight transport along major logistics corridors involves numerous actors, documents and handovers, often resulting in data silos, delays and limited visibility across the supply chain. The Marseille Fos Port Authority launched a proof of concept to improve coordination and data sharing along the Mediterranean–Rhône–Saône corridor. Stakeholders included port authorities, logistics operators, customs, shipping companies and inland transport providers. The objective was to enhance efficiency, transparency and trust in intermodal freight movements. The solution uses a blockchain-based data-sharing platform that allows authorised users to access protected logistics information, such as customs documentation, container status, weight, origin and destination, through controlled permissions. Data entries are recorded immutably, ensuring traceability across transport modes. The platform integrates with existing port and logistics systems, acting as a shared reference layer rather than replacing operational tools. The pilot improved information availability, reduced duplication of documents, and facilitated smoother coordination between actors. It demonstrated the potential for distributed ledgers to support resilient and efficient logistics ecosystems in complex port environments.

title: University certificates verification in many Spanish Universities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: University of Murcia, Polytechnic University of Cartagena (UPCT), and the San Antonio Catholic University
source_description: Spanish universities have faced increasing risks of academic credential falsification and administrative burdens in verifying qualifications for employers and international institutions. Three universities—the University of Murcia, the Polytechnic University of Cartagena and the San Antonio Catholic University—launched a joint pilot to test a shared digital standard for certificate verification. Stakeholders included universities, students, employers and accreditation bodies. The objective was to minimise diploma fraud while simplifying verification processes across institutions. The solution is based on a distributed ledger infrastructure where academic certificates are issued digitally and registered as immutable records. Graduates can share their credentials electronically, and verifiers can confirm authenticity against the ledger without contacting the issuing university. The system supports interoperability between institutions through a common certification standard. The pilot reduced verification times, lowered administrative costs, and strengthened trust in academic qualifications. It also demonstrated how multiple universities can collaborate on a shared digital infrastructure, paving the way for scalable national or regional credential verification systems.

title: Verification of COVID-19 testing with blockchain in Austria
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Federal Ministry for Digital and Economic Affairs
source_description: Ensuring the authenticity of health credentials became a critical challenge during the COVID-19 pandemic, as public authorities faced fraud, misinformation, and growing concerns over data privacy. In Austria, the QualiSig project addresses these issues by enabling citizens to securely verify COVID-19 testing and related health information while retaining full control over their personal data. The initiative involves public authorities and leverages the national digital identity framework to support trusted interactions. The solution combines encrypted communications, decentralised data storage, and qualified digital signatures applied via mobile devices. Verifiable records are anchored on the Ardor blockchain using the Ignis tokenisation system, ensuring integrity and tamper resistance. The prototypes demonstrate improved fraud prevention, enhanced trust in digital health information, and strong privacy guarantees, delivering reliable, user-centric verification mechanisms for critical public health processes.

title: Loans and insurance services requests simplification
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Direzione dei Sistemi Informativi e dell’Innovazione (DSII), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF)
source_description: Public administration employees in Italy rely on complex processes to request loans and insurance services involving salary withholdings, requiring extensive coordination between the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), financial institutions and employees. These processes were slow, fragmented and prone to reconciliation errors. CreditoNet 2.0 was launched to modernise and simplify these interactions. Stakeholders include MEF, public employees, banks, insurance companies and payroll service providers. The objective is to streamline requests, improve data security and accelerate reconciliation. The solution uses SIAChain, a blockchain network involving major Italian banks, to create a shared, trusted infrastructure for exchanging and validating loan and insurance data. Requests, approvals and payroll withholdings are recorded on the ledger, enabling automated checks and reducing manual intervention. Integration with existing MEF and financial systems ensures continuity of operations. The pilot improved processing speed, reduced errors and reconciliation times, enhanced data security, and enabled a more transparent and efficient service model. It illustrates how distributed ledger infrastructures can modernise complex financial workflows in public administration.

title: Company Passport
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Establishing a company entirely through digital channels requires multiple parties to trust the identity, authority, and credentials of founders and representatives without relying on fragmented paper-based checks. In the Netherlands, this use case emerged from collaboration between the Royal Dutch Association of Civil-Law Notaries, the Dutch Blockchain Coalition, chambers of commerce, financial institutions, and the Tax and Customs Administration to explore how the company-formation process could become more secure and efficient in a fully digital environment. The objective is to support digital company creation by creating a trusted framework through which relevant parties can rely on validated business and identity information. The implementation developed the concept of an enterprise or company passport as a trust framework rather than a single standalone application. At a conceptual level, it uses shared digital credentials and interoperable trust components to allow authorised actors such as notaries, banks, and public authorities to access and rely on the same verified information during the incorporation process. The model was shaped as a public-private collaboration involving legal, financial, and governmental stakeholders. The impact includes the potential to simplify digital incorporation, reduce duplication in verification steps, and improve trust across participating organisations. It also supports interoperability and creates strategic value by laying a common foundation for safer and more efficient digital business formation.

title: Carrière Wallet
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Employers, public bodies, and education providers increasingly need secure ways to verify qualifications and professional records, while individuals want greater control over who can access their credentials and under what conditions. In the Netherlands, the Career Wallet concept addresses this challenge by enabling people to manage digitally validated diplomas, certificates, proofs of conduct, and related records in a way that supports mobility between education and work. The objective is to give individuals more control over their verified credentials while making it easier for employers and institutions to receive trusted information when needed. The implementation centres on wallet-based technology for storing and presenting digital proofs, supported by practical experiments involving large employers, financial and recruitment partners, the Employee Insurance Administration Agency, the Municipality of Rotterdam, and the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. At a conceptual level, the solution uses verifiable digital credentials and wallet infrastructure to allow holders to share selected records securely, including within European blockchain-related initiatives for trusted exchange. The impact includes improved portability of qualifications, stronger privacy and user control, and more efficient verification of career-related information. It also supports scalability in labour-market and education processes and creates value by reducing friction in recruitment, onboarding, and skills recognition.

title: uNLock the world
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The uNLock initiative was launched in 2020 by a consortium of public and private organisations in the Netherlands to address the need for secure and verifiable sharing of COVID-19 test results during the pandemic. The objective was to enable individuals to prove their health status in order to access controlled environments such as events or venues, thereby supporting safer reopening of society. The solution consists of a digital infrastructure that allows users to store and share certified test results in a secure and privacy-preserving manner. Distributed ledger technologies and cryptographic mechanisms are used to ensure the authenticity and integrity of the shared credentials, while giving users control over their personal data. The system enables verification of test results by authorised parties without centralised data storage. While the initiative demonstrated the feasibility of secure digital health credentials in controlled settings, its relevance declined as pandemic-related restrictions were lifted

title: My pension rights transfer
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Transferring pension rights between schemes is often administratively complex, slow, and difficult for individuals to assess, particularly when they need to compare accrued value across different providers and understand the implications of a transfer. In the Netherlands, this use case was developed to simplify pension-rights transfer by giving users a clearer and faster way to find existing pensions and review transfer proposals. The objective is to make pension transfers more accessible, transparent, and secure, while reducing friction between pension administrators. The implementation resulted in the Mijnwaardeoverdracht.nl platform, developed with major pension providers and platform developers at APG under the Hyfen name. At a conceptual level, the platform connects the administrative systems of pension-sector organisations through a modular architecture that combines established technologies such as databases and cloud infrastructure with distributed ledger technology. The distributed ledger is used only where it adds value, specifically to create a shared understanding between participating parties, rather than as the whole solution. The impact includes quicker and simpler transfer processes, better comparability between pension arrangements, and improved coordination across providers. It also supports interoperability and scalability in the pension domain, while creating value for users by turning a traditionally cumbersome procedure into a more straightforward and digitally manageable service.

title: Electronic bill of lading (eBL)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: The electronic bill of lading initiative involves collaboration between Singapore and the Netherlands to modernise maritime trade documentation along the Europe–Far East trade lane. Traditional paper-based bills of lading are inefficient, prone to delays, and vulnerable to fraud, creating bottlenecks in global supply chains. The objective is to enable secure, interoperable, and legally recognised digital documentation for shipping transactions. The solution uses distributed ledger technologies and interoperable digital platforms to issue, transfer, and verify electronic bills of lading across different systems. The pilot demonstrated that documents generated on one platform could be validated and processed by another, supporting cross-platform interoperability. The system integrates digital identity, secure data exchange, and verification mechanisms to ensure trust and authenticity. While the pilot confirmed technical feasibility and potential efficiency gains, broader adoption depends on regulatory changes to recognise electronic documents as legally equivalent to paper-based versions.

title: Energy trading platform
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Local electricity markets face increasing complexity due to decentralised renewable generation, fluctuating demand, and grid constraints that traditional market mechanisms struggle to manage in real time. In Germany, energy producers, consumers, grid operators, and market authorities require more flexible trading models to balance local surpluses and bottlenecks efficiently while maintaining system stability. The BEST project, funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy and led by the Reiner Lemoine Institute, aims to design a decentralised electricity market framework that enables local energy trading and optimised grid usage. The objective is to support real-time balancing of supply and demand at local level, reducing congestion and improving the integration of renewable energy sources. The solution is implemented through a blockchain-based electricity market provider system (SMBS) that records transactions, matches local buyers and sellers, and manages market rules in a decentralised manner. Smart contracts support automated settlement and coordination between participants, while grid and metering data feeds enable near real-time operation. The project demonstrates improved market transparency, faster settlement, and more efficient use of local energy resources. Expected impacts include reduced grid congestion, lower balancing costs, enhanced renewable integration, and a scalable model for future decentralised energy markets.

title: Privacy engine
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Citizens using Antwerp’s digital services lacked meaningful control over personal data distributed across multiple municipal systems, while compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation required transparent consent management and data portability. Digipolis Antwerp, together with Jolocom, V-ICT-OR and the Flemish Government, launched the Blockchain on the Move initiative to create a Self-Sovereign Identity infrastructure embedded in the Antwerp City Platform as a Service ecosystem. The initial use case focused on change-of-address procedures, enabling residents to manage which public bodies could access specific attributes. The solution relies on distributed ledger technology to anchor decentralised identifiers and verifiable credentials, combined with cryptographic key pairs and a business rules engine governing permissions. Personal data remain under citizen control, while hashed proofs and consent records are registered on-chain and connected to municipal back-office systems through secure APIs. The architecture supports selective disclosure of attributes and auditable access logs. The project improved transparency, strengthened privacy-by-design compliance and reduced administrative friction in data exchange between agencies. It demonstrated a scalable model for citizen-centric identity management within local government digital platforms.

title: Digital talent profile
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Children’s talents and personal interests are often recorded informally and remain fragmented across schools, youth organisations and associations, limiting the ability of educators and supervisors to nurture strengths consistently over time. The City of Antwerp introduced the Digital Talent Profile to address this challenge by creating a trusted way to collect, represent and share children’s talents beyond organisational boundaries. Stakeholders include children, parents, educators, youth organisations and municipal services. The objective is to empower children by giving them ownership over how their talents are documented and shared, while enabling supervisors to better support personal development through a holistic and portable profile. The solution is implemented using a decentralised digital identity approach based on distributed ledger technology. Individual talent statements are captured as claims, supported by proofs and attestations issued by trusted actors, each recorded with a unique and immutable timestamp. These records are managed through digital wallets that allow children, with appropriate guardianship, to control consent, scope and duration of data sharing. The pilot improves trust, data portability and privacy, reduces duplication of assessments, and enhances collaboration across youth services. It delivers qualitative benefits in empowerment and personalisation and provides a scalable foundation for citizen-centric identity services.

title: European Social Security Pass
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cross-border mobility within the European Union creates significant challenges for the verification of social security coverage, as citizens moving between Member States must rely on fragmented, paper-based, or slow administrative procedures. Public authorities, employers, and mobile citizens face delays, errors, and uncertainty in proving entitlement to social security rights. The European Social Security Pass pilot addresses these issues by exploring a digital solution for secure cross-border verification of social security status and identity. Launched in 2021, the initiative involves around a dozen Member States and aims to assess technical, organisational, and legal feasibility ahead of possible large-scale deployment. The solution is developed using the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI), the EU-wide platform designed to support trusted cross-border public services. Social security credentials and identity attributes are issued and verified through decentralised mechanisms, enabling citizens to manage their data while authorities can reliably validate entitlements across borders. Interoperability with national systems and compliance with EU data protection rules are built into the design. The pilot demonstrates faster verification processes, reduced administrative burden, improved fraud prevention, and greater user control. It lays the groundwork for a more efficient, secure, and citizen-centric approach to social security coordination across Europe.

title: BIMChain: the blockchain application for managing BIM files
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Building Information Modelling projects involve multiple actors exchanging complex digital files throughout design, construction and operation phases, often leading to disputes over file ownership, versioning and responsibilities. Italferr developed BIMChain to address transparency and trust issues in collaborative BIM environments. Stakeholders include infrastructure designers, engineers, contractors, clients and asset managers. The objective is to ensure traceability, accountability and trust in the lifecycle management of BIM files while supporting collaborative workflows. BIMChain integrates distributed ledger technology into BIM processes to create a shared environment governed by smart contracts. Each BIM file and modification is associated with a verifiable digital identity, recording who performed which action, with what role and at what time. Smart contracts regulate access rights, responsibilities and exchange conditions between parties, while metadata and transaction logs are anchored immutably to the ledger. The solution integrates with existing BIM tools without duplicating large files on-chain. The pilot improves collaboration efficiency, reduces disputes, enhances auditability and supports compliance in complex infrastructure projects. It demonstrates how blockchain can strengthen governance and trust in digital construction ecosystems.

title: Diploma Notarisation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: ICE - Agenzia per la promozione all'estero e l'internazionalizzazione delle imprese italiane
source_description: Educational institutions and employers require reliable mechanisms to verify academic diplomas, while issuing bodies must protect against falsification and disputes over authenticity. ICE, the Italian Trade Agency, launched a pilot to certify diplomas issued for the 52nd CORCE “Fausto De Franceschi” Master programme in internationalisation. Stakeholders include graduates, ICE, academic partners and employers. The objective is to guarantee authenticity, date certainty and immutability of issued diplomas, while simplifying verification processes. The solution uses distributed ledger technology to notarise diploma data by anchoring cryptographic representations of certificates on a shared ledger. Each notarised record provides proof of existence, authorship and integrity without exposing personal data publicly. Verification can be performed independently by authorised parties by comparing diploma data against the ledger record. The pilot reduces verification time, strengthens trust in qualifications, and lowers administrative overhead for issuing and verifying entities. It also provides graduates with portable, verifiable credentials, demonstrating the potential of blockchain-based notarisation for education and professional certification.

title: A blockchain platform for public administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Federazione Lavoratori Pubblici e Funzioni Pubbliche
source_description: Public administrations and trade unions often rely on paper-based or fragmented digital procedures for approvals, negotiations and certifications, limiting transparency and slowing decision-making. Blockchain Italia developed a blockchain-based platform for the Federazione Lavoratori Pubblici e Funzioni Pubbliche (FLP) to support secure and auditable administrative processes. Stakeholders include trade unions, public employees, employers and administrative bodies. The objective is to enable legally robust, transparent and remote execution of administrative and contractual procedures. The platform applies distributed ledger technology to notarise decisions and procedural steps, including budget approvals, remote trade union conciliation, supplementary collective agreements and diploma notarisation. Each action is recorded immutably, creating a shared and verifiable process history accessible to authorised parties. Integration with existing organisational workflows allows gradual adoption without disrupting operations. The pilot improves procedural transparency, reduces delays, enables remote participation and strengthens trust among parties. It illustrates how blockchain platforms can modernise governance processes in public administration and labour relations.

title: Secure Digital Identities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Digital services across sectors require secure and interoperable identity solutions, yet fragmented identity systems create barriers to cross-sector and cross-border services. The IDunion cooperative was established to develop a shared self-sovereign identity ecosystem in Germany, supported by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy. Stakeholders include technology providers, public authorities, businesses and citizens. The objective is to establish a production-ready identity network supporting people, organisations and devices across multiple domains such as education, mobility, e-health and industry. The solution is based on self-sovereign identity principles using distributed ledger infrastructure to anchor decentralised identifiers and verifiable credentials. Identity wallets allow users to store and present credentials issued by trusted parties, while a test network supports interoperability and governance across partners. The pilot improves identity security, user control and interoperability, reduces dependency on central identity providers and enables new digital services. With a functioning test network and multiple applications, IDunion provides a scalable foundation for trusted digital identity ecosystems.

title: Swiss Ledger: Private, institutional and non-profit blockchain network
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Swiss institutions required secure and transparent methods for managing digital assets and credentials that met the country's high standards for financial services and data protection. Swiss Ledger was established as a private, institutional, and non-profit blockchain infrastructure providing distributed ledger services to Swiss organisations across sectors including finance, government, and academia. The platform enables secure credential management, asset tokenisation, and data integrity verification whilst maintaining compliance with Swiss regulatory requirements. Operating since 2021, Swiss Ledger provides a permissioned blockchain environment where participating organisations can issue and verify digital credentials, track assets, and maintain auditable records. The infrastructure supports Switzerland's broader digital transformation objectives whilst preserving the privacy and security standards that characterise Swiss financial and institutional services.

title: National Green Pass
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The San Marino Digital Covid Certificate covers vaccination against Sars-Cov2, past infection or negative test result. The certificate issued has a validity of 1 week starting 15 days after the first vaccination dose or 9 months from the completed vaccination cycle. The certificate is issued upon personal request, in a paper or digital format, by the ISS or facilities authorized by the San Marino health authorities. The San Marino Digital Covid Certificate, using a public key for issuance and validation, has been set up as a national infrastructure at San Marino Innovation S.p.A. This ensures the integrity, authenticity and control of the data contained therein. The entity temporarily performs the functions of Country Signing Certification Authority (CSCA) and is in charge of issuing the Root Certificate for the generation of public and private keys necessary for signing the digital certificates. According to the Ministry of Health and Social Security, the extremely efficient development is owed fully to the multi-layered, fruitful collaboration between San Marino’s public entities and private partners DNV and VeChain.

title: PlanetWatch: monitoring air quality
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Traditional air quality monitoring relies on expensive governmental stations providing limited geographic coverage and delayed data publication, leaving many pollution hotspots undetected and populations without timely warnings. PlanetWatch, a French startup and CERN spin-off, developed a global air quality monitoring network using the Algorand blockchain to create the first immutable ledger for environmental data. The platform incentivises individuals and organisations to deploy low-cost sensors through PLANET token rewards, with over 25,000 sensors deployed globally by late 2021. Initial deployments in Milan and Taranto, Italy, demonstrated the system's capability to provide dense, real-time monitoring complementing official stations at a fraction of the cost. Data collected undergoes validation through CERN's C2MON acquisition framework before blockchain recording, ensuring reliability. The Algorand Foundation supported the initiative through grants, recognising its environmental and public health potential.

title: Blockchain service infrastructure
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Italy lacked a national blockchain infrastructure for public services, limiting the country's ability to participate in European initiatives and deploy distributed ledger solutions for citizen services at scale. IBSI (Italian Blockchain Service Infrastructure) was launched in January 2021 by a consortium including AgID, Poste Italiane, INAIL, INPS, Sogei, Politecnico di Milano, University of Cagliari, and others to create Italy's first national blockchain network for public services. The project aims to develop applications supporting digital certificates, Made in Italy supply chain traceability, and sustainable energy models using Distributed Ledger Technology. IBSI operates in synergy with the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI), with Italy receiving €149,928 through the Blockchain4Italy project for EBSI node deployment. The infrastructure implements the Once Only principle, enabling citizens and businesses to provide data once for reuse across public administrations.

title: Pharmaledger: blockchain enabled healthcare
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Innovative Medicines Initiative (IMI) and the European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries and Associations (EFPIA)
source_description: The healthcare sector faces persistent challenges related to fragmented data, complex supply chains, lengthy drug development processes, and limited trust between stakeholders. Pharmaceutical companies, regulators, healthcare providers, and patients require secure and interoperable systems to exchange information while ensuring transparency, compliance, and data protection. PharmaLedger addresses these needs through a large-scale collaborative initiative funded under the Innovative Medicines Initiative, bringing together pharmaceutical industry leaders, public bodies, research institutions, SMEs, and patient organisations. The project aims to enable a trusted digital platform supporting healthcare processes across three core areas: pharmaceutical supply chains, clinical trials, and health data management. The platform is implemented using distributed ledger technologies to ensure data integrity, traceability, and controlled access among authorised participants. Smart contracts and decentralised governance models support shared processes, while sensitive data is managed in compliance with regulatory and ethical requirements. PharmaLedger demonstrates how shared digital infrastructure can reduce inefficiencies, improve collaboration, and shorten development timelines. The expected impact includes reduced healthcare costs, improved drug traceability, faster and more transparent clinical trials, and enhanced trust across the healthcare ecosystem, providing a scalable foundation for digital transformation in the sector.

title: Public procurement: streamlined and faster digital procedures
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Associazione Nazionale Società Organismi di Attestazione - Unionsoa
source_description: Public procurement processes are often characterised by complex documentation, fragmented qualification checks and slow administrative procedures, increasing costs and delaying projects. This pilot, proposed by UnionSOA and IBM, aims to fully digitise qualification and documentation management in public procurement. Stakeholders include contracting authorities, suppliers, qualification bodies and oversight institutions. The objective is to simplify administrative processes, ensure legal certainty and improve transparency across the procurement chain. The solution uses a blockchain platform deployed on IBM Cloud, structured around notarisation and notification services. Qualification documents and dossiers are notarised on the ledger, providing proof of existence, originality and provenance, while each procedural step is recorded immutably to ensure traceability. Authorised actors can access validated information without repeated submissions. The pilot reduces processing times, lowers administrative burden, improves auditability and supports faster, more reliable procurement procedures. It demonstrates how blockchain can enable end-to-end digital transformation in public procurement systems.

title: Ecocoin: encouraging virtuous behavior
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Encouraging citizens to adopt sustainable behaviours such as recycling and low-emission mobility requires mechanisms that can reliably measure actions and translate them into tangible rewards. Municipalities often struggle to track these activities transparently and at scale, while citizens lack incentives that are trusted and easy to use. The Ecocoin pilot was created to address this gap by assigning concrete value to virtuous environmental actions within a local circular economy. Stakeholders include citizens, municipal waste collectors, local authorities and affiliated commercial partners. The objective is to promote sustainable behaviour while strengthening local economic circuits. The solution combines interconnected sensors used by waste collectors to measure recycling activities with a blockchain-based ledger that records verified actions immutably. Citizens create a digital profile with an associated wallet; when waste is delivered and measured, tokens are generated automatically and credited to the wallet. These tokens can then be spent within participating local networks. The pilot improves transparency, prevents manipulation of data, and builds trust in incentive mechanisms. It delivers qualitative benefits in citizen engagement, supports measurable environmental outcomes, and offers a scalable model for municipalities seeking to reward sustainability while reinforcing local economies.

title: Blockchain for emergency services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Emergency services require rapid, secure access to physical spaces to save lives and protect property, yet traditional key management and access authorisation processes often cause delays. In the Polish city of Olsztyn, police, fire, and ambulance services faced operational inefficiencies when responding to incidents requiring immediate building access. The objective of this use case is to improve response times and operational effectiveness by enabling authorised emergency crews to access buildings without manual key handovers or administrative delays. The city conducted a pilot using a blockchain-based access management solution known as SmartKey. The system connects smart contracts deployed on the Ethereum network with physical IoT devices installed in buildings and emergency vehicles. Access rights are managed digitally and activated automatically during emergencies, allowing authorised responders to unlock doors securely and auditable. The trial demonstrates faster emergency response, reduced operational friction, and improved coordination between services. Qualitative benefits include enhanced safety for citizens and responders, greater accountability through tamper-proof access logs, and a scalable model that can be extended to other cities and critical infrastructure environments.

title: Blockchain-based service to register digital acts at the Court of Cremona
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Judicial systems rely on secure, reliable, and timely registration of legal documents, yet many courts still depend on paper-based or fragmented digital processes that hinder efficiency and continuity, particularly during emergencies. At the Court of Cremona, the Gip-Gup section faced the risk of operational disruption during the COVID-19 lockdown, threatening delays in hearings and case backlogs. The objective of this use case was to ensure continuity of judicial activities while strengthening the integrity and traceability of digital legal documents. In collaboration with Stampiz, the court implemented a service to register digital acts such as judgments, files, copies, and certificates. The solution anchors cryptographic proofs of documents on a blockchain while keeping the files stored securely on the court’s internal servers, ensuring anonymity and preventing unauthorised access. Registration is fully digital and does not require moving files outside the court’s infrastructure. The initiative enabled uninterrupted hearings during the pandemic, accelerated recovery of postponed cases, and improved reliability of registry operations. It demonstrates increased efficiency, stronger evidential integrity, and a robust, scalable approach to digital justice administration.

title: Digital credentials for graduates at University of Lille
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: France's largest public university faced substantial administrative burden from diploma verification requests whilst graduates experienced delays obtaining proof of qualifications for employment or further study. The University of Lille partnered with BCdiploma to implement blockchain-based digital credentials through the Dem-Attest project, issuing bilingual (French/English) certificates that are tamper-proof and valid for life. Since July 2021, the university has issued over 80,000 blockchain certificates covering 700 diploma types at approximately 20,000 per year. The system uses the Avalanche blockchain with an estimated energy footprint of just 0.025g CO2 per credential. The University of Lille leads the Fr.EBSI project integrating with the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure and participates in EBSI-VECTOR for W3C Verifiable Credentials deployment. Online verification has been accessed over 132,000 times, demonstrating strong adoption by employers and institutions.

title: EnergieKnip, Energy Wallet
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: European student mobility programmes like Erasmus faced administrative friction from credential verification requirements, with universities unable to efficiently validate transcripts and qualifications from partner institutions across borders. The EBSI multi-University pilot, launched through the Early Adopters Programme in 2021, brought together 11 universities from 11 countries and 2 European university alliances to test cross-border Verifiable Credentials for education. Six scenarios were developed including Erasmus transcript validation, cross-border PhD applications, European student card verification, and diploma recognition for employment. The pilot demonstrated end-to-end exchange of W3C-standard credentials via EBSI-compliant digital wallets, with institutions including KU Leuven and Italian universities testing the Belgium-Italy corridor.
