title: Automated image recognition for determining the type of wood
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Ensuring the legal origin of timber products is a key requirement under the European Timber Trade Regulation, which obliges market participants to accurately document the wood species used in traded goods. Manual identification of wood species is labour-intensive, requires specialist expertise, and is difficult to apply at scale for inspections and compliance checks. This use case addresses the need for efficient and reliable verification methods that support regulatory enforcement. Stakeholders include regulatory authorities, inspection bodies, and timber traders responsible for due diligence. The objective is to enable large-scale verification of declared wood species and reduce the risk of illegal timber entering the market. The solution involves the development of automated image recognition systems that analyse macroscopic and microscopic wood images. By learning distinguishing visual patterns across species, the system supports consistent classification and comparison against declared information. Integrated into inspection workflows, it enables rapid screening of products and supports expert decision-making. The results include faster and more scalable compliance checks, reduced dependence on scarce specialist resources, and improved detection of mislabelled timber. The initiative strengthens enforcement of timber regulations, supports sustainable forestry, and enhances transparency in the wood supply chain.
supporting_source_urls: Bendszusn, R. (2022). Make-or-buy in the area of Artificial Intelligence: Insights from AI use cases in the German public sector (master's thesis). Hertie School, Berlin.

title: Monitoring biological diversity in agricultural landscapes with remote sensing
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Maintaining and enhancing biodiversity in agricultural landscapes is a central objective of agri-environment-climate measures under the EU Common Agricultural Policy. Policymakers and environmental agencies require consistent, large-scale monitoring tools to assess habitat quality, land-use intensity, and landscape structure over time. Traditional field surveys are accurate but costly and limited in spatial coverage. This project addresses the need for a nationwide, spatially explicit monitoring approach that captures biodiversity-relevant habitat features across agricultural landscapes. Stakeholders include agricultural authorities, environmental agencies, and policymakers responsible for evaluating and designing biodiversity measures. The objective is to establish a robust indicator framework that reflects landscape and field-level characteristics relevant to different taxonomic groups. The solution uses Earth observation data from the Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellites within the Copernicus programme to model habitat features and land-use intensity at large scales. Spatial indicators are derived to describe landscape structure, elements, and management intensity in cropland and grassland areas. The results provide consistent, repeatable monitoring of biodiversity-related patterns at national level. The project supports evidence-based policy evaluation, improved targeting of agri-environment measures, and long-term tracking of biodiversity trends.
supporting_source_urls: Bendszusn, R. (2022). Make-or-buy in the area of Artificial Intelligence: Insights from AI use cases in the German public sector (master's thesis). Hertie School, Berlin.

The pilot applies automated translation systems trained on extensive existing linguistic corpora held by the institution. These systems learn from previously translated documents and continuously improve translation accuracy across relevant language pairs. The solution is integrated into existing translation workflows, allowing human experts to review, correct and refine outputs rather than translating from scratch. The impact includes faster turnaround times, reduced workload for routine translations and better prioritisation of expert human resources. Qualitatively, the project improves operational responsiveness and supports knowledge sharing in multilingual environments, while laying the groundwork for scalable language services across government.

title: AI in numerical weather and climate forecasting
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Numerical weather prediction relies on complex physical models and vast quantities of observational data, including satellite imagery. Processing and integrating this data efficiently remains computationally demanding and may limit forecasting precision, particularly in extreme weather scenarios. The German Weather Service (DWD), in collaboration with Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, developed an AI-supported neural network approach to enhance the processing of satellite imagery within forecasting workflows. The objective is to improve predictive accuracy and optimise the integration of observational data into numerical models. The system uses deep neural networks trained on historical meteorological datasets to extract relevant atmospheric patterns from satellite images and translate them into parameters usable by forecasting models. The AI component operates alongside traditional physics-based simulations, providing complementary inputs that refine model outputs. The approach has been implemented within operational research environments at DWD. It contributes to more accurate short-term forecasts, improved detection of extreme weather events and enhanced computational efficiency, supporting better-informed public warnings and climate resilience planning.
supporting_source_urls: Bendszusn, R. (2022). Make-or-buy in the area of Artificial Intelligence: Insights from AI use cases in the German public sector (master's thesis). Hertie School, Berlin.

title: AI-based Integrated identity management for asylum procedures, improving plausability, data quality and security aspects
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: German Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF)
source_description: Asylum procedures require accurate registration and verification of personal identity under challenging conditions, often involving missing documents, language barriers, and high case volumes. Manual processes increase the risk of data inconsistencies, duplicate records, and security vulnerabilities. This use case supports the Federal Office responsible for asylum procedures by improving the quality, plausibility, and security of identity data. Stakeholders include caseworkers, asylum authorities, and applicants whose cases depend on accurate and fair identity assessment. The objective is to streamline registration processes while strengthening data integrity and preventing fraud. The solution integrates multiple automated support tools into a single identity management system. These include automated transcription of names from non-Latin scripts, dialect analysis to support origin verification, biometric image checks to prevent duplicate files, and extraction of relevant information from mobile devices when documents are unavailable. The system supports caseworkers with structured, evidence-based inputs while maintaining oversight and control. The results include improved data quality, reduced duplication, enhanced security, and more efficient case handling. This leads to faster, fairer asylum procedures and increased trust in administrative processes.

title: Chatbot for the 2021 Federal Elections
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Elections require well-informed citizens who understand voting procedures, the electoral system, and key democratic principles. During the 2021 Federal Elections, the Federal Agency for Civic Education sought to improve access to reliable information and support voter engagement, particularly among digitally active audiences. Traditional information channels can be difficult to navigate or overwhelming, especially for first-time voters. The objective of this use case was to provide accessible, structured, and neutral information about the election process and related political topics. The solution involved deploying an interactive chatbot that delivered curated content on voting procedures, electoral system structure, and practical considerations before election day. Information was organised into thematic dialogues, complemented by quizzes that allowed users to test their knowledge. The chatbot was accessible through digital channels commonly used by citizens, enabling on-demand interaction. The initiative improved accessibility to civic information, encouraged active learning, and supported informed participation in the electoral process. Qualitative results include increased user engagement, clearer understanding of democratic procedures, and a scalable communication tool for future civic education initiatives.

title: Sat4GWR_IF-Bund – Remote sensing & AI for the register census
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Maintaining an accurate and up-to-date register of buildings and dwellings is essential for population statistics, spatial planning, and evidence-based policymaking. Traditional register maintenance relies heavily on administrative updates and manual checks, which can lead to inconsistencies, delays, and incomplete coverage. The Sat4GWR_IF-Bund innovation project addresses these challenges by supporting the German register census with independent, area-wide verification of building data. Stakeholders include the Federal Statistical Office, public administrations, and policymakers who depend on reliable building and housing information. The objective is to enhance data quality assurance, complement register-based census methods, and support the long-term maintenance of building registers. The solution applies neural network–based image analysis to satellite imagery and aerial photographs to automatically detect buildings and derive characteristics such as building size and usage. These outputs are compared with existing register data to identify discrepancies and support validation workflows. Remote sensing data is used as an auxiliary, non-intrusive source that scales nationwide. The project improves completeness, consistency, and reliability of census data, reduces manual verification effort, and establishes a scalable approach to register maintenance, strengthening the statistical foundation for public decision-making.

title: Machine learning increases biotechnological protein production
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Biotechnological production of proteins, such as those used in vaccines and therapeutics, is complex and sensitive to numerous biological and process variables, making yield optimisation challenging. Researchers at the Paul Ehrlich Institute initiated this project to improve predictability and efficiency in protein synthesis within host organisms. Stakeholders include biomedical researchers, biomanufacturers and public health institutions. The objective is to enhance production yields and process reliability to support biomedical innovation. The project develops mathematical and computational models that integrate experimental data from biotechnological production processes. These models capture relationships between process parameters, biological responses and output yields, enabling more precise predictions and optimisation strategies. By embedding these models into research and development workflows, researchers can test scenarios digitally before applying changes in laboratory or production settings. The results include improved yield forecasts, reduced trial-and-error experimentation and broader applicability across different biotechnological use cases. Qualitatively, the project accelerates research cycles, reduces costs and supports scalable protein production critical for vaccines and advanced therapies.

title: KISTRA (use of artificial intelligence for the early detection of criminal offenses) - research project
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Online hate crime poses growing societal risks, yet early detection and prevention raise complex legal, ethical and operational challenges for security authorities. The KISTRA research project was initiated to explore how digital tools could support earlier identification of hate-related offences while respecting fundamental rights. Stakeholders include law enforcement agencies, legal experts, social scientists, technology researchers and civil society. The objective is not operational deployment, but the development of scientifically grounded insights, safeguards and prototypes for responsible use. The project combines socio-scientific, legal and ethical analysis with the development of technical demonstrators. Analytical methods are applied to publicly available online content to explore patterns associated with hate crime, while governance frameworks define acceptable use conditions. The results include software demonstrators, ethical guidelines and legal assessments that inform future policy choices. The impact lies in improved understanding of risks and opportunities, clearer boundary conditions for technology use, and a foundation for transparent, accountable approaches to digital crime prevention.

title: Automated border control via Easypass Registered Traveler Program - biometric face recognition system
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: International airport border control in Germany faced growing passenger volumes requiring faster processing whilst maintaining security standards and compliance with Schengen external border regulations. The Federal Police implemented EasyPASS, an automated border control system using biometric facial recognition developed by Bundesdruckerei, secunet, and Cognitec to verify travellers' identities against their e-passport chip photos. The system is deployed at Frankfurt, Munich, Hamburg, Hannover, Düsseldorf, Stuttgart, Berlin Brandenburg, and Cologne/Bonn airports, available to EU/EEA citizens aged 12+ and registered third-country nationals from the USA, Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, and the UK. Travellers place their e-passport on the document reader, then proceed through gates where cameras capture facial images for 1:1 comparison against stored biometric data, with information also checked against Schengen databases. Data is stored for 48 hours (extendable to 30 days for police investigations), and the system strictly limits facial recognition to identity verification purposes under the Passport Act.

title: KI4LSA – Artificial Intelligence for Adaptive Traffic Signal Control
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Municipalities of Bielefeld, Gütersloh, Lemgo, Neuss, Rheine and Soest
source_description: Increasing urban traffic congestion leads to longer travel times, higher fuel consumption, and increased noise and air pollution. Optimising traffic signal systems is a critical lever for improving traffic flow in dense city environments, yet conventional control strategies struggle to adapt to dynamic traffic conditions. The KI4LSA project addresses this challenge by exploring adaptive control of traffic lights in inner-city areas. Stakeholders include transport authorities, municipalities, and road users seeking smoother traffic flow and reduced environmental impact. The objective is to optimise traffic signal behaviour in real time to minimise congestion and unnecessary stopping. The solution uses reinforcement learning, a data-driven control approach trained in detailed traffic simulations. Traffic signal controllers learn optimal strategies by observing traffic states and evaluating outcomes such as queue length and waiting time. After training, the learned control policies are evaluated against conventional approaches. The project demonstrates improved traffic flow, reduced stop-and-go behaviour, and lower emissions resulting from fewer accelerations and idling periods. The results highlight the potential of adaptive signal control to improve urban mobility efficiency and environmental performance, while providing a transferable framework for future smart traffic management systems.
supporting_source_urls: Bendszusn, R. (2022). Make-or-buy in the area of Artificial Intelligence: Insights from AI use cases in the German public sector (master's thesis). Hertie School, Berlin.

title: Pilot project to support the future development of photos with AI

source_description: Municipal archives often hold vast photographic collections that are difficult to index and search due to limited metadata and manual cataloguing processes. The Heilbronn City Archive launched this pilot to improve access to its digital photo collections and enrich historical documentation. Stakeholders include archivists, researchers, local historians and the general public. The objective is to increase indexing depth and accelerate the availability of detailed information about archived images. The pilot trains image analysis systems to recognise approximately 1,500 individuals and around 200 distinctive buildings using existing labelled photographs. The resulting metadata is integrated into the HEUSS online archive database, enabling faster and more detailed tagging of images. title: AI Beach Capacity Monitoring

title: Robotic Automation Plan
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

title: ELASTIC – Autonomous Transport Network for Urban Tramways
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban public transport systems require precise situational awareness to ensure safety, reliability, and efficient operation, particularly as cities move towards higher levels of automation. The ELASTIC project addresses this need by developing a software architecture for advanced mobility systems, with a focus on autonomous and assisted transport networks. The pilot, deployed on Florence’s tramway network, involved transport operators, city authorities, and technology providers. The objective was to enhance real-time monitoring of tram operations, infrastructure, and surrounding environments without compromising passenger privacy. The solution integrates multiple onboard and roadside sensors, including cameras, radar, lidar, and inertial measurement units, installed on tram vehicles and at stops. Sensor data is processed in real time using perception and data fusion techniques to extract information on tram positioning, obstacle detection, and movement of vehicles and pedestrians. Visual data is analysed on the fly and immediately discarded, ensuring that no personal data is retained. The pilot demonstrates improved operational awareness, enhanced safety, and better incident prevention. It provides a scalable and privacy-preserving foundation for future autonomous public transport systems in urban environments.

title: Nantes Social Water Pricing
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Access to affordable water is a fundamental right, yet low-income households often struggle with utility costs. Traditional means-tested assistance programmes require complex application processes and frequently miss eligible beneficiaries who are unaware of available support. Nantes Métropole developed an open-source algorithm to determine eligibility for its social water tariff (Tarification Solidaire de l'Eau), guaranteeing that no household spends more than 3% of income on water for reasonable consumption of 30 cubic metres per person annually. The algorithm calculates eligibility based on household income and family composition using data from the Caisse d'Allocations Familiales (CAF). For CAF beneficiaries with family quotient below the threshold, assistance is granted automatically. Other residents can apply at their town hall, where agents enter information into Deltas software developed in-house by Nantes Métropole. The algorithm processes data in real time, providing immediate eligibility determination. The source code is published under the CeCILL-B open-source licence. In 2024, 5,866 households benefited from the social water tariff, receiving €407,153 in total assistance. Since January 2025, reformed Agence de l'Eau charges have been integrated into the pricing structure. The open-source approach supports transparency in public decision-making and enables other municipalities to adapt the algorithm for their own social pricing programmes.

title: Nantes Solidarity Transport Pricing
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public transport affordability is crucial for social inclusion, yet fixed-price ticketing can exclude low-income residents from mobility services essential for employment, healthcare access, and social participation. Nantes Métropole implemented an algorithmic system for solidarity transport pricing (Tarification Solidaire Transports) on its Naolib public transport network. The algorithm determines eligibility for free travel or discounts up to 50% on unlimited annual passes based on household income and family composition. All households with a family quotient of 900 or below qualify for solidarity pricing. Users apply at their local town hall, where agents collect supporting documents and enter information into Deltas, software developed by Nantes Métropole. The algorithm processes data in real time, immediately notifying applicants of their entitlement level. Benefits apply to all household members regardless of age. Since May 2023, the eligibility threshold was raised from 600 to 900 family quotient, significantly expanding coverage. The solidarity pricing programme extends beyond metropolitan residents to include commuters from surrounding areas who travel within Nantes Métropole. This ensures transport affordability for the most vulnerable populations whilst supporting labour market access and social cohesion across the metropolitan region.

title: Carbon Intelligent City - Paris
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cities face increasing pressure to accurately measure, understand, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions across all sectors, from buildings and transport to industry and energy production. In Paris, fragmented data sources and limited temporal resolution make it difficult to link emissions to concrete activities and evaluate the impact of climate policies. The Carbon Intelligent City pilot addresses this gap by providing a comprehensive, multi-scale emissions monitoring system. Stakeholders include city managers, policymakers, businesses, NGOs, and citizens seeking transparent and actionable climate information. The objective is to support evidence-based climate action through detailed, science-based emissions tracking at city, district, and street level. The solution combines diverse datasets within a unified platform, using advanced analytics to extract activity signals from defined areas of interest and infer associated CO₂ emissions. Satellite imagery and other data sources are analysed to detect operational activity, such as industrial site usage, and translate these signals into emissions estimates. The pilot improves transparency, enables continuous monitoring, and supports scenario analysis and impact assessment. It strengthens the city’s capacity to manage emissions strategically and engage stakeholders in collective climate action.

title: Carbon Intelligent City - Copenhagen
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Achieving climate neutrality requires cities to move beyond aggregated emissions inventories towards dynamic, activity-based monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions. In Copenhagen, the need for precise, spatially resolved emissions data is critical to guide urban planning and track progress towards ambitious climate targets. This pilot within the AI4Cities project applies the Carbon Intelligent City approach to the Danish context. Stakeholders include municipal authorities, urban planners, businesses, and civil society organisations. The objective is to provide a reliable, transparent emissions information system that supports informed decision-making at multiple urban scales. The solution integrates heterogeneous datasets into a single analytical platform, where automated methods extract activity patterns from areas of interest and infer corresponding emissions. By linking observed activity to emissions factors, the system generates timely and comparable emissions estimates across sectors such as transport, buildings, and industry. The pilot improves the granularity and responsiveness of emissions monitoring, supports evaluation of policy interventions, and enhances public transparency. It demonstrates how data-driven emissions intelligence can strengthen climate governance and accelerate urban decarbonisation strategies.

title: IX3 - Mobility Pilot Project in Paris
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban traffic inefficiencies contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions, particularly through frequent stopping and re-acceleration at traffic lights. The IX3 mobility pilot in Paris addresses this issue by optimising traffic signal management to smooth vehicle flows. Stakeholders include city transport authorities, road users, and residents affected by congestion and air pollution. The objective is to reduce unnecessary stops, improve driving continuity, and lower traffic-related emissions at city scale. The solution combines real-time machine vision sensors with traffic light controllers to observe traffic conditions and dynamically adjust signal logic. Visual data is processed locally to extract anonymous traffic metrics, such as vehicle counts and flow patterns, without storing personal identifiers or retaining footage beyond quality assurance. The system continuously adapts signal timing to actual traffic demand. Pilots and earlier deployments show that city-wide adoption can reduce traffic-related emissions by around 2%, alongside improved travel times and driving comfort. The project demonstrates a privacy-preserving, scalable approach to intelligent traffic management with measurable environmental and mobility benefits.

title: IX3 - Mobility Pilot Project in Helsinki
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban traffic congestion in Helsinki contributes to unnecessary fuel consumption, emissions, and reduced travel comfort, particularly due to frequent stopping and waiting at red lights. Traditional traffic signal control systems are often rule-based and insufficiently responsive to real-time traffic conditions. This pilot, part of the AI4Cities project, addresses the need for more adaptive and efficient traffic management that supports the city’s environmental and mobility goals. Stakeholders include the City of Helsinki, transport authorities, technology providers, and road users. The objective is to reduce stop-and-go traffic, improve flow continuity, and lower traffic-related emissions without requiring major infrastructure changes. The solution integrates real-time machine vision sensors with existing traffic light controllers, enabling continuous observation of traffic conditions such as vehicle presence and flow intensity. These data feed optimisation logic that dynamically adjusts signal timing to actual demand. The system is developed in collaboration with MarshallAI and Dynniq, combining expertise in computer vision and traffic management. Only anonymous traffic data is processed, and video footage is not retained beyond quality assurance. The pilot builds on earlier deployments showing that city-wide adoption can reduce traffic-related emissions by around 2%, while also improving travel times, driving comfort, and overall traffic efficiency in a scalable and privacy-preserving manner.

title: BerDiBa Project: Berlin Digital Railway Operation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: BerDiBa Project addresses the need to modernise urban rail transport in Berlin by increasing automation, safety and operational reliability under real traffic conditions. As part of the Siemensstadt innovation initiative, a consortium of twelve partners is collaborating over four years to research and validate technologies that enable automated train driving while ensuring passenger safety and infrastructure integrity. The project seeks to enhance rail efficiency, reduce human error and support future digital railway operations within Berlin’s public transport system. The solution is based on high-performance sensor systems installed on and within trains to provide continuous environmental perception. Machine learning models process visual and sensor data to detect track obstacles, identify hazards affecting passengers and monitor changes in rail infrastructure. The system integrates perception modules with train control and operational management platforms, enabling automated decision support and adaptive responses during live operations. Funded under Berlin’s ProFIT programme, the initiative supports application-oriented research and large-scale testing. Expected impacts include improved safety, reduced operational disruptions, enhanced monitoring accuracy and the foundation for scalable automated rail travel in metropolitan environments.

title: Signalen - AI Categorisation of Public Space Reports
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: City of Amsterdam and other dutch municipalities
source_description: Municipalities receive large volumes of reports from residents concerning issues in public space, such as waste, infrastructure damage or nuisance, which must be routed quickly to the correct department. Manual triage is time-consuming and can delay resolution. Signalen was developed as a shared, open-source system by and for Dutch municipalities to streamline the intake and handling of such reports. Stakeholders include local authorities, civil servants responsible for service delivery and residents submitting reports. The objective is to improve response times, reduce administrative workload and ensure consistent handling across municipalities. The system automatically categorises incoming reports based on their content and routes them to the appropriate municipal unit. It uses language-based classification models trained on historical report data, relying primarily on keyword recognition and probabilistic categorisation. The platform is API-driven and integrates with existing municipal case management systems. Personal data is optional and excluded from automated processing, ensuring privacy by design. Signalen is currently used by municipalities serving over two million residents and processes more than 600,000 reports annually. The system has improved operational efficiency, reduced misrouting, and increased transparency for citizens, while its open-source nature supports scalability, reuse and long-term sustainability across the Netherlands.

title: Energy Optimisation of Buildings
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal buildings represent a major share of urban energy consumption, yet optimising energy use while maintaining indoor comfort is operationally complex. Copenhagen Solutions Lab and Copenhagen City Properties initiated this pilot to reduce energy consumption, emissions and costs across municipal buildings. Stakeholders include facility managers, city authorities, energy providers and building occupants. The objective is to support energy-efficient operations without compromising indoor climate quality. The project integrates building management system data, energy consumption records, indoor climate measurements and external data such as weather and grid conditions. Predictive optimisation tools generate operational recommendations for heating, ventilation and electricity use, accounting for fluctuating demand and supply constraints. The impact includes reduced heating and electricity bills, lower CO₂ emissions and improved operational insight for facility managers. Qualitatively, the pilot enhances comfort, supports climate targets and provides a replicable model for data-driven energy management at city scale.

title: HOLONI – Blockchain-Based Local Green Energy Exchange
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cities seeking to accelerate the energy transition face challenges in efficiently exchanging locally produced renewable energy and rewarding prosumers for their contributions. In many urban contexts, surplus solar energy is underutilised due to fragmented systems and limited incentives. The HOLONI project, part of AI4Cities, addresses this challenge by enabling reliable and transparent exchange of local green energy within urban communities. Stakeholders include municipalities, solar prosumers, energy retailers, and local businesses aiming to increase renewable self-consumption and community-based energy sharing. The objective is to automate incentive mechanisms and improve redistribution of locally generated energy surpluses. The solution uses distributed ledger technologies to record energy exchanges and automatically execute result-based reward schemes. Transactions related to energy production, consumption, and incentives are immutably logged, ensuring transparency, traceability, and trust among participants. Smart contracts enable automated settlement and reward distribution based on predefined sustainability criteria. The pilot demonstrates improved efficiency in local energy exchange, increased engagement of prosumers, and fair redistribution of benefits within the community. It provides a scalable and trustworthy foundation for decentralised energy markets, supporting urban decarbonisation and strengthening local energy ecosystems.

title: HOLONI – AI for Urban Solar Potential Assessment
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Unlocking the full potential of urban solar energy requires accurate assessment of production capacity and surplus at city scale, yet municipalities often lack tools to analyse this potential dynamically. This HOLONI pilot within AI4Cities focuses on enabling data-driven planning and coordination of local solar energy generation. Stakeholders include city administrations, sustainable brands, energy retailers, and prosumers interested in collective climate impact. The objective is to predict solar generation and surplus across the urban fabric and use these insights to support local energy exchange and new community-based business models. The solution applies predictive analytics to diverse urban datasets, including building characteristics, solar exposure, and consumption patterns, to estimate current and future solar surplus potential. These insights support planning of incentive schemes, energy sharing strategies, and commercial relationships between stakeholders. The system integrates with local energy platforms to align predictions with operational decision-making. The pilot enables municipalities to better understand city-wide renewable potential, supports efficient matching of supply and demand, and strengthens community engagement around sustainability goals. It demonstrates how predictive intelligence can drive more effective local energy systems and accelerate the transition to clean, collective urban energy models.

title: SPIKE – Energy Pilot Project in Copenhagen
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Buildings account for a significant share of urban energy consumption, yet many existing facilities lack the flexibility to optimise energy use without costly renovations. The SPIKE pilot in Copenhagen addresses this challenge by enabling real-time optimisation of building energy consumption while maintaining occupant comfort. Stakeholders include building owners, occupants, energy communities, and city authorities pursuing energy efficiency and decarbonisation targets. The objective is to reduce operational energy use and integrate buildings into flexible, community-based energy systems. The solution deploys a scalable plug-and-play kit of sensors and controllers that interfaces with existing HVAC systems. Real-time data is used to fine-tune energy usage dynamically, without structural changes. An integrated platform orchestrates energy loads and renewable production under an “Energy as a Service” model, enabling coordination at community level. The pilot achieves on average 20% operational energy savings and over 90% in-comfort time for occupants. It also demonstrates the potential to aggregate flexible buildings into a virtual power plant at urban scale, supporting grid stability, renewable integration, and cost-effective energy management.

title: Spike - Energy Pilot Project in Amsterdam
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: In Amsterdam, achieving climate goals requires scalable solutions that reduce building energy consumption while enabling participation in local energy communities. Many buildings operate inefficiently due to static control systems and limited integration with renewable energy sources. This SPIKE pilot, part of AI4Cities, aims to demonstrate how existing buildings can become active components of a flexible urban energy system. Stakeholders include municipalities, building managers, occupants, and energy providers. The objective is to optimise energy use in real time, improve comfort, and support local energy balancing without major retrofits. The solution uses a plug-and-play hardware kit combined with a unified digital platform that continuously adjusts HVAC operation based on real-time conditions. The platform supports “Energy as a Service” by orchestrating demand and renewable production across multiple buildings. Results mirror those achieved in other pilots, with average energy savings of around 20% and high comfort levels for occupants. The project shows how buildings can be aggregated into virtual power plants, enabling scalable energy flexibility, reduced emissions, and new value chains within urban energy communities.

title: LAIban - A chatbot for children
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Children in municipal preschools frequently ask practical questions about daily routines, activities and schedules, which can place additional demands on staff. The City of Helsingborg introduced LAIban to support children’s independence while complementing the role of educators. Stakeholders include children, preschool staff, municipal administrators and parents. The objective is to provide accessible, age-appropriate information while fostering children’s confidence and inclusion. LAIban operates as a conversational assistant deployed across all 80 public preschools in Helsingborg. It responds to common questions using structured content and language models trained on predefined educational and administrative data. The system supports multiple languages, reflecting the demographic diversity of its users, and adapts responses accordingly. Children were actively involved in the design and iterative improvement of the assistant, influencing both content and functionality. LAIban also explains its own role and limitations to children, supporting transparency and digital literacy. The solution remains in active use and has improved children’s autonomy, reduced repetitive questions for staff and enhanced inclusiveness through multilingual support. Its participatory design approach has strengthened trust and usability, while its controlled scope ensures reliability and age-appropriate interaction.

title: AI Safety Perception Patterns
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Perceived safety is a critical factor influencing how citizens use and experience urban spaces, yet it is difficult to measure systematically over time. The AI Safety Perception Patterns project, developed by Senseable Stockholm Lab in collaboration with the City of Stockholm, addresses this challenge by creating a reproducible, data-driven approach to mapping perceived safety. Stakeholders include urban planners, architects, policymakers, and residents concerned with inclusive and secure public environments. The objective is to support long-term monitoring of perceived safety and evaluate the impact of urban interventions. The solution combines multiple data sources, including web-based surveys and urban data, to model safety perception across the city. Analytical methods identify patterns and generate spatial representations that are integrated into the city’s GIS platform. The approach is designed to be fully replicable, using the same code and methods year after year, enabling longitudinal analysis. The results provide planners with actionable insights into where and why safety perceptions vary, supporting evidence-based urban design. The project delivers a scalable framework for monitoring social sustainability and assessing the effectiveness of policy and design interventions over time.

title: AVENUE – Mobility Pilot Project in Tallinn
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban authorities increasingly need to align shared mobility policies with ambitious greenhouse gas reduction targets, yet lack tools to quantify the climate impact of different regulatory strategies. In Tallinn, policymakers face complex choices around fleet caps, pricing, and incentives for shared mobility services, with limited visibility of their emissions outcomes. The AVENUE pilot addresses this challenge by providing a decision support capability to assess and monitor the carbon footprint effects of shared mobility policies. Stakeholders include city leaders, transport authorities, and mobility operators. The objective is to enable data-driven, timely decisions that support climate mitigation while maintaining effective mobility systems. The solution combines large-scale geolocated mobility data from anonymised mobile network records and operator-shared datasets with urban data sources. Demand prediction models simulate modal choice behaviour and assess how regulatory measures influence shared mobility usage. Scenario analysis evaluates resulting emissions impacts. The pilot improves policymakers’ ability to compare strategies, anticipate outcomes, and track progress over time. It supports more effective regulation of shared mobility, enhanced accountability of climate policies, and measurable reductions in transport-related emissions at city scale.

title: AVENUE – Mobility Pilot Project in Stavanger
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Designing shared mobility policies that effectively contribute to greenhouse gas reduction is a growing challenge for medium-sized European cities. In Stavanger, authorities require robust evidence to understand how regulatory choices affect travel behaviour and emissions. The AVENUE pilot responds by offering a data-driven framework to analyse and monitor the environmental impact of shared mobility strategies. Stakeholders include municipal decision-makers, transport planners, and mobility providers. The objective is to support climate-aligned policy design through continuous measurement and scenario-based evaluation. The solution integrates anonymised geolocated mobility data and operator-provided information to model demand and modal shift patterns. Predictive models simulate how changes in policy parameters influence the uptake of shared mobility services and the resulting emissions footprint. These insights enable comparison of alternative regulatory approaches and ongoing monitoring of their effectiveness. The pilot strengthens strategic planning, reduces uncertainty in policy decisions, and enhances the city’s capacity to implement evidence-based mobility measures that contribute to decarbonisation and sustainable urban transport systems.

title: MPAT – Mobility Policy Auto Tuner Pilot in Tallinn
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cities aiming to decarbonise transport must identify where shared micro-mobility can most effectively replace car trips, yet traditional planning tools offer limited insight into spatial and temporal dynamics. The MPAT pilot in Tallinn addresses this gap by enabling targeted optimisation of mobility policies to maximise emissions reductions. Stakeholders include city transport authorities and policymakers seeking to accelerate low-carbon mobility adoption. The objective is to identify priority areas for policy interventions such as subsidies or fleet adjustments and to quantify their climate impact. The solution analyses travel patterns to determine where shared electric bicycles, scooters, or mopeds are most likely to displace internal combustion vehicle trips. Forecasting models anticipate growth in micro-mobility demand and evolving mode shift patterns. Policy scenarios are evaluated based on their projected CO₂ savings and monitored over time. The pilot demonstrates improved precision in policy targeting, greater transparency in emissions outcomes, and enhanced ability to adapt measures dynamically. It provides a practical tool for embedding climate objectives directly into mobility policy design and evaluation.

title: MPAT – Mobility Policy Auto Tuner Pilot in Amsterdam
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Amsterdam’s ambition to reduce transport emissions requires sophisticated tools to understand and influence modal shift towards low-carbon mobility. The MPAT pilot supports this goal by providing a data-driven engine to optimise shared micro-mobility policies. Stakeholders include municipal authorities and urban planners responsible for balancing accessibility, sustainability, and public space management. The objective is to maximise the emissions reduction potential of shared electric mobility while anticipating future demand. The solution combines spatial analysis of travel behaviour with predictive modelling to identify locations where micro-mobility can most effectively replace car journeys. Policy levers such as incentives, parking regulations, and fleet size adjustments are evaluated based on their projected climate benefits. Continuous monitoring allows policymakers to track performance and refine interventions. The pilot enhances strategic planning, supports transparent assessment of policy impacts, and contributes to measurable CO₂ reductions. It demonstrates how predictive analytics can guide more effective and adaptive urban mobility policies aligned with climate targets.

title: Milli, AI Chatbot for Mental Health
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Adolescents often face barriers to accessing mental health information and support, including stigma, lack of anonymity and limited service availability. Milli was developed in Finland to provide a confidential entry point for young people seeking information about mental health concerns. Stakeholders include adolescents, healthcare providers, psychologists and public health institutions. The objective is to improve early access to reliable information and guide users towards appropriate support when needed. Milli operates as a conversational assistant that responds to anonymous user queries and provides tailored information based on the user’s age group. It processes text inputs to identify themes and risk indicators, enabling differentiated responses and escalation in urgent situations. If signs of self-harm or crisis are detected, the system directs users to emergency services or trusted adults. Identifying information is automatically deleted, and users can request explanations about data use and system functioning. Milli currently handles between 500 and 1,200 queries per week. Reported impacts include improved accessibility to mental health information, reduced barriers to help-seeking and strengthened trust through transparency, privacy safeguards and user-centred design. Ongoing development focuses on fairness, accessibility and inclusive language.

title: Intelligent Wellness Platform Experiment
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Espoo sought to improve preventive social, healthcare and education services by better understanding citizens’ needs before problems escalated into costly or irreversible social exclusion. Traditional service planning relied on siloed data and reactive interventions, limiting the city’s ability to act early and in a targeted way. In collaboration with Tieto (now Tietoevry), Espoo launched an experiment to test whether large-scale data analysis could support more timely, citizen-centric welfare services. Stakeholders included municipal social and healthcare departments, education services, policymakers and the city’s residents. The objective was to assess whether predictive insights could inform service planning and resource allocation while respecting strict data protection requirements. The solution integrated longitudinal data from social services, healthcare and education covering the years 2002–2016, representing around 520,000 residents and over 37 million service interactions. Data were anonymised at source, encrypted in transit and processed in a secure analytical environment. Predictive models were used to identify risk patterns associated with social exclusion and future service needs, with results fed into planning processes rather than individual-level decisions. The experiment demonstrated that data-driven insights could support earlier interventions, more efficient service planning and new preventive service pathways. Qualitatively, it showed strong potential for improving wellbeing outcomes while reducing long-term social and healthcare costs.

title: Gallery Visitor's AI Analysis
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Gallery Visitor’s AI Analysis responds to the Hugh Lane Gallery’s need to obtain accurate, non-intrusive insights into visitor numbers and movement patterns in order to improve exhibition planning, optimise spatial design and strengthen health and safety management. Working with Dublin City Council’s Smart City team, the Gallery sought a privacy-conscious technological approach capable of delivering reliable analytics without compromising visitors’ rights. The objective was to better understand how audiences engage with exhibitions and facilities while maintaining full compliance with data protection principles. The implemented solution uses a network of connected cameras combined with edge processing technology developed with Arm to capture anonymised visual data. Computer vision techniques analyse movement flows without identifying individuals, and aggregated outputs are visualised through heat mapping to highlight high-traffic zones and dwell times. Data processing is designed according to privacy-by-design principles, ensuring no personally identifiable information is stored. The insights generated support curatorial decision-making, space utilisation planning and visitor flow management. The approach enhances operational efficiency, improves visitor experience and demonstrates how advanced analytics can be deployed responsibly within cultural institutions.

title: AI-controlled Smart Traffic Junctions in Manchester
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The rapid growth of walking and cycling requires traffic management systems that can dynamically prioritise different road users while maintaining safety and efficiency. In Greater Manchester, traditional signal control struggled to adapt to changing travel patterns, particularly during increased active travel uptake. Transport for Greater Manchester implemented AI-controlled smart junctions to address this challenge. Stakeholders include transport authorities, pedestrians, cyclists, and motorists. The objective is to improve junction performance, support active travel, and optimise traffic flow. The solution uses sensors with embedded intelligence to anonymously detect and classify road users in real time. Traffic signals are dynamically adjusted to prioritise pedestrians or cyclists when demand increases. Deployed initially at selected sites and later scaled to 20 junctions, the system operates without collecting personal data. The project improves safety, reduces waiting times for active modes, and enhances network efficiency. It demonstrates a scalable approach to adaptive traffic management that supports sustainable mobility and more inclusive urban streets.

title: Behaviour Analytics to Measure Impact of Social Distancing in Transport
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, transport authorities faced unprecedented challenges in ensuring passenger safety while maintaining essential mobility services. Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) needed timely insights into how travellers moved through interchanges and where social distancing was difficult to maintain. Existing CCTV systems provided visual coverage but limited analytical value. TfGM partnered with startup Humanising Autonomy to pilot a behaviour analytics solution at key transport hubs, including Bolton and Wythenshawe interchanges and Wigan bus station. The objective was to support rapid, evidence-based decisions on temporary infrastructure changes and operational measures. The implementation analysed live and recorded CCTV footage through a cloud-based platform that extracted anonymised behavioural patterns, such as crowd density, group formation and directional movement. The system generated dashboards highlighting hotspots where distancing compliance was challenging, without identifying individuals. Insights were integrated into TfGM’s operational decision-making processes. The pilot enabled faster identification of problem areas, informed layout adjustments and supported safer passenger flows. Qualitatively, it improved situational awareness, reduced reliance on manual observation and demonstrated how existing infrastructure could be leveraged to enhance public safety during emergencies.

title: Gavius Virtual Assistant
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal social services often struggle to provide timely, clear, and personalised information on social benefits, leading to underutilisation of available aid and administrative overload. The City Council of Gavà led the Gavius project to improve citizens’ access to social assistance by simplifying how benefits are discovered, requested, and managed. Stakeholders included social services staff, municipal managers, citizens—particularly vulnerable groups—and seven public and private partners. The objective was to reduce bureaucratic barriers, accelerate benefit processing, and improve the quality of interaction between the municipality and residents. The solution was implemented as a virtual assistant accessible via mobile devices, designed to guide users through available social aids, eligibility criteria, application processes, and follow-up. The system integrates municipal databases, service workflows, and rule-based decision logic to provide tailored responses and automate parts of case handling. In addition to the citizen-facing assistant, separate virtual assistants were developed for municipal staff and managers to support internal processes. The project was funded through ERDF under the Urban Innovative Actions programme and formally concluded in February 2023. Reported outcomes include improved accessibility to social benefits, reduced administrative burden, and faster processing times, demonstrating the feasibility of conversational digital services in local welfare administration.

title: Rimini Chatbot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Citizens seeking information about municipal services often rely on email, phone calls or in-person visits, creating pressure on administrative staff and limiting accessibility outside office hours. The City of Rimini introduced a digital assistant to provide continuous support to residents navigating municipal services. Stakeholders include citizens, municipal departments and customer service staff. The objective is to improve access to information, increase citizen autonomy and reduce the workload on traditional service channels. The chatbot is embedded in the city’s institutional portal and interacts with users through natural language queries. It is trained on administrative service descriptions, procedures and FAQs, and continuously improves its responses based on user interactions. The system integrates with municipal content management systems to ensure up-to-date information. The assistant is available 24/7 and complements existing communication channels rather than replacing them. The solution remains in active use and has improved response times, reduced routine enquiries handled by staff and enhanced user satisfaction. Its conversational design supports intuitive interaction, while continuous learning contributes to scalability and long-term service quality.

title: AI Algorithm used toclassify unemployed people in Poland
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Polish government implemented an AI algorithm aimed at profiling individuals without jobs and establishing an automated system to assist in determining the support they could receive, utilizing their personal data and responses from job center interviews. However, this initiative was abandoned in December 2019 due to its deficiency in transparency and violations of data protection rights.

title: Hello Charly - AI chatbot assisting students making decisions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Young people often struggle to navigate complex education and career choices, particularly when information is fragmented or difficult to personalise. Hello Charly was developed to provide accessible guidance to students aged 14–24 through familiar digital channels. Stakeholders include students, educational institutions, career advisors and public authorities. The objective is to support informed decision-making while ensuring anonymity and ease of access. The service engages users through conversational interactions, asking structured questions to understand interests, preferences and aspirations. It draws on a large, curated database covering more than 850 professions and 110,000 training pathways. Users can explore options, compare alternatives and build personalised scorecards without registering or sharing personal data. Hello Charly is available via web and popular social media platforms. Since its launch in 2016, it has been used by over 220,000 people in France. Reported impacts include improved engagement with guidance services, greater clarity for students and reduced reliance on traditional counselling resources. Its anonymity-first design and broad coverage have supported scalability and sustained uptake.

title: PARCOURSUP | Screening of university applicants in France
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: France introduced Parcoursup to manage the allocation of university places following reforms that allowed institutions to select applicants. The system addresses the challenge of matching student preferences with available study programmes at national scale. Stakeholders include prospective students, universities, the Ministry of Higher Education and admissions staff. The objective is to coordinate applications, manage capacity constraints and standardise admissions procedures. Parcoursup collects student preferences, academic records and programme criteria, and applies algorithmic sorting to prioritise applications. While human decision-making remains central at institutional level, the system supports ranking and matching processes. Parcoursup has faced criticism regarding transparency and perceived fairness, particularly due to limited disclosure of sorting logic. Despite ongoing public debate, the system remains in use nationwide. Impacts include faster processing of large application volumes, centralised coordination and reduced administrative fragmentation, alongside continued scrutiny concerning accountability and explainability.

title: DELIA | Algorithm to predict location and perpetrator of crime
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Law enforcement agencies in Milan sought more effective ways to prevent and investigate serial crimes, particularly commercial and bank robberies, which had significant social and economic impacts. Traditional policing methods struggled to identify patterns across large volumes of crime data over time. The City of Milan’s Questura began long-term field trials of predictive crime analysis tools developed by startup KeyCrime, with the objective of supporting investigative work and targeted prevention strategies. Stakeholders included police analysts, operational units, judicial authorities and academic evaluators. The solution analysed historical crime records, spatial and temporal patterns, and offence characteristics to identify links between incidents and likely future scenarios. Over successive trial phases, the system evolved into the DELIA platform, improving usability, analytical performance and pattern-linking capabilities. Results were reviewed by the Italian Ministry of Justice and independently evaluated by the University of Essex to ensure objectivity. The impact was significant: between 2008 and 2019, commercial robberies in Milan decreased by around 58%, while bank robberies in the wider province fell by approximately 89% between 2009 and 2019. The project demonstrated strong operational value in crime prevention and investigation.

title: Resource Allocation System
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Adult social care authorities must translate assessed needs into indicative budgets in a way that is fair, transparent, and flexible enough to reflect individual circumstances, while still allowing professional judgement and support planning to shape the final outcome. In Devon, the Resource Allocation System is used to generate an estimated personal budget for community care, giving practitioners, the person being assessed, and their representatives a structured starting point for planning how identified needs might be met. The objective is to support consistent budgeting, provide early visibility of the likely scale of support, and guide discussion without turning the estimate into a fixed entitlement or a substitute for professional judgement. The implementation uses a rule-based budgeting framework linked to assessment information, applying published principles, standard rates, and eligibility-related rules to generate an estimated budget. At a conceptual level, the system combines assessment data, defined cost assumptions, and policy rules covering matters such as social isolation, replacement care, and shared care, while leaving room for review, challenge, and revision during support planning. The impact lies in greater transparency, more consistent budget estimation, and better use of practitioner time. It also supports a strengths-based approach by treating the budget as guidance within a broader planning process rather than as an automatic final decision.

title: 80 councils in the UK use AI to identify possible frauds in welfare claims
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Local authorities in the UK are responsible for administering welfare benefits while preventing fraud and error. To manage limited investigative resources, around 80 councils introduced automated risk screening tools to flag claims for further review. Stakeholders include councils, welfare claimants, investigators and technology providers. The objective is to prioritise checks and reduce erroneous payments. The system analyses administrative data associated with claims and assigns risk indicators that inform follow-up actions by caseworkers. Human review remains mandatory before any decision is taken. Investigations revealed that certain variables, including age, influenced risk assessments, raising concerns about bias and proportionality. As a result, the use of such systems has come under legal, regulatory and public scrutiny. While tools continue to be used, councils have been required to review practices, improve governance and ensure compliance with equality and data protection standards. Impacts include efficiency gains in case selection, alongside heightened awareness of the need for transparency, oversight and safeguards in automated welfare administration.

title: RADAR-rechts | Assessing the risk of violence by far-right extremists
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Following a series of fatal right-wing extremist attacks in Germany in 2019 and 2020, federal and state law enforcement authorities faced increasing pressure to strengthen the prevention of politically motivated violent crime. To support a more systematic and person-centred approach, the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) developed RADAR-rechts, a structured risk assessment instrument designed to prioritise individuals known from the right-wing extremist spectrum who may pose an acute threat of committing life-threatening violence. The tool supports police forces nationwide by enabling consistent prioritisation of so-called dangerous and relevant persons and identifying cases requiring more detailed individual risk analysis. RADAR-rechts is based on a scientifically grounded, rule-based analytical framework that evaluates standardised behavioural, situational and criminological indicators drawn from police data and professional assessments. The system integrates with existing police workflows while preserving human responsibility for final decisions. Since becoming operational in May 2022, RADAR-rechts has improved the consistency and transparency of risk management across Germany, allowing law enforcement agencies to allocate preventive and investigative resources more effectively. Its introduction represents a significant step towards standardised, evidence-informed approaches in the person-oriented prevention of far-right extremist violence.

title: VicomTTS - Quality synthetic voices
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: VicomTTS was developed to address the limited availability of high-quality digital services in the Basque language, which can hinder its everyday use in public, educational and personal contexts. The service provides citizens, learners and institutions with a reliable tool for converting written Basque text into clear, natural-sounding speech, supporting linguistic inclusion and accessibility. Built as a digital public service, VicomTTS uses neural speech synthesis models implemented in Python and executed via the PyTorch framework, trained on Basque-language datasets to ensure accurate pronunciation and intelligible prosody. The system is deployed as an online service designed for low-latency performance and high reliability. While initial uptake was lower than anticipated, the service has steadily gained popularity and is now processing approximately 5,000 requests per day. Performance metrics indicate that around 50% of requests are handled in under one second, with a reported success rate of 99.7%. VicomTTS demonstrates how advanced speech technologies can contribute to the preservation and digital normalisation of minority languages while delivering a scalable and dependable public-facing service.

title: Enhancing road safety through automatic identification of traffic violations
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Enhancing Road Safety through Automatic Identification of Traffic Violations addresses persistent risks caused by behaviours such as driving without seat belts and using mobile phones while driving. These infractions contribute significantly to road accidents and increase the burden on enforcement authorities. Public administrations face challenges in detecting violations efficiently and processing sanctions in a timely manner. The objective is to strengthen deterrence and improve compliance through automated monitoring mechanisms that complement traditional policing. The solution employs computer vision models deployed on roadside or mobile camera systems to automatically detect seat belt non-use and handheld phone usage. Image recognition algorithms analyse video streams, classify violations and extract relevant evidence, which is then transmitted to enforcement platforms for validation and sanction processing. The system integrates with existing traffic management and administrative databases to streamline case handling. By automating detection and optimising the sanction workflow, authorities can increase enforcement consistency and reduce manual workload. Expected impacts include improved road safety outcomes, faster processing of offences, more efficient allocation of enforcement resources and a reduction in human error in violation assessment.

title: Fraud detection in family allowances (Groeipakket)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Fraud Detection in Family Allowances (Groeipakket) addresses the need to safeguard the Flemish Government’s family benefits system, which distributes approximately €4 billion annually to 1.6 million children residing in Flanders. The scheme operates through automated rights assignment, granting customised financial support based on household circumstances and parental income. Detected fraud exceeding €500,000 in 2022 highlighted vulnerabilities requiring enhanced monitoring capabilities. The objective is to support file managers and social inspectors by identifying irregularities at an early stage and preventing financial losses. The implemented solution uses data analytics and predictive modelling techniques to detect patterns indicative of fraud across administrative and income datasets.
