source_description: Global cotton value chains are complex and fragmented, making it difficult for governments and companies to ensure traceability, compliance, and sustainability from production to retail. Risks such as forced labour, environmental harm, and lack of transparency undermine due diligence efforts and consumer trust. The UNECE pilot project addresses these challenges by supporting traceability and accountability across the cotton supply chain, involving farmers, processors, manufacturers, brands, regulators, and consumers. The objective is to provide practical tools that enable reliable verification of origin, production practices, and sustainability claims, aligned with international policy and trade frameworks. The solution implements a distributed ledger–based traceability system that records key events and data points along the value chain, from field to shelf. Standardised data models developed under the UN/CEFACT framework ensure interoperability and consistency, while secure digital records enable verifiable information sharing among authorised actors. The pilot improves transparency, supports regulatory compliance, and strengthens due diligence processes. It enables more responsible sourcing, reduces information asymmetries, and enhances trust between stakeholders. Overall, the initiative contributes to more sustainable cotton value chains and provides a scalable reference model for traceability in the garment and footwear sector.

title: LBChain - Blockchain sandbox
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The Bank of Lithuania, as central bank and financial market supervisor, seeks to promote innovation in the fintech sector while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and maintaining financial stability. Start-ups and technology firms often face challenges in testing novel financial services within existing supervisory frameworks and accessing regulatory guidance during early development stages. LBChain was established as a technological and regulatory sandbox to provide a controlled environment where innovative solutions can be developed and assessed. The platform is based on blockchain architecture and combines distributed ledger infrastructure with supervisory support, enabling participants to test smart contracts, payment solutions and other ledger-based services under defined conditions. Secure nodes and predefined testing scenarios allow experimentation without full market exposure, while regulators observe performance and compliance aspects. The initiative fosters collaboration between innovators and authorities, accelerates product development cycles and reduces regulatory uncertainty. As a result, it strengthens the competitiveness of the national fintech ecosystem and supports responsible deployment of emerging financial technologies.

title: Transforming International Remittance for Serbian Diaspora using Blockchain and Digital Identity
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: To reduce remittance costs and increase transparency in cross-border transfers, UNDP Serbia partnered with AID:Tech to pilot a blockchain-based remittance solution targeting the Serbian diaspora. Traditional remittance channels often involve high fees and limited traceability, constraining economic benefits for recipient communities. The system tokenises remittance value into blockchain-based digital assets linked to specific entitlements such as utilities or goods. Transactions are recorded on a distributed ledger, enabling traceability while preserving user privacy through cryptographic mechanisms. Digital identity components authenticate senders and recipients, ensuring that funds or entitlements reach intended beneficiaries. The pilot, launched in 2018 in the City of Niš, covered the full remittance journey from diaspora sender to local service redemption. The solution aimed to lower transaction costs, improve accountability and stimulate local economic activity. By combining distributed ledger infrastructure with digital identity verification, the initiative demonstrated an alternative model for secure, transparent remittance delivery.

title: Blockchain of Frequencies
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The rapid growth of wireless devices and digital services has increased demand for radio spectrum, a finite public resource that must be carefully managed to avoid interference and ensure service quality. During major cultural, political and sporting events, numerous wireless microphones and devices operate simultaneously, creating risks of signal conflicts in Programme Making and Special Events bands. The French National Frequency Agency sought to improve transparency and coordination in frequency allocation within general authorisation bands. A blockchain-based booking platform was developed to register and manage frequency reservations using distributed ledger technology. The system records allocations in an immutable and transparent manner, enabling authorised users to reserve frequencies while preventing double bookings and ensuring traceability. Smart contract functionalities manage permissions and updates across stakeholders involved in event organisation and spectrum management. The solution enhances reliability and coordination, reduces interference risks and improves overall quality of service during high-profile events, supporting more efficient and accountable spectrum governance.

title: DiBiHo - Digital Credentials for Higher Education Institutions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Higher education institutions face growing demand for secure, interoperable, and internationally recognised academic credentials, as student mobility and digital service delivery increase. Paper-based certificates and fragmented digital solutions create administrative burdens, slow verification, and limit cross-border recognition. The DiBiHo project addresses this challenge by exploring a trusted digital infrastructure for academic credentials that can be used nationally and internationally. Stakeholders include German higher education institutions, students, employers, and credential evaluators. The objective is to define a vendor-independent, interoperable standard for issuing, storing, presenting, and verifying digital academic credentials. The solution investigates distributed infrastructure approaches that allow institutions to issue tamper-resistant credentials while enabling learners to control and share them securely. Common standards and governance principles are defined to ensure long-term interoperability, legal validity, and alignment with European and international frameworks. The project improves efficiency in credential management, reduces verification costs, and enhances trust in academic records. It supports student mobility, lifelong learning, and digital transformation in higher education, while providing a foundation for scalable, future-proof credential ecosystems independent of specific technology providers.

title: Competency certificates in Small Private Online Courses (SPOCs)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Universities issuing digital certificates for online courses must ensure authenticity, prevent fraud and enable straightforward verification by employers and other institutions, as conventional digital documents can be copied or altered and often require manual validation. The project aimed to strengthen trust in competency accreditations generated through the OPEN edX Learning Management System and formally issued by the university. A blockchain-based mechanism was implemented to anchor each certificate to a distributed ledger by storing a cryptographic hash of the credential on-chain, creating a tamper-evident and time-stamped record linked to the learner’s achievement. The certificates remain accessible through the LMS, while external stakeholders can verify their validity by comparing the document with the ledger entry, without relying on intermediaries. The solution reduces administrative workload and verification time, enhances transparency and portability of qualifications, and increases confidence in digital credentials across academic and professional contexts.

title: Intelligent management of Aid to Citizens and companies
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Andalusian administration was required to rapidly distribute large-scale financial aid to citizens and businesses to protect employment and economic stability. The volume and complexity of aid schemes made manual processing inefficient, error-prone, and difficult to scale. This use case addresses the need to accelerate aid delivery while ensuring compliance, transparency, and accountability. Stakeholders include public administrators, beneficiaries, and oversight bodies. The objective is to automate complex administrative workflows to process aid applications quickly and reliably. The solution applies robotic process automation to handle repetitive, rule-based tasks such as data validation, eligibility checks, and application processing. Automated workflows integrate with existing administrative systems, while human oversight is retained for exception handling and decision-making. Since implementation, the system has processed more than 300,000 aid applications, significantly reducing processing times and administrative workload. The initiative improves service delivery, ensures timely support to citizens and companies, and strengthens institutional resilience during crises. It demonstrates how intelligent automation can enhance public sector efficiency, scalability, and responsiveness in high-pressure policy contexts.

title: Monitoring structure health of bridges with InSAR
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Flemish Ministry of Mobility and Public Works (MOW)
source_description: Public authorities responsible for bridge management must ensure structural safety while optimising inspection budgets and minimising traffic disruption. Conventional monitoring relies on periodic visual inspections and targeted topographic surveys, which may fail to detect gradual deformations at an early stage. The project explores whether satellite-based interferometric analysis can support daily bridge management by identifying millimetre-level displacements and prioritising on-site investigations. Using Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), phase differences between successive radar satellite images are processed to calculate surface deformation over time. Different satellite data sources and processing techniques are assessed to determine their suitability for bridge monitoring, with algorithms designed to filter noise and automatically flag anomalous displacement patterns. The results are compared with ground-based measurements to validate accuracy and reliability. The approach aims to enable earlier detection of structural issues, more efficient allocation of inspection resources and reduced monitoring costs. By supporting risk-based maintenance planning and continuous remote observation, the solution enhances infrastructure safety, scalability of monitoring operations and evidence-based asset management.

title: Hello Lamp Post
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Environment Agency is responsible for protecting communities from flood and coastal risks, yet engaging diverse local audiences and providing timely, location-specific safety information has been challenging through traditional communication channels. The objective was to create an accessible, continuous engagement mechanism in high-risk areas in the South West of England and Newcastle, improving public awareness and preparedness. Hello Lamp Post introduced an interactive 24/7 conversational platform accessible via mobile devices, allowing residents to interact with physical infrastructure such as flood defences through text-based messaging. The system uses natural language processing to interpret questions and deliver contextualised information, drawing on curated flood safety guidance and local data. Conversations are geo-referenced to specific assets, ensuring relevance and enabling authorities to analyse recurring concerns. The initiative increased public interaction with flood risk information, improved accessibility outside office hours and generated insights into community awareness gaps. This supports more responsive communication strategies, strengthens trust between authorities and citizens and enhances resilience through scalable, place-based digital engagement.

title: ViEWS - The Political Violence Early-Warning System
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Violence Early-Warning System was launched in 2017 by Uppsala University and the Peace Research Institute Oslo to support policymakers and humanitarian actors in anticipating organised political violence. The objective is to provide transparent, evidence-based forecasts of conflict fatalities up to 36 months ahead across Africa and the Middle East. ViEWS integrates historical conflict event data, socioeconomic indicators, political variables and spatial-temporal datasets into statistical forecasting models. Ensemble modelling techniques and machine-learning algorithms generate monthly probabilistic predictions at fine geographic resolution. Results are published through an open online platform, enabling users to explore forecast scenarios and underlying data. The system enhances anticipatory action planning, resource allocation and early intervention strategies. By making methodology and forecasts publicly accessible, ViEWS strengthens transparency and reproducibility in conflict forecasting. Its structured modelling framework supports continuous updates and methodological refinement as new data become available.

title: Citibeats – Ethical AI for Social Understanding
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Governments and public organisations often struggle to interpret large volumes of unstructured citizen feedback from social media, surveys and open data sources, limiting their ability to detect emerging social concerns and respond proactively. The objective is to transform dispersed textual data into structured insights that inform policy design and service delivery while ensuring ethical data practices. The platform applies natural language processing and machine learning techniques to analyse large-scale text datasets, identifying themes, sentiment patterns and leading indicators of social trends. Algorithms classify content into policy-relevant categories and generate dashboards that visualise geographic and temporal patterns, using anonymised and aggregated data to protect privacy. The system integrates open data streams and institutional datasets to provide near real-time monitoring of public discourse. The solution enables earlier identification of societal risks, evidence-based prioritisation and more inclusive decision-making. By automating large-scale text analysis, it reduces manual workload, enhances analytical capacity and supports scalable, data-driven governance grounded in citizen perspectives.

title: Madrid Mobility 360 (multimodal planner for urban commuting)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Empresa Municipal de Transported del Ayuntamiento de Madrid
source_description: Madrid Mobility 360 was developed to provide residents and visitors with an integrated digital tool for planning journeys across multiple transport modes in the city. Urban commuters often face fragmented information across public transport, carsharing and bicycle services. The application aggregates data from transport operators and mobility providers into a unified platform offering route calculation, real-time updates and integrated payment options. The route planner uses optimisation algorithms to estimate current and projected journey times, incorporating live traffic data and vehicle capacity information for selected bus routes. Users can compare transport options, purchase tickets and view estimated carbon dioxide emissions associated with each trip. The system supports multimodal planning by integrating public transport schedules, shared mobility availability and geolocation services. By centralising mobility information, the app improves travel efficiency, enhances user experience and supports sustainable transport choices. It contributes to smart city mobility management and data-driven urban planning.

title: Transforming Public Healthcare and Education Using AI-powered Mixed Reality Technology
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Faculty of Medicine, University of Belgrade
source_description: The Government of Serbia, in collaboration with Microsoft, explored the use of mixed reality technologies to enhance healthcare delivery and medical education. Healthcare systems often face challenges in providing access to specialised expertise, particularly in complex cases requiring multidisciplinary input or remote consultation. The objective of this initiative is to enable remote collaboration among healthcare professionals and improve training opportunities for medical students. The solution combines mixed reality environments with data-driven analytical tools to allow clinicians to visualise patient data and medical scenarios in immersive formats. It supports real-time collaboration, enabling experts to contribute to diagnosis and treatment planning regardless of location. The system also facilitates remote education by simulating clinical scenarios for training purposes. While the initiative demonstrates potential to improve efficiency, reduce the need for physical presence, and enhance learning experiences, no recent evidence confirms large-scale deployment or continued operational use.

title: My First Salary - a project to address youth unemployment
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Young graduates often face a difficult transition from education to work, particularly when they lack practical experience and employers are hesitant to recruit first-time entrants during uncertain labour-market conditions. In Serbia, the My First Salary programme was designed to address this gap by helping young people under 30 obtain their first work opportunity while supporting employers in filling roles with subsidised early-career talent. The objective is to reduce youth unemployment, shorten the waiting time for a first job, and make the application and recruitment process far less bureaucratic than conventional state-support schemes. The implementation is built around a fully digital platform that automates application handling, approval, eligibility checks, and candidate-employer matching. At a conceptual level, the system combines digital identity and certificate-based registration, automated verification of company and candidate conditions, and a recommendation algorithm that helps match participants to opportunities. The programme also includes dashboards and visualisation tools to support administration of the scheme. The impact includes a simpler zero-paper process, faster access to support for both employers and young applicants, and more efficient matching between labour demand and available candidates. It also improves scalability and transparency in programme delivery while creating public value through a more accessible route into first employment.

title: HOPE - Healthy Outdoor Premises for Everyone
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban air quality monitoring traditionally relies on a limited number of fixed stations, providing only coarse-grained insights into citizens’ actual exposure to pollution. In the Helsinki region, this limits the ability of individuals and policymakers to understand air quality variations at neighbourhood or street level. The HOPE project addresses this gap by enabling hyper-local air quality monitoring through a dense, participatory sensing network. Stakeholders include citizens, city authorities, researchers, and public health organisations. The objective is to provide accessible, location-specific information on air pollution exposure in daily life. The solution combines data from fixed monitoring stations with crowdsourced measurements collected via portable sensors carried by citizens. These data are aggregated and visualised on digital maps, providing near real-time insights into air quality across the city. The project enhances spatial coverage, raises public awareness, and supports evidence-based urban planning and health interventions. HOPE empowers citizens with actionable information, improves understanding of pollution dynamics, and supports targeted measures to improve urban environmental health and quality of life.

title: Aeolus – Mid-altitude maritime monitoring platform for security, search & rescue and environmental monitoring
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Maritime authorities require wide-area surveillance to address security threats, coordinate search and rescue operations and monitor environmental risks, yet conventional ship-based sensors have limited range constrained by low elevation. The Aeolus project aims to extend maritime situational awareness by elevating monitoring systems to mid-altitude, thereby expanding coverage without deploying additional vessels. The platform consists of an airborne sensor system operating at approximately 450 metres above a host ship, increasing the observable area by more than eleven times compared with standard configurations. It can be deployed using different lifting mechanisms and remain operational for extended periods. Equipped with optical and radar sensors, the system transmits real-time data to onboard command centres, where information is processed and integrated with existing surveillance systems. The solution enhances detection capabilities for vessels, persons in distress and environmental anomalies, while improving operational efficiency. By increasing coverage and persistence at relatively low cost, the platform strengthens maritime safety, supports faster response times and enables scalable monitoring across diverse missions.

title: Monitoring slavery from space
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Brick kilns across the South Asian “Brick Belt” are associated with high prevalence of forced labour, yet the absence of reliable data on their number and distribution has hindered effective intervention by governments and non-governmental organisations. The project sought to generate an evidence base to estimate the scale of kiln operations and, by proxy, potential exposure to modern slavery. High-resolution satellite imagery was analysed to identify and map kiln structures across regions of Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Nepal. Image recognition techniques and spatial analysis were used to detect characteristic kiln shapes and validate findings against ground-truth information. The resulting geospatial dataset enabled a more credible estimate of kiln numbers and their geographic concentration. By providing transparent, large-scale evidence, the initiative supports targeted inspections, policy prioritisation and resource allocation. It enhances situational awareness for anti-slavery actors and demonstrates how satellite data can improve accountability, scalability of monitoring and informed action against labour exploitation.

title: R2D3: Active-waiting robot for the disabled people’s waiting room
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Seine-Saint-Denis Innovation Lab developed the R2D3 robot to improve accessibility and user experience for individuals visiting the Departmental House for Disabled Persons. Waiting times in administrative services can be challenging, particularly for users with diverse needs and varying levels of digital literacy. The objective is to provide an inclusive and engaging way to deliver information and support users during waiting periods. The solution consists of an interactive robot equipped with speech recognition and multilingual capabilities, enabling it to communicate with users in a simple and accessible manner. It delivers information on administrative procedures and services through conversational interaction, using natural language processing and pre-programmed knowledge bases. The system is designed to be user-oriented and adaptable to different user profiles. As a pilot initiative, it demonstrates the potential to reduce the digital divide, improve access to information, and enhance user experience, although no evidence confirms broader deployment.

title: Voice assistant services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Aylesbury Vale District Council sought to expand digital access to local government information by offering residents an alternative to web-based and telephone enquiries. The objective was to improve convenience and accessibility for routine questions relating to council services, payments and waste management. The council became the first UK local authority to launch an Amazon Alexa skill, enabling residents to obtain information through voice commands. The service integrates structured council data and frequently asked questions into Amazon’s voice interface using predefined intents and dialogue flows. Users can ask about political leadership, council tax payment options, recycling guidance and book assisted waste collections. Requests are processed through Amazon’s voice recognition infrastructure and linked to council information systems via secure APIs. The solution increases out-of-hours access, reduces pressure on contact centres and broadens digital inclusion for users preferring voice interaction. It demonstrates how local authorities can leverage commercial voice platforms to extend service delivery channels efficiently.

title: Alexa skill - vehicle tax and MOT
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency introduced an Alexa skill to simplify access to information about vehicle tax and MOT expiry dates. Vehicle owners often needed quick confirmation of compliance deadlines without navigating government websites. The objective was to provide a convenient, hands-free information channel. Users can ask Alexa when a vehicle’s tax or MOT is due by stating the registration number. The service connects Amazon’s voice recognition system with DVLA databases through secure application interfaces, retrieving real-time status information. Structured query handling ensures that only publicly accessible vehicle compliance data are returned, without disclosing personal details. The implementation reduces friction in accessing regulatory information and encourages timely renewals, supporting road safety and compliance. By leveraging a commercial voice platform, DVLA broadened service accessibility while maintaining existing digital channels. The initiative illustrates integration of public registers with consumer voice technologies for citizen-facing information services.

title: Alexa skill and Google home app - checking state pension age
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Department for Work and Pensions developed a prototype voice service enabling citizens to check their state pension age through Amazon Alexa and Google Home devices. Many users sought quick clarification of eligibility timelines without navigating detailed guidance pages. The objective was to provide simple, accessible answers via voice interaction. The service uses predefined conversational flows and structured eligibility rules based on date of birth. Users provide relevant information verbally, which is processed through the respective voice assistant platforms and matched against pension age legislation encoded in the application logic. The system returns an estimated pension age without storing personal data beyond the session. By offering voice-based access, DWP aimed to enhance accessibility for users with limited digital literacy or visual impairments. The prototype demonstrated the feasibility of integrating statutory rules into consumer voice platforms while maintaining privacy safeguards and limiting responses to informational guidance rather than personalised entitlement decisions.

title: Alexa skill - enquiring about tax credits
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: HM Revenue and Customs launched an Alexa skill to support over three million tax credit customers during renewal periods, when contact volumes are typically high. The objective was to provide accessible guidance on renewal deadlines, required information and general eligibility queries. The service integrates structured knowledge content into Amazon’s voice assistant using defined intents and scripted dialogue paths. Users can ask about renewal dates, documentation requirements and payment information. The system retrieves up-to-date guidance from HMRC information sources without enabling transactional account access or disclosure of sensitive personal data. By automating responses to common enquiries, the skill reduces call centre demand and improves response times during peak periods. The initiative broadens digital engagement channels while preserving existing secure online and telephone services for account-specific matters. It illustrates the use of voice platforms for scalable dissemination of public information in high-demand administrative processes.

title: Alexa skill - personalised weather report and forecast
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The UK Met Office introduced an Alexa “Flash Briefing” skill to provide personalised weather forecasts and updates through voice interaction. The operational goal was to extend access to official meteorological information beyond traditional broadcast and web channels. Users can request weather updates for selected regions, receiving spoken forecasts tailored to their preferences. The service integrates the Met Office’s forecasting datasets with Amazon’s voice recognition and delivery platform. Structured content feeds and location-based parameters generate region-specific briefings, while forecast data are updated regularly from meteorological models and observation systems. The solution enhances accessibility, enabling hands-free access to authoritative weather information in homes and workplaces. It supports public safety and daily planning by delivering timely updates through widely adopted consumer devices. The deployment demonstrates integration of national forecasting infrastructure with commercial voice ecosystems to expand reach and user convenience.

title: Big Data Analysis for HR efficiency improvement
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Ministry of Public Administration sought to improve organisational efficiency, workforce planning and employee satisfaction, but faced fragmented human resources data and limited analytical capacity to extract strategic insights. The pilot project aimed to assess how a big data tool deployed on the Governmental State Cloud Infrastructure could support advanced analysis of HR datasets. The solution integrated personnel records, performance indicators and administrative data into a centralised analytics environment, applying data mining and statistical techniques to identify patterns related to staffing levels, absenteeism and organisational performance. Dashboards and reporting tools enabled managers to explore trends and simulate scenarios for workforce optimisation. By consolidating data sources and automating analysis, the project enhanced evidence-based decision-making in HR management. Anticipated benefits include improved allocation of human resources, increased organisational effectiveness and better-informed strategies to support staff development and satisfaction, while demonstrating the scalability of cloud-based analytics within public administration.

title: Kora - virtual assistant
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Municipality of Heidenheim introduced Kora, a virtual assistant designed to provide round-the-clock responses to common citizen enquiries. The objective was to improve accessibility to municipal information while reducing administrative workload. Kora operates as a self-learning chatbot integrated into the municipal website, handling approximately 70 enquiries per day with a reported success rate of 99 per cent at launch. The system uses natural language processing to interpret user questions and match them to a structured knowledge base of predefined answers. Machine-learning components refine intent recognition over time based on interaction patterns and supervised updates. Initial high-demand topics included weather, local events and coronavirus-related guidance. The chatbot standardises responses, shortens waiting times and ensures consistent information delivery outside office hours. By automating routine enquiries, the municipality can allocate staff resources to more complex cases requiring individual attention, enhancing service efficiency and digital engagement.

title: Chatbot Munich
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The IT-Department of the municipality of Munich is developing a chatbot for Munich which is supposed to complete the current services like the common emergency number 115, the service portal and mobile apps.

title: Steuerchatbot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Tax administrations receive large numbers of routine questions about declarations, deadlines, and procedures, and handling these enquiries manually can consume staff time that could otherwise be used for more complex taxpayer support. In Baden-Württemberg, the Karlsruhe finance administration introduced a tax chatbot to answer simple questions related to tax declarations and make basic guidance available through a digital self-service channel. The objective is to improve accessibility to standard tax information, reduce waiting times for routine enquiries, and offer citizens a more convenient entry point into tax-related guidance. The implementation uses a conversational chatbot provided through the Baden-Württemberg tax administration’s digital service environment. At a conceptual level, the solution combines a question-and-answer interface with a structured knowledge base on tax topics, enabling users to ask common questions and receive immediate responses without having to contact the tax office directly. The chatbot is positioned as a front-line support tool for straightforward matters rather than for complex or case-specific advisory work. The impact includes quicker access to tax information, reduced pressure on telephone and counter services, and a more scalable way to provide standard guidance. It also improves the user experience by making tax support available through a simple digital interface that can handle repetitive enquiries consistently and at any time.

title: DB Smile - the national railway service chatbot for job seekers
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Deutsche Bahn introduced DB Smile to streamline recruitment processes and support job seekers navigating employment opportunities within the national railway company. The operational challenge was to manage high volumes of candidate enquiries and simplify application procedures. DB Smile functions as an interactive chatbot on the company’s recruitment platform, guiding users through job searches, answering application-related questions and facilitating submission of applications via chat. The system uses natural language processing to interpret queries and match candidates with suitable vacancies based on role preferences and qualifications. Integrated with Deutsche Bahn’s recruitment database, the chatbot provides real-time information on openings and application status. By automating responses to frequently asked questions and enabling conversational job matching, DB Smile accelerates the recruitment journey and reduces administrative burden. The solution improves candidate experience, shortens response times and supports efficient talent acquisition within a large public transport organisation.

title: SEMMI - Avatar
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Deutsche Bahn developed SEMMI Avatar to enhance customer service interactions in stations and other service environments by providing an engaging digital interface capable of handling routine enquiries. The operational objective is to complement human staff, improve accessibility and deliver consistent information across locations with varying infrastructure constraints. SEMMI Avatar is built on the SEMMI Conversational AI platform and combines speech recognition, natural language understanding and animated visual representation to create a multimodal human–machine interface. The system can be deployed on existing or new display hardware, indoors or outdoors, with or without touchscreen functionality, and adapts responsively to different screen sizes and formats. User queries are processed through conversational models that interpret intent and retrieve relevant information from integrated service databases. The avatar delivers responses through synchronised speech and visual cues, creating an interactive experience. The solution improves service availability, reduces waiting times for routine questions and supports scalable deployment across transport hubs and public-facing environments.

title: SEMMI - Robot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Customer-facing organisations often struggle to provide multilingual, consistent and accessible front-office support, particularly in high-traffic environments such as transport hubs or service centres. SEMMI Robot was designed to enhance on-site customer interaction by answering routine enquiries in visitors’ native languages, reducing waiting times and improving service accessibility. Stakeholders include service providers, customer service staff and end users. The robot combines speech recognition, natural language understanding and multilingual conversational models to interpret user queries, retrieve relevant information from integrated knowledge bases and generate context-appropriate responses through speech synthesis and on-screen displays. The system connects to backend information systems, such as timetables or service databases, enabling real-time responses. Early deployments indicate improved user engagement, reduced pressure on frontline staff and enhanced customer experience, particularly for international users. The solution remains in progressive development and deployment phases across selected sites, with no confirmed large-scale standardisation across all potential service locations.

title: SEMMI - Hotline
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: High call volumes and repetitive enquiries place significant strain on customer service centres, leading to long waiting times and rising staffing costs. SEMMI Hotline was conceived as an advanced interactive voice response solution capable of handling routine enquiries autonomously while escalating complex cases to human agents. Stakeholders include contact centre operators, service agents and callers. The system uses automatic speech recognition, intent classification models and dialogue management frameworks to conduct natural conversations, access integrated customer databases and provide real-time responses. Cloud-based telephony integration allows rapid scaling to handle simultaneous calls without proportional increases in staffing. Reported benefits include reduced agent workload, shorter waiting times and improved scalability during peak demand. The solution continues to evolve, with ongoing enhancements to conversational capabilities; no definitive information indicates full replacement of traditional call centre models at scale.

title: Urban Cockpit - a digital twin of Bad Hersfeld
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The municipality of Bad Hersfeld developed the Urban Cockpit as a publicly accessible digital twin to increase transparency and improve urban management. The objective was to aggregate heterogeneous municipal data into a single visual platform supporting informed decision-making and citizen engagement. The system integrates open-source datasets and sensor data into a geospatial dashboard that visualises real-time and static information. Data layers include parking occupancy, waste bin fill levels and locations of electric vehicle charging stations. Geographic information systems and data integration tools harmonise inputs from different municipal departments, enabling dynamic visualisation on an interactive map. The platform allows residents to monitor service availability and urban conditions, while municipal staff use the same data to support operational planning. By centralising urban indicators, the Urban Cockpit enhances situational awareness, promotes transparency and supports data-driven governance. The digital twin approach enables scalable expansion to additional datasets and smart city applications.

title: Traffic flux representation with AI in Lisbon
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Lisbon City Council partnered with the National Civil Engineering Laboratory and Instituto Superior Técnico to improve integrated traffic management in a densely populated urban environment. The operational challenge was to collect and interpret diverse mobility and contextual data to support coordinated transport planning and congestion mitigation. The initiative deploys data analytics systems that gather information from traffic sensors, mobility services and contextual urban datasets. Machine-learning models classify traffic patterns and estimate flow dynamics across the road network, generating predictive and descriptive indicators for decision-makers. Integrated dashboards visualise congestion levels and support scenario analysis for traffic regulation measures. The system enhances coordination between agencies and enables evidence-based planning of mobility interventions. By transforming raw mobility data into actionable insights, Lisbon strengthens its capacity to manage traffic flux proactively, optimise infrastructure use and improve travel conditions for residents and visitors.

title: Baggage handling at the Copenhagen Airport
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Copenhagen Airport introduced data-driven optimisation in 2016 to improve baggage handling efficiency and passenger experience. Managing baggage flows requires precise coordination of staff and conveyor systems to minimise delays and queue times. The airport implemented predictive analytics models that analyse operational data, flight schedules and historical handling patterns to forecast where staff deployment would most effectively empty aircraft and load baggage onto conveyor belts. Optimisation algorithms recommend resource allocation to reduce bottlenecks and improve turnaround times. The system integrates with airport operational management platforms, providing decision support to supervisors. By anticipating workload peaks and adjusting staffing dynamically, the solution shortens waiting times, enhances punctuality and improves passenger satisfaction. The initiative demonstrates how advanced analytics can optimise complex logistics environments, increasing operational efficiency while maintaining safety and reliability in airport ground handling processes.

title: Cluny Abbey using AR and 3D recordings to visualise "what has today disappeared"""
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The town of Cluny implemented a digital heritage initiative to enhance visitor engagement by reconstructing historical environments that are no longer physically present. Cultural heritage sites often face challenges in conveying their original scale and significance due to the loss or deterioration of structures. The objective is to provide visitors with an immersive understanding of the abbey’s historical context. The solution uses augmented reality and three-dimensional modelling to recreate the abbey and its surroundings, based on historical documents, architectural plans, and visual records. Visitors can access digital reconstructions through AR interfaces installed on-site, enabling them to visualise past structures in their original locations. The system integrates a comprehensive database of 2D and 3D assets for both public engagement and scientific use. As an implemented solution, it enhances cultural interpretation, improves visitor experience, and supports research and preservation efforts.

title: Fietsbarometer - barometer for cycleways safety
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Province of Antwerp developed the Fietsbarometer as a web-based participatory platform to assess and improve cycling safety, particularly on home-to-school routes. The objective was to gather detailed, location-specific insights from adolescents regarding perceived and observed safety conditions in school neighbourhoods. Participants digitally map their daily cycling routes and evaluate factors such as infrastructure quality, traffic intensity and hazardous points. The platform aggregates geolocated inputs into spatial datasets, which are visualised through interactive mapping tools. Data analytics functions identify recurring safety concerns and prioritise areas requiring intervention. Municipal planners use these insights to inform infrastructure improvements and traffic management measures. By combining citizen-generated data with geographic information systems, the Fietsbarometer strengthens evidence-based policy-making and youth engagement in mobility planning. The approach enhances transparency and supports targeted investment in safer cycling environments across Flemish municipalities.

title: Jelbi - the mobility app for Berlin's public and sharing services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Jelbi was launched by Berlin’s public transport authority BVG to integrate public transport and shared mobility services into a single digital platform. Urban travellers often face fragmented booking and payment systems across transport providers. Jelbi aggregates buses, trains, carsharing, bike sharing and e-scooter services within one application, enabling route planning, booking and payment through a unified interface. The platform integrates real-time transport data, availability feeds from mobility partners and secure payment processing systems. Route optimisation algorithms propose multimodal journeys tailored to user preferences and current conditions. Physical Jelbi stations across Berlin provide co-located access to shared vehicles, reinforcing the digital–physical integration. The app enhances user convenience, encourages multimodal travel and supports sustainable urban mobility by reducing reliance on private car ownership. By centralising mobility services, Jelbi strengthens cooperation between public and private providers and contributes to Berlin’s smart city transport strategy.

title: NOMAD - the travel-app to travel anywhere in the Nordics
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Nordic Open Mobility and Digitalisation initiative aims to enable seamless cross-border travel across Nordic countries by promoting interoperable Mobility as a Service solutions. Travellers often encounter fragmented booking systems and limited integration between national transport providers. NOMAD seeks to establish a market-enabler framework combining technological standards and business practices that support MaaS roaming. The system architecture allows users to plan, book and manage multimodal journeys across borders through a single interface. Interoperability protocols connect transport operators, payment systems and journey planning services, facilitating integrated ticketing and administration of international trips. Data exchange standards ensure compatibility between participating platforms while respecting national regulatory requirements. By fostering cross-border cooperation and digital integration, NOMAD enhances user convenience, supports sustainable mobility choices and strengthens regional transport connectivity. The initiative contributes to harmonising smart mobility ecosystems across the Nordic region.

title: Explore.Porto - discover and explore the city through a digital platform
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The Municipality of Porto developed Explore.Porto to provide visitors and residents with an integrated digital tool for navigating the city and accessing up-to-date information on attractions and mobility options. Urban tourists often face fragmented sources of information covering points of interest, transport routes and local services. The objective was to centralise these datasets into a single web-based and mobile application offering intuitive and real-time guidance. The platform aggregates geolocated information from municipal databases and authorised partners who can create and update points of interest on an interactive map. Route optimisation functions analyse available mobility options, suggesting the most efficient paths between selected locations and highlighting nearby attractions. The system integrates tourism content, transport data and spatial analytics within a unified interface, enabling personalised exploration of the city. By consolidating dispersed information streams, Explore.Porto enhances user experience, supports sustainable mobility choices and strengthens digital engagement with the city’s cultural and commercial ecosystem.

title: RePAIR – Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Cultural Heritage Reconstruction
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Archaeological artefacts are often discovered in thousands of fragments, making physical reconstruction a painstaking and time-consuming task that requires scarce expert skills. Many damaged artworks remain in storage for decades due to the effort required to restore them. The RePAIR project addresses this challenge by supporting archaeologists and conservators in reconstructing fragmented cultural heritage. Stakeholders include museums, researchers, conservation experts, and the public. The objective is to dramatically reduce the time and effort needed to restore large, shattered artefacts while preserving scientific and cultural integrity. The solution develops an intelligent robotic system capable of digitally analysing fragments, identifying matching pieces, and physically assembling artefacts autonomously. Advanced pattern recognition and shape-matching techniques guide robotic manipulation, enabling precise reconstruction. The system is tested on complex frescoes from the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Pompeii. RePAIR accelerates restoration timelines, reduces manual labour, and enables the recovery of artefacts previously considered too complex to reconstruct. It opens new possibilities for preserving and showcasing cultural heritage through scalable, technology-enabled conservation.

title: Chatbot - German Federal Employment Agency
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Federal Employment Agency introduced a chatbot to improve accessibility to information on employment services and social benefits. Citizens frequently seek guidance on unemployment benefits, short-time allowance, child supplement, training opportunities and related administrative procedures, creating high enquiry volumes. The chatbot provides a digital self-service channel available at all times through the Agency’s website. It uses natural language processing to interpret user questions and match them with curated responses drawn from official guidance content. Structured dialogue flows guide users to relevant pages, forms and contact points. The system automates responses to routine enquiries while redirecting complex or case-specific matters to human advisers. By standardising information delivery and reducing response times, the chatbot alleviates pressure on call centres and improves user convenience. The deployment supports scalable digital service provision while maintaining human oversight for personalised assistance and legal determinations.

title: Chatbot Guido
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The State of North Rhine-Westphalia implemented Chatbot Guido to simplify access to information regarding online business registration procedures. Entrepreneurs and business owners often require clear guidance on administrative steps, documentation requirements and digital submission processes. The objective was to provide immediate, structured answers through a conversational interface integrated into the state’s business service portal. Guido operates using predefined question–answer pairs and natural language processing components that classify user intent and deliver relevant guidance. The chatbot directs users to appropriate online forms, explains procedural steps and clarifies regulatory requirements. By automating responses to frequently asked questions, the system reduces administrative burden on service desks and improves accessibility for businesses seeking to register or modify operations. The solution enhances efficiency in public service delivery and supports digitalisation of business administration processes across the state.

title: Digitale Assistenz Ina
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Integration Office of the State Government of Schleswig-Holstein
source_description: The state of Schleswig-Holstein introduced the digital assistant Ina to provide information related to the Integration Office, particularly on matters concerning disability and workplace inclusion. Citizens and employers often require guidance on rights, benefits and administrative procedures, leading to frequent general enquiries. Ina offers a conversational interface embedded in the state administration website, delivering responses based on curated knowledge content and structured dialogue paths. Natural language processing components interpret user input and map questions to predefined topics such as disability support, financial assistance and legal frameworks. The system provides general information and directs users to relevant forms or contact points, while complex or individual cases remain handled by human staff. By offering continuous digital assistance, Ina improves accessibility, reduces waiting times and supports consistent information dissemination. The initiative contributes to inclusive digital public services while preserving professional oversight for case-specific decisions.

title: TWIN4ROAD@Essen: AI-based analysis and forecast
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Managing Germany’s extensive road network requires continuous assessment of pavement condition and infrastructure assets, yet the volume and complexity of data make manual evaluation inefficient and costly. The City of Essen launched TWIN4ROAD to build a comprehensive digital representation of its road infrastructure to support maintenance planning and investment decisions. Data are collected using ground penetrating radar, mobile laser scanning, 3D measurements and high-resolution imagery to create a detailed inventory of road surfaces and subsurface structures. Advanced data analytics and machine learning models process these datasets to assess current damage, identify structural weaknesses and forecast potential pothole development. The resulting digital twin integrates condition data with spatial information systems, enabling automated evaluations and scenario analyses. The approach improves accuracy and timeliness of maintenance planning, reduces inspection costs and supports preventive interventions. By providing a reusable infrastructure inventory, the system also benefits other municipal services operating in public road space, enhancing cross-departmental coordination and long-term asset management.

title: KI4Forst - Monitoring the Forest with Satellite Data and AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geoinformation aims to improve forest monitoring and management by leveraging satellite data. Traditional methods for assessing forest conditions are resource-intensive and may not provide timely or comprehensive insights into environmental changes such as drought damage or pest infestations. The objective is to enable automated, large-scale monitoring of forest areas and their condition. The solution involves developing an automated processing chain that applies deep learning techniques to satellite imagery. Image classification models, based on artificial neural networks, are trained to detect forest areas and distinguish between different forest types, such as deciduous and coniferous. The system also identifies changes in vegetation health and potential damage. Outputs are integrated into geospatial information systems for visualisation and decision support.

title: Chatbot Govii
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Flensburg piloted Chatbot Govii in 2021 to streamline access to municipal administrative services and contact information. Residents often encounter difficulty identifying the correct department or procedure for specific requests. Govii provides a conversational interface on the city’s website, enabling users to ask questions in natural language and receive structured guidance. The system relies on predefined knowledge bases and intent recognition models to classify enquiries and retrieve relevant service descriptions, contact details and application links. By automating responses to routine queries, the chatbot reduces the need for direct phone or in-person enquiries and improves navigation of municipal services. The deployment enhances service efficiency, shortens response times and supports digital-first interaction with the administration. It also allows municipal staff to focus on complex cases requiring personalised attention.
supporting_source_urls: Bendszusn, R. (2022). Make-or-buy in the area of Artificial Intelligence: Insights from AI use cases in the German public sector (master's thesis). Hertie School, Berlin.

title: Starting up smoothly: chatbot service (Virtual Agent Network) for foreign entrepreneurs in Finland
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Immigration Service, Patent and Registration Office and the Tax Administration
source_description: Starting a business as a foreign entrepreneur can require interaction with multiple agencies covering immigration, registration, patents, and tax, and this fragmentation often creates confusion, duplicated effort, and avoidable delays. In Finland, the “Starting up Smoothly” initiative was designed to reduce these barriers by connecting the conversational services of the Immigration Service, the Patent and Registration Office, and the Tax Administration into a more seamless user journey. The objective was to break down agency silos and give entrepreneurs a more coherent route through immigration, business-registration, and taxation questions. The implementation linked three virtual agents—Kamu, PatRek, and VeroBot—through a shared conversational network, using natural language understanding to detect when a user’s question fell outside one bot’s scope and hand over the conversation within the same chat window to the most relevant agency bot. However, Finnish official material from the start of the project described the inter-agency cooperation as a trial ending in June 2019, and Migri later announced that Kamu itself was discontinued after 31 October 2024, even though PRH still operates its Trade Register chatbot. The impact of the original project was to demonstrate smoother inter-agency digital support, but its current status is best described as partly absorbed into successor services rather than still running unchanged.

title: 120 Words per Minute - a Training App for Basal Automated Reading
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Primary schools face a persistent literacy challenge, as a substantial share of pupils do not reach fluent reading speed by the end of primary education and often struggle to recover later. In Schleswig-Holstein, the “120 Words per Minute” project was conceived to support the “Lesen macht stark” programme by converting a printed diagnostic and training approach into a more flexible app-based tool for schools. The objective is to improve reading fluency, make diagnosis and support easier to use in everyday teaching, and enable children to practise independently or in pairs while giving teachers a more continuous way to monitor progress. The implementation centres on an app that digitises the phases of the existing reading-support programme and uses speech-to-text methods to automate the level check that children would otherwise complete manually. Public descriptions of the project present it as a digital education solution intended to support classroom use from the earliest training stages and to simplify the practical application of the methodology in school settings. The expected impact includes improved reading fluency, more practical use of diagnostic support at school level, and a more scalable method for early literacy intervention, especially for children at risk of falling behind.

title: KI4GeoSeDa – AI-Based Georeferencing of Specialist Data Pools for Semantic Data Integration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geo-Information
source_description: The Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geoinformation, in collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, aims to improve the integration of heterogeneous spatial datasets used in public administration. Many specialised databases contain location references in unstructured textual form, making it difficult to integrate them into standardised geospatial systems. The objective is to enable automated georeferencing and semantic integration of such data. The solution uses natural language processing and machine learning techniques to analyse address data and linguistic spatial references, converting them into precise geospatial coordinates. These outputs are then integrated into existing spatial data infrastructures, enabling unified access and analysis. The system supports semantic enrichment and interoperability across datasets. As a pilot project, its focused on algorithm design and validation includes with expected benefits including improved data integration, enhanced decision-making, and more efficient use of geospatial information.

title: AI-Supported unmanned aeriasl vehicles (UAVs) for Ecological Agriculture and Forestry
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: This project explores the use of unmanned aerial vehicles to support ecological agriculture and forestry management. Monitoring weeds, crop health, and forest conditions typically requires significant manual effort and may lack precision at scale. The objective is to enable automated and efficient environmental monitoring and intervention. The solution involves adapting an existing AI-based weed detection system to operate on low-power embedded hardware mounted on drones. Machine learning models process visual data captured by onboard sensors to identify weeds and assess vegetation conditions in real time. The project also investigates the transferability of these models to forestry applications. Integration with drone platforms allows flexible and targeted data collection across large areas. As a research and development initiative, the system is still being tested and validated, with expected benefits including reduced labour requirements, improved precision, and more sustainable land management practices

title: Support the integration of job seekers with artificial intelligence
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The University of Applied Sciences Kiel, in collaboration with Jobcenter Kiel and the Institute for Labour Market and Vocational Research, is developing tools to improve the integration of job seekers into the labour market. Employment services often face challenges in matching individuals with suitable job opportunities and training pathways, particularly when dealing with diverse profiles and labour market dynamics. The objective is to enhance counselling services through data-driven recommendations. The solution uses machine learning techniques, including self-organising maps and reinforcement learning, to analyse anonymised data and cluster job seekers based on skills, experience, and labour market conditions. These clusters are used to generate personalised recommendations for employment, retraining, and further education opportunities. The system is designed to complement the expertise of job centre staff and support decision-making processes. The project aims to improve matching efficiency and service effectiveness, although no evidence confirms full operational deployment.

title: Autonomous Fawn Tracking System - AROS
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Farmers and wildlife-protection volunteers have only a short time to locate hidden fawns in fields before mowing begins, and manual searches with thermal drones can still be labour-intensive, weather-sensitive, and dependent on multiple people. AROS was designed in Schleswig-Holstein to address this by automating more of the detection and localisation process so that fawns can be found and rescued more efficiently. The objective is to protect wildlife, reduce dependence on scarce human resources, and enable more reliable pre-harvest scanning of fields across different conditions. The implementation combines autonomous drone flight, thermal and visual sensing, computer-vision models based on convolutional neural networks, and geolocation functions that send the detected animal’s GPS position and aerial view to the farmer and hunter for intervention. Technical reporting describes an autonomous fawn-tracking system with high positioning accuracy, while project material presents the solution as a collaboration between nAIture and public actors in Schleswig-Holstein. The expected impact is faster rescue, better field coverage, and a more scalable wildlife-protection workflow during mowing season.

title: “Demenzwegweiser-SH” (Schleswig-Holstein Guide to Dementia)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Social Affairs, Youth, Family, Senior Citizens, Integration and Equality of Schleswig-Holstein
source_description: Demenzwegweiser-SH was created to centralise and maintain up-to-date information on dementia-related services across Schleswig-Holstein. Individuals and families often struggle to identify regional counselling centres, specialist doctors, care options and support services. The platform functions as a searchable database providing structured information on medical, social and legal aspects of dementia, including nursing care insurance, legal guardianship and non-pharmacological therapies. Automated data processing techniques support continuous updating and categorisation of entries, ensuring that regional service information remains current. Information extraction and classification tools organise content into thematic categories and geographic locations. By consolidating dispersed information into a single digital guide, the platform enhances accessibility for patients, caregivers and professionals. It improves transparency of available support networks and facilitates informed decision-making regarding care pathways.

title: MASIRI – Multi-Agent Simulation for Integrated Energy and Mobility Systems
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The integration of energy and mobility systems, such as vehicle-to-grid solutions, depends not only on technical optimisation but also on human behaviour and decision-making. Traditional system models often neglect how users’ experiences, preferences, and habits influence energy and mobility usage.
