The MASIRI project addresses this gap by exploring how behavioural insights can improve the design and regulation of integrated energy and mobility systems. Stakeholders include researchers, system designers, policymakers, and energy providers. The objective is to understand and simulate interactions between human behaviour and intelligent energy systems to optimise resource use. The solution develops a multi-agent simulation framework in which intelligent agents represent energy users with psychologically informed behaviour models. These agents interact within simulated vehicle-to-grid environments, allowing analysis of how different incentives, regulations, and system designs influence outcomes. The project improves understanding of behavioural dynamics, supports more realistic system modelling, and informs better policy and infrastructure design. MASIRI contributes to more efficient, user-centred, and resilient energy and mobility systems that align technical optimisation with real-world human behaviour.

title: Licence to practice
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The issuance and verification of professional licences for graduates in regulated professions, such as engineering or medicine, is often a manual and time-consuming process, particularly in cross-border contexts. In Cyprus and Greece, where many students study abroad, delays, administrative burden, and risks of fraud undermine efficiency and trust. The objective of this use case is to streamline the issuance, sharing, and verification of professional credentials across borders. The solution leverages the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) to enable secure, verifiable digital credentials. Academic and professional authorities issue licences in a digital format that can be shared and validated across jurisdictions using distributed ledger technology. The system ensures authenticity, integrity, and traceability of credentials while reducing reliance on paper-based processes. As a pilot initiative involving stakeholders such as GUnet, the Cypriot Deputy Ministry, and ETEK, it demonstrates potential to reduce processing times, administrative costs, and fraud risks, while improving cross-border mobility and trust in professional qualifications.

title: Helsinki Map Service
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Helsinki Map Service is a browser-based geospatial platform providing comprehensive mapping and real-time urban data to residents, businesses and visitors. The operational objective is to centralise spatial information about city infrastructure, services and environmental conditions into an accessible digital interface. The system integrates geographic information systems with datasets covering traffic conditions, public transport, real estate, buildings, outdoor lighting, cycling and walking routes and municipal services. Real-time feeds update traffic and mobility layers, while thematic map tools allow users to visualise specific categories of interest. The platform supports interactive exploration, search functions and layered data visualisation through a web-based map viewer. By consolidating diverse geospatial datasets, the service enhances transparency, supports urban planning and enables residents to make informed mobility and property decisions. The initiative strengthens Helsinki’s data-driven governance and open data ecosystem.

title: Talbotti - Helsinki's financial management service chatbot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Helsinki introduced Talbotti as a digital contact channel for its financial management services to improve accessibility and reduce pressure on traditional customer service channels. Residents and city employees frequently require guidance on invoicing, payments and financial procedures, often outside standard office hours. Talbotti provides round-the-clock responses to common enquiries and, during opening hours, allows seamless transfer to a live chat with a customer adviser. The chatbot uses natural language processing to interpret questions and retrieve information from curated knowledge bases and financial service databases. It offers self-service guidance, up-to-date information and direct links to relevant webpages, streamlining access to forms and instructions. Interaction data are analysed to refine responses and improve intent recognition over time. By automating routine queries, Talbotti shortens response times, enhances user experience and enables staff to focus on complex cases requiring individual assessment. The solution strengthens service continuity and operational efficiency within municipal financial administration.

title: Sotebotti hester
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Helsinki’s Social Services, Health Care and Rescue Services Division introduced Sotebotti Hester to improve access to information across a broad range of welfare services. Citizens often seek guidance on maternity clinics, child health services and other social and health-related provisions. The chatbot provides a digital interface available at all times, delivering structured information and directing users to relevant services. Hester operates using predefined dialogue paths and natural language understanding components that classify user intent and retrieve content from official service databases. It guides users through service descriptions, contact information and procedural steps, while complex or sensitive matters remain handled by professionals. By automating responses to frequently asked questions, the system reduces call volumes and enhances accessibility outside office hours. The solution supports consistent information delivery and facilitates navigation of health and social care services, contributing to improved user experience and more efficient allocation of administrative resources.

title: Dutch cycling intelligence
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Dutch Cycling Intelligence programme developed the Digital Twin “Atlas of the Accessible City” to provide data-driven insights into urban accessibility and cycling infrastructure. Coordinated by Logistics Community Brabant in collaboration with academic partners and Argaleo, the initiative addresses the need for integrated analysis of mobility bottlenecks and opportunities in urban environments. The Atlas aggregates publicly available datasets and, where applicable, private data sources into a three-dimensional geospatial visualisation platform. Geographic information systems and data analytics tools map traffic flows, cycling routes and accessibility indicators, enabling stakeholders to identify congestion points and infrastructural gaps at a glance. The digital twin translates policy questions into measurable spatial insights, supporting planning decisions and infrastructure investment. By centralising and visualising complex datasets, the system enhances collaboration between public authorities and research institutions, strengthens evidence-based mobility policy and improves strategic planning for accessible and sustainable urban transport networks.

title: Atlas Cyclable Utrecht
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Commissioned by the Province of Utrecht, Atlas Fietsbaar Utrecht was developed within a digital twin framework to assess cycling accessibility, particularly in relation to educational institutions. Policymakers required detailed insights into route quality, infrastructure performance and optimal locations for bicycle tunnels. The platform integrates publicly available transport data with advanced bicycle usage analyses into a centralised dashboard. Geospatial modelling and traffic data processing tools visualise cycling flows, detect bottlenecks such as traffic light delays and evaluate accessibility scenarios. The dashboard enables users to explore route efficiency and identify priority areas for infrastructure development. By translating mobility data into actionable policy insights, the Atlas supports targeted investment in cycling infrastructure and promotes sustainable transport. The system enhances transparency and decision-making efficiency by offering user-friendly access to consolidated, data-driven indicators relevant to regional planning and educational accessibility strategies.

title: Atlas Multimodal Brabant – Digital Twin for Freight Corridors (Netherlands)

Users can identify accessible terminals from their location, evaluate route options and contact operators directly through integrated communication functions. Data integration and visual analytics tools provide insights into corridor usage and sustainability performance, enabling evidence-based decisions on modal shifts and collaborative transport solutions. By centralising freight information and environmental metrics, the Atlas enhances transparency, supports emission reduction goals and improves efficiency in regional logistics networks. The platform strengthens cooperation between public authorities, academic institutions and private transport actors within Brabant’s multimodal strategy.

title: Crowd management dashboard in 's-Hertogenbosch

Data analytics tools process current flow information and analyse trends, answering questions such as peak entry times and predominant directions of movement. The system provides municipal staff with situational awareness to support timely crowd control measures and communication strategies. By combining real-time monitoring with historical analysis, the dashboard enables data-driven decisions that balance public health considerations with economic activity. The initiative enhances urban resilience and supports safe city centre management through digital twin technologies and mobility analytics.

title: Outdoor Mobility Digital Twin at TU Delft

The solution integrates data from sensors that convert visual inputs into privacy-preserving representations, combined with external data sources such as public transport locations and infrastructure status. These data are visualised in a three-dimensional digital twin dashboard, using heat maps to indicate crowd density and movement patterns. Advanced analytics are applied to identify congestion and support scenario analysis. As a pilot, the system demonstrates the potential to improve situational awareness, enhance safety, and optimise space utilisation, although no evidence confirms long-term operational deployment.

title: Chatbot - Municipality of Senigallia

source_description: Municipal administrations often receive a high volume of general enquiries from citizens, many of which concern routine information that can be handled more efficiently through digital self-service than through direct staff intervention. In Senigallia, this use case centres on a chatbot introduced on the municipality’s official website to respond to general citizen enquiries and provide a more accessible first point of contact. The objective is to improve responsiveness, make common information easier to obtain, and reduce the burden on municipal staff dealing with repetitive requests. The implementation uses a website-based conversational interface embedded in the municipality’s digital environment. At a conceptual level, the chatbot serves as a front-end guidance tool that interprets user questions and returns prepared answers or directions to the relevant information, helping citizens navigate services without needing to identify the correct office in advance. The solution is intended for general enquiries rather than personalised case handling, making it suitable for high-volume, low-complexity interactions. The impact includes faster access to municipal information, improved user convenience, and a more efficient allocation of staff effort. It also supports the wider digitalisation of citizen services by creating a scalable channel for routine communication and by improving the municipality’s ability to handle enquiries outside traditional contact methods. The official municipal site confirms the broader digital service context in which this type of web-based support is delivered.

title: Chatbot - Municipality of Treviso

The objective is to offer a more immediate and accessible way to obtain basic information, reduce dependence on manual front-office responses, and simplify the first step in accessing public services. The implementation uses a web-based chatbot integrated into the municipality’s digital environment. At a conceptual level, the solution provides a conversational entry point through which users can ask general questions and receive guidance towards the relevant information or service area, rather than navigating the full structure of the administration unaided. As with many municipal chatbots, its role is likely focused on standard information and routine support rather than on complex individual casework. The impact includes faster access to general municipal information, improved convenience for users, and more efficient handling of repetitive enquiries. It also supports service scalability by extending the municipality’s digital front door and strengthening the consistency of first-line communication across online channels. The municipality’s current digital portal and service structure show the wider administrative context into which this kind of citizen-support functionality fits.

The chatbot retrieves instructions from official knowledge bases and directs users to relevant forms and webpages. If unable to resolve an enquiry, Hubot generates a service request to student advisers or transfers the user to a live chat when available. By automating responses to common questions, the system reduces response times and supports continuous access to essential academic information. The deployment enhances efficiency in student services while preserving human interaction for complex or individual cases requiring personalised support.

title: Blockchain to increase security in foreign aid disbursement in Demnark
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Aid disbursement in fragile or corruption-prone environments raises a longstanding public-administration challenge: how to ensure that funds reach the intended beneficiaries securely, transparently, and with reduced leakage. The Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs explored this issue in a Danida report that considered whether blockchain and cryptocurrency-based approaches could improve traceability and integrity in development assistance. The objective was to test whether distributed-ledger models might reduce corruption risks, strengthen beneficiary access to funds, and modernise aid-delivery mechanisms. At a conceptual level, the proposed implementation would use blockchain-based transaction records and digital-payment mechanisms to track disbursements and potentially route aid more directly to end recipients. The case is therefore framed as an innovation concept for development cooperation rather than a conventional administrative service. The expected impact lies in stronger transparency, improved traceability of transfers, and greater confidence that funds can reach intended beneficiaries safely, while also contributing to wider debate on how emerging financial technologies might support more accountable aid delivery.

title: Chatbot Publio - EU Publication Office

source_description: Publio is the virtual assistant of the Publications Office of the European Union, designed to help users navigate extensive digital repositories of EU documents and institutional information. Researchers, professionals and citizens often require support in locating specific publications, organisations or officials within complex databases. Publio provides a multilingual conversational interface available in English, French and Spanish. The assistant uses natural language processing to interpret user queries and match them with indexed content across the Publications Office website. It retrieves document references, organisational details and relevant links, guiding users through search results without requiring advanced search skills. By facilitating structured interaction with large document repositories, Publio improves discoverability, reduces search time and enhances accessibility to EU information resources. The solution supports transparency and public access to official documentation through scalable digital assistance.

title: AI for analysing investigative data in Austria

source_description: Austrian authorities implemented advanced analytics tools to process and analyse large volumes of investigative data in complex cases involving fraud and financial crime. Investigators face challenges in extracting relevant information from heterogeneous datasets, including documents, communication records and transactional data. The solution applies machine-learning techniques for classification, metadata extraction and relationship detection across structured and unstructured data sources. Natural language processing and pattern recognition models identify semantic correlations, trace information origins and map communication flows. Visual analytics components generate network graphs and fraud pattern visualisations without requiring custom coding for each case. The system integrates into investigative workflows, supporting analysts in identifying hidden links and prioritising lines of enquiry. By automating data processing and pattern detection, the solution accelerates investigations, improves analytical depth and enhances evidence-based decision-making while maintaining human oversight in prosecutorial actions.

title: Court of Ravenna - digital signature
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Courts increasingly need secure, traceable ways to authenticate documents and preserve confidence in judicial records as procedures become more digital. In Ravenna, this project was described as an enhancement to the court’s existing IT system through the addition of a digital-signature solution and data storage on a private or consortium permissioned blockchain. The objective is to improve the integrity, authenticity, and traceability of judicial documents while fitting within an existing court information environment rather than replacing it. The implementation, as described in European public-sector blockchain case documentation, combines digital-signature workflows with permissioned distributed-ledger storage so that document events and validation information can be recorded in a controlled blockchain environment. At a conceptual level, the solution is aimed at strengthening evidential trust and process reliability in a judicial setting where records must remain tamper-evident and attributable. The anticipated impact is stronger document security, better traceability, and a more robust digital workflow for judicial administration, especially where authenticity and auditability are essential to procedural trust.

title: Lawyers' blockchain-based register in Malta
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Malta sought to modernise the management of lawyers’ warrants by replacing fragmented and paper-based records with a transparent, reliable and accessible digital register. Previously, verifying whether a lawyer was duly authorised required consultation of administrative records that were not fully interoperable or publicly searchable, limiting transparency for citizens and institutions. The pilot project aimed to create the first electronic register of lawyers in Malta, enabling government, legal professionals and the public to access consistent and up-to-date warrant information. A blockchain-based architecture was implemented to store and synchronise records in an immutable and decentralised ledger. The system was initially developed as a private blockchain to ensure controlled participation, with a design allowing future migration to a public blockchain for non-personal data such as names and warrant status. Cryptographic mechanisms ensure data integrity and traceability of updates, while authorised entities can validate entries in real time. The initiative enhances trust in legal services, reduces administrative verification time and strengthens transparency, providing a scalable digital infrastructure for professional registers.

title: DigiAkkoord - blockchain-based approval processes for government activities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Government approval workflows often involve many actors, documents, and hand-offs, making it difficult to ensure transparency, trust, and efficient coordination across the full chain of transactions and authorisations. DigiAkkoord was presented as a project using a permissioned blockchain to support workflow, transaction, and document approval processes in government. The objective is to increase trust, improve traceability, and streamline approval procedures where multiple parties need a shared record of validated process steps. The implementation, as described in European public-sector blockchain material, uses a permissioned distributed ledger to record approval events and workflow progression in a controlled environment suitable for public administration. At a conceptual level, the approach seeks to create a shared, tamper-evident process layer across approvals, rather than relying only on fragmented back-office records. The expected impact is greater transparency, stronger process integrity, and better efficiency in document approval and inter-organisational workflow handling, particularly where several public actors need a common, trusted view of procedural progress.

title: Known Traveller Digital Identity Pilot Project (KTDI)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: International travel requires repeated identity checks across airlines, airports, border agencies, and other actors, and this fragmented process can create friction, redundancy, and security inefficiencies. KTDI was developed to explore whether a trusted, decentralised digital identity could simplify this end-to-end journey by allowing traveller data to be shared and reused in a more secure and interoperable way. The objective was to test a traveller-centric identity model that could support smoother airport passage, reduce repeated manual checks, and improve trust between public and private travel actors. The implementation combined decentralised identity concepts with technologies such as biometrics, blockchain, mobile devices, and cryptography. In the pilot model, travellers would upload information in advance, and the system would use biometric recognition, including facial-image matching, to support functions such as automated check-in and airport gate passage. The impact of the project lies in demonstrating a possible future travel architecture and informing best practices for digital identity in cross-border mobility, with potential benefits in speed, convenience, interoperability, and more efficient use of identity data across the travel ecosystem.

title: Digital receipt processing at the Swedish Tax Agency

The solution tested distributed ledger concepts and secure data-sharing mechanisms to record transaction data in a tamper-resistant format, enabling authorised stakeholders to access verified information directly. Digital receipts are standardised, stored electronically and linked to accounting systems, reducing manual input and reconciliation tasks. The approach supports automated validation and traceability of transactions, facilitating more efficient audits and compliance checks. Expected benefits include reduced administrative costs for businesses, improved accuracy of tax reporting and enhanced transparency in financial flows, contributing to a more efficient and trustworthy taxation ecosystem.

title: FAKE-ID - Video analysis using AI to detect false and manipulated identities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The rapid spread of manipulated video content poses growing risks to trust, security, and democratic processes, as falsified or synthetic identities can be used for fraud, disinformation, and impersonation. Public authorities, media organisations, and digital platforms require reliable methods to detect such content at scale. The FAKE-ID project addresses this challenge by supporting the identification of falsified and manipulated identities in video material. Stakeholders include security agencies, technology providers, and institutions responsible for safeguarding digital integrity. The objective is to improve the detection of deep-fake videos and manipulated identity representations to strengthen trust in digital media. The solution develops advanced video analysis methods that examine visual and temporal inconsistencies in facial movements, expressions, and image artefacts. Trained models analyse video streams to identify signs of synthetic manipulation under varying recording conditions. The project establishes robust evaluation frameworks and datasets to ensure reliability. The impact includes improved detection accuracy of manipulated videos, reduced risk of identity fraud, and enhanced resilience against disinformation. FAKE-ID contributes to safer digital environments and supports the development of trustworthy media verification technologies.

title: Environmental monitoring of sea trouts with AI

The solution uses underwater cameras to capture video sequences, which are analysed using deep learning models trained to distinguish sea trout from other objects such as leaves or different fish species. The system processes visual data to detect and count individuals in real time or through batch analysis. This approach enables scalable and consistent monitoring across different locations. The system demonstrates potential to improve efficiency and data quality in environmental monitoring.

title: Differentiation of ship types on satellite radar images

The solution applies deep learning techniques to satellite radar images, enabling the identification and differentiation of ship types based on their radar signatures. These models are trained on labelled datasets and integrated into earth observation systems used by authorities and organisations. The system supports applications such as maritime surveillance, environmental monitoring, and enforcement. The project demonstrates potential to improve detection accuracy and operational efficiency, although full deployment details remain limited.

title: CONMAR - studying contaminated sites with underwater drones

The solution combines underwater drones with data integration and analysis tools to collect and process information on contaminated areas. Machine learning techniques are applied to analyse sensor and imaging data, supporting detection and assessment of hazards. The project also integrates existing datasets from research organisations, government agencies, and industry to create a comprehensive knowledge base. As a research and development initiative, the project is ongoing, with expected outcomes including improved environmental monitoring, informed policy decisions, and enhanced remediation strategies.

title: MoCaB - Reliable mobile support for caring relatives

Sensors capture relevant data from everyday activities to recognise situations and trigger appropriate recommendations, while maintaining an overview of the condition of the person receiving care. Intelligent algorithms process contextual information to provide timely prompts, educational resources and links to support services. Data protection and privacy safeguards are integrated into the architecture to ensure secure handling of sensitive health information. The solution seeks to reduce stress, improve care quality and strengthen carers’ resilience, offering scalable digital support that complements existing health and social care services.

title: Data4UrbanMobility - Development of application-driven tools for mobility information
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban mobility planning increasingly depends on integrating diverse data sources to understand traffic dynamics, user behaviour, and emerging mobility services. Data4UrbanMobility addresses this gap by developing application-driven tools that support data-informed mobility decisions. Stakeholders include urban administrations, mobility service providers, and citizens. The objective is to enable evidence-based planning, development, and operation of innovative mobility services. The solution integrates regional and historical mobility data from multiple sources and applies data extraction, integration, and analytical methods to create event-based views of mobility systems. Predictive models generate forecasts of traffic behaviour and system development, while tailored analytics tools support specific use cases. All components are brought together in a unified platform. The project improves situational awareness, supports proactive planning, and enables more efficient mobility services. It contributes to better-coordinated transport systems, improved user experience, and data-driven urban mobility governance.

title: AI^2 - (Aphid identification through artificial intelligence)

The solution uses machine learning and deep learning techniques to analyse images from airborne insect traps, identifying and classifying species such as aphids. Neural networks are trained on labelled datasets to recognise visual patterns and quantify insect populations. The system enables rapid and standardised analysis across multiple locations. As an ongoing development project, it demonstrates potential to significantly reduce processing time, improve consistency of results, and support early detection and management of invasive pests.

title: AI-TEST-FIELD – Semantic Environment Perception for Intelligent Sensor Systems
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: Safe operation of autonomous and assisted systems requires reliable perception of complex and changing environments. Current sensor systems often struggle to deliver consistent and certifiable outputs under varying conditions, limiting deployment in safety-critical contexts. AI-TEST-FIELD addresses this challenge by developing the foundations for robust, trustworthy sensor systems. Stakeholders include industrial developers, certification bodies, and operators of automated systems. The objective is to enable sensor technologies that provide stable and interpretable guidance for action across diverse environmental scenarios. The solution focuses on semantic environment perception using learning-based approaches that fuse data from multiple sensor modalities. Models are trained and tested in controlled environments to ensure robustness and consistency of outputs. Emphasis is placed on reproducibility, validation, and suitability for certification. The project delivers reference architectures, datasets, and testing methodologies. The impact includes increased reliability of intelligent sensor systems, improved safety assurance, and accelerated industrial adoption. AI-TEST-FIELD supports the deployment of trustworthy perception technologies in domains such as automated transport and industrial automation.

title: BETTER-WEEDS - AI to recognise weed species
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Julius Kühn Institute Federal Research Institute for Cultivated Plants (JKI)
source_description: Farmers must balance effective weed control to protect crop yields with growing societal and regulatory expectations for environmentally sustainable practices and biodiversity preservation. Conventional blanket herbicide application can harm beneficial plant species and increase ecological pressure. The BETTER-WEEDS project aims to develop cost-effective and time-efficient tools to record weed species and densities at field level, enabling differentiated management strategies. High-resolution field imagery and sensor data are analysed using machine learning-based image recognition models trained to distinguish between competitive and non-competitive weed species. The system generates area-specific maps indicating species distribution, density and ecological traits, which are then used to design tailored management plans. By identifying competitively weak or rare species with ecosystem benefits, the approach supports selective interventions rather than uniform treatment. The solution enhances operational efficiency, reduces input costs and promotes biodiversity-friendly farming practices. It contributes to improved sustainability and ecological performance while maintaining agricultural productivity through data-driven, site-specific decision support.

title: BoniKI - plant-specific assessment by autonomous systems
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: FZI Research Center for Computer Science
source_description: Assessing plant health, growth, and pest infestation is essential for sustainable agriculture, yet manual inspection is labour-intensive, costly, and dependent on expert judgement. Sampling-based methods provide limited resolution and may miss early signs of stress or disease. The BoniKI project addresses this challenge by enabling automated, plant-level assessment at scale. Stakeholders include farmers, agronomists, and agricultural service providers. The objective is to increase efficiency, transparency, and sustainability in crop monitoring and decision-making. The solution uses unmanned aerial systems to capture high-resolution imagery of agricultural fields. Data processing pipelines separate crops from weeds and background elements, followed by automated assessment of plant condition using trained analytical models. The system derives relevant scoring parameters and generates actionable insights for field management. The project aims to deliver an integrated, user-friendly solution for routine agricultural use. The impact includes reduced monitoring costs, earlier detection of stress or infestation, and more targeted interventions. BoniKI supports precision agriculture and contributes to more resource-efficient and resilient farming practices.

title: DynAWI - Predict extreme weather situations reliably and region-specific
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Julius Kühn Institute Federal Research Institute for Cultivated Plants (JKI)
source_description: Extreme weather events increasingly threaten agricultural productivity, yet timely and region-specific assessment tools are often lacking. Farmers and public authorities need reliable indicators to anticipate yield impacts and support risk management decisions. DynAWI addresses this need by developing a process chain for monitoring and analysing extreme weather conditions in agriculture. Stakeholders include agricultural agencies, researchers, and private sector users of environmental data. The objective is to provide scalable, regionally differentiated indicators that link weather extremes to crop yield outcomes. The solution integrates geospatial datasets within a scalable data infrastructure and applies analytical models to derive dynamic agricultural weather indicators. These indicators capture the intensity, duration, and spatial extent of extreme conditions relevant to crop development. Outputs are made available through standardised interfaces for integration into national and European data spaces. The project improves early warning capabilities, supports impact assessment, and enhances planning under climate uncertainty. DynAWI contributes to more resilient agricultural systems and informed adaptation strategies in the face of climate change.

title: FreshRegio – making the quality of fruit and vegetables measurable
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Quality assessment of fruit and vegetables is critical for regional agriculture and efficient food supply chains, yet traditional inspection methods are often subjective, labour-intensive, and limited in predictive power. FreshRegio addresses this challenge by enabling objective, data-driven evaluation of product quality and shelf life. Stakeholders include farmers, distributors, retailers, and consumers. The objective is to strengthen regional food systems by improving transparency and reducing waste. The solution combines near-infrared sensor technology with analytical models to assess internal quality attributes of produce non-destructively. Measurements are processed to predict freshness and remaining shelf life, supporting informed decisions along the supply chain. The system simplifies quality control processes and enables consistent evaluation across batches. The impact includes reduced food waste, improved product differentiation, and stronger trust between producers and buyers. FreshRegio contributes to more sustainable food systems by aligning quality measurement with regional agricultural value creation.

title: HEB KI– Artificial intelligence searches to improve barley variety
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, Institute for Agricultural and Nutritional Sciences
source_description: HEB KI focuses on improving plant-breeding decisions by increasing genetic diversity in barley while reducing the resources required to identify promising crosses. Barley breeders need to introduce useful traits from wild or diverse accessions, but selecting which genetic material should be crossed and tested can be expensive, slow and uncertain. The project therefore aims to expand the HEB-25 barley population towards HEX-35 by selecting suitable accessions from a wild barley population in a more targeted way. The implementation further develops and adapts the XSeedScore algorithm for barley, combining genome and phenome datasets to prioritise breeding material with the highest expected value. Conceptually, the system links genetic information, observed plant traits and predictive scoring so that breeders can focus field trials and controlled experiments on the most promising candidates. This enables a more systematic approach to introducing novel alleles into barley breeding. The expected impact is faster and more resource-efficient variety development, improved breeding diversity and better selection of lines with agronomically useful traits. By reducing trial-and-error, HEB KI can help breeders use limited experimental capacity more effectively while strengthening the resilience and adaptability of future barley varieties.

title: KAMI – Dairy cow respiratory rate monitoring
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Leibniz Institute for Agricultural Engineering and Bioeconomy
source_description: KAMI responds to the need for earlier and less intrusive detection of illness and stress in dairy herds. Respiratory rate is a sensitive indicator of animal condition, reflecting heat stress, fear, pain and possible disease processes, but conventional observation requires visual counting of flank movements, which is labour-intensive, intermittent and may disturb the animals. Farmers therefore need a practical monitoring approach that can identify individual changes before welfare problems or financial losses escalate. The KAMI project develops a prototype for automated, image-based and contact-free detection of respiration in dairy cows. Its implementation combines camera-based monitoring with data-driven analysis and links breathing information with other parameters such as milk quality, movement, feeding and rumination behaviour. Conceptually, the system captures visual signals, estimates individual respiratory patterns and translates deviations into actionable warnings. The expected impact is improved animal welfare, earlier response to health or stress events, reduced medication use, better use of performance potential and lower economic losses for farms. By enabling continuous and objective monitoring without attaching devices to animals, KAMI offers a more scalable route to precision livestock management and more informed herd-care decisions.

title: KIBREED – using AI to grow site-adapted plants
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Leibniz Institute for Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Research (IPK)
source_description: KIBREED addresses the difficulty of breeding crop varieties that remain productive under local environmental conditions and future climate pressures. Farmers require varieties that combine yield stability, resistance and regional adaptation, but plant-breeding decisions depend on many interacting factors, including genetic background, plant traits and environmental conditions. The project uses wheat as a model crop because of its global importance and the availability of rich breeding datasets. Its objective is to make advanced algorithms usable for selecting locally adapted varieties and strengthening agricultural resilience. The implementation integrates genotyping, phenotyping and envirotyping data through deep-learning procedures, allowing models to analyse genetic information, observed plant characteristics and environmental context together rather than separately. Conceptually, KIBREED combines multi-source biological and environmental data to improve prediction of which varieties are likely to perform well in specific locations. The expected impact is better variety selection, improved yield security, more efficient breeding processes and stronger sustainability in agriculture. By supporting the development of resistant and locally adapted crops, the project can contribute to food security, healthier nutrition and more ecological land use. Its value lies in connecting molecular, field and environmental evidence in a single predictive breeding framework.

title: KIdetect - Reliable detection of weed growth centers
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: KIdetect tackles a practical limitation in mechanical weed control: as weed infestation becomes denser, it becomes harder for camera-guided hoeing systems to identify where tools should act precisely. Farmers and agricultural-technology providers need methods that can target weeds selectively without damaging crops and without relying excessively on herbicides. The project therefore aims to detect weeds reliably and in real time, with particular attention to the spatial location of their growth centres, which may be hidden by leaves or neighbouring plants. The implementation uses image processing supported by artificial intelligence together with multispectral camera systems in the visible and short-wave infrared ranges. It also creates 3D reconstructions of weed areas so that growth centres can be located even under heavy infestation. Testing takes place in a controlled vertical-farming stand, where weed image data can be generated under adjustable lighting, wavelength and camera conditions before being processed with specialised methods. The expected impact is more accurate activation of hoeing devices, improved selective weed removal, lower chemical input and more reliable smart-farming equipment. By linking multispectral sensing, 3D reconstruction and real-time interpretation, KIdetect strengthens precision agriculture’s ability to manage weeds sustainably.

title: AI-iREPro - using AI to manage viticulture more efficiently
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Julius Kühn Institute Federal Research Institute for Cultivated Plants (JKI)
source_description: AI-iREPro addresses the difficulty of forecasting grape yield accurately at vineyard level. Winegrowers and wineries must plan labour, harvest logistics, transport capacity, cellar use and quality management before the final yield is known, while weather conditions, variety characteristics and annual growth patterns can cause large fluctuations. The project therefore develops digital tools for vineyard-specific yield prediction, helping producers make earlier and better-founded operational decisions. Its implementation combines modern sensor technology with intelligent forecast models, using historical yield data, environmental information, field observations and sensor-derived indicators. At a conceptual level, the system extracts features from vineyard data, models yield-related relationships and generates forecasts that can support both vineyard management and winery planning. It also contributes to grapevine breeding by increasing the efficiency and objectivity of yield assessment. The expected impact includes improved harvest planning, reduced waiting times during grape delivery, better utilisation of presses and fermentation tanks, stronger quality management and lower financial risk for winegrowers. The project produced high-performance prototypes and digital methods that can underpin new services for vineyard and winery management. Its broader value lies in making viticulture more predictable, data-supported and resilient to annual variability.

title: KINERA – Optimizing production processes in agriculture
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: University of Hohenheim, Department of Artificial Intelligence in Agricultural Engineering
source_description: KINERA focuses on improving the efficiency and resilience of agricultural production processes that rely on complex machinery. Modern high-tech farm equipment can be difficult to operate at its full potential, creating a performance gap between technical capability and practical field use. Farmers also face disruptions from weather, logistics, machine availability and other external factors, making operational reliability increasingly important. KINERA therefore aims to support both conventional tractor-implement combinations and autonomous field robots, especially in crop establishment, through better process coordination and adaptive decision support. The implementation integrates agricultural machinery into operational edge infrastructure and cross-company cloud infrastructure, allowing machines to use local data, communicate with other machines and draw on shared information. At a conceptual level, process data are analysed to provide setting support, self-adaptation and decision recommendations for farmers. The expected impact is higher machine utilisation, improved area performance, more efficient logistics and greater resilience of digitalised agricultural businesses under disruptive conditions. By combining field experiments, simulation and connected infrastructure, KINERA seeks to make advanced farm technology easier to operate and more reliable. Its business value lies in turning complex machines into coordinated, data-supported production systems that can sustain productivity while reducing inefficiency.

title: AI-Breeding – find the highest yielding strains quickly and accurately
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Justus Liebig University Giessen, Professorship for Plant Breeding
source_description: AI-Breeding addresses the need to accelerate plant breeding by identifying high-performing lines and hybrids more quickly, accurately and resource-efficiently. Breeders working on important crops must combine yield potential, environmental adaptation and genetic diversity, but conventional selection can require long cycles of field testing and complex interpretation of genome, phenotype and environmental information. The project brings together practical plant breeding, breeding theory, quantitative genetics, genome analysis and advanced prediction methods to improve selection success across different breeding stages. Its implementation develops and applies machine-learning methods for pattern recognition in highly complex genome, phenome and environmental datasets. These methods are used to predict performance-related and environment-dependent genetic structures in breeding populations, extracting data attributes that can support better decisions on combination ability, line selection and hybrid performance. Conceptually, the approach links genomic markers, phenotypic observations, environmental conditions and predictive modelling to support “big data”-based breeding. The expected impact is faster breeding progress, improved yield security and better use of large-scale biological datasets in practical breeding programmes. Rather than relying only on traditional trial-and-error selection, the project aims to make breeding decisions more evidence-driven and scalable, helping to develop crop varieties that remain productive under changing environmental conditions.

title: KRIBL - affordable robotics also for small businesses
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: University of Lübeck, Institute for Robotics and Cognitive Systems
source_description: KRIBL focuses on making agricultural robotics accessible to smaller farms, which may otherwise be excluded from advanced automation because current systems are often large, specialised and expensive. Organic and biological farming businesses need practical tools for monitoring, plant care and field operations, but the economics of highly automated machines tend to favour very large agricultural enterprises. The project therefore aims to develop compact, affordable and flexible robot systems that can be used in everyday agricultural settings without requiring excessive investment. Its implementation combines small mobile robots, sensor technology, field robotics, modular software and intelligent data processing to support precision tasks in biological agriculture. Conceptually, KRIBL explores how lightweight robotic platforms can perceive their environment, support crop and weed-related operations, and operate as part of a broader digital farming workflow. Recent project material also links KRIBL to containerised AI deployment and reproducible weed-detection workflows on mobile agricultural robots, showing how software modularity can improve maintainability and transferability. The expected impact is broader access to automation, reduced labour intensity, more precise field operations and improved competitiveness for smaller farms. By lowering the economic and technical threshold for robotics, KRIBL contributes to a more inclusive model of agricultural innovation rather than concentrating advanced technology only in large-scale operations.

title: mAInZaun – the intelligent fence that recognizes animal species
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Justus Liebig University Giessen, Institute for Animal Breeding and Domestic Animal Genetics
source_description: mAInZaun was created to improve herd protection in areas where grazing animals are exposed to predators, especially wolves. Livestock owners need effective protection, but conventional electric fences and deterrent systems may lose effectiveness when predators become habituated, and remote grazing sites often lack permanent infrastructure. The project therefore developed a modular, autonomous and intelligent protective fence able to recognise approaching animals and trigger appropriate deterrence measures. Its implementation combines sensors, local power supply, animal-species recognition and dynamic deterrent responses, including stimuli such as ultrasonic signals. The system is designed not only for integration into existing fences, but also for independent deployment in temporary safety zones, for example near roads, settlements, railways, hiking trails, tourist areas or landscape-conservation projects. Conceptually, mAInZaun links edge sensing, classification of approaching animals, automated alerting and context-specific deterrence. It can also integrate police, road-maintenance departments or railway authorities into the alert system where relevant. The expected impact is stronger protection of grazing animals, reduced economic losses for farmers, improved coexistence between livestock farming and wildlife conservation, and more flexible management of temporary risk areas. By reacting dynamically rather than relying on static barriers, the system seeks to maintain deterrent effectiveness over time.

title: Movi-Q – optimize visual quality controls intelligently
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: DIL German Institute for Food Technologye
source_description: Movi-Q addresses a persistent quality-control problem in the food industry: fruit, vegetables, meat and other natural products vary widely in appearance, while defects are often detected manually by visual inspection. This makes sorting resource-intensive, inconsistent and prone to human error, and it can contribute to unnecessary rejection of usable products or failure to remove defective material. The project, led through the DIL German Institute of Food Technologies in Quakenbrück, aimed to develop a mobile and modular prototype for visual quality detection that could be used by companies in different food-processing contexts. Its implementation combines image acquisition hardware, machine-vision methods, artificial intelligence and software modules able to identify defects and trigger downstream processes such as sorting. A key component is the creation of high-quality training data through a mobile image-capture unit that can be adapted to different products and application scenarios. Conceptually, Movi-Q links visual sensing, defect classification, process integration and practical guidelines for food companies. The expected impact is more reliable quality assurance, lower reject rates, reduced manual sorting effort and better resource efficiency. By demonstrating transferable application scenarios, the project helps food businesses assess where automated visual inspection can improve productivity, quality standards and sustainability.

title: RoLand - how to achieve low-cost automation in agriculture
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence
source_description: RoLand develops a low-cost robotic harvesting system for fruit production, with particular attention to open-field strawberry harvesting. Fruit farms face labour shortages, rising production costs and time-sensitive harvesting windows, while robotic harvesting solutions have historically been concentrated in greenhouse environments or designed at cost levels unsuitable for smaller farms. The project therefore aims to create a semi-autonomous mobile system that can harvest fruit independently under real outdoor conditions, including changing weather, uneven terrain and variable crop presentation. Its implementation combines a mobile robotic platform, fruit-recognition systems, an end-effector for harvesting, autonomous navigation and perception technologies. DFKI’s SHIVAA robot, developed in the project, is designed to identify ripe fruit and pick it in open fields, with the possibility of scaling work output through multiple compact units. Conceptually, the system integrates visual detection, motion planning, manipulation and field mobility in a platform intended to remain economically viable for smaller producers. The expected impact is reduced dependence on seasonal labour, improved supply security, more flexible harvesting by time of day and stronger competitiveness for regional fruit production. Public demonstrations indicate that RoLand has moved from design towards field-tested prototype capability, including public strawberry-field testing.

title: WeedAI – promoting non-chemical weed control in sugar beet cultivation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn, Faculty of Agriculture, Institute for Agricultural Engineering
source_description: WeedAI responds to the growing need for reliable evaluation of non-chemical weed-control technologies, especially in sugar beet cultivation. Mechanical and robotic weeding methods are increasingly important as agriculture seeks to reduce herbicide use, but assessing their effectiveness usually requires extensive field trials and labour-intensive manual ground-truthing. This slows innovation and makes it harder to compare tools, field conditions and weed-management strategies. The project therefore develops automated methods to assess how well weeding operations remove weeds while preserving crops. Its implementation is based on deep-learning methods for plant recognition, using image data to detect and distinguish sugar beet plants and weeds, estimate their position and size, and evaluate treatment outcomes. Conceptually, WeedAI links field imagery, crop-weed segmentation, object recognition and performance assessment into a system that can quantify both crop and weed responses after intervention. The expected impact is faster evaluation of weeding systems, lower trial costs, better evidence for non-chemical crop protection and more rapid development of sustainable weed-control technologies. Project outputs indicate that the system can make precise predictions on individual sugar beet and weed positions, even in fields unknown to the model, provided that high-quality drone and camera data are available.

title: AI-based tool for monitoring cultivated land in Lithuania using Copernicus Sentinel data
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Agricultural paying agencies must verify compliance with Common Agricultural Policy requirements across very large areas, but manual field inspections can be slow, expensive and disruptive for both administrations and farmers. Lithuania’s National Paying Agency worked with Geomatrix UAB and iTree Lietuva to use Copernicus Sentinel data and machine-learning methods for monitoring farm activities and land use during the agricultural season. The objective was to assess subsidy-related conditions more quickly and accurately, giving the agency an evidence base for checking claims and supporting more efficient distribution of CAP funds. The implementation developed SAGRIS, a Sentinel-based agriculture information service, and CAPCON, a CAP control service. These tools process Sentinel-1 and other satellite data to detect and classify land-cover and agricultural activity patterns relevant to subsidy control. At a conceptual level, the service combines Earth-observation imagery, pre-processing workflows, machine-learning classification, parcel-level monitoring and integration with paying-agency information systems. This allows checks to be carried out during the farming season rather than relying only on retrospective or sample-based inspections. The expected impact is faster compliance assessment, reduced need for on-site control, improved administrative efficiency and better targeting of follow-up checks. The case demonstrates how Copernicus data can be operationalised inside national agricultural administration, turning satellite observation into a practical tool for public funding governance.

title: AI for analysing incoming mail
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Courts receive large volumes of incoming documents through electronic communication channels, scanned files and structured or unstructured submissions, creating a substantial administrative burden before a case can even be processed. Austria’s Federal Ministry of Justice developed AI-supported incoming-mail analysis to automate routing and classification tasks that would otherwise require court staff to read, interpret and manually allocate documents. The implementation analyses input documents, extracts metadata, identifies file numbers or other identifiers and recognises procedure types where no file number is available. It can also support intelligent allocation, file creation, assignment to the appropriate case or organisational unit, categorisation of scanned documents and preparation of proposed document descriptions or names. At a conceptual level, the system combines document classification, metadata extraction, entity or identifier recognition and workflow-routing rules. Its role is administrative: it turns incoming material into structured, actionable information for court systems and staff. The expected impact is faster handling of incoming judicial documents, fewer manual routing steps, improved consistency in document registration and reduced administrative workload in court offices. This type of tool is particularly useful in digital justice environments because delays or errors at the intake stage can affect all later case-management processes. The Austrian justice framework presents such AI applications as support functions that do not replace or influence judicial decisions.

title: AI for digital file management
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Digital court files require consistent structure, accurate metadata and reliable separation of documents, particularly when legacy paper files are scanned in bulk or when incoming documents arrive in different formats. Austria’s Federal Ministry of Justice developed AI-supported digital file management to ensure that unstructured documents are processed uniformly and that metadata can be adopted automatically. The operational problem is that court staff must often separate individual documents from scanned batches, identify first pages, classify attachments and maintain a coherent digital file structure. The implementation supports detection of first pages after bulk scanning, separation of submissions and supplements, document description, classification, harmonisation of document titles and intelligent creation of file structures, including tables of contents. It can also support object-oriented views, such as grouping documents related to a particular party. At a conceptual level, the system combines document segmentation, classification, metadata extraction, title harmonisation and digital-case-file structuring. The expected impact is more consistent electronic files, lower manual effort, easier navigation for judges and court staff, and stronger quality in the transition from paper-based to digital workflows. In legal administration, this matters because document organisation directly affects searchability, procedural efficiency and the ability of professionals to understand the case file quickly. The system is best understood as a support layer for digital file management, not as a tool that interprets legal merits or influences case outcomes.

title: AI for anonymisation of court decisions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Publishing court decisions improves transparency, legal certainty and access to case law, but it requires careful protection of personal data, addresses, parties and other identifying information. Austria’s Federal Ministry of Justice developed AI-supported anonymisation to prepare court decisions for publication in the Legal Information System. The operational challenge is that manual anonymisation is time-consuming and must preserve the comprehensibility of the case while removing or masking information that could identify individuals or organisations. The implementation analyses decision documents, extracts metadata, recognises natural and legal persons, detects addresses and identifies the roles of actors within the case. It then supports anonymisation of personal data while aiming to maintain the legal and factual intelligibility of the decision. At a conceptual level, the system combines named-entity recognition, role detection, document analysis, metadata extraction and rule-guided anonymisation. Its expected impact is reduced manual workload, faster publication of case law, more consistent anonymisation and wider access to legally relevant decisions. The tool is especially valuable where courts produce large volumes of decisions and where publication depends on balancing transparency with privacy obligations. OECD material describes Austria’s Federal Ministry of Justice as implementing a comprehensive project to automate anonymisation of court decisions, with goals including efficiency, reduced manual effort and broader publication of anonymised decisions.

title: Ion - the world's first government advisor
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Governments increasingly seek tools to understand public concerns in real time, but turning large volumes of citizen expression into reliable policy insight raises questions about transparency, representativeness and accountability. Romania’s ION was launched in March 2023 as an artificial-intelligence government adviser, presented as a system that could collect and synthesise citizens’ opinions and concerns for public officials. The objective was to enhance citizen-government communication by receiving direct submissions through an official platform and monitoring public online content to identify issues that mattered to the population. The implementation combined an AI-branded public interface with sentiment or topic-analysis ambitions, aiming to generate a real-time snapshot of public mood and communicate it to government decision-makers. At a conceptual level, the system was intended to aggregate citizen messages, detect recurrent topics, summarise concerns and support public officials with a non-traditional channel of feedback. Its expected impact was more responsive government, broader participation and faster awareness of social priorities. However, the project soon faced criticism over transparency, data collection and unclear evidence of meaningful functionality. Later reporting indicated that ION had been reduced to a simple informational chatbot, and subsequent accounts suggested that it was removed from government premises after administrative change. The case is therefore best understood as an ambitious but short-lived experiment in AI-mediated civic listening.

title: Chatbot - LineaMadrid
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Large city administrations receive many routine questions from residents and visitors about municipal services, procedures, appointments, local taxes, transport, events and city information. Línea Madrid’s virtual assistant provides a conversational support channel on Madrid City Council’s institutional website, helping users find answers without needing to call, visit a service office or navigate complex web pages. The operational objective is to improve access to municipal information by offering immediate guidance through an online chat available across the council’s web environment. The implementation uses a chatbot or virtual-assistant interface that supports navigation, answers common questions and can connect users with personalised assistance where appropriate. At a conceptual level, the assistant interprets the user’s question, retrieves relevant municipal information and directs the user towards the appropriate service page, procedure or support channel. The expected impact is faster access to public information, reduced pressure on physical and telephone help centres, improved service availability outside office-based interaction and a more user-friendly digital front door for Madrid’s municipal administration. The value of the system lies in navigation and orientation: it helps citizens locate the right process or information but does not replace formal administrative decisions or case-specific assessment. The City Council describes the service as a 24/7 online chat available from all pages of the institutional website.

title: Virtual helsinki - digital twin of the city of Helsinki
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cities increasingly use three-dimensional models to communicate urban change, support planning, visualise public assets and make local environments accessible in new ways. Virtual Helsinki applies this logic to a digital twin of the Finnish capital, creating an interactive 3D environment that can support tourism, shopping, training, simulations, concerts, public engagement and virtual participation. The initiative transforms selected parts of Helsinki into immersive spaces where users can visit places remotely and experience the city through a virtual interface. The implementation combines 3D city modelling, game-engine environments, virtual-reality design and digital storytelling. At a conceptual level, real urban locations are reconstructed as navigable digital scenes, enabling users to interact with city spaces in ways that are not possible through maps or photographs alone. The expected impact is broader access to Helsinki’s urban and cultural environment, new formats for tourism and events, improved engagement with urban development and experimentation with virtual citizenship concepts. The use case is significant because it connects the technical digital-twin agenda with public-facing experience design: a 3D model is not only an analytical planning tool, but also a platform for services, participation and communication. Helsinki’s broader 3D city models are part of the city’s digital-twin infrastructure, combining open data, information technology and updating urban information.

title: Classification and automatic sorting of CEMs at the Italian National Institute for Social Security (INPS)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Certified email is one of the main channels through which Italian citizens communicate with INPS, including for pensions, disability, unemployment and other welfare matters. The volume and sensitivity of these messages create a major operational burden because staff must read each message and any attachments, understand the subject, identify the relevant service area and forward the case to the appropriate office. INPS developed an in-house AI system to classify and sort certified emails automatically while keeping data within INPS data centres to meet confidentiality and GDPR requirements. The implementation initially experimented with open-source GPT-2 and then moved to BERT, using transformer-based natural language processing to classify email content and attachments. At a conceptual level, the model analyses unstructured citizen communications, assigns them to relevant welfare-service categories and supports routing to the correct territorial or functional unit. Its expected impact is faster communication handling, reduced manual triage, shorter response times and major savings in administrative working days. The system also demonstrates the value of keeping sensitive public-service AI inside institutional infrastructure when the data include personal and welfare-related information. INPS reports that the project was included in IRCAI’s global Top 10 AI projects supporting the Sustainable Development Goals, and public technology-watch material describes the growth in certified emails from 3 million in 2019 to more than 6 million in 2023.

title: "INPS risponde"" - Optimised management of web requests to Customer Service"
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Digital customer-service channels can become inefficient when many requests must be handled twice: first by a front-line operator and then again by a specialist office. INPS Risponde receives large numbers of online requests from citizens seeking clarification on services, rules and individual procedures. The operational challenge is to distinguish simple requests that can be handled at first level from complex ones that require second-level intervention, thereby reducing unnecessary handovers and response delays.
