The objective of this initiative is to enhance the quality of digital services by identifying navigation patterns, friction points and content gaps experienced by users. The implementation focuses on the design and development of machine learning algorithms that analyse anonymous web navigation data, including page transitions, interaction sequences and usage frequency. These models generate aggregated insights and recommendations for improving information architecture, content clarity and interface design, while fully respecting data protection and anonymity requirements. The system is intended to integrate with existing web management processes and support continuous improvement cycles. Expected impacts include more user-centred digital services, reduced abandonment of online procedures and improved accessibility for different user groups. Qualitative outcomes include better-informed design decisions, increased trust in digital public services and a scalable analytics framework applicable across large public administration websites.

source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

The system introduces a centralised and automated calendar that integrates information on medical personnel, facilities and availability. Advanced scheduling logic applies prioritisation rules and planning-and-control principles to dynamically assign appointments. The platform also includes automated notification mechanisms, informing citizens of scheduled visits and enabling rescheduling through INPS digital channels. Anticipated benefits include more efficient use of medical resources, improved appointment adherence, reduced administrative workload and a more transparent and predictable experience for citizens undergoing medical examinations.

title: Implementation of AI chatbot to guide the compilation of UNIEMENS flows

It draws on regulatory texts, procedural rules and validation logic to answer questions, explain obligations and highlight common errors. The chatbot is intended to integrate with existing INPS digital services, offering real-time support without replacing formal controls. Expected impacts include improved data quality, fewer rejected submissions, reduced support requests to INPS offices and greater transparency for employers navigating complex reporting obligations.

title: Chatbot to support workers applying for a wage supplement support
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Accessing information on wage-supplementation benefits can be difficult for workers and beneficiaries when rules, procedures, and eligibility conditions are spread across multiple digital channels and documents. This use case addresses that problem by providing a conversational support service for people seeking information on Wage Supplementation Fund benefits, with the aim of making access to relevant guidance faster, simpler, and more convenient. The objective is to improve user experience, reduce the time needed to find the right information, and make support available continuously beyond traditional service hours. The implementation takes the form of a chatbot integrated into the relevant service environment, able to use data associated with the people interacting with it, particularly recipients of CIG, in order to provide more appropriate responses. The system is also described as incorporating artificial-intelligence and machine-learning functions so that it can learn from past interactions, user behaviour, and correction of previous errors. The impact includes quicker access to benefit-related information, greater service availability through 24-hour support, and improved user satisfaction. It also creates a more scalable front-line assistance channel by reducing dependence on manual information handling for repetitive benefit enquiries.

title: Customer Relations Management system evolution to support decision-making
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Large public administrations interact with millions of users across multiple channels, often resulting in fragmented data and limited strategic insight. INPS initiated the evolution of its Customer Relationship Management system to consolidate user interactions and support more proactive service delivery. Stakeholders include INPS service departments, case officers, management and citizens. The objective is to harmonise data collection across channels, improve monitoring and enable personalised services. The project focuses on integrating all interaction channels into a unified operational CRM platform, complemented by the gradual development of an analytical CRM layer. This includes reporting dashboards, monitoring tools and segmentation models that classify users based on needs, behaviours and life events. The approach follows an iterative and incremental development model, with early releases delivered to operational offices. Expected impacts include improved decision-making, more consistent service provision, better anticipation of user needs and long-term efficiency gains through data-driven service design.

title: Balancing tourist capacity via blockchain in Formentera
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Tourist destinations with fragile ecosystems face increasing pressure to balance economic benefits from tourism with the protection of natural resources and quality of life for residents. Formentera, a small island with limited carrying capacity, needed a mechanism to better distribute visitor flows and reduce overcrowding in highly frequented areas, while engaging both tourists and residents in sustainable behaviour. This use case addresses that challenge by involving the island council, tourism authorities, local businesses, residents, and visitors, with the objective of promoting more balanced tourism patterns and sustainable use of space. The solution is implemented through a decentralised incentive system based on blockchain and smart contracts, which integrates real-time data from the island’s Tourism Intelligence System via oracles. Based on current capacity and congestion levels, incentives are dynamically issued to encourage visits to less crowded areas or specific activities, such as museums, events, or public transport routes, with transactions recorded on the Alastria network. The approach improves transparency, traceability, and trust in capacity management, enables data-driven redistribution of tourist flows, and enhances visitor experience while protecting sensitive areas. It supports sustainable tourism, reduces pressure on overcrowded sites, and provides a scalable governance model for managing destination carrying capacity.

title: Secure visitor management with blockchain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Monastery of Santa María La Real
source_description: Managing visitor flows in heritage and tourism destinations requires balancing safety, capacity control and preservation of cultural assets. This solution introduces a digital monitoring system to improve visitor management while certifying implemented security measures. The platform integrates telematic capacity control, real-time flow monitoring and environmental indicators such as air quality into a unified management dashboard. Blockchain technology is used to certify compliance with safety protocols and provide tamper-resistant records of operational measures. Information panels and alert mechanisms support on-site staff in preventing overcrowding and mitigating risk situations. Analytical modules generate indicators on visitor behaviour, impact and asset conditions, enabling evidence-based management decisions. The system enhances transparency for authorities and stakeholders while improving safety and visitor experience. By combining monitoring, certification and analytics, the solution supports sustainable tourism management and scalable governance of high-demand heritage sites.

title: Innovation and Digital Transition Service – Mobility and Urban Regeneration Project
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Effective urban regeneration depends on accurate understanding of mobility patterns and congestion dynamics across public and private transport networks. This project aims to develop predictive models capable of forecasting traffic peaks on main urban thoroughfares using integrated transport data. Data from bus circulation systems and roadside sensors are aggregated into a central analytical platform. Machine learning models analyse temporal patterns, traffic density and mobility behaviour to anticipate congestion events in advance. The system supports scenario analysis and informs traffic management interventions or infrastructure planning decisions. By integrating heterogeneous data sources, the model enhances situational awareness for urban planners and mobility managers. Expected outcomes include reduced congestion, improved public transport coordination and more efficient urban space utilisation. The initiative supports data-driven urban regeneration strategies that align mobility planning with sustainability and quality-of-life objectives.

title: Improving trackside worker safety
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Railway maintenance activities expose trackside workers to significant safety risks, particularly when operating near live rail environments. Network Rail is exploring geofencing technology as an additional safeguard to reinforce existing safety protocols. Wearable devices connected to mobile and cloud-based systems use GPS, RFID, Wi-Fi or cellular signals to define virtual boundaries around safe working zones. When a worker approaches or crosses a predefined geofence, the device issues an immediate alert, providing a real-time warning. The system operates alongside established procedures rather than replacing them, adding an extra layer of situational awareness. Data from the platform can also support post-incident analysis and safety planning. The solution aims to reduce accidental incursions into hazardous areas, enhance compliance with safe working limits and improve overall workforce protection. By leveraging location-based technologies, the initiative strengthens preventative safety culture within rail infrastructure operations.

title: Metaverse-based centre for exibitions in Valencia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cultural venues increasingly seek new formats that can attract audiences through immersive and interactive experiences rather than relying solely on traditional exhibition models. In Valencia, Bombas Gens Centre d’Arts Digitals was established as a large-scale digital arts venue designed to host immersive exhibitions using extended reality and related technologies across more than 2,500 square metres of space. The objective is to expand cultural engagement through experimental exhibition formats, create new visitor experiences, and position the venue as a leading site for digital and immersive arts. The implementation combines multiple technological layers, including extended reality, virtual reality, augmented reality, holography, large-format projection, and AI-enabled interactive elements, within four exhibition halls equipped with more than 45 projectors and described by the venue as containing Europe’s largest metaverse room. At a conceptual level, the centre integrates immersive hardware, digital content production, and interactive exhibition design to support large-scale cultural experiences that blend art and emerging technologies. The impact includes richer visitor engagement, broader possibilities for experimental programming, and a scalable platform for immersive cultural production. It also creates strategic value by strengthening Valencia’s profile in digital arts and experience-based exhibition design.

title: Autonomous Road Inspection for Bizkaia Regional Council
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Maintaining road safety requires frequent inspection of infrastructure such as signs, markings, barriers, and work zones, yet manual inspections are costly, infrequent, and expose personnel to risk. The Bizkaia Regional Council faced the challenge of improving road asset monitoring while increasing coverage and responsiveness. The Autonomous Road Inspector addresses this need by enabling continuous, automated assessment of road conditions. Stakeholders include regional authorities, infrastructure operators, and road users. The objective is to enhance safety, optimise maintenance, and support proactive road management. The solution deploys vehicle-mounted sensing systems that capture visual and environmental data during normal traffic operations. Automated analysis identifies damaged or missing signs, degraded markings, unsafe barriers, construction zone conditions, and hazards such as slippery surfaces. Predictive functions support early detection of deterioration and risk. The impact includes more frequent inspections, reduced operational costs, improved worker safety, and faster response to hazards. The pilot demonstrates how automated monitoring can modernise road management, improve public safety, and deliver scalable benefits for regional infrastructure authorities.

title: Public AI Challenge - Hub Innovazione Trentino - Overtourism detection
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Overtourism places pressure on environmentally sensitive areas, leading to congestion, ecological damage, and reduced quality of life for residents and visitors. The Province of Trento sought tools to anticipate tourism peaks and manage mobility proactively. This use case addresses the need for data-driven forecasting to support sustainable tourism management. Stakeholders include regional authorities, transport planners, local communities, and visitors. The objective is to detect and predict overcrowding in specific areas and support timely mitigation measures. The solution integrates heterogeneous datasets, including road traffic data, mobile network activity, and weather information, to estimate visitor volumes and characterise tourism patterns. Data preparation and harmonisation enable effective analysis, while predictive models identify days and locations at high risk of overtourism. The impact includes improved forecasting accuracy, better traffic management decisions, and reduced environmental pressure on sensitive areas. The initiative supports evidence-based tourism governance and demonstrates how advanced analytics can help balance economic activity with environmental protection and quality of life.

title: Municipality of Messina pilots the Recycleye robot to select garbage and improve reciclying
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Messinaservizi Bene Comune partnered with Recycleye to deploy an AI-managed robotic waste sorting system at the Pace sorting centre, the first of its kind in Sicily. Municipal waste management requires precise separation of materials to improve recycling rates and reduce landfill reliance. The Recycleye robot combines computer vision with robotic manipulation to identify and pick specific material classes from waste streams. Trained visual recognition models classify items based on material characteristics, while automated robotic arms perform continuous sorting operations around the clock. The system integrates into existing processing lines, increasing throughput and consistency. By enhancing sorting granularity and operational continuity, the robot improves material recovery rates, reduces labour-intensive tasks and optimises cost efficiency. The deployment strengthens circular economy practices and supports data-driven waste management within the municipality.

title: ETIBLOGG – Local Energy Trading in Green Microgrids
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The transition to decentralised energy systems requires new market mechanisms that allow small-scale producers and consumers to trade electricity efficiently without relying on central intermediaries. In local microgrids, existing market structures often make trading small quantities of energy economically unattractive. The ETIBLOGG project addresses this challenge by enabling local electricity trading among prosumers and consumers. Stakeholders include households, small businesses, and local energy communities. The objective is to make peer-to-peer energy trading economically viable and support decentralised renewable generation. The solution establishes a digital trading framework for microgrids, enabling automated settlement of small energy transactions and transparent coordination between participants. Trading rules and transactions are recorded in a shared digital infrastructure, reducing transaction costs and administrative complexity. The impact includes increased local consumption of renewable energy, improved economic returns for small producers, and reduced reliance on centralised energy markets. ETIBLOGG contributes to more resilient, decentralised energy systems and supports the development of local green grids as part of the future energy landscape.

title: Pebbles – Peer-to-Peer Electricity Trading in Local Microgrids
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Local energy systems with high shares of renewable generation face regulatory and market barriers that limit direct trading between small producers and consumers. In regions such as Wildpoldsried, where many households already generate renewable electricity, surplus energy is often fed into central grids instead of being exchanged locally. The Pebbles project addresses this challenge by designing a sustainable and economically viable local energy market within a microgrid. Stakeholders include households, small and medium-sized producers, prosumers, local companies, and distribution network operators. The objective is to establish a replicable model for regional electricity markets that strengthens local value creation and energy autonomy. The solution implements a regional digital trading platform that enables peer-to-peer exchange of green electricity within the microgrid. Transactions between participants are securely recorded and settled using distributed ledger mechanisms, ensuring transparency and trust without central intermediaries. Market rules support flexible pricing and real-time balancing of supply and demand. The project demonstrates improved local consumption of renewable energy, increased economic participation of small actors, and reduced grid dependency. Pebbles delivers a scalable blueprint for decentralised energy markets, supporting the transition towards resilient, community-based energy systems.

title: Decide Madrid - Citizen Participation and Machine Learning
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Large-scale online participation platforms can suffer from information overload: thousands of proposals and comments make it difficult for citizens to find relevant initiatives, build consensus, and understand debates, while public officials struggle to synthesise input into actionable insights. Research using Madrid’s Decide Madrid platform (built on Consul) examined how to improve discovery, deliberation, and responsiveness so that participation remains meaningful as volume grows. Stakeholders include citizens submitting proposals and comments, city administrators responsible for engagement and policy feedback, and platform maintainers seeking scalable moderation and analysis tools, with the objective of improving user experience and the quality of participation outcomes. The approach applies natural language processing and machine learning to suggest proposals users may wish to support, cluster citizens by shared interests, summarise comment threads, and assist with drafting or aggregating responses and refined proposals. This is achieved by processing the text corpus of proposals and comments, extracting semantic representations, and using similarity, clustering, and summarisation techniques that can be integrated into the platform interface as recommender, navigation, and analyst-support features. Reported evaluations indicate these methods can address participation barriers by reducing noise, improving navigability, and helping users and administrators focus on salient themes, thereby increasing the practicality of digital democracy tools without requiring proportional increases in staffing.

title: AI in Evaluating Citizens’ Contributions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public administrations increasingly rely on citizen participation processes, yet analysing large volumes of written contributions remains time-consuming and inconsistent. This research-based pilot explores how natural language processing can support public decision-making by structuring and analysing citizen input. Stakeholders include public authorities, policymakers and citizens participating in consultations. The objective is to improve the efficiency, fairness and depth of analysis of public contributions while maintaining transparency. The approach applies computational text analysis to identify duplicate submissions, cluster contributions by topic and extract deeper insights such as arguments, sentiment and stakeholder perspectives. Large collections of textual submissions serve as the primary data source, enabling scalable analysis that complements human review rather than replacing it. The results show improved capacity to handle large-scale participation processes, reduced administrative burden and more evidence-based policy insights. While exploratory, the pilot highlights how advanced language analysis can strengthen democratic participation by ensuring that citizen voices are systematically considered in policymaking processes.

title: Mission KI - Museum-exhibition services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Deutsches Museum von Meistwerken der Naturwissenschaft und Technik (AdöR)
source_description: The German Museum Bonn initiated the Mission KI project to enhance public understanding of artificial intelligence through interactive exhibition installations. As part of a thematic reorientation of its AI forum, the museum sought to demonstrate the functioning of artificial neural networks in an accessible manner. The project involves acquiring and developing multi-part media demonstrations illustrating how machine learning systems improve performance through data-driven training. Interactive installations visualise single-layer and multi-layer neural network processes, translating complex computational concepts into engaging educational experiences. The exhibition integrates audiovisual displays and interactive components that allow visitors to observe learning mechanisms and model behaviour. By combining scientific content with immersive media, the project strengthens science communication and digital literacy. It enables visitors to grasp abstract AI principles through experiential learning while maintaining academic rigour and educational clarity.

title: Controlling and balancing public power grids with AI: TenneT usecase
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: TenneT initiated a Dynamic Purchasing System to renew and enhance IT systems supporting control and balancing of high-voltage electricity grids between 2021 and 2031. The energy transition increases variability in power generation and requires advanced forecasting and grid management tools. The tender focuses on expertise in EMS/SCADA systems, algorithm development and tool design to support real-time grid operations. Data analytics and optimisation algorithms are integrated into control platforms to monitor system stability, forecast imbalances and coordinate balancing actions. Enhanced analytical capabilities improve responsiveness to fluctuations in supply and demand, supporting reliable grid performance. By modernising operational technology and incorporating advanced modelling tools, TenneT strengthens grid resilience and efficiency while facilitating integration of renewable energy sources.

title: Computer-related and AI services for CATE project
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Flemish Audit Authority launched the CATE project to modernise audit processes through advanced data analytics and automation. Traditional auditing relies on periodic manual sampling, which may limit timeliness and coverage. The project seeks a private partner to develop innovative approaches using artificial intelligence, machine learning and data mining to assess management and control systems. The solution aims to integrate continuous data monitoring, anomaly detection and predictive analytics into audit workflows. By processing large datasets from administrative systems, the platform supports early identification of irregularities and evidence-based conclusions. The collaboration framework fosters co-development of digital auditing methodologies. The initiative enhances efficiency, improves risk detection and strengthens oversight capabilities within public financial management.

title: DZSF – Object Detection and Classification for Automated Rail Driving
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Higher levels of rail automation require technical systems to assume tasks traditionally performed by drivers, including continuous monitoring of the track environment to detect and classify objects that may affect safety or operations. Variability in weather, lighting and surrounding infrastructure creates significant challenges for reliable perception. Stakeholders include railway operators, safety authorities, technology developers and research institutions. The objective is to advance automated rail driving by improving object detection and classification capabilities based on robust data foundations. The approach integrates multi-sensor data, such as cameras, radar and LiDAR, and applies machine learning models trained on extensive, curated datasets to identify and categorise relevant objects in track and surrounding areas. Open databases are further developed to support training, validation and benchmarking of algorithms. The system architecture is designed to interface with onboard control and decision-support modules. Expected impacts include enhanced operational safety, increased network capacity through higher automation levels and improved standardisation of perception datasets across the rail sector.

title: Machine Learning in Simulation for Imaging Improvement
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Bundesamt für Ausrüstung, Informationstechnik und Nutzung der Bundeswehr
source_description: Military training simulations require high levels of visual realism to ensure effective preparation, yet conventional rendering methods may lack photorealistic detail, particularly across different spectral ranges. Stakeholders include defence research bodies, simulation software providers and training institutions. The objective is to enhance image quality and realism in simulation environments used by the Federal Armed Forces. The project applies machine learning techniques to improve visual outputs in both visible and infrared spectra. Neural network models are trained to enhance RGB imagery and synthetically generate infrared representations, enabling more accurate thermal simulations. These models are integrated into simulation platforms such as Virtual Battlespace 4, where they augment rendering pipelines and improve scene fidelity. Expected impacts include more immersive and realistic training environments, better representation of operational conditions and increased effectiveness of simulation-based exercises.

title: Water Management with AI in Seville
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: EMPRESA METROPOLITANA DE ABASTECIMIENTO Y SANEAMIENTO DE AGUAS DE SEVILLA, S.A. (EMASESA)
source_description: Managing the integral water cycle in large urban areas involves monitoring consumption, distribution networks and environmental conditions across diverse data sources. Fragmented systems can limit predictive capabilities and operational efficiency. Stakeholders include the municipal water utility (EMASESA), city authorities and residents. The objective is to establish a unified analytical platform to support data-driven water management. The solution comprises a cloud-based big data and machine learning platform built around a central data lake that ingests, standardises and classifies data from smart meters, operational systems and third-party sources. Analytical models support use cases such as demand forecasting, anomaly detection and network optimisation. The platform integrates with existing operational systems and enables scalable deployment of new analytics applications. Expected impacts include improved resource efficiency, reduced water losses, enhanced service reliability and data-driven planning for sustainable urban water management.

title: Digital procedures based on blockchain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public administrations must ensure transparency, traceability and trust in digital procedures, particularly for legally sensitive communications such as official notifications. Traditional digital systems may lack immutable audit trails accessible to citizens. Stakeholders include the regional government of Valencia, citizens, businesses and public IT entities. The objective is to strengthen transparency and trust in electronic administrative processes. The solution records each stage of electronic notifications on a blockchain-based registry, certified by the regional public technology company ISTEC using the BlockchainFUE platform. Each notification’s lifecycle—from issuance to expiration—is immutably logged, and citizens can access corresponding verification documents through their digital folders. The system integrates with existing e-government platforms while adding a distributed ledger layer to ensure integrity and traceability. Expected impacts include enhanced citizen confidence, improved evidentiary robustness in case of disputes and strengthened digital identity and governance frameworks.

title: DivAirCity – Citizen Engagement for Cleaner Air through Incentivisation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Improving urban air quality requires not only policy measures but also active participation from citizens in adopting greener daily behaviours. However, individuals often lack clear feedback, motivation, and incentives to change habits related to mobility, energy use, and lifestyle. DivAirCity addresses this gap by empowering citizens to actively contribute to cleaner urban environments. Stakeholders include residents, local authorities, environmental organisations, and urban communities. The objective is to promote sustainable behaviour and collective action to improve air quality at city level. The solution provides a decentralised digital application that allows users to monitor air quality, access educational content, and receive personalised incentives for environmentally friendly actions. Transparent recording of actions and rewards builds trust and accountability within the community. The platform fosters engagement by linking individual behaviour to shared environmental outcomes. The project increases public awareness, motivates behavioural change, and supports data-driven environmental governance. DivAirCity demonstrates how citizen-centric digital platforms can strengthen community involvement, improve environmental outcomes, and contribute to healthier, more sustainable cities.

title: Web3 Quadratic Funding for Public Infrastructure
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal budgeting can be vulnerable to low engagement and lobbying dynamics that prioritise narrow interests over broadly supported local needs. The City of Split piloted a quadratic funding approach to help allocate resources to community projects in a way that reflects both breadth of support and intensity of preference, aiming to create a fairer and more transparent process for deciding which neighbourhood improvements receive funding. Stakeholders include the city administration, residents, civic groups proposing projects, and ecosystem partners supporting funding rounds, with the objective of increasing participation and producing funding allocations that better match collective preferences. Launched in September 2023, the initiative builds on open-source quadratic funding infrastructure used in other public-goods contexts, using blockchain-based tools to manage project submissions, record contributions, and calculate allocations according to quadratic funding rules (where many small contributions can outweigh a few large ones). Smart contracts and public ledgers support auditable accounting, configurable round parameters, and transparent disbursement logic, while administrative tooling helps the city run rounds and verify outcomes. The pilot demonstrates how verifiable transactions and rule-based allocation can reduce administrative friction, strengthen trust, and encourage wider civic participation, with a model that could be replicated by other municipalities if governance and legal considerations are addressed.

title: PORO an LLM for Finland
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: European public institutions, researchers and companies increasingly rely on language technologies, yet most large language models are developed outside Europe and inadequately support smaller European languages. The PORO initiative was launched to strengthen European digital sovereignty by providing open, high-quality language models trained on European data. Led by startup SiloGen, in collaboration with the University of Turku and HPLT, the project aims to democratise access to advanced language models while ensuring alignment with European values, research openness and linguistic diversity. The first PORO model, a 34-billion-parameter system, focuses on English, Finnish and programming code, with plans to expand coverage to all official European languages. The models are trained using large multilingual datasets and high-performance computing resources from the LUMI supercomputer, combined with a dedicated software stack optimised for large-scale training. Open-source checkpoints enable reuse, fine-tuning and transparent evaluation by public and private actors. The initiative delivers strategic benefits by reducing dependency on non-European providers, improving language coverage for public services and research, and enabling innovation across sectors. PORO establishes a scalable foundation for sovereign European language infrastructure.

title: Modello Italia, the first Italian Foundational Large Language Model
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: European public administrations and enterprises require advanced language technologies aligned with national regulatory, privacy and security standards. Dependence on externally developed models may raise concerns regarding data sovereignty and compliance. Stakeholders include iGenius, Cineca, public administrations, regulated industries and research institutions. The objective is to develop a foundational large language model tailored to Italian and European institutional and business contexts. The model is designed as a large-scale neural network trained on several trillion tokens, with a focus on secure, compliant and domain-relevant applications in sectors such as healthcare, finance and national security. It will be released under an open-source licence and deployed within controlled infrastructures to meet high standards of privacy and governance. Expected impacts include strengthened technological sovereignty, improved access to generative language capabilities for public and private sectors and enhanced alignment with European regulatory frameworks.

title: Usage of Generative Ai in Spain justice
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Judicial systems face growing workloads, complex legal texts and increasing expectations for timely communication with citizens. In Spain, pilot initiatives have explored how generative language technologies can support judicial professionals without compromising legal safeguards. Stakeholders include courts, judicial staff, justice ministries and citizens seeking accessible legal information. The objective is to improve internal efficiency and external communication while maintaining judicial independence and accountability. The pilots, discussed within the framework of the European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ), focus on two main applications: assisting communication with citizens on legal procedures and summarising lengthy judicial documents. Language models are applied to structured legal texts and official documentation, with strict human oversight and defined usage boundaries. Systems are deployed as decision-support tools rather than automated decision-makers, ensuring that judges and clerks remain fully responsible for outcomes. Early findings indicate improved drafting speed, clearer public-facing explanations and reduced administrative burden for routine tasks. At the same time, limitations related to accuracy, bias and explainability are explicitly acknowledged. The pilots contribute to European best practices by clarifying where generative tools add value in justice systems and where legal or ethical constraints require careful restriction.

title: Vël'OK: Cycling for Survcoins
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Local authorities seek practical ways to encourage sustainable mobility and reduce carbon emissions while engaging citizens directly in climate action. In southern Luxembourg, nine municipalities operating the Vël’OK bicycle-sharing scheme introduced Survcoin, a digital reward mechanism designed to incentivise cycling. Stakeholders include municipal authorities, the Vël’OK operator CIGL and registered bicycle users. The objective is to promote low-emission transport while experimenting with alternative, community-based incentive models. Survcoin operates as a blockchain-based virtual currency awarded to users based on kilometres cycled between Vël’OK stations. After registering via a mobile application, users earn tokens automatically when using shared electric bicycles. Importantly, no location tracking is used; distance is calculated by extrapolating trips between stations, protecting user privacy. Blockchain infrastructure ensures transparent issuance, traceability and protection against manipulation. Users can redeem Survcoins within participating local circuits. The pilot demonstrates increased engagement with cycling services and raises awareness of sustainable mobility. It shows how distributed ledger technologies can support local climate objectives, foster behavioural change and enable trust-based incentive systems without intrusive data collection.

title: Generative Ai for German Public Administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: German public administrations face increasing demand for faster, clearer and more consistent public services amid staffing constraints and growing volumes of written communication. Federal, state and municipal authorities have begun piloting generative language technologies to support administrative tasks. Stakeholders include federal ministries, regional governments, municipalities and civil servants. The objective is to improve service quality and productivity while maintaining data protection, legal certainty and public trust. These pilots, often developed with startup Aleph Alpha, focus on tasks such as summarising documents, drafting internal notes, supporting correspondence and assisting research. Systems are deployed in controlled environments, typically hosted within Germany to meet sovereignty requirements. Outputs are reviewed by civil servants, and usage policies define acceptable applications. Early results show time savings in text-heavy processes, improved consistency in communication and better support for staff handling complex information. The pilots also surface organisational and skills-related requirements, informing broader digital transformation strategies. While not yet operational at scale, the initiatives provide valuable insights into how generative technologies can responsibly support public administration without automating decision-making or compromising accountability.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Topic Classification in the Domain of Public Affair
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: BiDA - Lab, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM)
source_description: Public affairs documents shape regulation, compliance and democratic oversight, yet their volume and complexity make systematic analysis challenging for both public institutions and private organisations. This research pilot investigates how large language models can support the classification of public affairs texts. Stakeholders include policymakers, regulatory analysts, companies and researchers. The objective is to improve transparency and accessibility by enabling structured analysis of large document collections. A dataset of over 33,000 public affairs documents, comprising more than 22.5 million tokens, was compiled using automated collection techniques. The task involves multi-label classification across up to 30 policy topics, reflecting the real-world complexity of regulatory texts. Several Spanish-language language models were evaluated under different configurations. The results demonstrate that domain-adapted models can achieve strong performance in classifying specialised documents, significantly reducing manual effort. The study highlights the potential of language models to support regulatory monitoring, policy analysis and corporate compliance. It also identifies challenges related to multilingual performance and domain specificity, providing a methodological foundation for future operational deployments in public affairs analysis.

title: Water monitoring using AI in South Tyrol
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Water utilities need better visibility over the condition and performance of distribution systems, yet smaller operators in particular often lack integrated tools for monitoring, maintenance planning, and rapid response to leaks, interruptions, or inefficient network behaviour. In South Tyrol, AiAqua addresses this challenge by offering a digital platform and app designed to help operators keep their water-distribution systems under closer and more continuous control. The objective is to improve the efficiency and sustainability of water-network management, reduce waste and service interruptions, and support better operational and investment decisions. The implementation combines a mobile application with a software-as-a-service platform that includes network-modelling functions, heuristic optimisation, machine learning, and data-analysis components. At a conceptual level, the system brings together monitoring data from measurement devices, alarms, images, notes, and network-configuration information to support day-to-day operational oversight and longer-term planning. The impact includes improved water saving, energy efficiency, and maintenance management, alongside better support for renovation planning and network resilience. It also creates value by giving small and medium-sized operators access to a more scalable and integrated water-management capability than they might otherwise be able to build independently.

title: Crypto Custody Services offered by a Federal bank
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Large regulated banks are increasingly under pressure to respond to institutional demand for digital-asset services while maintaining compliance, custody security, and integration with established banking operations. In Germany, Landesbank Baden-Württemberg entered into a partnership with Bitpanda to offer crypto custody and procurement services, primarily for corporate clients, reflecting an effort to extend traditional financial infrastructure into regulated digital-asset activity. The objective is to give clients access to secure storage and procurement of assets such as bitcoin and ether through a bank-grade environment, while allowing the bank to remain competitive in a market where digital-asset capabilities are becoming more relevant. The implementation relies on Bitpanda’s investment-as-a-service and custody infrastructure, with LBBW using the partner’s platform, licences, and technical stack as the basis for its own client-facing offering. At a conceptual level, the solution combines regulated banking relationships with specialised digital-asset infrastructure to create a compliant custody model for institutional use. The impact includes expanded service scope for corporate clients, stronger integration of digital assets into regulated finance, and a more scalable route for a large bank to enter crypto custody without building the full stack itself.

title: AI for improvement of AID systems
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Norwegian highway tunnels rely on Automatic Incident Detection (AID) systems to alert control centres to dangerous events, yet approximately 90 % of alerts are false positives due to misinterpretation of visual changes such as shadows or lighting variations. This pilot project investigates whether advanced image analysis techniques can improve detection accuracy while reusing existing technical infrastructure. Video feeds from tunnel cameras are processed using machine learning models trained to distinguish genuine incidents from benign visual variations. The enhanced system analyses contextual patterns rather than simple pixel changes, reducing misclassification. The pilot assessed integration with current monitoring equipment and evaluated performance during live operation. Results from the test period were highly positive, indicating a significant reduction in false alarms. Expected impacts include improved operational efficiency at traffic control centres, faster response to real incidents and enhanced tunnel safety through more reliable automated detection.

title: AI-based model to track the impact of the climate crisis on glacial resources
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Glaciers are critical natural resources and indicators of climate change, yet monitoring their evolution at scale remains complex, resource-intensive, and fragmented. Public authorities and research institutions require accurate, automated tools to track changes in glacial extent and structure in order to assess long-term impacts on water availability and environmental stability. This use case addresses these needs by supporting climate monitoring through systematic analysis of satellite imagery, involving public administrations, researchers, and environmental agencies. The objective is to improve the accuracy and timeliness of glacier monitoring to better understand the effects of the climate crisis. The solution is implemented through advanced image analysis models that process satellite data to automatically identify glacier boundaries, generate polygon representations, and detect equilibrium lines and their elevation. These models analyse temporal image sequences to identify changes in glacial mass and structure, integrating geospatial data into environmental monitoring systems. The approach significantly reduces manual analysis effort, improves consistency of measurements across regions, and enables large-scale, repeatable monitoring. It provides more reliable evidence for climate policy, supports water resource planning, and strengthens decision-making by delivering timely, data-driven insights into glacial retreat and its environmental consequences.

title: UrbanistAI, a generative AI platform for participatory planning and co-design: Jyväskylä use case
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Jyväskylä sought to revitalise public spaces in its city centre and reimagine the future design of the main high street through a more inclusive planning process. Traditional consultation methods can limit participation and make it difficult for residents to visualise proposed changes. To address this, the city organised a participatory workshop using a generative design platform to facilitate collaborative ideation. The platform employs generative image models to transform textual prompts and stakeholder inputs into visual urban design alternatives in real time. Participants explored multiple scenarios for streetscape improvements, public space functions and spatial layouts, supported by moderated discussion. The system enabled rapid iteration and comparison of design concepts, enhancing mutual understanding between citizens and planners. The workshop generated structured qualitative feedback and visual outputs to inform subsequent planning stages. The initiative strengthened civic engagement, improved transparency in early-stage design and demonstrated how interactive visual technologies can support more responsive and creative urban regeneration strategies.

title: UrbanistAI, a generative AI platform for participatory planning and co-design: Narva use case
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Narva aimed to make urban spaces more attractive and liveable for young people by actively involving students in shaping the city’s future development. Conventional planning processes often struggle to engage younger demographics effectively. To address this, a three-step participatory workshop series was organised using a generative design platform to stimulate co-creation. The system uses generative image models to translate participants’ ideas into alternative urban visions, enabling students to visualise proposals for public spaces and neighbourhood improvements. Workshops combined guided discussion with interactive scenario generation, allowing iterative refinement of concepts. Facilitators structured inputs to align creative exploration with planning constraints. The approach fostered dialogue, empowered youth participation and produced tangible visual material to support municipal decision-making. The initiative enhanced inclusivity in urban planning, strengthened community ownership of development processes and demonstrated the potential of digital co-design tools to engage underrepresented groups in shaping more vibrant and sustainable cities.

title: Basis of the digitised highway of the future: Highway Real-Time Digital Twin - Providentia++
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Managing increasingly complex traffic systems requires real-time situational awareness and predictive capabilities. Providentia++ expanded an existing test field by installing five additional networked stations equipped with over 75 sensors and high-performance computing units across motorway, rural and urban environments. Fibre optic and radio communication technologies connect decentralised processing units capable of handling approximately 20 Gbps of raw sensor data in real time. Advanced computer vision and data fusion algorithms detect anonymised traffic objects, track their trajectories and synchronise multi-modal sensor inputs to generate a dynamic digital twin of traffic conditions. The entire software chain—from object recognition to service interface distribution—was further developed and validated in live operation. Demonstrations showcased integration into virtual environments and driver assistance applications for predictive driving and precise congestion forecasting. The system enhances traffic monitoring accuracy, supports value-added mobility services and provides a scalable foundation for intelligent transport infrastructure and future automated driving ecosystems.

title: BUILDCHAIN - BUILDing knowledge book in the blockCHAIN distributed ledger - School buildings in Florence pilot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal authorities require comprehensive data to improve seismic resilience, safety and energy efficiency of public buildings. In Florence, a pilot within the BUILDCHAIN project applies the Digital Building LogBook platform to a portfolio of school buildings. Existing data from structural surveys, material testing, seismic performance assessments and safety indices are logged within a decentralised knowledge graph supported by blockchain technology to ensure traceability and data integrity. Analytical tools process these datasets to identify priorities for seismic retrofitting and support intervention planning, including classroom management during works. The platform also integrates escape route management and safety monitoring features. For energy optimisation, smart meters, smart plugs and environmental sensors collect operational data to inform efficiency improvements with minimal intrusion. By consolidating structural and operational information, the pilot enhances evidence-based asset management, supports safer learning environments and enables strategic planning for resilience and sustainability in municipal school infrastructure.

title: BUILDCHAIN - Building knowledge book in the blockCHAIN distributed ledger - "Hospital Real"" in Granada pilot"
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cultural heritage buildings face increasing risks from ageing, pollution, and climate-related stress, while maintenance decisions are often reactive and fragmented across institutions. The BUILDCHAIN project addresses the need for proactive, data-driven management of public and heritage buildings. In the “Hospital Real” pilot in Granada, stakeholders include municipalities, heritage managers, engineers, and conservation experts. The objective is to improve long-term preservation through integrated monitoring, predictive maintenance, and transparent documentation. The solution develops a Digital Building Logbook that aggregates structural, environmental, and historical data using a distributed ledger to ensure integrity and traceability. Sensor data on variables such as moisture, pollution, and vibration are combined with predictive degradation models to forecast deterioration processes. Hybrid analytical models and advanced system representations simulate the impact of inspection and maintenance actions. The project enables proactive interventions, reduces long-term maintenance costs, and improves resilience of heritage assets. BUILDCHAIN delivers a scalable framework for managing public buildings, transforming maintenance from reactive repair to predictive, evidence-based stewardship.

title: BUILDCHAIN - BUILDing knowledge book in the blockCHAIN distributed ledger - Hospital building in Slovenia pilot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Designing technologically advanced healthcare facilities requires coordinated management of complex construction, cost and performance data. This BUILDCHAIN pilot applies the Digital Building LogBook methodology to a new hospital in Ljubljana, integrating Building Information Modelling (BIM) with decentralised data management. The project standardises priced bills of quantities (PBoQ) and links them to BIM components through a structured Model Breakdown Structure, ensuring traceability across design phases. The BIM model evolves from conceptual to detailed design and construction, synchronised with cost management processes. Structural health monitoring sensors are incorporated to account for sensitivity of medical equipment to minor displacements. Blockchain-based infrastructure supports secure logging of lifecycle data and interoperability between stakeholders. The approach enhances transparency, improves cost control and strengthens structural performance monitoring. The pilot demonstrates how integrated BIM and distributed ledger technologies can support efficient management of complex hospital infrastructure throughout its lifecycle.

title: BUILDCHAIN - BUILDing knowledge book in the blockCHAIN distributed ledger - Multi-storey timber buildings
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The structural behaviour of tall timber buildings remains an emerging field requiring enhanced monitoring and modelling approaches. This BUILDCHAIN pilot validates integration between the Digital Building LogBook, BIM models and a hybrid digital twin interface for three cross-laminated timber buildings in the United Kingdom and Norway. Experimental forced vibration test data are collected and processed to compute modal properties using established analytical tools. These structural performance indicators are logged within the BUILDCHAIN platform and linked to corresponding BIM elements. An application programming interface aggregates logged data to generate hybrid digital twins reflecting actual structural behaviour. Comparative analysis across the three buildings supports refinement of conceptual design procedures for timber structures. The pilot enhances traceability of structural performance data, supports evidence-based design improvements and demonstrates how decentralised data management combined with digital twins can strengthen confidence in innovative construction methods.

title: KSI blockchain-backed e-Residency in Estonia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Cross-border digital entrepreneurship depends on trust in how identities, records, and transactions are secured, especially when users rely on government-backed systems without being physically present in the country. Estonia’s e-Residency programme was built to enable entrepreneurs to interact with the state digitally, and its security model incorporates Keyless Signature Infrastructure to strengthen accountability, integrity, and trust in the underlying digital environment. The objective is to support secure digital business activity, protect data and transactions, and allow users to see how their personal information is used within government systems. The implementation combines digital identity infrastructure with blockchain-based integrity technologies, including KSI, which is used within Estonia’s wider digital state architecture to secure data exchanges, log files, and critical systems. At a conceptual level, the approach does not use blockchain as a public ledger for transactions, but as an integrity layer that helps ensure records are tamper-evident and auditable while preserving privacy. The impact includes stronger confidence in digital entrepreneurship, improved traceability of data use, and greater resilience of key state systems that support e-Residency. It also creates public value by reinforcing the credibility of a fully digital state-backed business environment.

title: Estonian National Gazette with KSI-blockchain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Centre of Registers and Information Systems (RIK)
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: When a country relies entirely on a digital legal gazette as the sole official publication of laws and regulations, the integrity of that platform becomes critical, because any unauthorised change could undermine legal certainty across the whole system. In Estonia, the electronic National Gazette has been the only official publication point for laws and regulations since 1 June 2010, creating a need for especially strong safeguards against tampering. The objective is to ensure the trustworthiness and verifiability of the legal record by detecting any unauthorised alteration to published content as quickly as possible. The implementation uses blockchain as one security layer within the Gazette’s protection model, integrating hash values of published XML laws and regulations together with hash values of digitally signed versions into a cryptographic chain. At a conceptual level, this enables regular validation of the information published on the portal and immediate notification if unauthorised changes occur. The impact includes stronger confidence in the authenticity of legal information, improved resilience of a critical public register, and a more robust mechanism for ongoing verification in a fully digital legal-publication environment. It also creates value by showing how blockchain can support trust and integrity in government records without being the entire application architecture.

title: EOGuard - KSI-blockchain to protect earth observation data
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Earth observation data is increasingly critical for environmental monitoring, security, and scientific research, yet its growing volume and complexity expose it to risks such as tampering, corruption, and loss of provenance. Space agencies, data providers, and downstream users require strong guarantees that data has not been altered throughout its lifecycle. The objective of EOGuard is to ensure trust, integrity, and traceability of Earth observation data without disrupting existing mission infrastructures. The solution is implemented using Guardtime’s Keyless Signature Infrastructure (KSI) blockchain, which generates cryptographic proofs of data integrity, sequence, and time across the entire data lifecycle. From data acquisition and processing to distribution and access, integrity proofs are automatically created and verified, independently of data storage formats or satellite missions. The system integrates with existing databases and workflows with minimal overhead, ensuring compatibility and scalability. EOGuard provides continuous assurance against accidental corruption, malicious interference, or security breaches. The impact is increased trust in Earth observation products, reduced risk for critical decision-making, and improved resilience of space data infrastructures. It enables secure reuse of data at scale, supports regulatory and scientific confidence, and delivers long-term value by safeguarding sensitive and mission-critical information.

title: Elering AS and WePower pilot project to test large scale tokenization of energy data on the blockchain in Estonia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Transparent and efficient energy markets require secure exchange of consumption and production data, yet traditional systems limit traceability and cross-platform integration. Elering AS and WePower conducted a pilot to test large-scale tokenisation of energy data using blockchain technology within Estonia’s national infrastructure. WePower integrated its smart contract-enabled green energy trading platform with Elering’s Estfeed data exchange system, creating a proof-of-concept for nation-scale tokenisation. Energy production and consumption data were recorded on a distributed ledger, enabling secure, tamper-resistant representation of energy units as digital tokens. Smart contracts facilitated automated settlement and transparent tracking of green energy transactions. The pilot demonstrated feasibility of blockchain-based data management at system-operator scale. Expected benefits include enhanced transparency, streamlined trading processes and strengthened support for renewable energy markets. The initiative illustrates how distributed ledger integration can modernise national energy data ecosystems and promote sustainable energy adoption.

title: CyberSEAS (Cybersecurity in the Electrical Power and Energy System) - Estonian pilot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Electrical power and energy systems rely on operational technology devices whose firmware updates are typically supplied by manufacturers, creating potential vulnerabilities if update sources or repositories are compromised. The Estonian CyberSEAS pilot aimed to safeguard the integrity of device configurations within Elektrilevi, Estonia’s largest distribution system operator, by ensuring that only authorised firmware could be installed. The solution introduced a centralised control mechanism requiring all firmware updates to be cryptographically signed and validated before deployment. Guardtime’s MIDA technology, based on KSI blockchain infrastructure, was implemented to provide tamper-evident verification and secure key management. The central management system automatically rejected unauthorised or unsigned firmware versions, preventing accidental or malicious installation. By embedding cryptographic assurance into update processes, the pilot strengthened configuration control and reduced cyber risk exposure. The initiative demonstrates how distributed ledger-based integrity mechanisms can enhance resilience of critical infrastructure, supporting secure and trustworthy operation of national energy systems.

title: CUREX - seCUre and pRivate hEalth data eXchange
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Healthcare providers increasingly exchange sensitive patient data across organisational boundaries, exposing them to cybersecurity and privacy risks. The CUREX project aimed to enable healthcare institutions to assess realistic cyber threats and implement mathematically optimised mitigation strategies tailored to specific applications. The project developed a decentralised architecture incorporating a private blockchain infrastructure to ensure integrity and traceability of risk assessment processes and inter-organisational data exchanges. Advanced risk modelling tools analyse vulnerabilities and recommend safeguard configurations aligned with regulatory and operational requirements. The blockchain layer records transactions and assessment outcomes in a tamper-resistant manner, enhancing accountability among stakeholders. Privacy-preserving mechanisms and secure communication protocols protect sensitive information throughout the lifecycle of data sharing. The solution supports informed decision-making regarding cybersecurity investments and compliance measures. By combining quantitative risk analysis with secure distributed infrastructure, CUREX enhances trust, resilience and data protection in cross-border healthcare ecosystems.

title: Madrid City Council uses blockchain to trace documents within the administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Large municipal administrations process high volumes of internal documents and procedures, and tracing the status and history of those records across departments can be difficult without stronger mechanisms for transparency and integrity. In Madrid, this use case was developed to make it easier to verify the progress of administrative procedures and trace documents safely within the City Council’s workflow. The objective is to improve transparency, strengthen confidence in document handling, and streamline technical and administrative processes inside the municipal administration. The implementation uses a blockchain-based document-traceability solution developed with iCommunity, designed to record and verify progress through administrative procedures in a secure and transparent manner. At a conceptual level, the solution applies distributed-ledger principles to document workflow events so that records of movement and status can be checked more reliably across the administration. The project description also refers to the use of iCommunity’s utility token in parts of the technical and administrative process, although the core public-sector value lies in the traceability and verification layer. The impact includes more fluid document management, stronger procedural transparency, and improved efficiency in administrative execution. It also creates value by giving a large city administration a more scalable way to monitor and verify document flows.

title: Swarmchestrate EU project - Parking occupancy magnetometer sensor threshold recalibration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban parking management relies on accurate real-time data, yet sensor-based systems are vulnerable to environmental changes that degrade accuracy and require costly manual recalibration. In particular, magnetometer-based parking sensors are affected by natural fluctuations in the Earth’s magnetic field. The Swarmchestrate project addresses this operational challenge by enabling self-organising sensor networks that adapt autonomously. Stakeholders include municipalities, mobility service providers, and urban infrastructure operators. The objective is to maintain reliable parking occupancy detection while reducing maintenance effort and downtime. The solution connects distributed parking sensors into a coordinated network where decentralised orchestration agents analyse collective magnetic flux data. When abnormal behaviour is detected, sensors automatically recalibrate and reconfigure themselves without manual intervention. Secure coordination and data integrity are ensured through decentralised trust mechanisms and privacy-preserving analytics. The project improves data accuracy, reduces operational costs, and increases system resilience. Swarmchestrate demonstrates how self-organising sensor swarms can support scalable, adaptive urban infrastructure management and provide insights into broader environmental phenomena.

title: Swarmchestrate EU project - Digital Twin of Natural Habitat
