source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Managing complex environmental systems requires distributed computing approaches capable of processing real-time data across heterogeneous infrastructures. Within the Swarmchestrate framework, a demonstrator explores the creation of a digital twin of natural habitats supported by decentralised orchestration mechanisms. Interdependent computational units, organised as self-organising swarms, are coordinated by distributed orchestration agents operating within a dynamic orchestration space. Blockchain-based trust mechanisms, self-sovereign identities and advanced cryptographic methods ensure secure interaction and persistent user engagement. Real-time environmental data streams update the virtual representation, creating a persistent and interactive metaverse environment reflecting physical ecosystem changes. Privacy-preserving analytics protect user and environmental data while enabling collaborative exploration. The demonstrator tests scalability, interoperability and resilience of decentralised orchestration across cloud-to-edge infrastructures. By integrating digital twin modelling with secure distributed intelligence, the project advances immersive environmental monitoring and lays groundwork for large-scale, real-time virtual representations of natural systems.

title: Titormos - the citizens assist chatbot in the Municipality of Agrinio
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Titormos addresses limited accessibility and inefficiencies in citizen engagement with municipal services, where requests could previously only be submitted via phone during restricted hours. This constrained responsiveness and excluded citizens with limited availability or access to traditional channels. The objective is to provide a more accessible, efficient, and inclusive interface for citizens to obtain information and submit service requests. The solution implements a conversational interface capable of handling structured requests and free-form queries, supported by natural language processing and integration with municipal service databases. It captures user inputs, generates request tickets, and provides confirmations, while also enabling future integration with administrative and HR systems for analytics and reporting. A voice-based interface extends accessibility to users without digital access. The impact includes improved accessibility, faster response times, and enhanced citizen satisfaction. It also enables better data collection, operational efficiency, and scalability of municipal services, supporting more responsive and data-informed governance.

title: Deliberations @ Scale: Large-scale high-engagement citizen participation with generative AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Municipal decision-making often struggles to engage large numbers of citizens in meaningful deliberation processes. The Common Ground mobile application, developed in Eindhoven through a consortium of start-ups and local institutions, aims to scale citizen consultations using digital facilitation. The platform integrates an automated moderation system that structures discussions, summarises viewpoints and prompts balanced exchanges among participants. Natural language processing models analyse contributions in real time, grouping similar arguments and identifying emerging themes. The application has been tested in three consultation processes, evaluating usability and engagement levels. By lowering participation barriers and structuring dialogue, the system supports inclusive and organised civic debate. Future plans include national expansion and integration of moderated consultations into formal decision-making workflows. The initiative demonstrates how digital facilitation tools can enhance democratic participation, increase transparency and strengthen evidence-based policymaking through large-scale, structured citizen input.

title: Predicting Image Quality Degradation in Digital Radiology
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Azienda Provinciale per i Servizi Sanitari di Trento (APSS)
source_description: Optimal design of medical x-ray imaging systems is essential for delivering maximum image quality while minimizing radiation risk to patients. The performances of imaging devices could degrade over time. For this reason, quality control (QC) programs are in place in the health systems to verify that the clinical image quality remains acceptable over the years guaranteeing the diagnostic capability. The Medical Physicists (MP) is the responsible for the QC program, ensuring high standards in medical diagnostics and maintaining the reliability and safety of medical imaging. Currently MPs perform constancy quality checks on Digital Radiography (DR) system, acquiring radiological images on phantoms and extracting specific information (e.g., non-uniformity). The results are then compared to baseline values and any deviation is evaluated. In such scenario the QC tests only provide a “snapshot” of the system performance at a specific moment over time, until the next inspection or service event not allowing to anticipate malfunctions. The objectives of the project are two-fold: automating processing of radiological image, conducting images analysis using in-house software macros and bash script and discovering trends on an ongoing basis with the aim of detecting and fixing DR system performance problems before clinical operations are affected. Performance characteristics of 19 DR systems from 5 manufacturers have been analyzed over 10 years of monthly and annually QC test. Study has been focused on non-uniformity test, based on 4 image parameters and their tolerances: Local signal non-uniformity, Global Signal non-uniformity, Local Signal to Noise Ratio non-uniformity, Global Signal to Noise Ratio non-uniformity. 1825 images were analyzed running the in-house software macros and bash script on each image to calculate the 4 baseline metrics. The second step was developing a predictive model for assessing the degradation state of DR system using the automatically images-processed database. The model has to predict the pass/no-pass label for each image. The building process involves leveraging the combined strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTMs) to analyze sequential radiological images from a images-processed database, grouping images into sequences for effective analysis akin to video sampling. By analyzing the sequential radiological images, this model aims to preemptively identify trends in equipment degradation. This capability is crucial for maintaining high standards in medical diagnostics, ensuring reliability and safety in medical imaging and patient care. The CNN architecture, based on ResNet-18, efficiently extracted spatial features, while the LSTM component, incorporating temporal data, was crucial in detecting patterns of degradation over time. Training and validation of the model were conducted on cloud based machine-learning platform, providing the necessary computational resources and scalability. Data augmentation strategies were implemented to balance the dataset, particularly addressing the scarcity of no-pass labels, thereby enhancing the model’s predictive capability. The model demonstrated a consistent training loss, indicating effective learning, and achieved a validation accuracy of 88.2% after 100 epochs, showcasing its ability to accurately classify the condition of DR systems. This level of accuracy reflects the model’s strong performance and its potential to generalize well to new data. In summary, in this project we proposed a new approach to QC test, starting from the availability of images and data stored through 10 years of activity. A predictive tool, based on AI-model was developed for non-uniformity QC test, with the result of decreasing the interval to detection of substandard performance. This type of approach, in which the primary goal is to preemptively identify trends in equipment degradation, can change the QC scenario.

title: MODUL-F: empowering public administration through low-code/no-code
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public administrations in Germany face persistent challenges in digitising internal procedures, often relying on fragmented, manual, or paper-based processes that slow service delivery and burden staff. Developing custom IT solutions is costly and time-consuming, especially for smaller authorities. MODUL-F addresses this challenge by enabling administrations at federal, state, and local levels to digitise internal specialist procedures quickly and consistently. The objective is to support end-to-end digital workflows in line with the Online Access Act (OZG) while reducing dependency on bespoke software development. MODUL-F is implemented as a cloud-based software-as-a-service platform using a low-code/no-code approach. Administrative staff can create digital procedures by assembling pre-programmed, reusable modules that represent common administrative functions and rules. These modules can be shared across organisations, ensuring standardisation and interoperability. The platform is rule-based, allowing consistent execution of procedures without complex programming. As a result, administrations can digitise processes faster, lower development and maintenance costs, and improve consistency across jurisdictions. MODUL-F increases scalability, empowers non-technical staff, and accelerates digital transformation, delivering measurable efficiency gains and supporting sustainable modernisation of public administration.

title: "Responsible use of AI""- pilot project to enhahnce environmental monitoring within the Province of Fryslân in collaboration with Rijks ICT Gilde and the Z-Inspection® Initiative"
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Province of Fryslân and Rijks ICT Gilde
source_description: Environmental monitoring is essential for biodiversity protection, water management and climate mitigation, yet integrating advanced analytics into public administration requires careful governance. The Province of Fryslân conducted a pilot between May 2022 and January 2023 to evaluate a deep learning model designed to map heathland grasslands using satellite imagery. In collaboration with Rijks ICT Gilde and the Z-Inspection® Initiative, the project assessed technical performance, ethical implications and governance considerations. The model processed Earth observation data to classify vegetation patterns within nature reserves, supporting preservation efforts. Evaluation frameworks examined transparency, accountability and potential biases in the algorithm’s outputs. The pilot contributed to structured guidelines for responsible deployment of advanced analytics in environmental contexts. Outcomes include improved mapping accuracy, strengthened institutional capacity and enhanced oversight mechanisms, demonstrating how innovation and ethical assessment can be combined in public-sector digital transformation.

title: MareGraph: Towards an interoperable marine knowledge graph
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The aim of MAREGRAPH is to support the EU and its Member States in the achievement of ambitious marine themed objectives by semantically enriching, interlinking and providing high value and foundational datasets. These currently power the “effective biodiversity and conservation knowledge products” of today and will enable building the knowledge products of the future, where knowledge graphs and AI closely interact to support the marine public sector in making and building open knowledge on marine biodiversity. The MAREGRAPH project will provide an open linked data production and publication of three high impact datasets in the marine domain (the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS), Marine Regions and EurOBIS (the European Node of the international Ocean Biodiversity Information System) using state of the art technologies. This will allow the onboarding of essential marine datasets in the Common European Data Spaces. As such MAREGRAPH will provide a structural component in the digital transition of the marine landscape.

title: Parcel Monitoring Platform Flanders, an AI-based geo-imaging tool for data-driven policy formulation and evaluation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public authorities increasingly need continuous, parcel-level intelligence to support decisions in agriculture, energy, spatial planning, and environmental management, yet raw satellite imagery alone is often too noisy and technically demanding for direct policy use. In Flanders, Digitaal Vlaanderen and VITO developed the Parcel Monitoring Platform to provide more precise, timely, and actionable monitoring of land parcels in support of data-driven policy formulation and evaluation. The objective is to detect relevant changes in land use and parcel conditions more effectively and to give agencies evidence that can support operational monitoring and Green Deal-related policy tasks. The implementation combines AI and geo-imaging techniques with Sentinel time series, aerial imagery, GIS layers, and field data. Raw satellite images are pre-processed in Terrascope, while the CropSAR time-series service allows users to access derived Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 parameters for specific parcels without performing the image processing themselves. At a conceptual level, the platform uses data fusion and change-detection workflows to generate parcel-level notifications relevant to specific policy use cases. The impact includes better monitoring coverage, faster detection of meaningful changes, and stronger support for evidence-based public action. It also improves scalability by turning complex earth-observation data into reusable services for multiple governmental domains.

title: AI4Justice, Intelligent assistant to support judges in drafting sentences by locating texts of previous judgments and jurisprudence
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Centre de Telecomunicacions i Tecnologies de la Informació de la Generalitat de Catalunya (CTTI)
source_description: The time dedicated by judges to search for precedents and legal foundations to write a sentence is high and an impediment to being more agile in the drafting of sentences, causing a high response time and a sense of slow justice. Currently, the location of paragraphs of interest of legal or procedural references, of any documentary information or the entirety of the magistrates' own judgments or resolutions previously issued, which may be applicable or reusable in the drafting of new judgments or resolutions, becomes a manual and costly process that causes magistrates to spend a lot of time locating, remembering, and reviewing previous judgments, relying on their memory, both for their content and the date they were issued. In Catalonia, the judge usually performs a manual search in the procedural management application for justice (eJusticia.cat), in the archive of the magistrate's own judgments, or through the Judicial Documentation Center (CENDOJ), depending on the General Council of the Judiciary (CGPJ), as well as other repositories or jurisprudential databases. The search is more or less effective depending on what the magistrate remembers at that time from similar cases or parts of an old judgment that may be applicable to the current one. The unmet need is to locate reusable information within judicial documents, such as sentences issued in any instance and jurisdiction, in order to speed up and facilitate the drafting of new sentences by judges. Currently, the location of paragraphs of interest (headings, legal foundations, dispositive part or judgment), legal or procedural references or the entirety of the judges' previous sentences, that are applicable or reusable in the drafting of new sentences, becomes a manual and costly process that causes judges to spend a lot of time locating, remembering and reviewing previous judgments, based on memory, both of their content and of the date they were issued. The solution proposed is an assistant to judges and magistrates that, by entering an open text or prompt, can quickly, accurately, and relatedly obtain all applicable historical information for the sentence being drafted. In the same way, the assistant must provide the applicable legal foundations and sentence draft for a better management of mass litigation cases with hundreds of very similar claims accumulate that has also similar resolutions. It is important that the judicial powers have the necessary resources to ensure agile and efficient justice, such as having digital tools that facilitate the location of reusable information from previous sentences and jurisprudence to draft new sentences.

title: Bringing Justice closer to citizens through digitalisation: Virtual Desktop of Digital Immediation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Spanish Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Parliamentary Relation
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: The Spanish Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Parliamentary Relations launched the Virtual Desktop of Digital Immediation (EVID) in 2020 to facilitate remote judicial hearings while ensuring full legal guarantees. Courts needed a secure digital mechanism to conduct proceedings remotely without compromising procedural integrity, identity verification or evidentiary reliability. EVID provides a virtual environment enabling remote participation of judges, lawyers and citizens, integrating secure videoconferencing, document exchange and procedural management tools. To ensure non-repudiation, non-manipulation and non-impersonation, the system anchors key procedural events on a blockchain infrastructure. Cryptographic hashing and timestamping mechanisms record actions, documents and consents in an immutable distributed ledger, guaranteeing traceability and integrity throughout each hearing. Encrypted identity verification components support reliable participant authentication. By combining secure digital workflows with tamper-evident audit trails, EVID enhances accessibility, reduces travel and administrative burdens and supports environmentally sustainable justice services while maintaining procedural security and evidential robustness.

title: Application of Generative AI to the Generalitat de Catalunya to facilitate citizens' understanding of legal texts
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Autonomous Entitat Autònoma del Diari Oficial i de Publications (EADOP)
source_description: Legal texts are essential to public life, yet their technical language often makes them difficult for citizens to understand, limiting access to rights, obligations, and public information. In Catalonia, the Entitat Autònoma del Diari Oficial i de Publicacions and the Legal Portal of Catalonia address this issue by making plain-language summaries of legal rules available to the public, with the aim of improving comprehension, accessibility, and transparency in the dissemination of current law. The objective is to reduce the barrier created by specialist legal drafting and to help citizens navigate Catalan legislation more confidently, while making clear that the official legal text remains the only authoritative source. The implementation uses generative AI to produce unofficial summaries of Catalan legal rules in plain language for publication on the Legal Portal. The initial rollout covered 44 rules in Catalan and 44 in Spanish, with the Generalitat stating that the approach would extend to the more than 14,000 legal provisions then in force; later reporting indicated that more than 16,000 summaries had been made available. The summaries are expressly presented as informational, not as legal advice. The impact includes easier public access to legal information, faster large-scale production of citizen-friendly summaries, and improved transparency and inclusiveness in legal communication, while supporting a more scalable model for making complex public information understandable.

title: Mapping Portugal: leveraging Machine Learning for land registration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Territorial Cohesion
source_description: Accurate land registration is a longstanding challenge in Portugal, particularly for rural and mixed-use properties where ownership information may be incomplete, fragmented, or difficult to access. The BUPi initiative was created to modernise property management by improving the identification, georeferencing, and registration of land parcels, while also reducing regional disparities in access to information and supporting better territory management. The objective is to make property data more accessible and reliable, increase transparency, and provide a stronger evidence base for land governance, public planning, and sustainable development. The implementation combines the BUPi digital platform with machine-learning techniques that support property identification, anomaly detection, land-use classification, and faster processing of geospatial and registry-related information. At a conceptual level, the system links administrative property records with georeferenced parcel data and analytical tools so that land can be identified more precisely and processed more efficiently. Public reporting on the programme notes the scale of the task, with more than eight million land records still requiring georeferencing during the expansion phase, and highlights the use of advanced technologies to accelerate knowledge about the territory. The impact includes improved data quality, quicker land-registration processes, stronger transparency, and better support for strategic decision-making, creating a more scalable and accurate basis for understanding and managing Portuguese territory.

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to detect and predict river overflows
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Centre de Telecomunicacions i Tecnologies de la Informació de la Generalitat de Catalunya (CTTI)
source_description: Flood risk management requires rapid and accurate assessment of potential river overflows, yet traditional hydraulic models can be computationally intensive and slow to update. This initiative explores the feasibility of using advanced predictive algorithms to simulate flood risks more efficiently by combining flow measurements with geospatial datasets. The proof of concept initially focused on the Tordera river basin, integrating hydrological data, terrain models and environmental indicators into a unified analytical framework. Machine learning models were trained to estimate flood-prone areas and generate near real-time predictions of overflow scenarios. The system aims to complement conventional modelling approaches by providing faster decision-support outputs during emergency planning. Early results indicate improved computational efficiency and enhanced situational awareness. The approach supports agile emergency response, better resource allocation and scalable application to additional river basins, strengthening resilience to extreme weather events.

title: Application of drones for the transport of biological samples between a primary health centre and a hospital
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Centre de Telecomunicacions i Tecnologies de la Informació de la Generalitat de Catalunya (CTTI)
source_description: Timely transport of biological samples between healthcare facilities is critical for diagnostic accuracy and patient care, yet conventional road transport can be slow and subject to variability. This pilot project in the Girona health region evaluated a drone-based logistics route connecting the Hospital of Olot and the Vall d’en Bas primary care centre. The system conducted recurrent flights transporting blood and urine samples to the hospital and delivering medical equipment in return. Flight operations were assessed for cost, reliability and sample integrity compared with road transport. Results showed a reduction in transport time from 20 minutes by road to 7 minutes by drone, with improved sample quality due to reduced agitation and shorter exposure duration. The solution also demonstrated increased scheduling flexibility and responsiveness for urgent deliveries. The pilot highlights the potential of unmanned aerial logistics to enhance efficiency, reliability and quality in regional healthcare supply chains.

title: Streamlining administrative tasks through robotic process automation in the administration of Justice
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes
source_description: Justice administrations handle large volumes of repetitive administrative tasks that contribute to delays in legal procedures and increased workload for staff. In Spain, backlogs in processes such as nationality applications and criminal record cancellations highlighted the need for operational efficiency improvements. The objective of this initiative is to streamline routine administrative activities, reduce processing times, and allow judicial staff to focus on higher-value legal work. The solution is implemented through Robotic Process Automation (RPA), which automates structured, rule-based tasks across justice information systems. Software robots handle activities such as data entry, document verification, system updates, and status checks, operating across multiple legacy systems without altering their core architecture. The automated workflows run continuously and consistently, reducing errors and delays. The impact includes faster processing of applications, improved service delivery to citizens, and reduced administrative burden on justice personnel. The initiative delivers cost savings through efficiency gains, improves reliability and transparency of procedures, and enhances the overall responsiveness of the justice system, contributing to greater public trust and institutional performance.

title: Darmstadt im Herzen: a platform promoting sustainability and connected communities in Darmstadt
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban residents often rely on multiple disconnected applications and service channels for neighbourhood support, local information, waste collection, mobility, and community exchange, which can make everyday participation in city life less convenient and less inclusive. Darmstadt im Herzen was designed to bring these functions together in one platform in order to strengthen community ties, support sustainable behaviour, and improve citizens’ access to local services and information. The objective is to make everyday urban life easier while encouraging neighbourhood cooperation, environmental action, and stronger engagement with what is happening across the city. The implementation uses an app structured around three main areas: personal services, neighbourhood interaction, and city information. It combines practical tools such as a waste calendar and key finder with local sharing and mutual-help functions, event information, weather and webcam data, climate tips, service numbers, and sustainability incentives such as rewards for environmentally friendly mobility. At a conceptual level, the platform integrates local content, user participation, and urban-sharing features within one digital interface, while its further development has been linked to the DELTA energy-transition project in Darmstadt. The impact includes greater convenience for residents, improved access to local services and city updates, stronger neighbourhood interaction, and better support for sustainable everyday choices, offering a scalable model for digitally connected urban communities.

title: EMi Smart Employment: Emi: AI at the service of job matching and skills development in Galicia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Emprego en Galicia - la Xunta de Galicia
source_description: Employment services must support jobseekers and employers in a labour market that changes quickly, where skills gaps, mismatched expectations, and fragmented information can reduce the effectiveness of matching and guidance. In Galicia, EMi Smart Employment was introduced to improve how the public employment system supports unemployed people, employers, and frontline staff by connecting individual profiles more closely with labour-market demand. The objective is to provide more personalised, higher-quality services, guide jobseekers towards the skills the market requires, and give employment-service professionals better tools for decision-making. The implementation combines big data and AI to analyse users’ abilities, labour-market information, and employment patterns in order to suggest relevant skills-development paths and better job matches. At a conceptual level, the platform offers tailored services to jobseekers and employers while also equipping staff in the Galician Public Employment Service with stronger analytical tools to interpret labour-market data and support case management. The system is therefore both a public-facing guidance service and an internal decision-support resource. The impact includes more personalised employability support, stronger skills alignment with market needs, and improved quality of matching and advisory services. It also enhances trust in the employment system by improving service outcomes, while creating a more scalable and data-informed approach to workforce development across the Galician employment ecosystem.

title: Boosting efficiency and transparency in processing of Official Publications with AI tools - AI for summaries
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Official gazettes and public-information services handle very large numbers of notices and announcements, yet preparing concise, accurate summaries of those publications manually is resource-intensive and can slow publication workflows and reduce consistency. In Barcelona, the Service of the Official Provincial Gazette and Official Documentation and Publications sought to improve the efficiency and transparency of this process by automating the drafting of short summaries for official notices published in the provincial gazette. The objective is to reduce manual effort for both submitters and staff, speed up publication processing, and improve the accessibility of official information for users of the gazette and related public-information services. The implementation uses a supervised machine-learning and neural-network system trained on a large corpus of previous publications to generate summaries automatically in Catalan or Spanish. The project documentation states that the system was trained with 275,000 publications from 2013 to 2022, processes the first two pages of an announcement, and returns a summary of up to 100 words, while also recording manual edits for later retraining. The impact includes faster summary production, lower workload, improved consistency, and better scalability as publication volumes grow. It also supports transparency by making official content easier to understand and reuse within public-information services.

title: Boosting efficiency and transparency in processing of Official Publications with AI tools - AI for thematic classification
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public administrations publish large volumes of official notices across multiple gazettes and journals, and classifying those notices by topic or procedure is essential if citizens and organisations are to find relevant information quickly. In Barcelona, the same service behind the provincial gazette and official documentation search tools introduced CIDOBOT to support the thematic classification of official publications and improve the accessibility of public information disseminated through the CIDO service. The objective is to reduce the manual burden of classification, increase consistency across large document flows, and make it easier for users to track procedures, regulations, grants, procurement, and other official activity. The implementation uses a neural-network-based deep-learning model trained on human-produced summaries and classifications from a range of official bulletins and journals. At a conceptual level, the system performs documentary analysis of incoming public information and assigns it to thematic or procedural categories such as public procurement, collective agreements, local regulations, grants, and personnel selection. The project documentation explains that the model was trained using classified material from several official publications, including provincial bulletins, the Catalan official journal, and the national gazette. The impact includes faster and more standardised classification, improved discoverability of public information, and stronger transparency for users of CIDO, while also creating a replicable and scalable model for modernising administrative information management.

title: Data-driven water infrastructure maintenance in Burgas
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Ageing water infrastructure causes significant water losses, threatening sustainability, service reliability, and public resources. In some regions, leakage rates reach critical levels, requiring proactive detection and maintenance strategies. The Burgas municipality addresses this challenge by modernising water network monitoring to reduce losses and optimise asset management. Stakeholders include municipal utilities, maintenance operators, and residents. The objective is to detect leaks early, improve water supply reliability, and reduce long-term operational costs. The solution deploys vibration sensors along water pipes to continuously monitor acoustic patterns associated with leaks. Large volumes of sensor data are analysed using predictive models that distinguish normal operation from leak signatures in real time. Continuous automated monitoring enables faster detection than manual inspection methods. The project delivers reduced water losses, improved maintenance planning, and more efficient use of public funds. It strengthens resilience of water infrastructure, enhances service continuity, and supports sustainable water management, offering a replicable model for municipalities facing similar challenges across Europe.

title: MitosLOD: Exporting Linked Open Data from the Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Digital Governance and Ministry of Interior
source_description: MitosLOD enhances the Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services by making information on public services easier to search, retrieve and understand. The operational issue is that administrative service catalogues can be difficult for citizens, businesses and public officials to navigate when information is structured around formal terminology rather than the way users naturally express their needs. The project therefore aims to improve access to the MITOS registry through more intuitive, accurate and multilingual search functions. Its implementation combines Linked Open Data, semantic technologies, natural language processing and artificial intelligence techniques to interpret the meaning and intent behind user queries. Instead of relying only on keyword matching, the semantic search engine analyses relationships between public-service descriptions and translates natural-language questions into structured, machine-readable formats. This allows the system to return more relevant results and support multilingual access to registry content. Conceptually, the solution links public-service metadata, semantic relationships, NLP query interpretation and structured retrieval over the registry. The expected impact is a better user experience, more effective discovery of administrative services and improved reuse of public-sector information. By transforming registry data into semantically searchable content, MitosLOD supports transparency, accessibility and more efficient interaction with public administration.

title: E-peitharxika - an integrated information system to monitor the forms of disciplinary proceedings and disciplinary cases
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Greek public sector needed a more consistent and transparent way to manage disciplinary proceedings across a very large and fragmented administrative landscape. Before the introduction of a unified system, monitoring disciplinary cases across thousands of public bodies was difficult, limiting oversight, comparability and timely access to evidence for decision-making. E-peitharxika was developed to address this governance problem by creating a single point of supervision for the full lifecycle of disciplinary cases, from investigation and hearings to appeals and enforcement. The stakeholders include public bodies, disciplinary authorities, employees, policymakers and the wider public, with the objective of improving accountability, standardising oversight and strengthening trust in disciplinary justice. The solution is implemented as an integrated digital platform covering more than 2,000 public bodies and approximately 520,000 employees. At a conceptual level, the system consolidates case data, supports real-time statistical reporting, interoperates with national human-resources registries and exposes reusable datasets through a REST API, all on a secure, high-availability infrastructure using Azure G-Cloud services and ISO-aligned controls for security, quality and accessibility. The impact includes stronger transparency, more efficient supervision and better evidence for policymaking, supported by public access to statistical data. More broadly, the platform creates value by improving institutional integrity, enabling uniform and systematic oversight, and modernising a sensitive area of public administration through interoperable digital governance.

title: Alliance for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Europe’s language-technology landscape is fragmented by market size, linguistic diversity, and unequal access to high-quality data and infrastructure, which makes it difficult to build competitive large language models and related tools across all European languages. ALT-EDIC addresses this challenge by creating a common European infrastructure for language technologies, with a particular focus on strengthening the foundations for large language models while preserving linguistic diversity and cultural richness. The objective is to improve Europe’s competitiveness, expand the availability of European language data, and support interoperable language-technology capacity across participating states. The implementation uses the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium model, allowing member states to pool funding and resources in a coordinated structure. Official ALT-EDIC and related language-data-space materials describe activities including linguistic-data production and curation, evaluation and normalisation support, adaptation of models to user needs, and advice to the wider ecosystem. The impact includes stronger shared infrastructure, more reusable multilingual resources, and better conditions for developing European language technologies at scale. It also creates long-term strategic value by supporting common standards, reducing fragmentation, and reinforcing Europe’s capacity to develop language AI aligned with its regulatory, linguistic, and public-interest goals.

title: GPT-NL - A language model for the Dutch language and culture
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate
source_description: Many widely used language models are developed outside the Netherlands and may not adequately reflect Dutch language use, legal requirements, or national priorities around privacy, cultural context, and technological independence. GPT-NL was launched to address this strategic gap by creating an open Dutch language model designed to strengthen national capability in AI, data science, and data spaces while supporting compliance with European rules. The objective is to improve strategic autonomy, foster domestic expertise, and provide a trustworthy foundation for language applications built around Dutch language and culture. The implementation centres on the development of an open large language model funded by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy through RVO, with EUR 13.5 million allocated to the project after the “Facility for a sovereign Dutch language model” proposal was awarded in October 2023. At a conceptual level, the initiative focuses on building and governing a Dutch-language model in line with the GDPR and the AI Regulation, with an explicit aim of avoiding training sources that infringe privacy or intellectual-property rights. The impact is expected to include a stronger national knowledge base, improved access to compliant Dutch-language AI infrastructure, and greater capacity for public and private organisations to build applications suited to local linguistic and regulatory needs, creating long-term value through sovereign digital capability.

title: BgGPT - A bulgarian LLM
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: INSAIT – Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology
source_description: Many widely used language technologies provide limited support for smaller European languages, constraining digital inclusion and technological sovereignty. In Bulgaria, public institutions, businesses and citizens lack high-quality language models tailored to national linguistic and cultural contexts. The objective of BgGPT is to develop state-of-the-art generative language models designed specifically for the Bulgarian language and its users. The implementation involves training a series of open and freely available language models using curated Bulgarian-language datasets, supported by advanced computational infrastructure. The models are designed to serve a broad range of applications, including public administration, education, research and business services. Emphasis is placed on openness, transparency and alignment with European values. As the project is still in development, evaluation focuses on linguistic quality, robustness and applicability across use cases. Expected impacts include improved access to language technologies for Bulgarian speakers, strengthened national research capacity and reduced dependency on foreign-language-centric solutions. Qualitative benefits include enhanced digital inclusion, support for public sector innovation and a reusable foundation for Bulgarian-language digital services.

title: GenAI chatbot on the EU-FarmBook platform
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Farmers, foresters, advisers, researchers, and policymakers often need practical knowledge quickly, but relevant materials are frequently spread across projects, languages, and institutions, making them hard to find and apply. EU-FarmBook addresses this challenge by building an open online platform to support knowledge exchange across the European agricultural and forestry innovation ecosystem. The objective is to make research-based and practice-oriented resources easier to discover and use, while improving knowledge transfer between actors at regional, national, and European levels. The implementation includes an AI-powered conversational assistant developed with support from TNO, designed to help users retrieve relevant information interactively from the platform. At a conceptual level, the chatbot uses generative AI to respond to users in a conversational way while grounding its answers in the platform’s own database of contributions, tools, guides, and other materials. Recent project communications state that the AI technology is European and that the responses are based on content held within EU-FarmBook itself, supporting controlled and domain-relevant retrieval. The impact includes easier access to specialised information for users with different backgrounds, improved usability of a large cross-European knowledge platform, and more efficient dissemination of project results and practice-based insight. It also supports scalability by turning a growing repository into a more navigable and interactive service for rural communities.

title: CitiVERSE - LDT CitiVERSE EDIC
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cities across Europe are developing digital twins to support planning and public-service innovation, but these systems often remain local, fragmented, and difficult to connect into a broader European capability. The LDT CitiVERSE EDIC initiative was created to link existing local digital twins and form the foundation of a broader European CitiVERSE, enabling more coordinated development of data-driven and simulation-based tools for urban policy and citizen interaction. The objective is to strengthen cooperation between participating countries, improve the use of digital twins in smart-city policy, and support new forms of simulation and engagement around issues such as traffic, congestion, air quality, and decarbonisation. The implementation uses the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium model to establish a shared governance and infrastructure framework for networked local digital twins. At a conceptual level, the initiative connects data, analytics, simulation, and generative AI applications so that cities can model real-time or future urban conditions and also explore virtual-reality tools that help citizens understand proposed urban changes more easily. The Commission notes that Croatia, Estonia, France, Latvia, Portugal, Slovenia, and Spain initially called for the EDIC to be established. The impact lies in stronger interoperability between local digital twins, greater capacity for collaborative urban innovation, and more scalable smart-city services across Europe, creating both public-sector efficiency gains and better-informed citizen participation.

title: GPT-SW3 - The first large-scale generative language model for the Swedish language
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Swedish organisations increasingly need language technologies that reflect local linguistic realities and can be developed within a national ecosystem rather than relying entirely on foreign models. GPT-SW3 was created to address this need by providing a large-scale generative language model for the Nordic languages, with a primary focus on Swedish, through collaboration between AI Sweden, RISE, and WASP WARA Media & Language. The objective is to give organisations in Sweden access to a strong domestic foundation for language applications, while also strengthening the country’s applied AI capability across public, private, and academic sectors. The implementation uses a large-scale generative model based on the same broad technical principles as contemporary transformer-based language models, trained to support Nordic-language generation and downstream applications. At a conceptual level, the project combines national collaboration, technical development, and ecosystem building through AI Sweden, which brings together more than 120 partners and is funded by both the Swedish government and public- and private-sector participants. The impact includes a stronger Swedish-language AI infrastructure, new possibilities for organisations to build local language applications, and improved strategic capability in a domain often dominated by global providers. It also creates long-term value by supporting innovation in Swedish and Nordic language technology through a shared national platform.

title: Svea - A shared digital assistant for the public sector
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Kungsbacka municipality, Tjörn municipality, Gothenburg city, Region Skåne, Region Halland, and Västra Götaland Region
source_description: Public-sector organisations handle large volumes of text-based work every day, from drafting and revising documents to summarising material, classifying content, and supporting administrative processes, yet these tasks consume significant staff time and are difficult for single organisations to automate alone. In Sweden, the Svea initiative was created as a joint effort between authorities, municipalities, regions, and industry, coordinated by AI Sweden, to develop shared capability rather than fragmented local solutions. The objective is to support public employees in routine text tasks, free time for more interpersonal and creative work, and establish the conditions for national cooperation on shared AI solutions in the public sector. The implementation is organised in phases, beginning with data generation, change management, use-case identification, and prototype development, and continuing with large-scale testing and evaluation. Svea itself is a web-based chat assistant built on open-source, model-agnostic architecture running on Swedish infrastructure; it can already answer organisation-specific questions, summarise documents, extract information, and rewrite text in easy-to-read Swedish. AI Sweden states that participating organisations collectively spent 2,500 hours annotating training data for the assistant. The impact includes stronger reuse of data and effort across institutions, improved scalability of AI adoption, and better productivity in text-heavy public work, while helping organisations prepare for labour shortages and rising service demand.

title: LightOn's Paradigm platform - Generative AI at the Île-de-France Regional Council
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public sector agents often struggle to navigate complex internal documentation and information systems, leading to inefficiencies and increased workload for IT support teams. Stakeholders include regional council staff, digital transformation teams and technology providers. The objective is to provide instant, reliable access to technical documentation and internal knowledge resources. The solution deploys a generative AI-powered assistant built on large language model technology, trained and fine-tuned on the Region’s internal documentation corpus. Natural language queries are processed to retrieve and synthesise relevant information, delivering precise responses within existing digital work environments. The platform integrates with knowledge bases and information systems managed by the Digital Transformation Hub. Expected impacts include reduced time spent searching for documentation, lower support demand on IT teams, improved operational efficiency and enhanced digital maturity within public administration.

title: SOLARIS - Democratic responses to the challenges of deepfakes and infodemics
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are generative AI models capable of reproducing realistic images, videos and voice outputs. Because they have the potential to create highly realistic content, they can also pose a threat to democracies through the creation and circulation of deepfakes, which spread false information and undermine trust. In this context, the EU-funded SOLARIS project will focus on the challenges and opportunities posed by GANs in the context of democracy. It will study how deepfakes circulate and are trusted by users, thus threatening democratic processes. It will also develop regulatory guidelines about GANs and generative AI for the promotion of democratic engagement. The project will involve three use cases to simulate the circulation of threatening content, and co-create value-based GANs content to enhance digital citizenship.

title: TrustLLM - Democratise trustworthy and efficient LLM technology for Europe
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: TrustLLM is a Horizon Europe project designed to develop open, trustworthy and sustainable large language models for European languages, with an initial focus on Germanic languages and underrepresented linguistic communities. The strategic problem is that Europe needs language-model infrastructure that is transparent, reliable, energy-conscious and less dependent on closed non-European systems. Coordinated by Linköping University, the project brings together partners across Europe with expertise in natural language processing, high-performance computing, trustworthy AI, model evaluation and downstream deployment. The implementation will develop large language models trained on substantial multilingual European text resources, while addressing reliability, bias, hallucination, sustainability and accessibility. Conceptually, the project combines large-scale model training, exascale computing, trustworthiness research, open model development and ecosystem-building for modular and extensible European LLMs. The expected impact is stronger European capacity in language technologies, improved human-machine interaction across applications, wider access to open models and better support for industry, public services and research. TrustLLM is explicitly positioned as a response to the need for reliable generative models and mitigation of risks such as hallucinations and bias.

title: GENAI4LEX-B
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Alma Mater Studiorum – University of Bologna ALMA-AI
source_description: GENAI4LEX-B was developed to support parliamentary work in Italy by using generative AI for the preparation of legislative initiative acts. The institutional problem is that parliamentarians and parliamentary staff must navigate complex regulatory sources, amendments, policy objectives and legislative drafting requirements under time and information constraints. The project won the “Supporting the preparation of initiative acts” area in a call promoted by the Italian Chamber of Deputies, which selected three winning projects from 28 proposals. Its three prototypes are designed to help users explore regulatory sources, simplify and summarise amendments, and measure the alignment between bills and the policies they intend to pursue. The implementation combines generative AI, legal informatics, regulatory-source analysis, summarisation and legislative-support functions. The consortium is coordinated by Alma Mater Studiorum – University of Bologna / ALMA-AI and includes CNR-Igsg with Aptus.AI, Luiss Guido Carli University with Asimov AI, the University of Turin and the University of Verona. The expected impact is more efficient legislative preparation, improved access to regulatory context, clearer amendment analysis and stronger evidence on whether proposed bills match policy goals. Its value depends on careful human oversight and constitutional safeguards in parliamentary processes.

title: F13, the LLM used by the State of Baden-Württemberg in collaboration with Aleph Alpha
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Baden-Württemberg introduced F13 to support employees of the state administration in drafting, summarising and processing textual information more efficiently. The administrative challenge is that civil servants work with large volumes of documents, cabinet templates, notes and research material, which can slow workflows and reduce time available for substantive policy or service tasks. F13 is designed to relieve staff by providing text assistance functions tailored to administrative routines. The system was developed primarily by the Heidelberg-based company Aleph Alpha and presented by the Innovation Lab Baden-Württemberg, InnoLab_bw. Its implementation uses generative language-model technology to support several functions: a summary tool with selectable compression levels for pasted texts, a Cabinet Template Note function that converts uploaded cabinet templates into summarised note templates, a research assistant for preparing large volumes of information, and the “Vermerkomat”, which creates comprehensive flow text. At a conceptual level, F13 combines large language models, document processing, summarisation, text generation and workflow-oriented user interfaces within the state administration network. The expected impact is faster preparation of administrative documents, reduced repetitive writing work, improved handling of information-intensive tasks and more consistent support for employees. Since 2024, all staff with access to the state administration network can use F13, indicating a move beyond experimentation into full administrative deployment.

title: ALEIA digital assistant - Generative AI at the Île-de-France Regional Council
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The ALEIA digital assistant responds to the difficulty citizens face when trying to identify the regional aid schemes for which they may be eligible. Île-de-France has around 350 aid schemes, and this breadth of provision can make access confusing for residents, associations or other potential beneficiaries. The Regional Council therefore sought a tool that could guide users through the available support landscape and provide clear answers based on the region’s own documentation. Developed by the start-up Aleia, the solution combines a search engine and a conversational agent. It uses the French Mistral language model to formulate responses grounded in the region’s corpus of documents, while data are hosted in France and answers are continuously improved. The system is also designed to recognise when a user asks about support that falls outside the region’s responsibilities and to respond negatively rather than providing irrelevant guidance. Conceptually, the assistant combines document retrieval, generative language modelling, conversational interaction, controlled knowledge sources and French-hosted data infrastructure. The expected impact is simpler access to regional support, reduced user confusion, more efficient routing towards relevant schemes and less pressure on administrative staff handling repetitive eligibility questions. By linking conversational access with an official documentary corpus, the system can improve transparency and make regional aid more navigable.

title: Open Spanish LLM model in collaboration with IBM
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Spanish Government and IBM collaboration aims to develop open-source foundation models in Spanish and Spain’s co-official languages, including Catalan, Basque, Galician and Valencian. The strategic challenge is that Spanish and Iberian-language communities require generative AI systems that reflect their linguistic diversity, cultural context and public-interest requirements, rather than relying mainly on models optimised for English. The initiative was launched through a Memorandum of Understanding discussed in April 2024 between the Spanish Government and IBM. The implementation draws on IBM’s open-source AI framework and AI stack, with an emphasis on ethical, sustainable and community-driven model development. Conceptually, the project combines large and small language models, open-source development, AI supercomputing, multilingual training and community contribution mechanisms. The expected impact is stronger national and international Spanish-language AI capacity, improved access to generative AI tools for nearly 500 million Spanish speakers, and better support for co-official languages in digital services and innovation. The collaboration also aims to advance responsible generative AI technologies in Spain and support practical deployment in public and private contexts.

title: OpenGPT-X project to create a LLM "Made in Germany"""
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: OpenGPT-X was launched to strengthen Europe’s capacity in generative-language technologies by developing a large language model ecosystem rooted in German and European research, industrial capability and trusted data environments. The broader challenge is that advanced generative models are increasingly important for business applications and digital transformation, yet strategic dependence on non-European solutions may limit sovereignty, transparency and local innovation capacity. This use case therefore brings together partners from industry, research and media across the generative AI value chain, with the objective of advancing cutting-edge research while driving practical adoption in the German economy. The solution is implemented as a collaborative Gaia-X-related project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action, with total funding of around EUR 14 million and a project timeline spanning January 2022 to March 2025. At a conceptual level, the initiative develops large language model capabilities, supporting infrastructure and practical application pathways that connect foundational research with real business use cases. This includes work across model development, data spaces and deployment-oriented innovation within a trusted digital ecosystem. The expected impact is stronger domestic capability in generative-language technologies, greater readiness for enterprise adoption and improved alignment between research and market application. More broadly, OpenGPT-X supports technological sovereignty, boosts innovation capacity and creates long-term value by establishing a European foundation for advanced language-model development and use.

title: Development of GenAI-based tool for education by gov.uk - "Building a proof of concept for Generative AI feedback and resource generation in education contexts"""
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Teachers face substantial workload pressures linked to marking, feedback preparation and the creation of classroom resources, yet these tasks are central to maintaining teaching quality and supporting pupil progress. The National Institute of Teaching and the Department for Education explored this use case as part of a wider effort to transform teachers’ day-to-day work by reducing routine burdens while supporting stronger educational outcomes. The stakeholders include teachers, pupils and education-system leaders, with the objective of helping teachers evaluate work more efficiently, provide useful formative feedback and generate relevant learning activities aligned with the National Curriculum. The solution is implemented as a proof-of-concept tool based on large language models. At a conceptual level, the system uses generative-language capabilities to analyse pupil work against curriculum expectations, draft feedback for formative use and create supporting activities or resources for follow-up teaching. These functions are integrated as exploratory support for professional practice rather than as a replacement for teacher judgement. The expected impact is reduced time spent on repetitive instructional tasks, quicker preparation of feedback and stronger support for lesson adaptation to learner needs. More broadly, the project improves workflow efficiency, enhances the usability of digital tools in education and creates value by testing how generative systems can support teachers in practical, curriculum-linked classroom contexts.

title: Developing a Generative AI platform for construction cost management
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The BIM-GAIcost project develops a generative AI platform to improve productivity and accuracy in construction cost planning. The operational problem is that cost overruns are widespread in construction, while early cost planning often requires time-consuming manual work, fragmented data and limited certainty. Leeds Beckett University’s Futures of Systems, People and Projects laboratory received a £1.18 million Innovate UK grant to develop the platform after a successful feasibility study. The project upgrades the earlier costplan.ai prototype by integrating Building Information Modelling with generative AI and large language models trained on cost data. Conceptually, the platform will generate construction cost-estimation documents, automate BIM-related cost outputs, provide early cost advice and include accuracy indications to help predict and avoid overruns during planning. The expected impact is a major productivity gain, with the source indicating potential improvement of up to 85% by reducing the time required to prepare initial cost plans. The wider consortium includes The Property Box Group, London South Bank University, Birmingham City University, Leeds Beckett University, Milan Consulting, Ardeo and Kier Group.

title: Amsterdam: Generating sustainable materials with Generative AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The University of Amsterdam’s AI4SMM initiative applies artificial intelligence to the design of sustainable molecules and materials, shifting generative techniques from language to chemistry and materials science. The research challenge is that developing new materials for energy storage, industry, food and plastics can be slow, costly and experimentally intensive, while sustainability transitions require faster discovery of safer and lower-impact alternatives. The initiative is led by Bernd Ensing at the Faculty of Science and connects expertise in computer science, chemistry, ecology, physics and biology. The implementation uses machine-learning and generative approaches to model molecules and materials, replacing word-based associations with relationships between molecular structures and properties. Initial projects focus on areas such as energy-storage salts, sustainable steel, safe plastic and new plant proteins. Conceptually, the approach combines molecular data, computational chemistry, generative modelling, property prediction and experimental validation to propose promising candidates for further study. The expected impact is faster discovery of sustainable materials, better targeting of laboratory work and stronger integration between AI and sustainability research. By applying generative methods to molecules rather than text, the initiative can support innovation in sectors where material performance and environmental impact are central.

title: Qra - The first Polish open-source LLM
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Qra was developed to provide a strong Polish-language generative model trained specifically on Polish text, responding to the limited availability of open large language models optimised for Polish. The research and technology problem is that models primarily trained on English or multilingual corpora may underperform in Polish-language understanding, question answering and coherent text generation. Gdańsk University of Technology and the AI Lab at the National Information Processing Institute developed Polish generative neural language models using approximately a terabyte of Polish-language data. The implementation involved training open-source models on Polish text, with the Hugging Face model card noting that published versions were based on Llama 2 checkpoints and further trained on a cleaned, filtered and deduplicated Polish corpus of about 90 billion tokens. The models were trained using infrastructure from the PG TASK Computing Centre with 21 Nvidia A100 cards. The expected impact is improved Polish-language AI capacity, broader reuse by researchers and developers, and reduced reliance on foreign-language models for Polish applications. Because the models are open-source, users can download and adapt them to specific domains or tasks, including question answering and text generation.

title: OpenLLM-Ro - The first LLM in Romanian language
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: POLITEHNICA Bucharest, the University of Bucharest and the Institute of Logic and Data Science
source_description: OpenLLM-Ro was developed to address the limited availability of large language models specifically trained for Romanian, a gap that can constrain the quality of digital services, research tools and language technologies for Romanian-speaking users. The initiative brings together academic actors seeking to strengthen national language-technology capacity and provide an open model that can be further refined for different applications. The main stakeholders include POLITEHNICA Bucharest, the University of Bucharest, the Institute of Logic and Data Science, researchers working pro bono, developers, public or private organisations that may reuse the model, and Romanian-speaking end users. Starting in the second half of 2023, the research team worked on developing and training the model, with POLITEHNICA Bucharest also providing the computing power needed for training. The implementation involves large-language-model development, corpus preparation, training infrastructure, model evaluation and ongoing fine-tuning. Conceptually, the project creates a foundational Romanian-language model that can support downstream tasks such as text generation, summarisation, question answering, classification or conversational interfaces. Its expected impact is to reduce dependence on models optimised primarily for larger languages, improve Romanian-language processing quality, and support innovation in education, administration, business and research. The model’s online availability and continued fine-tuning indicate an evolving resource for the Romanian digital ecosystem.

title: GenAI-based chatbot to help the public access services on official websites
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Ireland’s GenAI chatbot initiative was designed to test how generative AI could help members of the public find information on government supports and services through official digital channels. The administrative problem is that citizens and businesses often need to navigate multiple public websites, schemes and eligibility pages, which can create friction and increase demand for direct assistance. The initial project aimed to deliver a “chat agent” able to provide information on business supports offered by the Government, with pilot funding from Microsoft and delivery in collaboration with the Office of the Government Chief Information Officer. Conceptually, the service uses generative AI to interpret user questions, retrieve relevant official content and provide conversational answers, while requiring safeguards around accuracy, transparency, human oversight and data protection. The expected impact is easier access to public information, reduced search burden for users, and better scalability for high-volume enquiries.
