A related public-facing Irish implementation is now visible through AskCI, an AI-powered chatbot on Citizens Information that uses generative AI to answer questions based on citizensinformation.ie content and was developed with the OGCIO.

title: FinGPT-3 - The open Finnish LLM
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: FinGPT-3 was created to expand the availability of generative language models for Finnish, a language that is less represented than English in many large-scale model ecosystems. The research challenge is to build models that can handle Finnish linguistic structures effectively and support applications in language technology, digital linguistics and natural language processing. The project is led by the TurkuNLP Group at the University of Turku, whose work spans corpus annotation, analysis, machine learning theory and applied language technologies. The National Library of Finland collaborated on the model development, and the project received support from the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101070350. In 2023, the team trained GPT-3-like generative models for Finnish. The implementation involves assembling and processing Finnish-language corpora, training large generative architectures, evaluating linguistic performance and making model outputs available for research or downstream application. Conceptually, FinGPT-3 provides foundational language-model capacity that can support Finnish text generation, summarisation, classification, information extraction and other NLP tasks. The expected impact is stronger technological coverage for Finnish, improved resources for researchers and developers, and reduced dependence on multilingual systems that may underperform for smaller language communities. By combining university expertise, national library resources and EU funding, the project contributes to Europe’s capacity for language-specific AI development.

title: NorGPT - The open LLM "Made in Norway"""
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: NorGPT forms part of Norway’s effort to develop large language models adapted to Norwegian language needs and national digital capacity. The core problem is that many large language models are optimised for English or broad multilingual use, while Norwegian users, organisations and public institutions need models that understand Norwegian linguistic structures, terminology and cultural context. Developed through NorwAI and NTNU, the initiative supports natural-language interaction so that users can work on language-related tasks through ordinary Norwegian queries rather than artificial syntax. The implementation involves collecting and processing Norwegian-language text resources, training large language models, evaluating performance, and making models available for research and experimental use. Conceptually, NorGPT can support tasks such as text generation, summarisation, translation, question answering and information retrieval. The expected impact is stronger Norwegian-language AI capacity, improved productivity for language-intensive work and reduced reliance on external models not optimised for Norwegian. Current NorwAI material indicates that work on Norwegian LLMs is active, while a recent technical report states that NorwAI models are openly available to Nordic organisations, companies and students for research and experimental use.

title: ‘Democratic Engagement through a Public Chatbot’ (DepuChat) - How GenAI can increase transparency
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: DepuChat proposes a public chatbot to make information on the Italian Chamber of Deputies more accessible, usable and transparent for citizens. The democratic problem is that parliamentary information is often technically complex, dispersed across institutional documents and difficult for non-specialist users to interpret. The project, developed by the IDEAS Research Centre at Roma Tre University in collaboration with the Department of Legal Sciences at the University of Florence, aims to bring citizens closer to institutions by allowing them to query information on the Chamber, its bodies and procedures, individual MPs, and political positions expressed by MPs and the Government. The implementation uses generative AI to create a conversational and potentially graphical interface over parliamentary data. Conceptually, the system combines institutional data retrieval, natural-language interaction, summarisation and visual presentation to help users explore parliamentary activity more easily. The expected impact is improved transparency, broader civic access to legislative information and stronger democratic engagement. The project was announced in July 2024 as a winner of the Chamber of Deputies’ call for ideas, so its current form appears to be a selected proposal or prototype rather than a fully operational public service.

title: Supporting Civil Servant with Generative AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Processing and Function Public Interministerial Directorate for Public Transformation (DITP) and the Interministerial Digital Directorate (DINUM),
source_description: France’s experiment on generative artificial intelligence in public services was launched to assess how such tools could support civil servants in responding to users more efficiently. The administrative problem is that public agents handle large numbers of online opinions, comments and procedural interactions, many of which require clear written replies but can be repetitive and time-consuming. The initiative involved 1,000 volunteer agents equipped with a tool to help draft responses to users during online procedures, while preserving a human-in-the-loop model: agents supervise, modify and approve responses before they are sent. The experiment is led by the Interministerial Directorate for Public Transformation and the Interministerial Digital Directorate, with a solution provided by Allobrain. The system uses generative language technology to propose draft responses based on anonymised data, meaning confidentiality is intended to be preserved. The model supports response writing rather than replacing the public official, and the approach is framed as a way to save time on specific tasks while strengthening human contact between public services and citizens. The planned extension to France services counters would broaden the support to agents assisting users face to face. The expected impact is faster response preparation, reduced administrative burden, improved consistency in written replies and more time for personalised support where human judgement is most valuable.
supporting_source_urls: Stanislas GUERINI experiments with generative artificial intelligence in public services | Interdepartmental Directorate for Public Transformation (modernisation.gouv.fr)

title: SNCF collect 3x more customer feedback with AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Railway operators need timely and detailed customer feedback to understand service quality, detect weak signals and respond to dissatisfaction before it damages trust. SNCF used AlloReview to improve the collection and analysis of passenger feedback across TER services, particularly in the Grand Est region. The operational problem was that traditional satisfaction surveys were not capturing enough qualitative information, while unsolicited passenger experiences were difficult to process at scale. The implementation combines QR codes, phone numbers, business cards and post-journey feedback mechanisms, allowing travellers to leave comments orally or in writing at different moments of the customer journey. AI-supported real-time analysis processes the resulting verbatims, identifies satisfaction levels and topics raised, and supports scenario-based follow-up. At a conceptual level, the system transforms open-ended voice and text feedback into structured customer intelligence, enabling SNCF to re-engage dissatisfied passengers, reward loyal customers and identify improvement opportunities. The expected impact is richer customer listening, faster detection of recurring problems, better segmentation of passenger satisfaction and stronger customer relationship management. The case demonstrates how AI can be used in transport not only for operations or mobility flows, but also for continuous service-quality improvement through large-scale qualitative analysis.

title: Legislab - monitoring legislative quality with GenAI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Legislab is designed to support analysis of the Italian legislative system and assist parliamentary offices in monitoring legal quality. The institutional problem is that new legislative proposals must be assessed against a large and continuously evolving corpus of laws, from the Constitution onwards, making it difficult to identify relevant precedents, overlaps, inconsistencies or references. The project, developed by the Politecnico di Milano and the Istituto Einaudi, is intended for the offices of the Chamber of Deputies and combines a database of Italian laws with analytical and generative functions. Its implementation allows users to input a topic or draft title and receive relevant articles and laws that may need to be considered. The system is deliberately constrained to reduce hallucination risks: it relies on existing legal data, objective information and linguistic metrics from scientific literature rather than generating free-form legal text. The expected impact is stronger legislative quality monitoring, faster identification of relevant legal sources and better support for expert legislative drafting, while preserving the role of legal professionals and parliamentarians in writing the law.

title: ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT: A Pre-trained Transformer Language Model for Italian Law
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Legal language differs substantially from general Italian because it contains technical terminology, Latin expressions, formulaic constructions and domain-specific references that general-purpose language models may not represent well. ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT addresses this gap by adapting transformer-based natural language processing to the Italian legal domain. The model was introduced by researchers at the Sant’Anna School of Advanced Studies to improve performance on downstream legal NLP tasks where generic Italian BERT models lose accuracy. The implementation starts from an Italian BERT architecture and performs additional pre-training on Italian civil-law corpora. At a conceptual level, the model learns contextual representations from legal texts, making it better suited to tasks such as legal classification, retrieval, information extraction or document analysis. This approach is important because many public-sector legal applications require high sensitivity to legal wording and cannot rely solely on models trained on Wikipedia, news or other general corpora. The expected impact is improved performance in Italian legal AI systems, stronger foundations for legal analytics, and a reusable research resource for courts, public administrations, legal publishers and academic projects. The published paper reports that ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT outperforms the general-purpose Italian BERT in domain-specific tasks, while a public Hugging Face entry indicates the model remains available as an open machine-learning resource.

title: LEGAL-BERT: The Muppets straight out of Law School
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Athens university of economics and business
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: LEGAL-BERT was developed to improve the application of transformer-based language models to legal-domain tasks, where general-purpose models may not perform optimally because of specialised vocabulary, reasoning patterns and document structures. The research problem is that BERT had achieved strong results across many natural language processing tasks, but guidance on how to adapt it to specialised domains had not been sufficiently tested for legal materials. The project therefore evaluates different strategies for applying BERT to legal downstream tasks, including using the original model directly, adapting it through additional pre-training on legal corpora and pre-training models from scratch on domain-specific legal data. The implementation also explores a broader hyper-parameter search space for fine-tuning, recognising that standard configurations may not generalise well to law. The resulting LEGAL-BERT family of models is intended to support legal NLP research, computational law and legal technology applications. Conceptually, the project combines domain-specific pre-training, transformer architectures, legal corpora and systematic evaluation across datasets. Its expected impact is improved model performance for legal text classification, retrieval and analysis, as well as more reliable methodological guidance for researchers and developers working in specialised domains. By releasing LEGAL-BERT, the project provides reusable infrastructure for legal AI experimentation and application development.

title: Predictice - Summaries of Court Decisions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Predictice uses generative language technology to make legal research more efficient by producing automatic summaries of court decisions. The practical challenge for legal professionals is that judicial documents can be long, technical and time-consuming to read, while some decisions may prove irrelevant only after several minutes of review. Predictice provides access to a large legal corpus of around 26 million documents, including court decisions, and aims to help users assess relevance more quickly. The implementation applies GPT-3 and ChatGPT-style language-model capabilities to the task of document synthesis. Rather than asking the model to produce legal advice, the tool focuses on summarising existing decisions, a use case considered more reliable by the Predictice team than generating autonomous legal answers. Conceptually, the system combines large-scale legal-document retrieval, generative summarisation, natural language processing and user-facing legal search functions. The expected impact is faster review of case law, reduced time spent on irrelevant documents, improved productivity for lawyers and legal researchers, and easier navigation of large legal databases. By providing concise summaries of lengthy decisions, Predictice can support legal professionals in prioritising which documents deserve closer reading. However, because legal interpretation remains sensitive, summaries should be treated as decision-support outputs and checked against the original court text.

title: Henchman - contract drafing with AI support
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Henchman supports legal professionals in drafting and improving contract clauses by extending the range of available drafting options during contract preparation. The practical challenge in legal work is that lawyers frequently need to adapt existing clauses to specific transactional contexts, client preferences or drafting conventions, while maintaining consistency, precision and speed. The platform is therefore relevant to law firms, in-house legal teams, contract managers and clients relying on efficient document production. Its objective is to make contract drafting more agile by helping users refine language, adjust wording and introduce clause-level variations without starting from scratch. The implementation uses GPT-3.5 to assist with targeted drafting operations, such as changing a clause from singular to plural or adding a new element to an existing provision. Conceptually, the system combines large language model functionality with contract-drafting workflows, allowing users to generate or modify text within a controlled legal-document environment. The expected impact is faster clause adaptation, reduced repetitive editing, improved consistency across contract drafts and greater productivity for legal teams. By supporting incremental drafting rather than replacing legal judgement, the tool can help professionals focus on negotiation strategy, legal risk and client-specific tailoring. Its value depends on appropriate human review, since AI-generated legal text must be checked for accuracy, enforceability and alignment with the intended contractual position.

title: Robin AI - LLM for supporting Legals
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Robin AI provides legal teams with a platform for accelerating contract review, drafting and editing through large language model functionality. The operational issue is that legal departments and firms often spend substantial time reading long contracts, identifying risks, suggesting amendments and aligning documents with client preferences. This creates pressure on turnaround times, especially where high volumes of contracts must be reviewed consistently. The platform is relevant to lawyers, in-house legal teams, commercial teams, clients and organisations seeking faster approval workflows. Its implementation uses large language models, including Anthropic’s Claude, to analyse contract text, support reading and editing, and suggest real-time changes based on client preferences. At a conceptual level, the system combines natural language processing, generative text functions, contract analytics, preference-based review logic and workflow integration. It can assist users by identifying relevant provisions, proposing edits and supporting the review process before approval. The expected impact is shorter contract-review cycles, more consistent application of drafting standards and reduced manual workload for routine legal-document tasks. The platform also has potential to improve collaboration between legal and business teams by making contract changes easier to understand and process. However, because the information provided acknowledges the possibility of AI errors, human legal supervision remains essential to validate outputs and ensure that proposed revisions are legally and commercially appropriate.

title: Harvey - LLM for supporting contract analysis
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Harvey is used in the legal sector to support contract analysis, due diligence, research and knowledge work across different practice areas. The business problem it addresses is the high volume and complexity of legal information that lawyers must review, compare and interpret, particularly in transactional matters, investigations or advisory work. Law firms and legal departments need tools that can accelerate document analysis while preserving expert oversight and professional responsibility. Harvey was reportedly rolled out by Allen & Overy and uses GPT-4 to help lawyers generate insights, recommendations and predictions. Its implementation draws on large language model capabilities for natural language understanding, document summarisation, information extraction, legal research support and analytical assistance. Conceptually, the platform can process legal materials, identify relevant issues, support due diligence questions, assist with drafting or research tasks and provide structured outputs for lawyer review. The expected impact is improved efficiency in document-heavy legal work, faster identification of relevant contractual or legal points, reduced time spent on repetitive analysis and stronger support for multi-practice knowledge work. By augmenting lawyers’ ability to navigate complex information, the tool can create business value through faster delivery and more scalable legal services. Nevertheless, its outputs must be reviewed by qualified professionals, because legal interpretation, strategic judgement and client advice cannot be delegated to automated systems.

title: INNOAIR - Green public transport on-demand in the Municipality of Sofia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Sofia faces persistent air pollution and traffic congestion, particularly in rapidly developing neighbourhoods with limited public transport coverage. The INNOAIR project aimed to improve urban mobility and air quality by piloting greener, on-demand public transport services in the districts of Manastirski Livadi and Buxton. Coordinated by the Municipality of Sofia and managed by the Sofia Development Association, the initiative tested five electric minibuses with a capacity of 20 passengers each during a one-year trial starting in 2023. Advanced routing algorithms were used to determine optimal service routes based on municipal datasets, including registered vehicles, public facilities and demographic information, complemented by data gathered through community engagement and urban walks. While routes remained fixed once defined, departure times operated on a demand-responsive basis. The pilot provided residents with alternatives to private car use, contributing to reduced traffic volumes and lower emissions. The project demonstrated improved accessibility, enhanced user satisfaction and measurable environmental benefits, supporting scalable deployment of intelligent, low-emission mobility services.

title: A new virtual assistant for the city of Kortrijk
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Kortrijk sought to enhance accessibility to municipal services and streamline citizen interactions as part of a broader regional digitalisation strategy supported by NextGenerationEU funding. Traditional service channels often require in-person visits or complex navigation of online portals. To address this, the city implemented “De Virtuele Assistent”, a digital platform combining transactional chatbot functionality with advanced language processing capabilities. The system enables residents, associations and businesses to obtain information about municipal services, book appointments and request official documents such as certificates and deeds through a single conversational interface. Integrated with existing administrative systems, the assistant supports automated processing of routine requests while escalating complex cases to human staff when necessary. Accessible via smartphone, tablet and desktop devices, the solution enhances inclusivity and service availability. Expected benefits include reduced administrative workload, faster response times and improved user experience, supporting more efficient and citizen-centred digital public services.

title: ‘Fix the Streets’ - AI that leverages citizen-produced data to improve the streets
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal engineering teams need timely, localised information on potholes, damaged signs, and other street defects, yet conventional inspections can miss issues or detect them only after delays. In Vaasa, the Fix the Streets initiative tackled this challenge by drawing directly on geo-located observations submitted by residents, turning citizen-generated reports into a richer operational picture of street conditions. The objective is to improve infrastructure monitoring, support faster and better-targeted maintenance decisions, and strengthen the city’s use of digital tools within its wider twin-transition and innovation agenda. The implementation combined a mobile application with a multi-format knowledge base built over two years from text, image, and video submissions. Working with Crowdsorsa, the Municipal Engineering Department used AI to analyse reported defects and linked the app with Vaasa’s digital signage and mapping systems for more precise localisation and follow-up. At a conceptual level, the solution joins crowdsourced data collection, geospatial mapping, and automated issue analysis in one workflow, while emphasising data minimisation in the handling of citizen input. The impact includes improved visibility of street health, more informed prioritisation of maintenance activity, and stronger evidence for infrastructure decisions. It also demonstrates a scalable model for combining citizen participation with digital monitoring to improve local public services.

title: Satellites for Wilderness Inspection and Forest Threat Tracking (SWIFTT)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Forest ecosystems face increasing risks from climate change, pests and biodiversity loss, yet monitoring large and remote areas remains resource-intensive. The SWIFTT project aims to provide forest managers with accessible and scientifically robust remote sensing tools to monitor and mitigate forest threats. The consortium integrates satellite imagery with advanced analytical models to detect changes in vegetation health, biodiversity indicators and environmental stress factors. Machine learning techniques process multi-temporal Earth observation data to generate risk maps and predictive assessments for forest management. The platform is designed to be user-friendly and cost-effective, enabling practical uptake by forestry professionals. Field validation and deployment are planned in large forest areas in Germany, France and Latvia to test operational feasibility. Anticipated impacts include improved early detection of forest degradation, enhanced biodiversity conservation and more informed climate mitigation strategies. The project strengthens data-driven forest governance and promotes sustainable ecosystem management across Europe.

title: The 'Wet Index’ project - an AI tool to predict local floods
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The tool was developed to tackle the increasing risk of flooding due to extreme weather events, which poses challenges for municipalities, landowners, and urban planners in anticipating and mitigating damage. Existing forecasting tools lack sufficient localisation and lead time for effective decision-making. The objective is to provide accurate, localised early warnings to support proactive planning and risk management. The solution uses predictive modelling techniques applied to geospatial and climate data to forecast flood risks at a local level, providing up to 48 hours of advance warning. The system integrates multiple data sources and is developed in collaboration with research institutions, with conceptual integration into municipal planning and emergency response systems. The impact includes improved preparedness, reduced damage from flooding, and enhanced decision-making for urban and rural planning. It also increases reliability and scalability of forecasting capabilities, delivering significant value in risk reduction and public safety.

title: Policies for Holistic Urban Mobility and Accessibility
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban congestion and accessibility barriers disproportionately affect people with disabilities, requiring targeted policy interventions informed by reliable data. The Municipality of Nicosia, within the AI4PublicPolicy initiative, developed a citizen-centric framework to design evidence-based mobility policies. The project focused on improving access to restricted streets during congestion and optimising parking availability for individuals with disabilities. Analytical models processed traffic data, Smart City platform information and inputs from License Plate Recognition cameras to assess access patterns and forecast congestion hotspots. Predictive tools supported dynamic policy adjustments to enhance mobility and parking accessibility. Co-creation workshops with local stakeholders ensured that policy design reflected community needs and practical constraints. The initiative enabled more precise targeting of interventions, reduced travel time for vulnerable users and strengthened inclusive urban planning. By integrating advanced analytics with participatory governance, the project contributes to fairer and more efficient mobility systems.

title: The AI-based LisNav application improves the lives of the visually impaired
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: For visually impaired people, moving independently through unfamiliar indoor and outdoor spaces can be difficult, especially where transport, navigation, and points of interest are not presented in accessible ways. LisNav was developed to address this challenge by improving how users perceive and interact with their surroundings, with particular value in navigating public transport environments and urban spaces. The objective is to increase independence, accessibility, and confidence by giving users real-time auditory support tailored to their location and immediate context. The implementation combines intelligent algorithms with real-time audio descriptions, drawing on publicly available datasets and user-contributed information such as local points of interest and transport details. In particular, the system provides information about bus stops and the wider bus-stop network, helping users orient themselves and travel more effectively. At a conceptual level, LisNav links location-aware data, accessibility-focused design, and audio interaction to create an augmented navigation layer for visually impaired users. Developed by 3FINERY, the solution applies AR-related capability in a way that supports practical, everyday mobility rather than generic mapping alone. The impact includes better access to transport information, greater autonomy in unfamiliar surroundings, and an improved user experience in navigating cities. It also offers a scalable digital-assistance model for inclusive mobility services.

title: RECITAL' Project: Immediate and Long-Term Energy Reduction
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal buildings represent a significant share of urban energy consumption, yet fragmented monitoring systems limit proactive management of inefficiencies. The RECITAL project in Noisy-le-Grand introduced an “energy hypervisor” to centralise and analyse ten years of consumption data across municipal buildings. The system aggregates data from smart meters and IoT sensors installed in each facility, enabling daily tracking of electricity and heating usage. Analytical models detect anomalies and trigger alerts when overconsumption patterns occur, supporting rapid corrective action. Historical data analysis informs long-term renovation and decarbonisation strategies, while real-time monitoring enhances operational efficiency. The integration of sensing infrastructure with advanced analytics allows targeted optimisation of energy use and improved performance benchmarking. Expected outcomes include reduced energy expenditure, lower carbon emissions and improved sustainability planning. The project demonstrates how data-driven building management can accelerate municipal energy transition efforts and support climate neutrality objectives.

title: CyberKit4SME - Democratizing a Cyber Security Toolkit for SMEs & Mes
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Small and medium-sized enterprises often lack the resources and expertise to implement robust cybersecurity measures, leaving them vulnerable to data breaches and operational disruptions. CyberKit4SME aimed to provide accessible, affordable and easy-to-use tools enabling SMEs and mid-sized enterprises to better monitor, forecast and manage cyber risks. The project developed practical encryption and system isolation solutions tailored to constrained IT environments, ensuring data protection without requiring advanced in-house capabilities. In addition, blockchain-based mechanisms were introduced to facilitate secure sharing of threat intelligence and incident reports between companies and Computer Emergency Response Teams. The toolkit integrates risk awareness modules and monitoring functions within a user-friendly interface designed for non-specialist users. By lowering technical and financial barriers, the initiative enhances cyber resilience across supply chains. Expected impacts include improved threat detection, stronger collaboration with response authorities and reduced vulnerability of smaller enterprises to cyberattacks, contributing to a more secure digital economy.

title: CITIES2023 - Co-creating resIlient and susTaInable food systEms towardS FOOD2030
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Urban food systems face challenges related to sustainability, traceability and coordination among diverse stakeholders. The CITIES2030 project brought together researchers, entrepreneurs, civil society and municipalities to transform how food is produced, transported, supplied and reused within urban food system ecosystems. A blockchain-based, data-driven management platform was developed to create a digital twin of the urban food system, integrating information across supply chains. The platform enables secure data exchange, transparency of transactions and monitoring of sustainability indicators throughout the lifecycle of food products. Analytical tools process system-wide data to identify inefficiencies and support evidence-based policy interventions. By fostering collaboration and trust among partners, the project promotes citizen-centred and resilient food governance. Expected outcomes include reduced waste, improved traceability and enhanced sustainability performance. The initiative demonstrates how digital twin modelling and distributed ledger technologies can strengthen urban food system coordination and long-term resilience.

title: PILLAR Robots - a project to increase the autonomy of AI-based robots
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: PILLAR Robots addresses a fundamental operational challenge in robotics: enabling robots to function with greater autonomy across different domains while ensuring that what they learn remains relevant to real deployment contexts. Many autonomous systems can acquire behaviours through training, yet they often struggle to generalise beyond narrow environments or to focus learning on what truly matters for practical applications. This use case therefore involves robotics researchers, developers and application-oriented stakeholders seeking to improve the adaptability and usefulness of autonomous machines in real-world settings. Its objective is to help robots acquire the knowledge and capabilities needed for target applications more efficiently by giving them a stronger internal basis for selecting, prioritising and acting on relevant goals. The solution is implemented by operationalising the concept of “purpose”, drawn from cognitive science, within robotic cognitive architectures. At a conceptual level, the project develops algorithms for purpose acquisition, mechanisms to bias perceptual, motivational and decision systems towards purposeful behaviour, and learning strategies for representations, skills and models that support both deliberative and reactive decision-making. These elements are designed to work together so that learning is not only autonomous but also better aligned with task relevance. The expected impact is increased robot autonomy, stronger domain independence and more effective acquisition of usable skills. More broadly, the project creates value by improving the transferability, reliability and practical utility of autonomous robots in applied settings.

title: Aquatic Litter Drones
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Monitoring marine and freshwater litter is essential for environmental protection, yet manual surveys are labour-intensive and inconsistent. This use case establishes a service that processes drone imagery to detect and classify floating litter in water bodies and on beaches. Unmanned aerial vehicles conduct surveys at varying altitudes, generating high-resolution images that are uploaded to a digital platform. Two convolutional neural network models analyse the imagery to quantify and categorise observed waste, producing standardised datasets for environmental management. The system integrates image storage, processing and analytics into a unified workflow, enabling scalable monitoring across regions. Field applications in collaboration with international organisations have demonstrated operational feasibility and support for clean-up initiatives. The approach enhances accuracy, comparability and timeliness of litter assessments. By providing actionable data for policymakers and local stakeholders, the solution strengthens environmental monitoring, supports targeted interventions and contributes to marine ecosystem preservation.

title: SignAvatar – AI Speech to SignLangauge Translator at the Belgrade airport
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Hearing-impaired travellers can be excluded from essential transport information when announcements are delivered only through spoken audio or standard text displays that do not fully meet their communication needs. At Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport, this use case was introduced to improve accessibility by translating passenger announcements into sign language and making key travel information easier to understand within the terminal environment. The objective is to reduce communication barriers, improve passenger experience for deaf and hard-of-hearing users, and demonstrate how inclusive announcement systems can be integrated into major transport hubs. The implementation uses SignAvatar’s TransportSign solution, which automatically converts speech and text into sign-language output displayed on screens. During the airport trial, five screens were installed across the terminal, and the same solution has also been adopted at Belgrade’s central railway station. At a conceptual level, the system combines speech and text processing with sign-language generation so that operational messages can be communicated in a more accessible visual form. The impact includes improved accessibility of real-time passenger information, a more inclusive travel environment, and reduced dependence on ad hoc assistance for understanding announcements. It also provides a scalable model for transport operators seeking to make station and airport communications more equitable and user-centred.

title: Inter-municipal Chatbot MUNI - Aarhus
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Citizens often find municipal websites and self-service systems difficult to navigate, particularly when they are unsure which service they need or how to complete a process such as obtaining a passport, using MitID, or arranging childcare. MUNI was created to improve this interface between citizens and local government by offering a more conversational and accessible route into municipal services across a large inter-municipal collaboration in Denmark. The objective is to supplement or partially replace traditional self-service pathways with more efficient and user-friendly AI-supported interaction, while ensuring that people can still reach a human adviser if the automated route does not resolve their need. The implementation combines chatbot technology with integrations into municipal call-centre and self-service systems, including Puzzel and Selvbetjening.nu, and more recent descriptions present MUNI as an AI-driven chat and voicebot. Public descriptions of the project report collaboration across 36 municipalities, with the potential to expand further, and note that since launch citizens have rated the service highly, averaging 2.43 out of 3. Where the chatbot cannot provide sufficient help, it can offer a callback from a call-centre agent. The impact includes faster access to municipal guidance, better user experience, and stronger scalability of citizen support across participating authorities.

title: Itla View – Crowdsourcing and AI-based digital tool for knowledge management and systems change in public sector
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Itla View is a digital tool to help local services address the fragmentation of information across services supporting children, young people, and families, where stakeholders lack a shared, up-to-date understanding of well-being and service needs. This limits the ability to identify risks early and coordinate preventive actions. The objective is to create a shared situational awareness to support proactive and coordinated service delivery. The solution aggregates observations from field actors with indicator data and contextual information such as local news, applying analytical techniques to identify patterns and relationships across datasets. The system enables visualisation and interpretation of combined insights, supporting decision-making across organisations. It is conceptually integrated into local service ecosystems to facilitate collaboration and data sharing. The impact includes improved early identification of needs, stronger preventive interventions, and enhanced coordination among stakeholders. It also supports more efficient resource allocation, better service outcomes, and long-term system-level improvements in public sector effectiveness.
vendor_reported: Hahmota Ltd. (responsible for the design and technical implementation of the web platform) and VXT Research Ltd. (handling semantic search and backend processing)

title: Humanising Authonomy - Behavioural AI to improve the safety of public transport
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public transport and freight operators in London face a persistent road safety challenge in complex urban environments, where interactions between buses, heavy vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, and other road users can change rapidly and create significant risk. Within the context of Transport for London’s Freight Lab and the wider ambition to meet Vision Zero by 2041, this use case aims to strengthen vehicle safety standards and reduce deaths and serious injuries by improving how vehicles detect and respond to human behaviour. The stakeholders include transport authorities, fleet operators, drivers, vehicle technology providers, and road users. The implementation uses real-time intent prediction software that analyses live camera feeds to interpret and anticipate the behaviour of pedestrians, passengers, and surrounding vehicles. Behavioural models and computer vision techniques infer likely movement patterns and provide inputs to vehicle decision systems, supporting functions such as automated emergency braking, front and near-side alerts, and rear-view camera monitoring. The solution is designed to integrate with different levels of vehicle autonomy, from driver assistance in conventional vehicles to more automated environments. The expected impact includes faster hazard recognition, improved driver awareness, and more reliable preventive action, contributing to safer streets, better compliance with evolving safety standards, and reduced operational and social costs linked to collisions.

title: Generative AI Assistant PARLA for the City of Berlin
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Public administrations and political institutions generate thousands of documents, but finding the right information quickly across parliamentary papers, committee procedures, and written questions can be time-consuming for civil servants, journalists, associations, and citizens alike. In Berlin, PARLA was developed to make this documentary landscape more searchable and intelligible by supporting research across a large corpus of public documents. The objective is to reduce the effort involved in navigating administrative and parliamentary records, improve access to public information, and provide answer suggestions that remain traceable to their documentary sources. The implementation uses AI to search and synthesise information from more than 10,000 public documents, including answers to written parliamentary questions and main committee procedures, and presents results through a question-answer interface. The system generates proposed answers based on the underlying text and cites the documents used, while also warning users that generated responses are not legally binding and should be checked against the linked sources. At a conceptual level, PARLA combines retrieval, synthesis, and source referencing in one research assistant for public documentation. The impact includes quicker information retrieval, improved transparency through traceable sourcing, and better support for daily work in parliament and administration, while also making complex documentary repositories more usable for external stakeholders.

title: ABILITY - Improving the accessibility of digital images for blind users
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: For blind and visually impaired people, digital images often remain difficult to access in a meaningful way, because standard image analysis tools are typically designed around the assumptions and preferences of sighted users. This creates a gap between what current systems can technically describe and what users actually need in order to form an accurate and useful mental representation of visual content. The objective of this use case is to improve accessibility by developing image interpretation tools tailored to the needs, expectations, and sensory strategies of blind and visually impaired users, with these users involved directly as co-designers and evaluators. The implementation combines computer vision, large language models, and visual-assistant language models with extensive user studies, tactile interaction research, and iterative testing. The partners are also developing dedicated hardware, including a tactile tablet and a pin-display device capable of presenting simplified object outlines, zoomed elements, and other selected outputs derived from image analysis. The system concept therefore links multimodal models with tactile interfaces and user-centred evaluation methods. The anticipated results include more relevant and nuanced image descriptions, improved usability and trust, and a more inclusive digital experience. More broadly, the project supports accessible design innovation, stronger user adoption, and better alignment between emerging image technologies and real user needs.

title: A2I - Networked hearing system with innovative sensors
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: In audiological, occupational health, and cardiological care, clinicians often rely on fragmented observations and periodic assessments, which can limit their ability to identify emerging issues early and respond with appropriately tailored interventions. This is particularly relevant where hearing-related data may also provide insights into wider physiological conditions, yet such information is not routinely captured or connected across care pathways. The purpose of this use case is to create a user-centred socio-technical system that improves prevention, diagnosis, and care processes by using sensor-based data gathered in and around the ear. The implementation combines innovative hearing-related sensors with data analysis methods to process continuous or repeated health signals collected from wearable or ear-based devices. Analytical models are used to detect patterns relevant to audiological status, occupational exposure, and cardiological indicators, while the overall architecture links sensing technologies, health data processing, and evaluation workflows in a conceptually integrated system. The development approach is explicitly user-focused, ensuring that the technical design reflects clinical and practical needs. The expected impact includes earlier identification of health risks, better continuity of care, and more efficient clinical decision-making. Additional value lies in improved service integration, stronger preventive capacity, and the potential to scale monitoring and assessment across multiple healthcare contexts with greater reliability and personalisation.

title: RenovAlte - Resilient planning and design of renovation projects
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Building renovation projects frequently encounter delays, cost overruns and vulnerability to changing environmental conditions, undermining long-term sustainability objectives. RenovAIte aims to develop resilient planning methodologies for housing renovation and infrastructure maintenance through advanced simulation and data-driven analysis. The project creates a simulation environment capable of modelling renovation scenarios using sensor data and predictive analytics. Adversarial resilience learning techniques are applied to evaluate potential disruptions and optimise project design under uncertain conditions. The system supports decision-makers in selecting renovation strategies that minimise delays and reduce the need for premature re-renovation. Integrated monitoring of streets and buildings enhances situational awareness and long-term asset management. By combining simulation modelling with adaptive optimisation, the project strengthens robustness of renovation planning. Expected benefits include improved project efficiency, enhanced climate resilience and more sustainable use of public and private resources in the built environment.

title: FloReST - Intelligent tools for urban flood resilience
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Increasing frequency of heavy rainfall events has exposed urban areas to significant risks of flash flooding, causing damage to infrastructure and disrupting communities. Municipal authorities require tools to plan emergency drainage routes and improve resilience, but traditional hydraulic modelling approaches are complex, time-intensive, and difficult to scale. The FloReST project, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, aims to enhance urban flood resilience by providing decision-support tools tailored to local conditions. The solution combines hydraulic-numerical modelling with machine learning techniques to simulate and optimise emergency water drainage pathways across urban environments. These models are supported by data from terrain, infrastructure, and environmental sources, enabling scalable analysis of larger catchment areas. The project also includes user-oriented applications designed to support municipalities and infrastructure operators in planning and response. Pilot testing of a smart application with end users took place in 2024. The approach demonstrates improved modelling efficiency and usability, supporting better preparedness and risk mitigation, although full operational deployment remains under evaluation.

title: Albert France Services - GenAI tool to support public servants
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Front-line public-service advisers often need to consult large volumes of guidance and partner documentation in order to answer citizen questions accurately, which can slow down interviews and reduce the time available for direct support. Albert France Services was introduced to assist advisers in the France Services network by giving them quicker access to reliable information tailored to the user situation they are handling. The objective is to support public servants rather than replace them, improve the speed and consistency of responses, and make it easier to navigate the documentation used in day-to-day case support. The implementation forms part of the broader Albert initiative developed by DINUM and Etalab as a sovereign, open, and secure generative AI capability for public administration. In the France Services version, the tool uses a natural-language response engine that draws on documentation from France Services partners and practical fact sheets from servicepublic.fr, returning sourced answers in French through a search-style interface. More broadly, official materials describe Albert as an interministerial inference platform hosted in a secure sovereign environment. The impact includes faster retrieval of dependable information, better support for advisers handling varied citizen needs, and improved operational efficiency in front-line public service. It also creates a reusable model for scaled adoption of generative AI across administrations.

title: GenAI for Legislative Drafting - Ministry of Transports
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Legislative drafting requires civil servants to examine large volumes of legal, policy, and background material, making the process time-consuming and cognitively demanding, particularly when consistency, traceability, and language quality must be maintained throughout. In this context, the Ministry of Transport and Communications sought to improve the efficiency of drafting work while also reinforcing Finland’s strategic autonomy in digital capability. The objective of the use case was to test whether a practical support service could help drafters navigate legislative content more effectively and retrieve relevant information in a structured manner. The implementation consisted of a service demonstrator built by Futurice around Finnish-language large language models, delivered through a chatbot-style interface. At a conceptual level, the solution allowed legislative drafters to query legislation and related materials in natural language, with the model supporting information retrieval, question answering, and synthesis over large text collections. The system design explored how domestic language models could be incorporated into policy workflows while remaining aligned with public sector requirements. The results indicate potential for reducing time spent searching and reviewing documentation, improving accessibility of complex legal material, and supporting more efficient drafting processes. The wider business value includes strengthened experimentation capacity, greater technological sovereignty, and a foundation for more scalable digital support in public administration.

title: GenAI for Legislative Drafting - Prime Minister's Office
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Analysing statements submitted during consultation rounds is a demanding part of legislative preparation, as officials must review substantial volumes of written feedback, identify recurring themes, and produce coherent summaries under time pressure. This creates an operational challenge in terms of workload, speed, and consistency, especially when consultation material is extensive and diverse in style or content. The purpose of this use case was to assess whether automated support could help the Prime Minister’s Office process consultation responses more efficiently and accelerate the preparation of summary material for legislative work. The implementation tested the Finnish Poro language model in a summarisation setting, with the experiment carried out by Silo Gen AI Oy and funded by Sitra. At a conceptual level, the approach used a Finnish large language model to generate condensed summaries from consultation texts, exploring how language technology could support document analysis in a policy environment. The trial focused on the model’s ability to synthesise large volumes of textual input into usable outputs for expert review. The results showed clear potential for increasing efficiency in the analysis of consultation rounds, even though the summaries produced were not yet of sufficient quality for operational adoption. Even so, the exercise generated valuable learning on model limitations, future capability needs, and opportunities to improve productivity, scalability, and evidence handling in legislative processes.

title: LUMI - the Made-in-Europe chatbot for Heidelberg
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal residents often need simple guidance on everyday administrative matters, yet city websites can be difficult to navigate when users do not know the exact terminology or service path they need. Heidelberg introduced Lumi to create a more natural and convenient way for citizens to interact with the city through a chat-based interface rather than conventional menu navigation. The objective is to support citizens with routine administrative tasks, improve access to public information, and learn from real interactions in order to refine a more tailored digital-assistance service for the city. The implementation uses large language models developed by Heidelberg-based company Aleph Alpha and draws on publicly available information from the city of Heidelberg to generate responses. The city explains that Lumi can already help with issues such as changing address within Heidelberg or finding waste-paper collection times, and that after an internal testing phase it was opened to citizens so the system could learn what residents ask and how they phrase requests. At a conceptual level, the solution combines a public information base with an LLM-powered conversational interface designed for municipal use. The impact includes easier access to city information, a more intuitive user experience, and better scalability of first-line citizen support, while also giving the city a practical way to experiment with European AI capability in public services.

title: GPT-enabled chatbot of the Rhineland-Palatinate Development Agency
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Agencies that run many projects and programmes often hold relevant information across numerous internal and public materials, making it difficult for users to obtain quick, targeted answers about activities, tasks, and ongoing work. The Rhineland-Palatinate Development Agency addressed this issue by experimenting with an AI assistant that responds to questions about the agency’s projects and remit through its website. The objective is to improve access to organisational information, reduce the effort required to search through scattered material, and test how conversational interfaces can support communication about public development activity. The implementation uses a GPT-enabled assistant that has been specially configured with information about the agency’s own activities, rather than relying only on the general background knowledge of the underlying model. At a conceptual level, the system combines a large language model with agency-specific material to generate answers about projects and responsibilities through a web-based conversational interface. The impact includes easier access to relevant information, quicker resolution of routine informational queries, and a more user-friendly digital front door for stakeholders interested in the agency’s work. It also offers a practical model for limited-scope deployment of generative AI in public-sector communication and knowledge access.

title: ZüriCityGPT
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: People seeking information about city administration often face a familiar problem: official websites contain a great deal of useful content, but search and navigation do not always produce direct answers to practical questions. ZüriCityGPT addresses this by offering a conversational layer over publicly available information about Zurich, allowing users to ask questions in natural language and receive concise answers rather than a list of links alone. The objective is to make local administrative information easier to access, reduce friction in finding relevant guidance, and demonstrate how city-related public information can be made more usable through a question-answer interface. The implementation uses a chatbot grounded in content published on the City of Zurich website; public descriptions of the project explain that it can answer questions based on that material and also offers a version linked to the Swiss LLM Apertus. At a conceptual level, the solution combines retrieval over a defined public corpus with generative answering to provide more precise responses about city services and local administration. The impact includes a more accessible user experience, quicker access to relevant local information, and a scalable way to make complex city websites easier to use. Public project information also makes clear that the tool is Zurich-focused but not officially affiliated with the City of Zurich.

title: DutchCycling - Cycling Lifestyle AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Streets in many cities remain dominated by cars, limited greenery, and fragmented cycling infrastructure, making it difficult for residents and planners to imagine what a healthier, more bicycle-friendly street could look like in practice. The DutchCycling Lifestyle AI project addresses this challenge by giving people a simple way to visualise how an existing street might be transformed into a greener and more cycle-oriented environment inspired by Dutch design principles. The objective is to stimulate public imagination, support discussion on liveability and active mobility, and make the Dutch cycling approach more tangible for users anywhere in the world. The implementation combines generative AI with Google Street View imagery and the expertise of Dutch cycling specialists, allowing users to enter an address, select or upload a street view, and generate alternative visualisations of a more sustainable street layout. At a conceptual level, the tool links image-based generation with mobility-design knowledge to create plausible illustrative scenarios rather than detailed engineering plans. Public project material also makes clear that the tool was designed primarily as an inspiration device and that the concept has since been made open source after the original public tool was taken offline. The impact lies in widening public engagement, making policy ideas easier to communicate visually, and providing a scalable digital method for promoting cycling-friendly urban transformation.

title: IVORY – ‘AI for Vision Zero in Road Safety’
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Delft University of Technology Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management
source_description: Achieving major reductions in road fatalities requires more than isolated technical improvements, as road safety depends on the interaction between vehicles, infrastructure, human behaviour, governance, and public trust. In support of the United Nations target to halve traffic deaths by 2030 and the European Vision Zero strategy to eliminate road fatalities by 2050, this use case aims to build a robust framework for responsible innovation in road safety while developing specialist expertise across sectors. The stakeholders include universities, industrial partners, associated organisations, researchers, and road safety actors from ten countries. The implementation takes the form of an industrial doctoral network bringing together engineering, data science, and ethics of technology to develop new responsible AI applications for road-user assistance and infrastructure safety management. The programme integrates research training, cross-sector collaboration, and applied experimentation, with 13 researchers working on solutions that combine advanced analytical methods, domain knowledge, and governance considerations. Rather than a single product, the system is a coordinated innovation and learning platform designed to connect research outputs with real-world road safety needs. The expected impact includes stronger interdisciplinary capability, improved methods for safer transport systems, and a more scalable pipeline of expertise. It also creates long-term value through knowledge transfer, international collaboration, and more reliable foundations for future road safety innovation.

title: DIPLOMA Project - Electronic, Didactic and Innovative Platform for Learning based On Multimedia Assets
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The e-DIPLOMA project was initiated in response to challenges identified during the rapid transition to online learning caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, including disparities in access to technology, insufficient teacher training, and limitations in existing digital learning environments. The objective is to enhance the quality, inclusiveness, and effectiveness of distance education across Europe by developing a next-generation e-learning platform. The project adopts a co-creation approach involving educators, students, families, and policymakers to ensure that the platform addresses real user needs. The solution integrates multiple advanced technologies, including immersive environments, intelligent tutoring components, interactive content delivery, and conversational interfaces, to create engaging and adaptive learning experiences. It also incorporates analytics to monitor learning progress and personalise content. As an ongoing EU-funded research and innovation project, the platform is under development and validation. Expected impacts include improved learner engagement, accessibility, and pedagogical outcomes, although large-scale deployment results are not yet available.

title: Eduthek - The learning platform on AI for schools
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research ( BMBWF )
source_description: Schools need accessible, up-to-date teaching materials on artificial intelligence, yet many teachers and families lack the time or specialist expertise to assemble reliable resources independently. Austria’s Eduthek responds to this by providing a dedicated digital space within the Ministry’s wider learning platform where teachers, pupils, and parents can access curated material on AI in a structured and reusable format. The objective is to improve AI literacy in schools, support teaching on a fast-changing topic, and make high-quality educational resources easier to find and apply across different levels of schooling. The implementation uses the Eduthek platform as a central repository and delivery channel for learning content, with a specific AI focus area that is continuously expanded and updated. The official course page describes the section as an overview of freely available teaching materials for lower and upper secondary education, designed to help schools address both the opportunities and the challenges raised by AI in everyday life and work. At a conceptual level, the solution combines digital curation, thematic organisation, and open access to support classroom use without requiring each school to build its own material base. The impact includes broader access to AI-related teaching resources, more consistent support for educators, and a scalable way to strengthen digital and technological understanding across the school system.

title: Humphrey - AI tool to streamline public services, eliminate delays through improved data sharing, and reduce costs
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
source_description: Public services often suffer from fragmented data, repetitive administrative work, and slow internal processes, which can delay service delivery and reduce the time civil servants can spend on higher-value tasks. Humphrey was introduced by the UK government to address these operational bottlenecks across the civil service by improving productivity, reducing reliance on manual document handling, and supporting faster, more consistent decision-support processes. The objective is to modernise government operations, improve internal efficiency, and reduce costs through a shared suite of AI tools rather than isolated pilots in individual departments. The implementation consists of a family of government-built AI tools developed by the Incubator for AI for tasks such as summarisation, consultation analysis, and administrative support, with civil servants interacting through secure digital interfaces. Public government sources show that Humphrey has already been used to review consultation responses and, in 2025, was also trialled with 25 councils to support work in areas such as planning and social care, indicating that it has moved beyond concept stage into active experimentation and deployment. The impact includes faster processing of large document volumes, reduced administrative burden, improved scalability of internal government work, and potential savings in consultancy and operational costs, while also building a reusable AI capability across public administration.

title: GOV.UK App chatbot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
source_description: Citizens often need to interact with multiple government services through separate websites and processes, making routine tasks time-consuming and difficult to navigate. The GOV.UK App was created to simplify this experience by giving people a single mobile entry point to government services, while the associated GOV.UK Chat capability is intended to make complex information easier to access through conversational interaction. The objective is to improve usability, reduce friction in service navigation, and provide faster access to relevant guidance across government. The implementation combines the GOV.UK App with GOV.UK One Login and an AI-powered GOV.UK Chat feature that uses generative AI to answer questions based on GOV.UK guidance. Official UK sources state that GOV.UK Chat was piloted with 10,000 business users, answered almost 24,000 questions, achieved relevant answers in about 90 per cent of cases, and blocked all tested prompt-manipulation attempts; the government’s algorithmic transparency record also confirms it as an active GDS system. The impact includes more accessible digital public services, quicker resolution of routine information needs, and a more scalable way to guide users through government content, while creating a foundation for more personalised and proactive service delivery through the app.

title: AI Applications within INAIL
