source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Europe faces a strategic need for large language models and related infrastructure that are developed within its own technical, regulatory, and linguistic context rather than relying only on external providers. OpenGPT-X was created to cover the full generative-AI value chain, from training data and scalable GPU infrastructure to model development and practical prototypes, so that European actors could test and build productive use cases from the beginning. The objective is to advance research, strengthen digital sovereignty, and enable industry partners to explore practical generative-AI applications through proofs of concept and deployable models. The implementation was a consortium project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action from January 2022 to 31 March 2025, combining research institutions and industry partners. Official Fraunhofer sources confirm that the project has ended, while also showing that its outputs continue through model families such as Teuken and through published use-case and code materials. The impact includes open multilingual model assets, stronger European capability across the generative-AI stack, and reusable technical results that can support future industrial and public-sector applications even after the formal project period has finished.

title: GenerativeAI @ TEMS
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public-service media organisations need trustworthy, rights-aware ways to engage with generative AI, especially where questions of data use, attribution, verification, and audience trust directly affect their core mission. Within the Trusted European Media Data Space, the GenerativeAI @ TEMS activity addresses this by creating a framework for discussion and collaboration around the use of AI in media-data environments, with the EBU treating AI as a strategic priority. The objective is to help media actors adopt generative AI responsibly, protect rights and provenance, and ensure that high-quality media data can support trustworthy AI systems. The implementation is not a single chatbot or model, but a coordinated initiative involving publications, stakeholder engagement, data-space development, and collaboration with companies such as Mistral. Recent TEMS and EBU materials show that the topic remains active in 2025, including discussion of AI governance priorities and the role of TEMS as an enabler of trusted, rights-cleared media content for AI-related use cases. The impact lies in shaping governance, data access, and collaboration conditions for future AI deployment in public-service media, creating strategic value through standards, interoperability, and trusted data practices rather than through one direct end-user service.

title: GenerativeAI @ LDS
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Europe’s language-technology ecosystem needs much larger volumes of trustworthy language resources if it is to support strong multilingual LLMs and generative-AI applications across official, regional, and minority languages. The European Language Data Space addresses this challenge by building a data market and exchange infrastructure for language resources, with the generative-AI dimension focused on making those resources available as an enabler for European language technologies. The objective is to assemble a broad user and provider community, improve access to language data, and strengthen the foundations for a more inclusive European LLM and GenAI landscape. The implementation centres on the LDS platform and marketplace, which are being developed under the EU Data Strategy as infrastructure for sharing language data and models between public and private actors. Current official sources show that the platform is live, that versions continue to be released, and that the infrastructure and user group are still growing, which matches the description of an initiative still in build-out rather than fully complete. The impact includes improved availability of multilingual language resources, stronger support for European language technologies, and a more scalable market structure for exchanging data needed to train and improve future language models across Europe.

title: Virtual St. Peter's Basilica with Artificial Intelligence
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Historic and religious landmarks are often difficult to document, interpret, and open up fully to the public, especially in areas that are physically inaccessible or too fragile for close everyday access. The digital twin of St. Peter’s Basilica was created to address this by enabling pilgrims, visitors, historians, and preservation specialists to explore the site in a detailed virtual environment while also supporting conservation and communication goals linked to Jubilee 2025. The objective is to make the Basilica more accessible and understandable, extend public engagement beyond physical visits, and create a precise digital representation that can assist interpretation and preservation. The implementation combines photogrammetry, AI, and immersive digital presentation techniques to reconstruct the Basilica in 3D, including areas normally unavailable to visitors. The official platform presents this as an AI-powered digital experience, with interactive online exploration and related immersive exhibitions that connect history, art, and spirituality through a virtual model. At a conceptual level, the solution merges high-resolution capture, 3D modelling, and AI-assisted interpretation into a digital twin environment. The impact includes global access to an iconic cultural site, richer educational and visitor experiences, and a scalable model for using advanced digital reconstruction to support heritage accessibility and stewardship.

title: Decentralised Autonomous Organisation for freelance work
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Freelance work is often coordinated through fragmented platforms, informal governance, or conventional management structures that can increase transaction costs, create ambiguity over rules and payments, and weaken trust between contributors. In decentralised digital work environments, there is a need for new organisational models that allow teams to manage resources, responsibilities, and incentives transparently without relying on a fixed management hierarchy. The purpose of this use case is to provide a more efficient and trust-based operating model for freelance collaboration in Web3 settings, where work, reputation, and funding can be coordinated through programmable rules. The implementation is embodied in MINOS, a platform that operates as a decentralised autonomous organisation and uses blockchain-based code to define and enforce organisational rules. Its architecture is structured around domains and permissions, allowing teams, projects, or departments to organise work and control access to functions, while funding pots and expenditure units manage token-based payments. In parallel, a domain-specific reputation mechanism records the value of contributions over time, supports merit-based decision-making, and aligns reward distribution with recent participation. The impact includes lower coordination costs, stronger transparency in resource allocation, and more reliable collaboration across distributed freelance networks. It also improves organisational flexibility, supports scalable governance, and enables a more structured and incentive-compatible approach to digital work.

title: Digital Asset Platform
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Across Europe, smaller bond and equity issuances, especially those linked to SMEs and renewable-energy projects, often struggle to attract a broad investor base because traditional securities processes are costly, fragmented, and difficult to scale. A key challenge is to create an infrastructure that connects issuance, registration, custody, trading, and settlement more efficiently while remaining compatible with regulatory requirements and existing market structures. The objective of this use case is to reduce friction in capital formation and help address funding gaps by making tokenised securities easier to issue, manage, and trade. The implementation is delivered through NYALA’s Digital Asset Platform, built on the public Polygon PoS chain, which supports the minting, distribution, registration, and custody of tokenised securities while linking on-chain and off-chain ownership information. The platform functions conceptually as a back-end engine connecting investment platforms into a broader trading ecosystem under the DLT Pilot Regime, with off-chain trading through an existing multilateral trading facility and on-chain settlement infrastructure. It also integrates an e-money token for delivery-versus-payment and automated dividend distribution. The impact includes improved efficiency and transparency across the securities value chain, broader investor access to previously sub-scale instruments, and stronger scalability for digital capital markets. It also offers lower operational friction, faster settlement, and greater potential to mobilise financing for growth-oriented and sustainability-linked projects.

title: Verifiable Web for AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Many AI systems rely on external information sources that may be inaccurate, manipulated, or impossible to verify, creating risks around hallucinations, bias, provenance, and misuse of data. For public bodies, infrastructure operators, and large organisations, this weakens trust in generated outputs and limits the safe deployment of AI in knowledge-intensive environments where factual grounding and ownership of information matter. The goal of this use case is to create a more trustworthy foundation for AI by making source information discoverable, verifiable, and attributable across decentralised environments. The implementation is based on OriginTrail’s Decentralized Knowledge Graph, a permissionless network operating above a blockchain layer and designed to provide a trusted knowledge foundation for AI applications. Within this architecture, decentralised retrieval-augmented generation extends conventional RAG by organising external knowledge in a structured graph and associating it with provenance and ownership signals, thereby supporting neuro-symbolic decentralised AI. The technology is intended for a wide spectrum of uses, including industry, infrastructure, science, and misinformation-related applications, and conceptually integrates decentralised data publishing, knowledge graph structuring, and AI retrieval workflows. The impact includes more reliable generated content, stronger resistance to manipulation, and improved transparency about where information comes from. It also supports scalable knowledge sharing, incentivises data ownership, and increases the business value of AI systems that depend on auditable, high-integrity information.

title: Trrue Chain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Impact investment and ESG-linked fundraising frequently suffer from high transaction friction, fragmented compliance processes, and persistent concerns about the credibility of sustainability claims. Investors, project sponsors, and regulators all need mechanisms that improve trust, reduce cost, and maintain legal certainty without losing the benefits of digital infrastructure. The purpose of this use case is to optimise fundraising for impact-focused projects by combining distributed-ledger technology with governance mechanisms that support ethical standards and regulatory compliance. The implementation is centred on Trrue Chain, a blockchain infrastructure designed to verify on-chain data through a network of trusted participants while preserving legal relationships required for regulated financial activity. Built with Polkadot Substrate and Cumulus, the system enables interoperability across blockchains and is intended to connect traditional financial markets with Web3 environments. At a conceptual level, it combines governance protocols, verification layers, and interoperable digital-asset tooling to support compliant fundraising and help address greenwashing risks in financial services. The expected impact includes faster and more secure fundraising processes, lower operational cost than traditional systems, and improved confidence in the quality and integrity of impact investment data. It also supports scalability for responsible investment ecosystems and creates business value by making ESG-positive projects easier to finance within a more transparent and regulation-aware framework.

title: Tokenization and fractional ownership of real estate and RWAs
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Access to high-value assets such as commercial property and other real-world assets has historically been limited to institutional investors and wealthy individuals, largely because of high entry thresholds, illiquidity, and complex transaction structures. This restricts participation, narrows sources of capital, and reduces the flexibility with which assets can be financed or traded. The objective of this use case is to widen access to asset-backed investment opportunities by enabling fractional ownership and more liquid participation in real estate and other tokenised real-world assets. The implementation is provided through REClosure’s financial technology platform, which tokenises underlying assets and divides ownership into digital units that can be offered to a broader investor base, including retail participants. At a conceptual level, the platform links asset tokenisation, ownership representation, and marketplace trading functions so that value derived from rental returns or asset appreciation can be associated with fractional digital holdings. The example presented for the sandbox describes a €20 million office property split into 500 units of €20,000, illustrating how tokenisation can lower barriers to entry while preserving tradability. The impact includes broader investor inclusion, improved liquidity for traditionally illiquid assets, and greater flexibility in capital raising. It also supports more scalable market participation, expands access to diversified investments, and increases the efficiency with which real-world assets can be financed and exchanged.

title: Certificate Management System for the Global Trade dominium
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Global trade still depends heavily on fragmented document flows, repeated data entry, manual validation, and paper-based certificates, creating delays, fraud risks, and weak visibility across logistics, mobility, and supply-chain operations, particularly in sensitive sectors such as food and agriculture. The purpose of this use case is to create a more trustworthy, efficient, and scalable way for businesses, authorities, and supply-chain partners to exchange, sign, verify, and track certificates and related trade documents while reducing operational friction and improving compliance. The implementation is based on a fully automated certificate management system developed by ReLOG3P and Morpheus.Network. At a conceptual level, it combines a cloud-based self-service portal, an integrated document-handling database, digitisation tools such as OCR and uploaders, and digital sign-off capabilities, with blockchain back ends on Ethereum and Hyperledger plus IPFS-based immutable trails. Each uploaded document receives a decentralised unique identifier and a timestamped provenance record containing creation, access, signature, and revision data, while APIs allow integration with authorities and ERP systems. The impact includes faster shipment execution, improved supplier management, proactive alerts for non-compliant or expiring certificates, reduced delays and rework, and stronger traceability. It also increases trust in document authenticity, supports food and goods safety, lowers operating costs, and provides a scalable foundation for more transparent and compliant global trade processes.

title: Universal trust registry
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: As digital identity, verifiable credentials, and Web3 services expand, public bodies, businesses, and regulators face a growing challenge in determining who can be trusted to issue, verify, and rely on digital attestations across different technical environments. Existing trust frameworks are often tied to specific ledgers or ecosystems, which limits interoperability and makes it harder to prepare for regulatory frameworks such as eIDAS 2.0, the European Digital Identity ecosystem, and related digital-market requirements. The objective of this use case is to create a more flexible and portable model for managing trusted accreditation structures across distributed environments, so that institutions can operate trusted lists and trust chains without being locked into a single ledger. The implementation is being developed by a consortium led by Soverio with cheqd, Danube Tech, and Netis. At a conceptual level, the solution uses a ledger-agnostic architecture for trust registries and sequential, traversable lists of verifiable accreditations built on distributed-ledger infrastructure, drawing on DID Core and DID URL practices and extending the EBSI trust-chain model into a broader universal trust registry approach. The expected impact includes stronger interoperability across identity ecosystems, improved readiness for future regulatory compliance, and easier cross-platform trust management. It also offers greater scalability for digital credential ecosystems, lower integration friction, and more robust foundations for trusted digital services in both public and commercial settings.

title: Hosted Wallets Services for non-crypto-asset / non financial related tokens
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Organisations using tokenisation for everyday services such as event tickets, museum access, proof-of-attendance records, or fan engagement often face a regulatory problem: although their tokens are not financial instruments or crypto-assets under MiCAR, the hosted wallets embedded in their applications may still technically receive, hold, or transfer crypto-assets, including for transaction fees. This creates uncertainty, potential compliance burdens, and a risk that firms using distributed-ledger technology could face significantly higher operational costs than competitors delivering similar services through non-blockchain technologies. The aim of this use case is to clarify how such wallet services can be provided on a level playing field while preserving innovation in non-financial token use. The implementation is being explored by the 2Tokens consortium with partners including Amdax, Custodiex, Celebratix, Metaseum, TDE, and CMS. Conceptually, the solution examines hosted or white-label wallet models for non-financial tokens, alongside the possibility of lighter regulatory treatment or exemptions, while still accommodating the technical reality that wallets may need to process network fees or hold transferable digital assets. The impact could include lower compliance friction, reduced cost barriers for service providers, and more viable adoption of token-based services in mainstream cultural and consumer applications. It also supports regulatory clarity, fairer competition, and greater scalability for digital-token services whose primary purpose lies outside financial markets.

title: Three judges under suspicion of ‘cheating’ with artificial intelligence
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: This case is not a public-service innovation project in the usual sense, but rather a controversy about the alleged use of generative AI in judicial drafting, which raises questions about transparency, accountability, and the acceptable role of automated tools in the justice system. In Portugal, suspicion arose after an appeal-court ruling reportedly contained odd phrasing and citations that lawyers argued might have been produced with the help of an AI system, prompting scrutiny of whether judges had relied on such tools in preparing a decision. The issue matters because courts depend on trust, legal accuracy, and human responsibility, and any use of AI in judicial reasoning or drafting can affect confidence in the integrity of judgments. The reported implementation, insofar as it can be described as one, would have involved a judge or judges using a general-purpose generative AI assistant to help produce legal text rather than a formally authorised court system integrated into judicial workflow. Public reporting indicates that the judges disputed the allegations and that the matter led to official discussion and inquiry rather than confirmation of an endorsed technology solution. The impact of the episode lies in highlighting governance risks: it intensified debate about standards for AI use in courts, the need for human oversight, and the importance of clear rules on whether and how judges may use generative tools.

title: LLM-Based Agents for User Story Quality Enhancement in Agile Development
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: In agile software development, poorly specified user stories can reduce productivity, create misunderstandings and increase rework. Austrian Post Group IT explored automated approaches to enhance user story quality within development teams. An Autonomous LLM-based Agent System was implemented with specialised agent roles reflecting Product Owner and Requirements Engineer perspectives. Large language models were employed to analyse, rewrite and refine user stories, improving clarity, structure and acceptance criteria. The system operated within existing agile workflows, providing iterative suggestions while preserving contextual alignment. Evaluation by 11 professionals across six agile teams indicated significant improvements in comprehensibility and consistency, although challenges related to optimal story length and contextual precision were identified. The initiative demonstrates how structured language model agents can augment requirements engineering processes, enhance collaboration and improve overall software development quality through targeted automation support.

title: Camilla, Virtual assistant for public competitions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public recruitment processes often generate very high volumes of candidate questions, and applicants can struggle to interpret open notices, timelines, procedures, and requirements without waiting for manual replies. Camilla was introduced by Formez, in collaboration with CSI Piemonte, to make information about public competitions easier to access and to reduce response times for people interested in ongoing calls. The objective is to provide always-available guidance, improve the applicant experience, and streamline the handling of repetitive questions in a high-demand recruitment environment. The implementation uses a generative-AI virtual assistant accessible through a dedicated web interface, trained and tested extensively by a Formez task force with technical support from CSI Piemonte. Formez reported that the tool went live on an experimental basis after more than 500 tests and that it operates 24/7 to answer questions about competitions managed by the institute; later reporting stated that it had already served over 5,000 users and handled around 22,000 questions, and that its scope had expanded to include ranking-related queries. At a conceptual level, the solution combines generative answering with institution-specific recruitment information in a public-facing assistant. The impact includes faster applicant support, lower pressure on manual help channels, and a scalable way to improve access to public competition information.

title: Streamlining and digitization of the export process
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Export procedures frequently involve repetitive data sharing, paper-based documentation, fragmented communication between stakeholders, and manual checks that increase processing time, create opportunities for document forgery, and reduce visibility across the supply chain. For exporters, logistics providers, and public authorities, this leads to avoidable administrative effort and slower trade execution, especially when compliance, document authenticity, and secure information exchange must be maintained across organisational boundaries. The objective of this use case is to redesign the export process so that it becomes more digital, more secure, and more efficient from end to end. The implementation, developed by VERAG Spedition AG with Atez Yazılım Teknolojileri A.Ş., uses a hybrid distributed-ledger architecture with a custom DLT layer that allows permissioned enterprise participants to build applications and execute smart contracts for eligible users while complying with regulatory and KYC requirements. Encryption technologies protect confidentiality and integrity, and APIs and integration tools connect the solution with existing networks to support interoperable data exchange. The proof of concept delivered a 40% reduction in work steps, enabled paperless transactions, and removed intermediaries from certain processes. The broader impact includes stronger traceability, lower fraud risk, better cooperation among stakeholders, and reduced environmental burden through dematerialisation. It also improves operational speed, cuts administrative cost, and provides a scalable route towards more resilient and transparent export operations.

title: Digital Gilt Instrument
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Government bond issuance relies on mature but highly structured market infrastructure that can involve manual processes, fragmented records, and limited programmability across trading, settlement, and post-trade activities. In that context, the UK government is testing whether a digitally native sovereign debt instrument can modernise capital-market operations while preserving market integrity and fitting within an appropriate regulatory framework. The objective of this use case is to explore how distributed-ledger infrastructure can be applied across the full lifecycle of a sovereign debt issuance and to stimulate wider adoption of such infrastructure in UK capital markets. The implementation takes the form of the Digital Gilt Instrument pilot, jointly managed by HM Treasury and the UK Debt Management Office, with issuance planned on a platform operating within the Digital Securities Sandbox. Conceptually, the instrument is a new, short-dated, transferable government security held on a DLT platform, designed to test on-chain settlement, over-the-counter trading functionality, interoperability with traditional and DLT-based market participants, and greater transparency of ownership and transaction records. The expected impact includes faster and more automated market processes, stronger auditability, and reduced reliance on manual reconciliation. More broadly, the pilot is intended to improve efficiency, security, and resilience in capital markets, support innovation in digital financial infrastructure, and create a scalable foundation for future forms of digitally issued public debt.

title: Route and shift planning with AI in the health and elderly area
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Denmark’s route and shift planning initiative aims to improve the organisation of home care and home nursing across municipalities. The operational problem is that planning citizen visits, staff shifts and travel routes in elderly and health care is administratively heavy, complex and time-consuming, especially where municipalities must manage workforce constraints and changing care needs. The initiative supports implementation and dissemination of AI-based solutions for route and shift planning, with the objective of improving resource management and ensuring better planning of visits, duty rosters and home-care routes. Its implementation is organised through municipal implementation partnerships and focuses not only on technical systems, but also on competencies, organisational change and collection of lessons from participating municipalities. Conceptually, the system applies optimisation and predictive planning to match staff availability, care visits, geography, time windows and service constraints. The expected impact is more efficient use of personnel, reduced administrative workload, improved continuity of care and better planning quality for citizens receiving home-based services. The initiative receives DKK 22.8 million in funding.

title: AI-enabled speech-to-text in the health and elderly area
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Denmark’s speech-to-text initiative aims to reduce the documentation burden for staff working in health, home care and elderly services. The operational problem is that employees spend substantial time producing care records and placing documentation correctly in municipal IT systems, which can reduce time available for direct citizen care. The initiative focuses on developing and testing an AI-supported solution that converts audio recordings into medical-record text and helps staff decide where the generated content should be placed in the municipal system. It builds partly on experience from Thisted Municipality and will involve Copenhagen, Aarhus, Aalborg and other municipalities. Conceptually, the system combines speech recognition, natural language processing, documentation assistance and workflow guidance for municipal care records. The expected impact is faster record creation, improved documentation quality, less administrative pressure on care staff and more consistent placement of information in municipal systems. The initiative receives DKK 8.5 million in funding and forms part of Denmark’s wider effort to scale practical AI solutions across municipalities. A related Danish TALT speech-recognition project has reportedly shown time savings and is ready for national roll-out, suggesting that the policy area is moving from testing towards broader implementation.

title: ROSE - Route optimisation module for waste logistic platforms - Montana (BG) pilot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal waste collection often runs on fixed schedules that do not reflect actual container fill levels, leading to unnecessary journeys, higher operating costs, avoidable fuel use, and excess emissions. For municipalities and waste-management operators, this creates both a financial and an environmental burden, especially where available operational data is underused and vehicle routing is not dynamically aligned with real needs. The aim of this use case is to improve the efficiency and sustainability of urban waste collection by ensuring that collections take place only when needed and with the most suitable routing and vehicle allocation. The implementation, led by Theoremus, uses an advanced logistics routing engine that clusters waste containers according to historical fill rates, assigns the most appropriate vehicles to each cluster, and optimises collection schedules using transport data patterns. The solution builds on Digital Waste Monitoring Platforms and has been deployed in Cascais and Montana within a trans-European project context. The results are already measurable: the project anticipated a 10–20% reduction in miles driven and operating cost, and in the Montana pilot weekly collection distance fell by 10.2%, from 173.03 km to 155.36 km, with fuel consumption and CO₂ emissions reduced by a similar margin. This improves operational performance, lowers congestion and heavy-vehicle presence on local streets, and creates stronger long-term value through more data-driven and scalable waste-management practices.

title: ROSE - Route optimisation module for waste logistic platforms - Cascais (PT) pilot
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Waste collection services face constant pressure to reduce costs, emissions and congestion while maintaining reliable collection standards across urban areas. Traditional collection routes can be inefficient when they do not reflect the actual fill levels of containers or the most suitable deployment of available vehicles, leading to unnecessary mileage, wasted time and avoidable fuel consumption. ROSE addresses this operational problem by helping municipalities organise waste collection more intelligently and only when necessary. The stakeholders include city authorities, waste-management operators and logistics planners, with the objective of improving the efficiency and sustainability of collection operations through smarter route design and scheduling. The solution is implemented as an advanced logistics routing engine that clusters waste containers on the basis of historical fill-rate patterns, assigns the most appropriate vehicles to each cluster and optimises collection schedules using transport data. At a conceptual level, the module combines route optimisation, demand forecasting and vehicle-assignment logic, building on Theoremus’ experience with Digital Waste Monitoring Platforms and integrating with broader waste-logistics workflows. The system is being deployed in Cascais and Montana, demonstrating its applicability across different urban contexts. The expected impact is fewer vehicle miles travelled, lower operational time and reduced costs, together with lower fuel consumption, emissions and traffic burden. More broadly, ROSE improves scalability, supports cleaner urban operations and creates value through more data-driven and sustainable waste-management practices.

title: AI MOVE - AI mobility optimisation and vehicle efficiency for public transport
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Many public-transport-priority systems still rely on transponders installed on vehicles communicating with traffic lights, a set-up that typically benefits only municipal operators and excludes other high-occupancy services. This limits the effectiveness of traffic prioritisation in increasingly mixed mobility environments where demand-responsive transport and other non-municipal providers also play an important role. AI MOVE addresses this gap by seeking to make urban traffic management more inclusive and efficient across a broader set of public and shared transport vehicles. The stakeholders include transport authorities, public-transport operators, demand-responsive providers and city traffic managers, with the objective of reducing congestion and improving journey efficiency by extending priority mechanisms beyond traditional municipal fleets. The solution is implemented through enhanced CCTV systems deployed at intersections and transit zones, using computer vision to recognise high-occupancy vehicles and support dynamic prioritisation through existing infrastructure. At a conceptual level, the system combines video analytics, vehicle-recognition models and traffic-signal integration to identify eligible vehicles in real time and adapt signal behaviour accordingly. This approach avoids the limitations of hardware installed only on selected vehicles and creates a more flexible foundation for priority management. The expected impact is improved traffic flow for public transport, more cost-effective use of existing infrastructure and broader coverage across transport providers. More broadly, the project enhances urban mobility efficiency, supports scalable traffic management and creates value through reduced congestion and more equitable prioritisation.

title: URBANITE - AI-driven insights to optimise public transport systems
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public-transport planning has often depended on surveys and interviews, which are valuable but slow, expensive and limited in their ability to capture real, constantly changing mobility patterns across a city. As a result, transport authorities and operators may lack the detailed and timely evidence needed to understand current demand, anticipate future shifts and optimise multimodal services effectively. URBANITE addresses this challenge by providing cities and transport organisations with a richer, more dynamic understanding of how people actually move. The stakeholders include municipalities, public transport authorities and public transport operators, with the objective of improving operational planning, anticipating future demand and supporting the creation of safer and more sustainable urban mobility systems. The solution is implemented through the integration of historical data, GPS traces, mobile-network information and passenger data, analysed using advanced modelling techniques to reconstruct and predict mobility demand across buses, trams, trains and bicycles. At a conceptual level, the platform combines data fusion, predictive analytics and movement modelling to produce actionable insights into both present and future transport needs. These outputs can then support network design, service planning and operational adjustment. The expected impact is more precise planning, better alignment between services and demand, and reduced reliance on costly traditional data collection. More broadly, URBANITE improves scalability in mobility analysis, enhances decision quality and creates value through more efficient, sustainable and user-responsive public transport systems.

title: SAFELIGHT project: Analysis of visibility in roads and streets during the night to avoid accidents of vulnerable users
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Municipality of Las Rozas de Madrid
source_description: Many urban locations, such as pedestrian crossings, cycle lanes and narrow pavements near traffic, become especially hazardous at night when poor visibility increases the risk of accidents for vulnerable road users. Municipalities often struggle to identify these lighting-related risks systematically, and conventional inspection methods may not be frequent or detailed enough to support timely maintenance decisions. SAFELIGHT addresses this challenge by helping cities detect high-risk locations and improve illumination where it matters most for safety. The stakeholders include host cities, road-maintenance teams, mobility planners and vulnerable users such as pedestrians and cyclists, with the objective of reducing night-time accident risk through better-targeted lighting interventions that can be integrated into ordinary maintenance operations. The solution is implemented through the Autonomous Urban Inspector for Lighting, which analyses road and street visibility using data collected in the urban environment and automatically identifies locations where conditions are unsafe. At a conceptual level, the system combines automated inspection, risk assessment and recommendation functions, after which Flash Lighting proposes the most suitable technical responses for each site. A second inspection is then carried out once lighting changes are implemented in order to validate the improvement in visibility. The expected impact is more precise identification of dangerous locations, more efficient maintenance planning and better evidence for safety interventions. More broadly, SAFELIGHT creates value by providing a scalable, operationally usable method for improving urban lighting and helping reduce accidents involving vulnerable road users.

title: DO IT SMARTer - An AI-based Management and Control System for Energy in Public Buildings
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: DO IT SMARTer addresses the need to optimise energy flows in buildings through an AI-based management and control system, with demonstration sites in Romania and Norway. The operational problem is that public, residential and educational buildings often consume energy inefficiently, while building managers require practical tools to reduce consumption, costs and carbon intensity without compromising comfort. The project is an industrial and experimental research cooperation focused on cognitive energy-management techniques. Its implementation aims to design, develop and test energy-management and control algorithms, including monitoring and targeting, measurement and verification, and optimisation tools for smart buildings. The system is demonstrated in three pilot buildings and seeks to reach technology readiness levels 6–7. Conceptually, the solution combines building-energy monitoring, data analytics, AI-based control logic, optimisation of energy flows and integration with heating or power-to-heat technologies. The expected impact is improved energy efficiency, lower operational costs and reduced carbon intensity in public and residential buildings. The project’s stated objectives include reducing household energy consumption and costs by up to 20%, while also supporting bilateral cooperation between Romanian and Norwegian partners in energy management research.

title: BgGPT – a cutting-edge Bulgarian artificial intelligence integrates in Municipality of Burgas' services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Burgas Municipality introduced BgGPT to improve access to municipal information and services for citizens and businesses, becoming the first Bulgarian municipality to deploy the Bulgarian AI system in local administration. The administrative problem is that citizens often need to navigate municipal decisions, registers, signals, service pages and responsible municipal companies, which can be fragmented and difficult to search. BgGPT is intended to make these materials easier to understand and use. The implementation has two main functions. First, it synthesises decisions of the Burgas Municipal Council and presents them in summarised form, indexed by topics and sessions. Second, an AI chatbot is planned for the municipal website to direct users to the correct electronic service or provide direct information on signals, elections, municipal registers and responsible municipal entities. Conceptually, the system combines Bulgarian-language generative AI, document summarisation, topic indexing, conversational interaction and service-routing functions. The expected impact is improved transparency of local-government decisions, easier access to administrative services, better-informed residents and reduced pressure on staff handling repetitive information requests. By applying a national-language model in a municipal setting, the pilot also demonstrates how locally developed AI can be adapted to public-service delivery.

title: Smart Burgas - integrated platform for urban data
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Smart Burgas brings together data from smart devices and urban systems to improve the monitoring, transparency and management of the city environment. The municipal challenge is that modern cities generate information across transport, infrastructure, environment, services and public spaces, but this data can remain fragmented if it is not integrated into a common platform. Residents, visitors, municipal departments, city managers and service operators are the principal stakeholders. The platform is designed to help the municipality observe what is happening in the city, facilitate control, improve service organisation and make urban information more visible to the public. Its implementation consists of an integrated monitoring platform that collects and displays data from smart devices and systems operating in Burgas. Conceptually, the solution combines urban sensing, data aggregation, dashboard visualisation, public information tools and service-management support. By enabling residents and guests to observe city conditions more easily, it also contributes to transparency and civic awareness. The expected impact is improved quality of life, better coordination of municipal services, more responsive urban management and stronger evidence for decision-making. For the administration, integrated urban data can help identify problems, monitor performance and allocate resources more effectively. For citizens and visitors, the platform provides a clearer view of local conditions and supports more informed interaction with the city.

title: Smart Public Lighting in City of Sveta Nedelja (Croatia)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Sveta Nedelja smart public lighting pilot tested how existing public lighting infrastructure could become a platform for energy management, environmental monitoring and urban sensing. The municipal problem is that public lighting is a major operational asset, but conventional lighting systems offer limited remote control, monitoring or capacity to generate wider city data. The pilot aimed to improve energy efficiency, quality of life, public safety and reduction of light pollution. The implementation, developed with HT Group, connected 80 control and communication modules to existing lighting poles. The solution can operate across several network technologies, including 3G, 4G, 5G and NB-IoT, and is applicable to different types of public lighting. The smart poles enabled remote wireless monitoring and control of lamps, measurement of energy indicators, and additional sensing functions such as temperature, humidity, pressure, UV radiation, air quality, pedestrian passage and traffic noise. Conceptually, the system combines IoT connectivity, smart lighting control, environmental sensing, remote monitoring and city-data collection. The expected impact is reduced energy use, better maintenance insight, improved environmental monitoring and a foundation for broader Smart City services using existing infrastructure.

title: Enaibler - AI for ethical policies and services across European regions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: European Regions Network for the Application of Communications Technology (ERNACT)
source_description: Public authorities increasingly recognise the strategic importance of advanced digital technologies, yet many regional and local administrations still lack the practical capacity, frameworks and confidence needed to translate this potential into better public policies and services. ENAIBLER addresses that institutional challenge by helping public-sector organisations across Europe strengthen their readiness to adopt advanced tools in an open, transparent and ethically grounded way. The project brings together nine partners from six EU regions, including regional and local authorities, development agencies and a university, all of whom are involved in shaping or supporting policy instruments linked to digital transformation. Its objective is to empower the public sector to unlock the benefits of these technologies while improving the quality, ethics and transparency of the services and policies delivered to citizens. The solution is implemented through interregional cooperation, policy learning and capacity-building activities aimed at supporting organisations in the design and adoption of appropriate approaches. At a conceptual level, the project combines policy exchange, institutional support and shared experimentation to help partners strengthen governance, implementation capability and ethical practice across their territories. The expected impact is better-informed public administrations, stronger regional policy instruments and more responsible deployment of advanced digital services. More broadly, ENAIBLER creates value by improving public-sector capability, supporting trustworthy innovation and helping regions embed more transparent and citizen-oriented approaches to digital transformation.

title: AI4Citizens - Supporting ethical and effective AI governance in European cities and regions
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cities and regions face growing pressure to modernise public services through advanced digital technologies, but adoption can be hindered by uncertainty around governance, ethics, risk management and the practical design of enabling policy mechanisms. AI4Citizens addresses this challenge by helping local and regional governments strengthen their ability to introduce such technologies safely and effectively, while ensuring that implementation serves the public interest. The stakeholders include local and regional policymakers, public-sector organisations and partner institutions engaged in interregional cooperation, with the objective of improving and creating policy mechanisms that support responsible adoption and, in turn, enhance citizens’ wellbeing and regional vitality. The solution is implemented through interregional exchange, co-creation and learning processes focused on good practices, innovative solutions and governance models relevant to public-sector deployment. At a conceptual level, the project draws on key elements of governance frameworks and implementation processes, enabling partners to compare approaches, identify gaps and develop policy improvements suited to their own institutional contexts. This process is designed not merely to share examples, but to drive concrete policy change and better governance arrangements. The expected impact is stronger governance capacity, more robust and ethical policy instruments and improved readiness for adoption at local and regional level. More broadly, AI4Citizens creates value by supporting safer innovation, more coherent public-sector transformation and a more trustworthy relationship between digital progress and citizen benefit.

title: AI Sandbox in the Košice Self-Governing Region (KSK) - Xploro application
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Innovation Center of the Košice Region (ICKK)
source_description: The Košice Self-Governing Region’s AI Sandbox provides a controlled environment for testing artificial intelligence solutions within regional public-administration infrastructure, and Xploro was one of the selected applications in its first cycle. The broader operational problem is that public administrations often need to experiment with innovative technologies while managing legal, technical and organisational risks before wider adoption. The sandbox, initiated by the Innovation Center of the Košice Region, gives companies, universities and start-ups a structured route to test solutions for public services and internal processes. Participants undergo benefit analysis, technical evaluation, feasibility assessment and legal compliance review. Xploro specifically addresses tourism and visitor experience by providing an AI-supported guide that recommends places of interest and delivers information in audio or text form. Conceptually, the application combines location-aware guidance, recommendation functions, natural language content delivery and digital tourism support. The expected impact is twofold: for the regional administration, the sandbox strengthens capacity to evaluate AI tools responsibly before deployment; for tourism users, Xploro can simplify travel, enrich visits and improve access to information about sites. The inaugural sandbox attracted more than ten applications, with two selected for testing, indicating a selective and structured experimentation process. The project’s value lies in combining innovation testing with public-sector governance and practical service improvement.

title: AI Sandbox in the Košice Self-Governing Region (KSK) - Recruapplication
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Innovation Center of the Košice Region (ICKK)
source_description: Recru was selected for testing within the Košice Self-Governing Region’s AI Sandbox, a controlled and educational framework created to experiment with artificial intelligence solutions in public-administration settings. The institutional challenge is to improve the digitalisation of regional services and internal processes while ensuring that new tools are assessed for benefits, technical feasibility, implementation readiness and legal compliance before broader deployment. The main stakeholders include the Innovation Center of the Košice Region, the regional administration, participating companies, universities, start-ups, HR teams and applicants who may interact with recruitment processes. Recru focuses on human resources, offering a modern recruitment-management solution intended to simplify and accelerate the hiring process. The implementation is designed to support employers across recruitment tasks, enabling them to focus more directly on candidates. Conceptually, the tool may combine candidate management, workflow automation, recruitment analytics, communication support and AI-assisted processing of hiring information, although the specific technical modules are not detailed in the information provided. The expected impact is faster recruitment administration, more structured candidate handling and reduced repetitive workload for employers. Within the sandbox, the broader value is the ability to test such a system safely in a regional public-sector environment. Since more than ten solutions applied and two were selected, Recru’s inclusion indicates that it met the initial benefit, feasibility and compliance screening requirements.

title: LifeSaver - enhancing medical services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: LifeSaver aims to strengthen Estonia’s emergency medical services by improving resource allocation, service-area design and system-wide preparedness through data-driven and predictive tools. The operational challenge is that emergency medical systems must respond quickly under uncertain and changing demand, while ensuring that ambulances, staff, dispatch arrangements and service areas are organised effectively. The project focuses on modernising life-saving assistance by using predictive analytics, real-time monitoring and transparent system insights to support faster and more effective emergency responses. The implementation includes the LifeSaver Intelligence Platform and a comprehensive review of Estonia’s emergency medical system by international experts. The platform supports analysis of response patterns, demand forecasting, resource optimisation and identification of improvement projects. The LifeSaver programme identified ten potential innovation projects, from which the Estonian government selected five for future implementation. Conceptually, the initiative combines operational EMS data, predictive modelling, service-area analysis, monitoring dashboards and strategic planning for emergency care. The expected impact is better allocation of emergency resources, faster response capability, improved patient outcomes and stronger public-sector innovation capacity. Estonia was the first country to work with International SOS and Airbus Helicopters on the LifeSaver programme.

title: BrAIn – BRinging Artificial INtelligence towards SMEs
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: BrAIn supports SMEs in the Danube Region in understanding, adopting and benefiting from artificial intelligence and Industry 4.0 technologies as part of a transition towards more sustainable and human-centric Industry 5.0 models. The regional problem is that SMEs across the Danube area face uneven digital maturity, labour shortages, cost pressures, industrial transformation and limited internal capacity to adopt advanced technologies. The project therefore focuses on knowledge transfer, skills development and targeted transnational interventions in sectors such as manufacturing, agrofood, healthcare and sustainable energy. The implementation is structured as an Interreg Danube Region project that equips stakeholders and SMEs with AI-related knowledge, supports pilot solutions and builds on previous regional innovation results. Conceptually, the initiative combines capacity building, technology transfer, pilot experimentation, stakeholder networking and sector-specific AI adoption support. The expected impact is improved SME competitiveness, stronger readiness for Industry 5.0, more balanced regional development and better alignment between AI adoption and economic, environmental and social sustainability. By working across the Danube Region, BrAIn addresses the fact that AI capability gaps are not only technological, but also organisational, skills-based and territorial.

title: iTranSys - Public Transport Optimisation Powered by AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Považská Bystrica adopted iTranSys to improve the planning and operation of public transport in a town of around 40,000 residents. The main operational pressure was the combination of driver shortages and inefficient scheduling, which can increase costs, reduce service reliability and negatively affect passenger satisfaction. The stakeholders include the City of Považská Bystrica, public transport operators, drivers, passengers, municipal planners and residents who rely on local mobility services. The objective is to make route and timetable planning more efficient while maintaining or improving service quality. The implementation uses an AI-powered optimisation tool that automates aspects of public transport planning, including timetable generation and route scheduling. Conceptually, the system can analyse passenger demand, operational constraints, available drivers, route structures and service-frequency requirements to generate more efficient transport plans. By supporting automated scenario analysis and schedule optimisation, it reduces dependence on manual planning and allows the municipality to respond more flexibly to capacity constraints. The reported impact includes significant annual financial savings, improved passenger satisfaction and reduced per capita CO₂ emissions. These results suggest that the tool delivers both operational and environmental value by using resources more efficiently, improving service attractiveness and supporting more sustainable urban mobility.

title: LUCID – Data intelligence for cities and urban logistics
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: LUCID develops a data-driven platform to improve urban logistics by optimising routes, reducing congestion and improving the use of loading and unloading spaces. The operational challenge is that freight and last-mile logistics contribute significantly to urban congestion, emissions and fuel consumption, while cities and operators often lack a shared evidence base for managing delivery flows. The project integrates public city data and private logistics-operator data to provide real-time insights for both city planners and logistics actors. Its implementation uses advanced analytics and machine-learning methods to support route planning, operational decision-making and more efficient allocation of urban logistics infrastructure. Pilot testing is foreseen in Madrid, Las Rozas and Prague, with logistics operators involved to validate the platform in real-world settings. Conceptually, LUCID combines data integration, predictive analytics, route optimisation, loading-space intelligence and city-dashboard functionality. The expected impact is lower delivery costs, reduced environmental footprint, less congestion and better planning capacity for local authorities. By bringing together public and private data, the project supports a more coordinated model of urban logistics management in rapidly growing cities.

title: SmartDriveAI - digitising accident reporting
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: SmartDriveAI was developed to modernise accident reporting in public transport by replacing slow, paper-based processes with real-time digital reporting and predictive safety insights. The operational problem is that conventional accident documentation can delay response, fragment evidence and limit authorities’ ability to identify recurring safety patterns. In Graz, the project involved Graz Linien and Mapular, with drivers equipped to submit GPS-tagged reports, photographs and incident details through a multilingual digital interface. The implementation integrates external data such as weather conditions and uses analytics to generate proactive safety alerts and insights for city authorities and operators. Conceptually, the platform combines mobile accident reporting, geodata technologies, real-time data capture, predictive modelling and safety-dashboard functionality. Pilot results reported by Mapular indicate a 90% reduction in reporting time, 100% data integrity during the pilot phase and identification of three key accident patterns. The expected impact is faster reporting, better data quality, improved resource allocation, stronger road-safety analysis and more proactive prevention of recurring incidents. The initiative also demonstrates how public transport operators can use structured operational data to move from reactive accident handling to evidence-based safety management.

title: SAFELY - Road Safety Analytics System
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipalities often rely on recorded accidents alone to understand road-safety problems, yet this reactive approach can miss hidden risks and delay intervention until serious incidents have already occurred. SAFELY was developed to help local authorities move from monitoring past crashes to proactively identifying hazardous conditions before further harm occurs. The platform addresses the need for a more complete understanding of road safety by combining multiple data sources rather than relying only on official accident counts. The stakeholders include municipalities, traffic planners, road-safety teams and local communities, with the objective of prioritising interventions more effectively, allocate resources with greater precision and strengthen evidence-based transport planning. The solution is implemented as a data-driven analytics platform that integrates accident records with traffic patterns, road geometry, environmental data and citizen feedback. At a conceptual level, the system uses clustering techniques such as DBSCAN and ST-DBSCAN, together with geospatial visualisation, to reveal risk hotspots and hidden hazards that are not obvious in raw crash statistics. These insights are presented through actionable hazard maps and planning outputs that fit municipal workflows and align with standards such as CADaS, GDPR and the European Interoperability Framework. The impact has been measurable: in Şanlıurfa, interventions supported by SAFELY were associated with an over 80% reduction in reported accidents and a 90% drop in injuries between 2014–2015 and 2020–2021. More broadly, the platform offers a cost-efficient, scalable and credible model for saving lives through proactive road-safety management.

title: ELIAS - European Lighthouse of AI for Sustainability
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: ELIAS addresses a strategic challenge facing Europe: how to accelerate advanced technological research and application in ways that contribute directly to sustainability goals while also respecting ethical and societal considerations. Climate change, the energy crisis and related environmental pressures require new forms of collaboration between academia and industry, yet the pathway from research excellence to deployable solutions is often fragmented. This use case therefore brings together researchers, emerging talent, industrial partners and innovation stakeholders with the objective of building a strong European ecosystem for sustainability-oriented technological development. The project seeks not only to advance research, but also to ensure that resulting solutions generate practical value for society and the environment. The solution is implemented through a programme that combines fundamental academic research, industrial application work, talent development and partnership-building across Europe. At a conceptual level, ELIAS creates a collaborative structure in which advanced methods are developed, tested and translated into seven pilot use cases over the project’s duration, while also supporting the broader research community and strengthening links between scientific and commercial actors. This model is intended to foster both technical progress and responsible innovation. The expected impact is stronger European leadership in sustainability-focused research, improved pathways from research to application and a more capable innovation ecosystem. More broadly, ELIAS creates value by aligning scientific excellence, industrial relevance and societal benefit around pressing environmental challenges.

title: PLLuM - Polish Large Language Model
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Wrocław University of Science and Technology
source_description: PLLuM, the Polish Large Language Universal Model, was launched to strengthen Poland’s capacity to develop open and responsible language technologies primarily trained on Polish text. The problem it addresses is the limited availability of high-quality, open-access language models designed around the linguistic, cultural and administrative needs of Polish users. The main stakeholders include Wrocław University of Science and Technology, the wider consortium of six Polish institutions, researchers specialising in artificial intelligence and linguistics, public-service providers, developers and citizens, including those at risk of digital exclusion. The project aims to create the first open Polish large language model and a related smart assistant that can support access to public services electronically and in person. The implementation involves large-scale Polish-language model training, dataset preparation, linguistic expertise, evaluation and the development of assistant functionalities aligned with ethical and responsible AI principles. These include attention to data representativeness, transparency and fairness. Conceptually, PLLuM can support natural-language interaction, information retrieval, text generation and user guidance in public-service contexts. Its expected impact is broader access to digital services, improved quality of Polish-language AI applications and reduced dependence on models developed primarily for other languages. By targeting digitally excluded users, the smart assistant also has potential to improve administrative accessibility and inclusion.

title: AID HCH – Advancing Humanities and Cultural Heritage with Artificial Intelligence
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: AID HCH is a Slovenian research initiative designed to advance the use of artificial intelligence in humanities research and cultural-heritage preservation. The strategic problem is that AI has been widely applied in natural sciences, engineering and medicine, but less systematically in humanities and heritage contexts, where digitised sources, archives, objects and conservation data require specialised methods and ethical safeguards. The project aims to establish Slovenia’s first comprehensive data space for humanities and heritage, strengthening cooperation with infrastructures such as E-RIHS, CLARIN and DARIAH. Its implementation combines AI tools, data-space development, digitised cultural and historical sources, predictive conservation methods, heritage storytelling and interdisciplinary frameworks for legal and ethical use. Conceptually, the project creates shared infrastructure and methodologies for analysing cultural-heritage data, supporting research collaboration and improving protection of heritage assets. The expected impact is stronger digital transformation in humanities research, better access to structured heritage data, improved conservation planning and greater international interoperability. The project also has a capacity-building function by connecting universities, libraries, heritage institutions and technical partners around common data and AI standards.

title: Enhancing healthcare policy evaluation through AI-driven analytics platform for the National Public Administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products
source_description: Bulgaria’s National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products initiated this project to improve how public authorities evaluate the real-world value of innovative and high-cost medicines. The policy challenge is that reimbursement decisions require evidence on clinical effectiveness, patient outcomes and budget impact, yet traditional evaluation processes may not fully exploit large-scale health data. Stakeholders include the National Council, healthcare policymakers, patients, clinicians, pharmaceutical companies, reimbursement authorities and public-finance actors responsible for sustainable spending. The objective is to support more informed decisions on whether and how medicines should be reimbursed, while balancing patient access with cost-effectiveness. The implementation uses artificial intelligence and big-data analytics to assess the real-world effectiveness of medicines after they enter clinical use. Conceptually, the platform can combine reimbursement records, treatment data, patient outcomes, medicine-cost information and analytical models to compare expected and observed performance. This enables decision-makers to identify which therapies deliver measurable value in practice and where public expenditure may need adjustment. The expected impact is stronger evidence for reimbursement policy, more efficient allocation of public funds, improved accountability for high-cost therapies and better patient care. By linking analytics with reimbursement governance, the project supports a more data-driven and outcome-oriented healthcare administration.

title: Automatic Detection of Impervious Surfaces
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Recklinghausen developed this software to give municipalities a more precise basis for monitoring sealed surfaces and planning climate-adaptation measures. The environmental problem is that impervious surfaces prevent rainwater infiltration and contribute to urban heat accumulation, increasing risks related to drainage, flooding and heat islands. In Germany, around 45% of settlement and transport areas are sealed, according to the Federal Environmental Agency statistics cited in the source material. Stakeholders include the District of Recklinghausen, participating cities, the Westphalian University of Applied Sciences, land registry and geo-information staff, environment and climate-protection departments and local residents.
