Integrated into recruitment workflows, the system processes large volumes of documentation consistently and efficiently. Since its launch in July 2022, approximately 14,000 merits have been verified. The impact includes significantly reduced processing times, improved consistency in scoring, and lower administrative burden. Staff can focus on complex assessments and decision-making, while candidates benefit from faster, more transparent recruitment processes, improving trust and efficiency in public employment systems.

title: Optimising businesses: Unlocking the potential of Quantum Computing
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Many strategic sectors, including transport, logistics, energy and finance, face complex optimisation problems where the number of possible solutions grows exponentially, making traditional approaches inefficient or impractical. In Galicia, organisations struggled to optimise routes, schedules and resource allocation while respecting multiple operational constraints. The objective of this pilot is to explore advanced optimisation approaches that can deliver better solutions to real-world business problems. The implementation was led by the Galician Supercomputer Centre in collaboration with Ayesa and focused on applying quantum and quantum-inspired algorithms to combinatorial optimisation scenarios. Representative industrial problems were modelled mathematically and tested using emerging quantum programming techniques and high-performance computing environments. The pilot evaluated feasibility, performance gains and integration pathways with existing decision-support systems. Results showed improved solution quality for selected optimisation problems and provided insights into where quantum approaches can complement classical methods. Qualitative impacts include strengthened innovation capacity, increased readiness of regional industries to adopt next-generation computing, and clearer pathways towards future commercial deployment as quantum technologies mature.

title: Q4Real: Quantum Computing for real industries
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Industrial companies often face shared optimisation and simulation challenges that limit efficiency, sustainability and competitiveness, yet lack practical frameworks to adopt emerging computational approaches. The Basque Government identified the need to accelerate adoption of advanced solutions across the industrial sector. The objective of this pilot is to bridge the gap between experimental quantum technologies and real industrial applications with sustainable impact. The implementation established a collaborative framework bringing together industry, research and technology providers to standardise quantum programming practices. The project developed reusable components, reference architectures and a shared knowledge base for different classes of quantum problems, alongside emerging quantum software engineering methodologies. These elements were tested on representative industrial use cases to assess feasibility and performance. The pilot strengthened technical capacity, reduced barriers to entry and aligned innovation efforts with market needs. Qualitative impacts include improved industrial readiness, shared standards for future development and a clearer route to commercialisation of quantum-enabled solutions, supporting long-term digital leadership.

title: 5G pilot in Andalusia for the María Zambrano Train Station
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Red.es
source_description: Large transport hubs require efficient passenger navigation and proactive infrastructure maintenance to ensure safety, comfort and operational continuity. At María Zambrano train station, managing complex spatial layouts and real-time operational events posed challenges for both travellers and maintenance teams. The objective of this pilot is to enhance passenger experience and asset management through immersive digital tools. The implementation created a detailed digital twin of the station using Building Information Modelling, hosted in a cloud environment and connected via 5G. Two augmented reality applications were developed: a passenger guidance tool providing real-time navigation and points of interest, and a maintenance application supporting preventive and corrective tasks through visual overlays. The high-speed connectivity ensured immediate synchronisation of real-time data, including crowd levels and incidents. The pilot improved navigation efficiency, reduced maintenance response times and enhanced situational awareness. Qualitative benefits include improved service quality, safer operations and a scalable model for smart transport infrastructure.

title: Margot AI supporting the Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco - document search case
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public agencies managing complex regulatory domains often struggle to retrieve precise information quickly from large internal document repositories. The Italian Medicines Agency adopted Margot AI to support customer service and internal staff in accessing authoritative information. This use case involves AIFA staff, regulated stakeholders, and citizens, with the objective of improving response accuracy and efficiency. Margot AI is implemented using a retrieval-augmented generation architecture that connects natural language queries to internal databases and document collections. It searches, classifies, and retrieves relevant content, delivering precise answers while maintaining alignment with official sources. Integrated across existing systems and communication channels, it automates repetitive requests and supports staff in handling complex enquiries. The impact includes faster response times, reduced manual searching, and improved consistency of information provided. AIFA benefits from more efficient service delivery and better use of institutional knowledge, strengthening regulatory transparency and operational effectiveness.

title: Margot AI supporting the Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco - FarmaciLine assistance
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Citizens frequently seek reliable information on authorised medicines, indications, and regulatory decisions, placing high demand on public health information services. Within AIFA’s FarmaciLine service, Margot AI supports responses to these enquiries. This use case involves citizens, healthcare professionals, and AIFA operators, with the objective of delivering accurate, timely information on medicines. The system retrieves information from official sources such as Summaries of Product Characteristics and AIFA resolutions, ensuring responses remain authoritative. Integrated into FarmaciLine workflows, it handles repetitive questions and supports multilingual, consistent communication. The impact includes improved accessibility to trusted medicines information, reduced workload for operators, and enhanced user satisfaction. Citizens benefit from clear, immediate answers, while AIFA strengthens its role as a reliable source of pharmaceutical information.

title: Margot AI supporting the Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco - Monitoring platform
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: AIFA manages multiple monitoring registries used to track medicine use in clinical practice, which are complex and heterogeneous. Accessing the correct information quickly is essential for regulatory oversight and operational efficiency. This use case supports AIFA staff by simplifying interaction with monitoring registries. Margot AI retrieves relevant data and guidance from different registry systems, including therapeutic plans and multi-drug registries, through a unified conversational interface. Integrated with internal platforms, it automates information retrieval and supports staff decision-making. The impact includes reduced search time, improved accuracy, and better utilisation of monitoring data. This strengthens regulatory oversight, enhances operational efficiency, and supports evidence-based management of medicines within the Italian healthcare system.

title: AI-powered procurement platform
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Public procurement processes are often time-consuming, error-prone and vulnerable to inefficiencies that undermine transparency and competition. In Albania, authorities seek to modernise procurement practices to improve fairness and operational efficiency. The objective of this initiative is to streamline procurement workflows while maintaining strong human oversight. The implementation is developing a platform that supports drafting terms of reference, estimating costs and generating initial evaluation reports. All outputs are subject to review, with full audit trails tracking modifications. The system integrates procurement data and standard templates to support consistent application of rules. Expected impacts include reduced processing time, fewer errors and increased transparency. Qualitative benefits include fairer competition, improved trust among businesses and stronger governance of public spending.

title: AI for taxation project in Albania
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Combating tax evasion and financial crime requires timely detection of anomalies across large volumes of transactional data. Albania aims to enhance its tax administration by automating routine analysis while strengthening investigative capacity. The objective of this project is to improve detection of irregularities and free staff for complex cases. The implementation develops analytical models that process electronic invoices and customs declarations in near real time to identify unusual patterns. The system supports analysts rather than replacing them, integrating into existing workflows. Expected impacts include improved compliance rates, faster detection of risks and reduced manual workload. Qualitative outcomes include more effective enforcement, better use of human expertise and increased fiscal integrity.

title: AI for healthcare project in Albania
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Healthcare systems face pressure to detect diseases earlier and manage growing diagnostic workloads. Albania aims to strengthen diagnostic capacity through advanced digital tools. The objective of this project is to support clinicians in radiology by improving early detection and treatment planning. The implementation focuses on developing systems that analyse medical images to identify patterns associated with disease, support personalised treatment decisions and predict progression. These tools are designed to integrate into clinical workflows and support, not replace, medical judgement. Expected impacts include earlier diagnosis, improved patient outcomes and reduced diagnostic delays. Qualitative benefits include improved care quality, increased system resilience and long-term efficiency gains.

title: Nation-wide AI-powered smart city project
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Rapid urbanisation and increased mobility place pressure on city infrastructure, traffic management and emergency response. Albania has launched a nationwide initiative to modernise urban management across 20 cities. The objective of this project is to improve safety, mobility and service coordination through real-time data-driven management. The implementation develops an integrated platform that combines urban, traffic and public safety data into a central command and control environment. Analytical tools support traffic optimisation, incident detection and coordinated emergency response. Expected impacts include reduced congestion, improved road safety and faster response times. Qualitative outcomes include more resilient cities, better public service coordination and a scalable model for national smart city deployment.

title: UCRONIA - Utility Circular Economy Real-Time Operation Navigation Integration Assets
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: UCRONIA was developed by AMA S.p.A. to address a longstanding operational challenge in Rome’s urban hygiene services: the difficulty of managing a vast, complex and constantly changing city through fragmented information and reactive intervention models. In a metropolitan context where waste collection, street cleaning, environmental conditions, citizen reports and public events all affect service delivery, AMA needed a system capable of improving coordination, anticipating issues earlier and supporting more consistent decision-making. The stakeholders include operational managers, field teams, municipal authorities, citizens and technology partners, with the objective of moving from a reactive to a preventive model of urban hygiene management while improving service quality, sustainability and circular-economy performance. The solution is implemented through a real-time geographic digital twin that maps Rome’s urban infrastructure, including manholes, bins, tree-lined streets, vehicle fleets, citizen reports and environmental data, and feeds this information into a dedicated control room. At a conceptual level, the platform integrates geospatial intelligence, live operational data and decision-support capabilities to optimise routing, asset management and intervention planning across the city. Operated 24/7 in collaboration with partners such as Present S.p.A. and Esri Italia, the system has already shown its practical value during major events including papal funerals and Jubilee celebrations. The impact includes more efficient operations, stronger service continuity, better situational awareness and a scalable model for smart, data-driven urban environmental management.

title: IMPULSE Project - NemID card retrieval from lockers (IMPULSE - Denmark)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Access to digital public services in Denmark depends on NemID credentials, which vulnerable citizens frequently lose, limiting their ability to interact with authorities. Aarhus Municipality sought solutions to ensure equitable access for these groups. The objective of this pilot is to support vulnerable citizens by providing secure storage and retrieval of authentication credentials. The implementation introduced personal document lockers where NemID key cards could be safely stored. Access to each drawer is controlled through biometric facial recognition performed via the citizen’s mobile device, ensuring secure and exclusive access. The solution integrates with existing municipal support services and digital identity workflows. The pilot reduced credential loss, improved continuity of service access and increased digital inclusion. Qualitative impacts include enhanced autonomy for vulnerable users, reduced administrative burden on social services and improved trust in digital public services, demonstrating inclusive innovation in identity management.

title: IMPULSE Project - Gijón public services app
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Secure and user-friendly electronic identity systems are essential for accessing modern public services, yet many citizens face fragmented authentication experiences. The City of Gijón aimed to modernise access to municipal services while ensuring privacy and interoperability. The objective of this pilot is to enhance secure, citizen-centric digital identification within the public sector. The implementation explored integration of advanced identity technologies into municipal platforms, focusing on GDPR-compliant authentication and cross-service usability. The pilot leveraged existing infrastructure to test secure access to public services and evaluate interoperability at local and cross-border levels. Results include improved user experience, stronger data protection and increased confidence in digital services. Qualitative benefits include enhanced accessibility, reduced administrative friction and alignment with European digital identity objectives, supporting scalable adoption across public administrations.

title: IMPULSE Project - Entreprise digital drawer
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Businesses frequently face administrative inefficiencies when accessing public services, as they are required to repeatedly provide the same identity documents, registrations and certifications to different authorities, often across borders. This duplication increases costs, delays procedures and creates inconsistencies in data verification. Within the IMPULSE initiative, public administrations and business support organisations sought to simplify and secure enterprise access to digital public services while maintaining regulatory compliance. The objective of this pilot is to streamline business identification processes and enable trusted, reusable digital identities for enterprises. The implementation designed and tested a blockchain-based business identity solution, often referred to as a digital drawer, which enriches traditional business identities with verifiable attributes sourced from official business registers. These attributes can be securely shared with authorised public bodies on demand, with full traceability and user control. The system integrates with existing public service platforms and supports both domestic and cross-border service access. The pilot demonstrated faster onboarding to public services, reduced administrative burden for businesses and authorities, and improved trust in shared data. Qualitative impacts include higher data integrity, improved interoperability between administrations and a reusable framework that supports more efficient, transparent and scalable digital services for enterprises.

title: IMPULSE Project - Civil registration & certification in Bulgaria
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Local administrations are under increasing pressure to deliver digital public services that are secure, reliable and compliant with data protection regulations, while maintaining accessibility for citizens. In the Municipality of Peshtera, existing electronic civil registration and certification services required strengthening to meet growing security and GDPR compliance demands. The objective of this pilot is to modernise municipal digital services by enhancing trust, data protection and operational robustness. The implementation built upon the municipality’s existing electronic service platform, integrating identity verification, secure data handling mechanisms and governance principles developed within the IMPULSE project. These enhancements focused on improving authentication, protecting personal data and ensuring that digital interactions between citizens and the municipality complied with European data protection requirements. The pilot enabled the municipality to test and validate these mechanisms in real operational conditions. Results included improved service reliability, stronger protection of citizen data and increased trust in digital civil services. Qualitative benefits include reduced administrative risk, greater efficiency in service delivery and a scalable model that other municipalities can adopt to modernise local e-government services while ensuring compliance and citizen confidence.

title: IMPULSE Project - Online complaints filing services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Filing a formal police complaint traditionally requires citizens to attend a police station in person, which can be time-consuming, inconvenient and particularly challenging for vulnerable individuals or those living far from urban centres. In the Basque Country, the Ertzaintza sought to modernise its complaint-handling processes while maintaining high standards of security, legal validity and public trust. The objective of this pilot is to enable citizens to securely submit complaints online, reducing administrative barriers and improving access to public security services. The implementation integrated advanced identity management mechanisms into the existing online complaints system, enabling secure authentication and verification of complainants. These mechanisms were designed and tested in collaboration with law enforcement personnel, ensuring alignment with operational requirements and legal constraints. The pilot included end-user needs analysis, system validation and staff training to support adoption. Results showed improved accessibility of police services, reduced need for in-person visits and more efficient handling of non-urgent complaints. Qualitative impacts include improved citizen convenience, better allocation of police resources and strengthened trust in digital public safety services. The pilot demonstrates a scalable approach for modernising law enforcement interactions while preserving security and procedural integrity.

title: BRIGHT - Local Energy Cooperative multi-market centralized aggregation for value stacking flexibility services (Belgium)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The De Nieuwe Dokken development in Ghent was designed as a highly sustainable urban district with housing, public facilities and a strong renewable-energy and circular-technology component. A key challenge in such environments is not only installing low-carbon infrastructure, but also ensuring that residents actively participate in energy management so that local flexibility can be used to support the grid and improve system efficiency. The BRIGHT pilot addressed this issue by helping turn a residential development into an engaged energy community. The stakeholders included residents, DuCoop ESCO, project partners and energy-system actors, with the objective of increasing energy awareness, encouraging participation in demand-response schemes and assessing the potential for integrating homes into a virtual power plant. The solution was implemented through smart services such as real-time visualisation of energy consumption, billing tools and smart-home features, supported by data-driven methods, blockchain and social-science approaches. At a conceptual level, the pilot combined Digital Twin models, Virtual Power Plant concepts and analytical services to characterise consumer behaviour and identify how residential demand could be coordinated more flexibly. This enabled technical innovation to be paired with user engagement rather than relying on infrastructure alone. The expected impact was greater resident participation, improved grid flexibility and better use of distributed energy resources. More broadly, the pilot created value by demonstrating how citizen-centred energy communities can support sustainability, resilience and more intelligent local energy management.

title: BRIGHT - Virtual Community Decentralized Aggregation in Slovenia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The energy transition increasingly requires active participation from consumers, yet many households lack the tools to engage effectively in local energy markets or optimise their energy use. In Slovenia, energy stakeholders sought solutions to empower consumers while maintaining security, transparency and system efficiency. The objective of this pilot is to enable peer-to-peer energy trading and integrated energy services through a secure, consumer-centric platform. The implementation combines edge-secure gateways, advanced metering infrastructure and digital twin models with a distributed transaction platform to support decentralised energy exchanges. Aggregate measurements are analysed to infer device behaviour without exposing individual consumption patterns, while users interact through a unified interface that integrates energy and non-energy services, including financial and safety-related applications. The pilot demonstrated improved consumer engagement, enhanced visibility of energy usage and new opportunities for local energy optimisation. Qualitative impacts include increased user awareness, support for decentralised energy markets and a replicable national model for virtual energy communities. The project illustrates how integrated digital infrastructures can support sustainable energy systems and active consumer participation.

title: iMaging Project - Beach Monitoring
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: SOCIB - Balearic Islands Ocean Observing and Forecasting System
source_description: Coastal authorities need timely and reliable information on beach conditions in order to protect the public, monitor environmental health and respond quickly to changing marine dynamics. Manual observation can be limited in speed, consistency and coverage, particularly when beach conditions change rapidly and multiple indicators must be tracked simultaneously. This use case, developed within the EU-funded iMagine project and led by SOCIB, addresses that challenge by improving the monitoring of beach environments through automated analysis of camera feeds. The stakeholders include coastal managers, environmental researchers and public-safety actors, with the objective of supporting near real-time understanding of shoreline conditions, strengthening beach safety and improving knowledge of ecologically significant coastal features. The solution is implemented through a prototype service that uses deep-learning image-segmentation techniques to analyse video from beach-monitoring cameras. At a conceptual level, the system processes visual data to detect and monitor Posidonia oceanica berms, which are relevant indicators of coastal health, and to identify rip currents, including their location and physical characteristics. These outputs provide actionable information for both environmental observation and risk management. Running from September 2022 to August 2025, the prototype demonstrates how automated image analysis can complement existing beach-monitoring practices. The expected impact includes faster interpretation of coastal conditions, improved support for beach management and stronger public-safety capability, alongside a more scalable approach to continuous shoreline observation.

title: iMaging Project - Ecosystem Monitoring at EMSO Sites by Video Imagery
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Marine ecosystem monitoring relies on continuous observation, yet manual analysis of underwater video footage is time-consuming and limits the ability to detect changes in biodiversity and environmental conditions at scale. Research infrastructures such as EMSO observatories require automated tools to transform large volumes of raw video into actionable scientific insights. This use case addresses these needs by supporting ecosystem monitoring at subsea observatory sites, involving marine researchers, infrastructure operators, and data scientists, with the objective of improving real-time understanding of marine environments. The solution is implemented through a video-based monitoring service that processes underwater imagery using deep-learning models for object detection and quality filtering. Deployed across EMSO sites including Obsea, the Azores, and SmartBay, the service identifies marine species, flags low-quality footage, and detects notable events such as prawn burrows, converting unstructured video into standardised, analysable datasets. Integrated data pipelines deliver near-real-time outputs to researchers and support reuse across observatories. The approach significantly reduces manual workload, improves consistency of observations, and enhances the timeliness and scale of ecosystem monitoring. It strengthens biodiversity assessment, supports long-term environmental research, and provides a scalable foundation for data-driven marine science.

title: iMaging Project - WITOIL Oil spill detection service
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: As part of the EU-funded iMagine project, the EyeOnWater initiative addresses the challenge of ensuring the quality and reliability of citizen-contributed data for environmental monitoring. Through a smartphone application, citizens submit photographs of natural water bodies such as rivers, lakes, and seas to support large-scale observation of water colour and related ecological indicators. Key stakeholders include citizens, environmental scientists, and research institutions that rely on consistent, high-quality visual data. The objective of the use case is to validate incoming images efficiently and at scale so that only suitable, scientifically usable photographs are incorporated into long-term environmental datasets. The service uses computer vision techniques to automatically assess the suitability of submitted images before they enter scientific workflows. Image segmentation and object detection models, including YOLOv8, are applied to identify whether an image contains a water body and to detect obstructions or irrelevant content. The models are trained on a labeled dataset of more than 10,000 images categorized into different quality classes. The validation pipeline is integrated into the mobile application backend, enabling near real-time processing and automated decision-making on image acceptance or rejection. The automated validation process significantly improves the consistency and reliability of citizen science data while reducing the need for manual review. Real-time filtering ensures that only high-quality images are added to long-term water colour datasets, increasing their scientific value and usability. The approach enhances scalability by allowing large volumes of submissions to be processed efficiently, supports faster data availability for researchers, and improves the user experience by providing immediate feedback on submissions. Overall, the solution strengthens the contribution of citizen science to environmental monitoring and ecological research.

title: iMaging Project - EyeOnWater app
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Marine oil spills are difficult to detect and track quickly across large sea areas, yet delays in identification can worsen environmental damage, complicate response planning and reduce the effectiveness of mitigation efforts. The Oil Spill Detection service within the EU-funded iMagine project addresses this operational problem by improving how spills are identified, monitored and modelled from satellite data. The stakeholders include researchers, environmental authorities and decision-makers responsible for marine protection and spill response, with the objective of strengthening early detection, improving situational awareness and making advanced monitoring tools easier to adopt in practice. The solution, also known as WITOIL, is implemented on the iMagine platform and uses deep-learning models trained on labelled imagery from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 satellites. At a conceptual level, the service combines satellite-image analysis, automated classification and spill-modelling functions to enhance the capabilities of existing systems such as OKEANOS. In addition to detection, it supports fuel-spill modelling, alert generation, documentation and training resources, allowing users to integrate the service more effectively into operational workflows. The prototype runs from September 2022 to August 2025. The expected impact is faster and more consistent spill detection, reduced manual screening effort and improved decision support for marine incidents. More broadly, the service increases scalability in environmental monitoring and strengthens the practical usability of Earth-observation data for pollution management.

title: Consular Digital Triage - Automating consular enquiry responses
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: British nationals abroad frequently contact consular services for urgent but routine issues such as lost passports, emergency travel documents, or eligibility for support, creating high volumes of written and telephone enquiries for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). The Consular Digital Triage use case was introduced to reduce this operational pressure while ensuring that citizens receive fast, accurate, and safe guidance. The primary stakeholders include British nationals overseas, consular staff, and central FCDO operations teams, with the objective of resolving common enquiries at first contact and allowing human staff to focus on complex or sensitive cases. The solution is implemented as a digital assistant that classifies incoming written enquiries and matches them to pre-approved guidance templates rather than generating open-ended responses. This rules- and model-based approach ensures consistency, policy compliance, and safety. The system integrates with existing consular contact channels and knowledge bases, enabling rapid response without manual intervention. The impact has been substantial: written enquiries were reduced by around 80% and calls by up to 50% within three months of deployment. Over time, the tool is projected to save the FCDO millions of pounds while improving response times, maintaining trust, and enhancing the overall experience for citizens abroad.

title: Barking and Dagenham AI Search and Webchat - Streamlining access to council services and information through AI-powered search and chat
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Residents often struggle to navigate council websites or contact centres to find accurate information on local services, leading to high call volumes and repeated enquiries. Barking and Dagenham Council introduced AI Search and Webchat to streamline access to council services, starting with waste collection and expanding to areas such as housing and council tax. Stakeholders include residents, customer service teams, and service departments, with the objective of resolving most routine questions digitally while preserving accessibility. The solution combines an AI-powered search interface and a conversational webchat tool that uses structured service data, including postcode-based logic, to deliver personalised responses. Both interfaces are integrated with council content systems and continuously refined through community feedback and monitoring. Traditional channels, such as phone and face-to-face support, remain available to ensure inclusivity. The impact has been measurable: the AI Search tool now handles around 18,000 sessions per month with a high first-time hit rate, while the chatbot manages approximately 4,450 conversations monthly with a 93% success rate based on user feedback. Together, the tools have significantly reduced general enquiries and call volumes, improved resident satisfaction, and enabled council staff to focus on more complex cases.

title: Aila: AI Lesson Assistant for UK teachers
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Department for Education (DfE) / Oak National Academy
source_description: Teachers face significant workload pressures when preparing high-quality, curriculum-aligned lesson plans tailored to diverse student needs. Oak National Academy developed Aila to support teachers in lesson planning while maintaining pedagogical quality and alignment with national curricula. Stakeholders include classroom teachers, school leaders, and curriculum designers, with the objective of saving time, reducing stress, and improving teaching consistency. Aila is implemented as a conversational lesson assistant that combines a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation, drawing exclusively on Oak’s quality-assured lesson repository. Teachers interact with Aila via a chat interface to generate lesson outlines, which can be iteratively refined to suit class context and teaching style. The system is designed to ensure factual accuracy and curriculum relevance by grounding outputs in trusted educational content. The impact has been strong: in its first two months, Aila supported 10,000 users in creating nearly 25,000 lesson plans, with 85% of teachers rating the quality as fairly high or very high. Nearly two-thirds reported reduced workload, with average time savings of around three hours and some saving up to 15 hours. Teachers also reported improved well-being, demonstrating clear educational and workforce value.

title: GCS Assist - Accelerating content creation for government communicators
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Government communicators must produce high-quality, timely content aligned with established standards and frameworks, often under tight deadlines. GCS Assist was developed in-house to support members of the UK Government Communication Service by accelerating routine content creation and review tasks. The key stakeholders are government communicators across departments, with the objective of saving time while maintaining consistency, accuracy, and best practice. Assist is implemented as a secure internal tool featuring pre-built, task-specific prompts tailored to communication disciplines such as press notices, stakeholder briefings, and campaign planning. The system enables users to brainstorm ideas, draft initial content, and review materials more efficiently than manual processes. Its design embeds Government Communication Service guidance and frameworks directly into workflows, ensuring outputs align with professional standards. Since going live in April 2025, following a prototype phase in late 2023, Assist has enabled communicators to complete tasks in a fraction of the time previously required. The impact includes faster turnaround times, improved productivity, and reduced administrative burden, allowing communication professionals to focus more on strategic thinking and stakeholder engagement rather than repetitive drafting tasks.

title: Magic Notes - Assisting social care workers through transcription and note-taking
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Social care professionals spend a significant proportion of their time on administrative documentation, reducing the time available for direct engagement with clients and contributing to workload pressure and burnout. In regional social care services in Wales, there was a need to reduce administrative burden while improving the quality of assessments. The objective of this pilot is to support social workers by automating transcription and structured note-taking during client interactions. The implementation deploys a speech-based system that records conversations, produces accurate transcripts and generates structured summaries aligned with assessment requirements. The tool integrates into existing workflows and allows practitioners to review and edit outputs. During the pilot, practitioners saved on average 25 minutes per assessment and approximately 7.5 hours per week, submitting assessments up to eight hours faster. Accuracy exceeded 97%, and users reported more natural conversations and higher-quality assessments. Qualitative impacts include reduced case backlogs, improved workload distribution and enhanced practitioner wellbeing. The pilot demonstrates significant productivity gains and improved service quality in social care delivery.

title: Logo Detection and Classification Toolkit (LDK) - Automating the detection of unauthorised logo use on websites
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Unauthorised use of official government logos on fraudulent or misleading websites poses risks to citizens and undermines trust in public institutions. HM Revenue & Customs, working with Central-Government partners, developed the Logo Detection and Classification Toolkit to automate the identification of such misuse. Stakeholders include enforcement analysts, government departments, and the public, with the objective of detecting and removing infringing websites quickly and accurately. LDK is implemented as an automated pipeline that scans the web via search engines, scrapes suspicious sites, and applies a deep-learning-based computer vision model to detect government logos. The system flags likely infringements for analyst review, integrating seamlessly into existing enforcement workflows. By automating what was previously a manual and time-consuming process, LDK reduces detection time from days to hours. The impact is significant: analysts can now take down 10–20 infringing URLs per month, with accuracy exceeding 97%. This improves public protection, strengthens brand integrity, and delivers substantial efficiency gains for enforcement teams.

title: SAM - Service AI Assistant Module - Streamlining routine queries through AI-powered contact centre tools
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Local authorities receive high volumes of routine enquiries about services such as waste collection, council tax and basic administrative procedures, placing sustained pressure on contact centres and frontline staff. Residents increasingly expect immediate, round-the-clock access to information. The objective of this pilot is to improve customer service efficiency while maintaining service quality and accessibility. The implementation introduces a conversational assistant that handles routine enquiries through automated dialogue and integrates with backend council systems to retrieve accurate, up-to-date information. The assistant operates continuously and escalates complex queries to human agents when necessary. Early testing showed response accuracy of approximately 93% and user satisfaction levels between 86% and 90%, based on direct feedback. The pilot reduced call centre workload, shortened response times and improved service availability for residents. Qualitative benefits include better staff focus on complex cases, improved citizen experience and a scalable solution for digital customer service in local government. The pilot highlights the value of automated assistance in enhancing public service responsiveness and operational efficiency.

title: Mia - Streamlining breast cancer screening with AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Breast cancer screening programmes face growing demand while radiology departments experience workforce shortages and increasing workloads, which can affect screening throughput and consistency. Radiologists must review large volumes of mammograms, often under time pressure, while ensuring that cases requiring further investigation are reliably identified. The objective of this pilot is to support clinicians in breast cancer screening by improving efficiency and maintaining high diagnostic standards. The implementation introduces an assisted assessment system that automatically analyses mammography images and provides recommendations on whether a case should be recalled for further examination. The system is integrated into existing screening workflows, supporting radiologists during image review rather than replacing clinical judgement. It processes large datasets of anonymised mammograms to detect patterns associated with potential abnormalities and highlights cases that warrant closer attention. The pilot demonstrated improved workflow efficiency, reduced reading time per case and more consistent prioritisation of high-risk images. Qualitative impacts include better workload management for radiologists, increased confidence in screening decisions and enhanced capacity of screening programmes. The pilot supports scalability of breast cancer screening services while preserving clinical oversight and patient safety.

title: Review Automoderation Tool - Automating content moderation on NHS.UK
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) / NHS England (NHSE)
source_description: NHS.UK receives around 100,000 user reviews each year, all of which must comply with strict moderation policies on personal data, abuse, discrimination, and safeguarding. Manual moderation by third-party reviewers led to delays and high costs, and many rejected reviews were never resubmitted, reducing valuable patient feedback. NHS England introduced the Review Automoderation Tool to address these challenges. Stakeholders include patients, NHS content teams, and service providers, with the objective of accelerating moderation while maintaining safety and quality. The tool automatically assesses reviews against moderation criteria, flagging issues for human oversight where necessary. Integrated into NHS.UK workflows, it processes reviews in seconds rather than days. The impact includes expert-level accuracy, dramatically reduced moderation times, and lower operational costs. Importantly, faster moderation has improved publication rates, preserving more patient feedback and enhancing transparency. The tool supports safer, more responsive digital services while ensuring NHS standards are upheld.

title: Warm Home Discount Energy Cost Predictor - Modelling energy costs to determine eligibility for Warm Home Discount scheme
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
source_description: Identifying households eligible for energy cost support is complex, particularly when relying on self-application processes that disadvantage less informed or vulnerable citizens. The Warm Home Discount Energy Cost Predictor was developed to improve targeting of support under the UK’s Warm Home Discount scheme. Stakeholders include the Department for Energy Security & Net Zero, energy suppliers, and low-income households, with the objective of issuing rebates more fairly and efficiently. The solution uses a statistical prediction model to estimate household energy costs based on property characteristics such as size, age, and type. By integrating these estimates with income-related data, the system identifies high-cost, low-income households proactively. The impact has been substantial: in 2023/24, over 90% of the 3 million rebates were issued automatically. This removed the first-come, first-served approach and ensured vulnerable households received support even if they were unaware of the scheme. The result is a fairer, more inclusive system with improved policy effectiveness and reduced administrative burden.

title: Stroke AI - Interpreting brain scans with AI to improve outcomes for stroke patients
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) / NHS England (NHSE)
source_description: Stroke treatment is extremely time-sensitive, and delays in diagnosis can have severe consequences for patient outcomes. Stroke AI was introduced across England to support clinical teams in rapidly interpreting brain scans and making treatment decisions. Stakeholders include clinicians, hospitals, and patients, with the objective of improving speed, accuracy, and consistency in stroke care. The solution analyses brain imaging data to support identification of stroke type and severity, integrating into existing radiology and clinical workflows. It provides decision support to clinicians rather than replacing clinical judgement. The impact is national in scale: all 107 stroke centres in England now use the technology, supporting care for around 80,000 stroke patients each year. Faster and more accurate assessments enable timely interventions, improving survival rates and long-term outcomes. The system demonstrates how advanced digital tools can enhance clinical capacity and deliver significant public health benefits in critical care settings.

title: ADRYX - Chatbot for real-time flight updates
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Passengers at large international airports often require up-to-date information on flights, services, and facilities, placing pressure on customer service teams. Aeroporti di Roma launched the AdRyX chatbot at Rome Fiumicino Airport to enhance the digital passenger experience. Stakeholders include travellers, airport operators, and commercial partners, with the objective of delivering instant, multilingual information. AdRyX is implemented as part of the Digiport platform and operates via popular messaging channels such as WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger. It provides real-time flight updates, wayfinding support, and recommendations for shops and restaurants, responding in Italian and English. Integrated with airport operational systems, the chatbot delivers accurate, timely responses without human intervention. Since its launch in June 2024, AdRyX has marked a significant step forward in digital service delivery, improving passenger satisfaction, reducing routine enquiries, and supporting smoother airport operations.

title: Faneque Double Tunnel - improving traffic with Automatic Incident Detection (AID) system
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Major road infrastructure projects must ensure smooth traffic flow and rapid incident response to maintain safety and minimise congestion, particularly in confined environments such as tunnels. The completion of the Faneque double tunnel on Gran Canaria’s La Aldea highway required advanced monitoring to manage increased traffic volumes and reduce travel times. The objective of this pilot is to enhance road safety and operational efficiency through early detection of traffic incidents. The implementation deployed an automatic incident detection system that analyses live video feeds from tunnel cameras to identify events such as stopped vehicles, accidents or abnormal traffic behaviour. The system operates continuously and integrates with traffic management platforms to alert operators in real time, enabling faster intervention. The pilot improved incident response times, reduced secondary accidents and supported smoother traffic flow through the tunnel. Qualitative impacts include increased safety for drivers, reduced congestion-related delays and improved reliability of critical transport infrastructure. The project demonstrates how advanced traffic monitoring can enhance resilience and efficiency in complex road environments.

title: Digitising university degrees with blockchain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Universities and graduates increasingly need academic credentials that are easy to verify, portable across borders and suited to more flexible forms of learning, yet traditional paper-based diplomas remain bureaucratic, slow to authenticate and poorly adapted to digital mobility. This use case, launched in September 2019 by Cineca, MIT and Italian universities including Padua and Milano-Bicocca, addresses that mismatch by rethinking how academic qualifications are issued and recognised. The stakeholders include universities, students, graduates, employers and international education institutions, with the objective of reducing administrative friction, supporting learner mobility and enabling a more modern concept of stackable and digitally usable credentials. The solution is implemented through blockchain-based issuance of academic certificates using the Blockcerts standard. At a conceptual level, universities create secure, portable and verifiable digital credentials that can be shared by graduates and validated independently without relying on repeated manual confirmation from the issuing institution. This architecture supports trusted authenticity while simplifying exchange across institutions and countries. By replacing or complementing conventional diplomas with digital credentials, the system aligns academic certification with new patterns of lifelong learning and international movement. The expected impact includes less bureaucracy, faster verification, greater convenience for graduates and improved interoperability across educational contexts. More broadly, the project creates value by modernising credential management and positioning universities to support a more flexible, digital and globally connected education ecosystem.

title: EUIPO connects to TMview and DesignView through blockchain
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: In 2021, the European Union Intellectual Property Office integrated blockchain technology into its TMview and DesignView platforms to improve cross-border intellectual property data exchange. Trademark and design information from national IP offices requires secure synchronisation and reliable verification to ensure transparency and trust. The integration connects participating offices through a distributed ledger that records updates in real time and maintains immutable transaction histories. Blockchain-based validation enhances interoperability and ensures that changes to trademark and design records are traceable and tamper-evident. Users can access authenticated histories of intellectual property rights, strengthening confidence in data integrity. Planned developments include downloadable blockchain certificates and an IP Wallet to manage verified records. By embedding distributed ledger infrastructure into existing databases, EUIPO improves efficiency, data consistency and trust in European IP information systems.

title: MADRE: a Banque de France blockchain project
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Before MADRE, the SEPA Creditor Identifier register operated through a centralised process that could take days to deliver codes to participating banks, creating delays, manual administration and unnecessary operational overhead. Banque de France launched MADRE in April 2018 to address this inefficiency and modernise a core financial-infrastructure process through a more distributed and automated model. The stakeholders include the central bank, participating banks and financial-sector operators relying on timely and reliable management of SEPA Creditor Identifiers, with the objective of accelerating issuance, reducing paperwork and improving the efficiency and robustness of registry operations. The solution is implemented through a private Ethereum-based blockchain that decentralises the ICS register and embeds process logic in smart contracts. At a conceptual level, the platform replaces a single central database with a distributed ledger architecture in which authorised participants can interact with shared, synchronised records while automated rules govern validation and issuance steps. This significantly reduces reliance on manual intervention and streamlines the overall process flow. As the first blockchain system brought into production by a central bank, MADRE also served as an important proof point for the operational use of distributed-ledger technology in regulated financial infrastructure. The impact includes a reduction in issuance time from days to minutes, lower processing costs, less paperwork and improved operational efficiency, demonstrating clear business value in speed, reliability and administrative simplification.

title: Smart Ivrea - Blockchain Technology in the Management of Smart Communities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Smart cities require coordination across energy, mobility and citizen services, yet fragmented systems often limit transparency and trust. Smart Ivrea, led by the Italian Agency for Digital Italy (AGiD), explores how distributed ledger technology can support integrated management of smart communities. Stakeholders include local authorities, service providers and citizens. The objective is to enhance transparency, coordination and participation in urban services. The project uses the Quadrans blockchain platform, an open-source, public and decentralised infrastructure, to record and manage community-related transactions and interactions. Blockchain enables verifiable records of service usage, resource distribution and citizen engagement, while smart contracts support automated processes across domains such as energy sharing and mobility services. The pilot demonstrates how decentralised infrastructure can reduce fragmentation, improve accountability and foster citizen trust. Although still experimental, Smart Ivrea provides a replicable model for municipalities seeking to integrate emerging technologies into sustainable urban governance.

title: Two italian universities partner to build the quantum computers of the future
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Maintaining competitiveness in advanced computing technologies requires long-term investment, coordinated research and strong collaboration between academic and industrial actors. In Italy, fragmented efforts and limited shared infrastructure have slowed progress in emerging computing fields. The objective of this initiative is to establish a robust national ecosystem capable of designing, developing and scaling next-generation quantum computing technologies. The partnership, launched in June 2025, brings together Planckian—a joint spin-off of the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale—and the QTLab centre of the Federico II University of Naples, aligning scientific research, engineering capabilities and infrastructure development. The implementation focuses on joint research programmes, shared laboratories and coordinated technology roadmaps covering hardware design, control systems and integration with existing high-performance computing environments. The initiative also fosters collaboration with industry and public research organisations to accelerate technology transfer and skills development. The expected impact includes strengthened national research capacity, improved access to cutting-edge infrastructure and increased attractiveness for industrial partnerships. Qualitative outcomes include accelerated innovation cycles, enhanced talent development and a strategic foundation for Italy’s long-term technological sovereignty in quantum computing.

title: AI use in the City of Kastav
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal administrations often manage competitive funding and co-financing processes that involve large volumes of documentation, manual evaluation and tight deadlines, placing strain on staff and reducing transparency. In the City of Kastav, authorities sought to modernise the tender submission and evaluation process while supporting fair and efficient decision-making. The objective of this pilot is to partially automate administrative workflows and improve the evaluation of funding applications. The implementation developed a prototype system that enables digital submission of tender documents, automatic extraction of key information and structured summarisation of project proposals. Applications are assessed against predefined criteria, generating evaluation proposals and ranked outputs that can be exported for further review by commission members. The system integrates with existing administrative tools and supports human oversight throughout the process. The pilot reduced administrative workload, shortened evaluation timelines and improved consistency in scoring. Qualitative benefits include greater transparency, improved traceability of decisions and enhanced efficiency for municipal staff, providing a scalable model for digital transformation in local public administration.

title: AI-Code - GenAi against disinformation: Use case 3
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Online disinformation increasingly relies on short-form videos, posing challenges for media professionals tasked with identifying coordinated influence campaigns. AI-CODE, a Horizon Europe project, addresses this issue through dedicated use cases. Use Case 2 focuses on detecting covert foreign influence in video-based social media content. Stakeholders include journalists, fact-checkers and media organisations. The objective is to improve the efficiency and accuracy of disinformation monitoring at scale. The solution automates the analysis of large volumes of videos from platforms such as TikTok and YouTube Shorts, extracting visual, audio and contextual features. Advanced models flag anomalies, coordinated patterns and potentially harmful sources for further human investigation. By reducing manual screening effort, the tools enable faster response to emerging information attacks. The pilot strengthens media resilience by combining automation with editorial oversight, contributing to more effective protection of the public information space.

title: AI-Code - GenAi against disinformation: Use case 2
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Media organisations increasingly experiment with generative tools, yet concerns remain about quality, bias and the risk of amplifying disinformation. AI-CODE Use Case 3 addresses this challenge by supporting responsible use of generative technologies in journalism. Stakeholders include journalists, editors and media trainers. The objective is to improve content quality while strengthening professional awareness of generative risks. The use case delivers tools such as an interactive simulator and an AI-based personal companion that help media professionals test scenarios, identify misinformation and refine editorial judgement. Rather than automating publishing, the tools focus on skill development and decision support. Early validation shows improved understanding of generative limitations and increased confidence in identifying misleading content. This use case contributes to building long-term trust in media by ensuring that emerging technologies reinforce, rather than undermine, journalistic standards.

title: Diia.Engine - Ukrainian open-source platform for the public sector digitalisation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Ukraine developed Diia.Engine to address longstanding weaknesses in public-service delivery, including fragmented administrative systems, dependence on paper-based procedures and limited interoperability between existing digital solutions. These structural problems made service development slower, more expensive and harder to scale consistently across institutions. The platform was introduced to provide government bodies with a common foundation for building digital services more quickly and more uniformly. The stakeholders include national agencies, municipalities, service designers and citizens using digital public services, with the objective of reducing development cost, accelerating delivery and improving standardisation across the public sector. The solution is implemented as a national low-code, open-source platform based on reusable modules and shared digital components, including chatbot functions and automated validators. At a conceptual level, institutions build services by assembling standardised blocks rather than developing each system from scratch, which shortens implementation cycles and improves interoperability. Diia.Engine is now used by 23 government agencies and municipalities; more than 40 digital services have been built on the platform, over 80% of them using standard modules, and around 40% of the population has accessed services created this way. Reported estimates indicate possible annual savings of up to USD 50 million if 100 registries are deployed through the platform. More broadly, Diia.Engine creates value through scalability, lower infrastructure use, faster service delivery and a replicable model for public-sector digital transformation.

title: TRACY: A big-data analytics platform for law enforcement investigations
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The TRACY project was implemented to address the growing need for secure, efficient, and interoperable use of electronic communications metadata in the investigation of serious and organised crime across EU Member States. Law Enforcement Authorities (LEAs) often face fragmentation in accessing and analyzing telecom data, which hinders cross-border cooperation and slows down criminal investigations. TRACY provides an AI-powered data analytics framework tailored for LEAs, improving the timeliness, accuracy, and interoperability of investigations. Preliminary results indicate a significant improvement in processing time and data correlation across jurisdictions. Pilot implementation of TRACY for 6 months in real cases demonstrated a 1000x acceleration in crime resolution. With the use of visual analytics TRACY manages to pinpoint the perpetrators in all cases outperforming manual resolution. TRACY received positive feedback from over 80% of end-users who rated the tools as user-friendly and operationally relevant. Qualitative feedback also highlighted increased confidence in the legal and ethical compliance of the TRACY system, thanks to its embedded privacy-by-design and auditability features. The solution has achieved its core objectives of (1) demonstrating the feasibility of harmonized metadata analysis workflows, (2) equipping LEAs with scalable analytics tools, and (3) informing EU-wide training and standardisation efforts. By addressing both technological and procedural gaps, TRACY contributes to a more resilient, interoperable, and intelligence-led law enforcement ecosystem in Europe.

title: Robic: Inclusive AI for Special Learning
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: This pilot project explores the feasibility and educational impact of an AI-supported social robotics solution in a special education setting. Implemented at Colegio Gaudem in Madrid, the initiative aims to enhance the personal, cognitive, and emotional development of students with special educational needs through personalised, structured interactions using Inrobic Clinic and Inrobic Virtual. Between November 2024 and March 2025, 300 sessions were conducted involving 28 students, mostly in group formats. High satisfaction scores were reported by educators and families, with notable improvements in communication, motor skills, and engagement across subjects like math and language. Students responded positively, treating the robot as a peer and showing increased motivation. Teachers integrated the solution smoothly into their practices, and families expressed strong interest in its continuation. Early findings support the value and effectiveness of AI-assisted robotics in promoting inclusive and adaptive education.

title: Interoperability Platform - Finnish metadata platform for semantic linked data specifications as a service
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Digital and Population Data Services Agency (Finnish Digital Agency)
source_description: Interoperability platform is a metadata portal, from which the users can find, what kind of data there is available, who provides it, and what is the structure of the data. When the users find useful metadata descriptions, they do not have to re-invent that information, but can reuse existing descriptions, and so save time and money. When the developers use the same datamodels and code sets, unnecessary variation can be avoided. For example, the idea of OOTS is to use data that is collected by a certain authority, so that there is no need to copy the data for other authorities. Those can request the information they need from the authority that owns the data. But one needs to know the contents of the data in order to request it in semantically correct manner.
