Some of these pilots are already in production, while others are in the analysis phase. All pilots are documented and shared openly.

title: Document Review in Service Requests powered by Gen AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Italian National Institute of Social Security (INPS)
source_description: INPS provides services where users are required to submit various types of documents to support their requests, which must undergo a thorough review to verify their validity. This process involves the manual review of millions of documents annually by operators, all within a constrained timeframe. This involves a wide variety of documents (invoices, contracts, travel tickets, payment receipts, etc), making the process highly time-consuming and error prone. The goal of the project was to streamline and enhance the verification process through AI-powered automation, reducing manual workload, ensuring consistency in checks, and improving response times for citizens. To address these challenges, an innovative solution has been developed, integrating on-premise Generative Artificial Intelligence technologies designed to support operators in document analysis activities. Key features of the solution include: • Automatic classification of documents based on both type and content; • Data extraction and verification, with automated comparison between the information in the documents, the tender requirements, and the associated metadata; • Smart visualization of AI-extracted fields, with automatic highlighting directly within the document for easy reference; • Decision support, offering a detailed summary of the extracted data, flagging any discrepancies, and assisting with manual validation. This solution significantly streamlines the verification process, reducing manual effort and increasing both the speed and consistency of checks, delivering concrete benefits to both staff and citizens. Moreover, the system’s ability to adapt and learn from new data ensures continuous performance improvement, supporting progressively more effective procedure management. The solution aims to deliver benefits for both operators and citizens. Overall, the implementation of Generative AI has proven to be a transformative step in modernizing the document verification process, setting a strong foundation for future innovation and scalability. The next objective is primarily to adopt this solution for the other services within the INPS system.

title: Text Simplification for Citizens with GenAI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Italian National Institute of Social Security (INPS)
source_description: Clear and accessible communication is essential to ensure that citizens can effectively navigate public services. INPS—Italy’s National Institute of Social Security and the largest welfare institution in Europe—serves approximately 45 million citizens through nearly 500 digital services related to pensions and welfare. The clarity of these service descriptions plays a critical role in guaranteeing equitable access and a positive user experience. To address the challenges of bureaucratic language, INPS has launched a structured simplification program aimed at making content understandable to users with a middle school level of education. Over 700 texts have been manually simplified so far, resulting in an increase in the average Gulpease readability score from 57 to 64—a substantial improvement in accessibility. However, this manual process is labor-intensive, requiring specialised linguistic and legal expertise, and is not easily scalable. The need for plain language in public administration has long been acknowledged in Italy. A 2002 directive still in force emphasizes that “all texts produced by administrations must be designed and written to be understood by those who receive them.” Yet institutional communication remains overly formal and complex, hindering citizens’ ability to fully access and understand critical services. While simplification improves transparency and public trust, it must also preserve the legal precision required for official documentation. To overcome these limitations, INPS has integrated Large Language Models (LLMs) into its simplification workflow, developing a semi-automated system—operating in a human-in-the-loop model—that is both scalable and efficient. This solution can process high volumes of content while ensuring readability, semantic accuracy, and legal compliance. A dedicated evaluation framework was introduced to measure key aspects of the output, including readability, fluency, and content preservation. User testing further validated the approach, confirming the quality of AI-generated content in comparison to both the original and manually simplified texts. The AI-based system delivers expert-level results in a fraction of the time and cost required by manual processes. It enhances INPS’s operational efficiency, standardizes quality across service pages, and ensures that content remains accessible and legally sound. Human oversight guarantees accuracy and relevance, while integrated metrics provide transparency and guide ongoing optimization. A large-scale user study involving A/B testing with 1,620 participants confirmed the model’s effectiveness. AI-generated texts were preferred in over 70% of cases when compared to the original versions and outperformed them across all measured dimensions: fluency (+14.1%), readability (+13.5%), clarity (+11.1%), and engagement (+12.3%). The AI semplified versions outperformed also the corresponding human simplified texts across all the qualitative metrics. Citizens are the ultimate beneficiaries of this transformation. By simplifying complex institutional language, INPS reduces barriers to access for individuals with limited language skills, lower educational attainment, or reading difficulties. More inclusive communication strengthens transparency, encourages greater civic engagement, and builds trust between citizens and institutions. Beyond INPS, this AI-driven approach has strong potential for adoption in other sectors where complex language limits accessibility—such as healthcare, legal services, taxation, and social welfare. Its ability to adapt to diverse regulatory and linguistic contexts makes it a powerful tool for modernising public communication across government systems. In summary, the integration of LLMs into INPS’s content simplification strategy demonstrates how generative AI can enhance accessibility, efficiency, and trust in public services—delivering clear, comprehensible, and citizen-centered communication at scale.

title: Once-Only Common Services: Croatia uses cloud native, cloud agnostic building blocks to make accessing the Single Market simple and easier for EU citizens and businesses
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: Croatia has adopted the Once-Only Technical System (OOTS) to simplify cross-border procedures for citizens and businesses within the EU. The system allows official documents (e.g., certificates, diplomas, permits) to be exchanged securely and automatically between competent authorities, removing the need for individuals or companies to resubmit the same data multiple times. Implemented across numerous central government institutions – including ministries, agencies, and national registers – OOTS improves efficiency, transparency, and interoperability in public administration. By connecting to the EU-wide OOTS Common Services, Croatia helps reduce administrative costs and processing times, supporting a more seamless Digital Single Market and making it easier for citizens and businesses to live, work, study, and operate across borders.

title: Generation of environmental technical reports using Generative AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Generalitat de Catalunya: Centre of Telecommunications and Information Technology (CTTI) together with the “Department of Territory, Housing and Ecologic Transition""
source_description: The Generalitat de Catalunya has piloted a Generative AI–based system for drafting environmental technical reports, developed by the Centre of Telecommunications and Information Technology (CTTI) and the Department of Territory, Housing and Ecologic Transition. The solution addresses the high volume and repetitive nature of authorisations for activities in protected areas—such as mountain races, drone flights, and forest management—where more than 4,500 reports are prepared annually. By combining visual-language models, geospatial algorithms, and a vectorised legal knowledge base, the tool analyses route data and regulations to automatically generate draft reports. This has reduced report preparation time by around 45%, saving nearly 800 hours of manual work per year, while improving consistency, objectivity, and transparency in administrative processes. The system is fully integrated with the Generalitat’s secure intranet and platforms such as SINATCAT, supports Catalan language outputs, and complies with interoperability, security, and data protection standards. Designed to be modular, scalable, and reusable, it improves efficiency, standardises decision-making, and strengthens public trust by ensuring clearer, more uniform environmental reporting.

title: ELA 360: Humanising Public Services Through Collaborative Innovation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: ELA 360 is a pilot by the Regional Government of Andalusia to improve care for ALS patients under Spain’s new ALS Law (Law 3/2024). ALS requires rapid, coordinated support, but traditional processes caused long delays and stress for families. With automated data flows and proactive service triggers, ELA 360 has reduced waiting times from 1 year to under 3 months and eliminated paperwork, ensuring patients receive essential services faster and with less burden. Developed through co-creation with patients, families, and professionals, the solution integrates health and social systems, improves transparency, and builds trust in public administration. First piloted at Hospital Virgen Macarena, its scalable, modular design makes it adaptable to other municipalities and vulnerable groups, offering a replicable model for more empathetic public services.

title: Docklands Digital Twin: Laying the Foundations for Smarter Urban Futures

source_description: The Docklands Digital Twin, developed by Dublin City Council under the Smart Docklands programme, transforms complex spatial data into an interactive 3D model to support more transparent, evidence-based urban planning. Unlike static maps and siloed reports, the twin integrates multiple datasets into a shared virtual environment, accessible via desktop, web, and VR. Internally, it helps city stakeholders visualise proposed developments and coordinate planning. Externally, it improves public engagement and trust by allowing residents and community groups to explore future changes in an intuitive, accessible format. Developed with interoperability and scalability in mind, the model has already inspired replication beyond Docklands and is positioned to expand into areas such as mobility, climate resilience, and citizen participation. Delivered through collaboration between Dublin City Council, SMEs, and academia, the Docklands Digital Twin lays the groundwork for a citywide digital twin strategy, modernising governance and shaping smarter, more inclusive urban futures.

title: Madrid, Digital Capital: City Intelligence, 5G, Interoperability, aimed at improving citizens' well-being through Emerging Technologies
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: As part of its Digital Transformation Strategy, Madrid launched the 5G Agenda to provide advanced connectivity infrastructure, enabling smart, sustainable, and people-centered public services. The initiative modernises internal municipal operations and public-facing services, improving urban mobility, emergency response, waste management, and administrative efficiency for over 3.4 million residents, 5 million daily users, and 11 million annual visitors. Key implementations include 5G urban corridors, IoTMADLab, autonomous vehicles at Mercamadrid, and the EUGENIA emergency network, as well as enhanced connectivity at Valdemingómez Technology Park. The project has led to significant efficiency gains, including €246 million saved over five years, a 95% reduction in paper submissions, and measurable improvements in citizen satisfaction. Beyond operational benefits, the 5G Agenda has strengthened public-private collaboration, fostered innovation, and reinforced Madrid as a European benchmark in advanced connectivity and smart city services.

title: KIRA - AI research assistant
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Secretary of State of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg (Senatskanzlei)
source_description: Hamburg’s KIRA Research Assistant was developed to help public administration staff manage large volumes of legal and social-services documentation more efficiently. The administrative challenge is that employees handling social benefits requests must interpret complex legislation, locate relevant guidance and provide consistent answers under time pressure. This can slow case processing and create uneven service quality if information is difficult to retrieve. The main stakeholders include the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, the Senatskanzlei, public administration staff, social-benefit applicants and the InnoTecHH Fonds supporting the project. KIRA operates as an AI-driven knowledge tool and chatbot that retrieves relevant documentation and provides accurate answers to staff queries. Conceptually, it combines document retrieval, question answering, knowledge-base search and conversational access to legal and administrative information. Pilot results indicate strong performance, with an 87% top-k accuracy rate, a usability score of 9.75 out of 10 on the SUS measure, and high satisfaction among staff. The expected impact is shorter research time, more reliable processing of social benefits requests, reduced pressure on employees and more consistent service delivery. By supporting staff rather than replacing their judgement, KIRA improves the administrative knowledge workflow and directly benefits citizens through faster and more dependable handling of requests.

title: ERP And CRM Costumisation for Project Management in the Public Sector
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: The use case by the Ephorate of Antiquities of Western Attica aims to optimise project management at the Ephorate of Antiquities of Western Attica and maximise expenditure absorption per funding source. It identified key challenges including limited resources, insufficiently trained staff, incomplete procedures, rigid schedules, and ongoing legislative changes. title: Pepper robot as an examination assistant and source of information
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Technical University of Applied Sciences Wildau
source_description: Pepper at TH Wildau is a deployed library assistant, based on SoftBank’s humanoid platform and the NAOqi software stack. The project adapts Pepper for a 24/7 academic library, where access is card-controlled outside staffed hours. The robot greets visitors, answers common questions, guides users to locations across three floors, gives short tours, and demonstrates equipment such as the printer–scanner–copier. The solution combines scripted behaviors with a lightweight NLP pipeline. Behaviors are authored in Choregraphe/Python as modular, rule-based flows for gestures, tablet prompts, and navigation sequences. Speech interaction uses an open, componentised chain: automatic speech recognition (speech-to-text), intent and entity extraction for library domains (orientation, lending, services, events), response generation from curated templates and FAQs, and text-to-speech. The team prioritises transparent, locally hosted components over closed assistants. For perception and mobility, Pepper uses classical robotics methods for localisation and path planning; autonomous driving is complemented by tablet teleoperation for safety and elevators. Two units are operated: “Wilma” serves in the library as a mobile information point; “Bernd” is used in the RoboticLab for testing and training. Content and dialogs are updated iteratively, with analytics from interactions feeding refinements to intents, utterances, and tour scripts.

title: Vienna AI with generative search (de: WienKI mit generative Suche)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Vienna has proactively embraced artificial intelligence to modernise public administration and deliver tangible benefits to citizens and employees. Recognising the disruptive potential of generative AI, Vienna developed WienKI, a holistic AI platform designed to improve efficiency, safeguard data sovereignty, and foster responsible innovation. WienKI brings together secure, user-friendly tools such as multilingual assistants, knowledge databases with anonymisation functions, and image generation, supported by a strong governance framework and continuous staff training. More than 2,500 employees are already actively using the system, with over 100,000 chat interactions, 85,000 image generations, and 14,000 curated knowledge documents to date. Built on a modular, open-source architecture, WienKI ensures compliance with GDPR, the EU AI Act, and strict security standards, whilst remaining transparent, scalable, and reusable by other public institutions. It enhances internal efficiency, strengthens accessibility across 103 languages, and encourages a culture of responsible innovation throughout the administration. WienKI demonstrates how public administration can act as a pioneer in times of technological change—balancing innovation and responsibility to create sustainable value for both employees and citizens.

title: AI-Enhanced Processing of Business Registrations for Faster Public Service Delivery
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Berufsgenossenschaft Energie Textil Elektro Medienerzeugnisse (BG ETEM)
source_description: The statutory accident insurer BG ETEM faced a sharp rise in electronic business registrations, causing long delays and a five-digit backlog. To resolve this, it introduced the EDA GWA AI solution, which integrates artificial intelligence and robotic process automation into its core system. The tool now automatically categorises most registrations, checks data against external registers, and reduces manual effort, enabling routine cases to be processed quickly while staff focus on complex ones. Since its rollout in 2024, over 100,000 registrations have been handled, response times have improved, and the backlog has already been cut by 13%. Built with open-source components such as Python, Scikit-learn, XGBoost and Docker, the plugin is transparent, explainable, and compliant with strict legal standards. Its modular, containerised design makes it cost-efficient, robust, and transferable to other statutory insurers. By combining automation with human oversight, the solution delivers faster services for businesses, greater efficiency for administration, and strong potential for reuse across the wider social insurance sector.

title: RehaPlus: AI-Powered Identification of Complex Rehabilitation Cases in Public Health Insurance
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Berufsgenossenschaft Energie Textil Elektro Medienerzeugnisse (BG ETEM)
source_description: The statutory accident insurer BG ETEM introduced RehaPlus to improve the early identification of complex rehabilitation cases requiring intensive case management. Previously, such cases were often detected late through manual reminders, leading to delayed interventions, higher treatment costs and longer recovery times. RehaPlus applies explainable machine learning models to continuously monitor case data and flag potential high-risk cases weeks earlier than before. This has replaced the outdated manual reminder process with proactive, automated monitoring, while ensuring case officers remain in control of final decisions. The result is improved efficiency, fewer documents to screen or complete, earlier interventions, and better recovery outcomes for insured workers. Since going live in 2021, RehaPlus has delivered high user satisfaction, with more than 90 per cent of staff rating it positively for improving efficiency and quality of work. Built with open-source components such as Python, XGBoost, Scikit-learn, Pandas and Docker, the solution is lightweight, explainable, cost-efficient and fully compliant with GDPR. Its modular architecture makes it portable across infrastructures and scalable to other social accident insurers, with the first reuse planned for 2026. By combining automation with transparency and human oversight, RehaPlus demonstrates how AI can create both internal efficiency gains (G2G) and societal value (G2C) through better rehabilitation outcomes.

title: AI-Based Virtual Assistant for Faster and Reliable Businesses Support
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Berufsgenossenschaft Energie Textil Elektro Medienerzeugnisse (BG ETEM)
source_description: The statutory accident insurer BG ETEM developed a virtual assistant (MeinAssistent) to support its “Members and Fees” department, which has seen a sharp increase in inquiries from businesses. Around 70 per cent of queries concern recurring issues such as registration or insurance fees, which were previously handled manually, causing long response times and high workloads. The assistant provides a three-tiered service: immediate answers from a legally verified FAQ catalogue, context-specific responses generated from official ETEM documents with clear source references, and transparent escalation to staff if no automated answer is possible. This ensures businesses receive reliable, accurate, and timely support while keeping human oversight for complex cases. Early results from the pilot show clear benefits: 24/7 accessibility for businesses, faster responses, reduced interruptions for staff, and high trust thanks to transparent answer paths. Pilot users have praised the clarity, reliability, and seamless handover to human officers. Built with open-source components including Python, LangChain, Hugging Face models, FastAPI, and Docker, the system is modular, containerised, and API-based, making it cost-efficient, portable, and adaptable to other contexts. Although still in pilot, the solution is being integrated into the MeineETEM portal and is designed for transfer to other public sector organisations by connecting it to their own FAQs and documents. By combining automation, explainability, and scalability, MeinAssistent strengthens efficiency and accessibility in public service delivery while reducing manual workload for staff.

title: Digital Service for Obligated Citizens to Declare the Cleaning of Their Properties to Prevent Fire Risks or Rapid Fire Spread
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Climate Crisis and Civil Protection / Hellenic Fire Service / Fire Service Headquarters / Department of Preventive Fire Protection
source_description: The digital platform akatharista.gov.gr is an innovative tool designed to prevent and manage forest and grassland fires in Greece by monitoring the cleaning status of privately owned plots, a key preventive measure against fire outbreaks. The system enables citizens to declare the fire-prevention cleaning activities they have undertaken on their plots each season and allows them to report hazardous plots to supervisory authorities, supporting proactive intervention. For public administration, the platform consolidates and organises critical data—including plot location, ownership, cleaning history, and reported risks—allowing central and local authorities, such as the Fire Service and municipalities, to monitor compliance, assess risk, plan targeted inspections, and take timely preventive action. Since its launch in 2024, over 1.5 million cleaning declarations and 20,000 citizen reports have been processed, resulting in more than 18,000 on-site inspections and more efficient resource deployment. Technologically, the platform integrates with national databases, supports real-time GIS visualisation of plots, and provides automated notifications to citizens. Its interoperable and user-friendly design ensures accessibility, traceability, and transparency, while statistical analysis capabilities inform policy decisions on fire prevention and civil protection. Akatharista.gov.gr exemplifies a digital governance solution that enhances public participation, strengthens accountability, and safeguards human life, property, and ecosystems.

title: ChatAmsterdam - an internally developed generative AI chatbot tailored to the municipality's needs and values to support civil servants in their daily activities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: ChatAmsterdam is an internally developed generative AI assistant designed to support civil servants in the Municipality of Amsterdam. Developed through a six-month research pilot involving over 800 employees, the application provides practical assistance with daily tasks while promoting AI literacy, ensuring digital security, and safeguarding sensitive municipal data. ChatAmsterdam operates within a secure, vendor-neutral environment, prioritising data ownership, privacy, transparency, and compliance with Dutch and European regulations. The platform enables integration with internal data sources, allowing staff to pose domain-specific questions and receive contextually relevant answers. By providing a safe alternative to commercial generative AI tools, ChatAmsterdam reduces shadow use of external platforms and facilitates responsible AI adoption. Its flexible architecture allows future expansion, including additional functionalities, AI-assisted workflows, and integration of new datasets, while ensuring alignment with organisational values and operational goals. The application reflects a user-centred design approach, incorporating continuous feedback, training, and co-creation with staff to maximise usability, trust, and impact.

title: AI tool for depersonalising sensitive data at the State Consumer Rights Protection Authority (SCRPA)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The personal data depersonalisation AI tool is an internally developed solution designed to enhance data privacy, security, and regulatory compliance. By automatically identifying, masking, encrypting, or removing Personally Identifiable Information (PII), the tool ensures that datasets used for development, testing, and analysis are fully anonymised, embedding a “privacy by design” culture across the organisation. This automation has reduced manual depersonalisation time from several hours to under 15 minutes, achieving a 95% efficiency gain, while maintaining 99.8% accuracy in PII detection. The solution is fully interoperable with existing internal systems, integrates seamlessly into data pipelines, and complies with GDPR, CCPA, and organisational policies. Its advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) capabilities allow context-aware recognition of PII in structured and unstructured data, outperforming traditional rule-based methods. The tool has delivered measurable impact, including an 85% reduction in data breaches involving unauthorised PII exposure, significant labour cost savings, and increased user confidence. By providing a reliable, scalable, and user-friendly solution, the AI tool strengthens operational efficiency, data integrity, and transparency, allowing secure data sharing with internal teams and external partners without compromising privacy.

title: Virtual Market Assistant for the State Consumer Rights Protection Authority (SCRPA)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: The Virtual Market Assistant is an innovative mobile application designed to enhance consumer safety by providing instant access to information on officially listed hazardous products and enabling users to report new risks. It allows barcode scanning for instant product safety checks and simplifies the submission of detailed hazard reports, including photos and descriptions, which are standardised for seamless use by regulatory authorities. Technologically, the app leverages familiar mobile, cloud, and database infrastructure, providing a scalable and user-friendly solution without requiring specialised equipment. It is designed with full interoperability in mind, adhering to the European Interoperability Framework at legal, organisational, semantic, and technical levels, ensuring seamless integration with national and transnational market surveillance systems. By increasing transparency, accountability, and public engagement, the Virtual Market Assistant strengthens trust between citizens and regulatory authorities, streamlines hazard reporting, and accelerates the removal of unsafe products from the market.

title: DONNA: A digital assistant for IT operations
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

The solution leverages a modular, containerised architecture (Kubernetes/Kubeflow) with components including vLLM, Milvus, LangChain, LangGraph, Langfuse, and OpenWebUI, ensuring scalability, technical interoperability, and data sovereignty. Designed following the European Interoperability Framework (EIF), DONNA aligns with legal, organisational, semantic, and technical interoperability principles, supporting seamless integration with internal IT workflows and potential future cross-government systems. By using fully self-hosted, open-source technologies, DONNA enhances transparency, auditability, and independence from proprietary vendors, while a user-centred development process involving IT operators ensured high adoption, usability, and alignment with operational realities.

title: AI agent for Prague 6: Simplifying communication between the office and citizens
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Citymind chatbot was implemented by Prague 6 to improve citizen-office communication and streamline access to public services. Its primary function is to provide citizens with a quick, intuitive interface to find information—covering topics such as passport issuance, ID cards, and local police services—while freeing officials from answering routine inquiries. The project, funded under the Horizon Europe CommuniCity programme, combines co-creation with citizens and municipal staff to ensure a user-centred design, resulting in a high user satisfaction rating of 4.05 out of 5. Technologically, the solution is scalable, secure, and user-friendly, integrating seamlessly into municipal websites with minimal technical effort. Its structured data processing ensures semantic interoperability, translating complex administrative content into plain, human-like language. The chatbot also generates analytical reports on common queries, supporting internal service improvements and enhancing organisational efficiency. The innovation process involved participatory development, iterative testing, and a replicability guide to support adoption by other municipalities. Citymind is commercially managed, ensuring ongoing support and continuous development, while being aligned with European interoperability and accessibility principles.

title: AI Literacy in Action: An Interactive and Reusable Prompting Workbook for Public Servants
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The AI Prompting Workbook was developed to rapidly build AI literacy among public administration employees, addressing the limitations of passive training formats and fulfilling capacity-building requirements under the EU AI Act. The interactive, self-paced workbook allows users to engage directly with an internal AI model (“LinzGPT”), experimenting with prompts, executing them in real time, and receiving instant feedback across 50 practical exercises. Internal metrics—voluntary enrolment, course completion, and certificate issuance—demonstrate high uptake and effectiveness, while qualitative feedback from the “AI Pioneers” focus group confirms its practical relevance and engaging format. Technologically, the solution leverages a lightweight web application and structured content (JSON-based exercises), enabling semantic, organisational, technical, and legal interoperability. It is designed for easy scaling and reuse, both internally and as a public Google Gemini Canvas, allowing other administrations to customise or expand the workbook without programming knowledge. The implementation followed a user-centric, agile process, combining in-house prototyping, co-creation with internal focus groups, and rigorous IT validation, with no external procurement required. The dual-delivery model ensures secure internal deployment while maximising public value and societal impact, supporting AI capacity-building and fostering a broader culture of digital empowerment across Europe.

title: Regional Digital Twin Platform for Climate Change
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Regional Digital Twin for Climate Change provides a data-driven platform for climate risk assessment, simulation, and decision support, addressing gaps in integrating EU-scale climate data into local and sector-specific operations. It enhances resilience across public services and critical sectors—energy, finance, agriculture, and emergency planning—by combining diverse datasets, AI and physical simulations, and a climate services marketplace. The platform also federates stakeholders, fostering collaboration and trust. Pilot users in Luxembourg report improved risk understanding, faster and more informed decisions, and strengthened public and financial resilience. Technologically, it integrates satellite, in-situ, topographic, and regional data via AI and HPC-powered cloud solutions, offering real-time insights and multi-sectoral services. Designed according to the European Interoperability Framework (EIF), the platform ensures legal, organisational, semantic, and technical interoperability. Transparency is enhanced through dashboards, open data where possible, and workshops for stakeholders. Its modular architecture allows scalable deployment across sectors, regions, and administrative levels, with the potential for broader adoption by other administrations. The project follows a user-centred innovation process, beginning with a Proof of Concept by Thales Alenia Space, LIST, and PwC, incorporating feedback from ministries and critical infrastructure operators to ensure practical, actionable outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence Services Oriented to Legal Documents
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Dirección General de Transformación Digital de la Administración de Justicia
source_description: The Ministry of the Presidency, Justice, and Relations with the Courts has harnessed Artificial Intelligence to manage vast volumes of unstructured legal information and streamline tens of thousands of procedures each year. AI tools support civil servants, judges, magistrates, and prosecutors by extracting and linking relevant information, generating timelines, summarising documents, and assisting with rule-based processes. A key initiative is the automatic transcription of hearings and trials, achieving an estimated 60% time saving, with over 3.28 million transcriptions completed to date, saving more than one million hours of work. AI services also produce plain-language and easy-to-read documents, enhancing accessibility for citizens, including those with functional or intellectual difficulties. The AI infrastructure combines natural language processing, supervised neural networks, Transformer-based models, and GPU-enabled servers, deployed within a secure microservices architecture. Services are accessible via portals such as ADIA and Carpeta Justicia and include anonymisation, document summarisation, intelligent assistants, and translation tools. These tools are integrated across multiple internal applications and are already being reused by other administrations, demonstrating scalability and interoperability. Development followed a user-centred, iterative process involving legal experts, linguists, programmers, and administrative staff. Solutions were piloted on a small scale and then expanded strategically, supported by knowledge-sharing initiatives such as the Justice Digital Transformation Forum. Overall, AI innovations have transformed operations, improved efficiency, fostered a culture of innovation, enhanced accessibility, and strengthened transparency and public trust in the justice system.

title: Diia.AI: The World's First National AI Agent for Government Services
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
source_description: On September 1, 2025, Ukraine became the first country in the world to introduce an AI assistant for government services via its Diia portal. Announced by Digital Transformation Minister Mykhailo Fedorov on Telegram, the AI tool is currently in open beta testing. Designed to enhance convenience and efficiency, it guides users through accessing public services, recommends the most suitable options based on their personal situations, and can even provide vital personal data—such as insurance records—within the chat interface.

title: Digital Management Platform for Public Administrations Sedipualb@
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Provincial Council of Albacete (Diputación de Albacete)
source_description: SEDIPUALB@ is a digital platform created by the Provincial Council of Albacete to enable fully digital administrative management for municipalities. Initially launched to serve local governments within the province, it provides a shared, open, and interoperable system that simplifies administrative processes and eliminates barriers such as licensing costs or dependence on political cycles. Delivered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, the platform is built on open technologies and deployed in the cloud, ensuring scalability, flexibility, and cost-efficiency. Albacete became the only province in Spain where all municipalities adopted a unified digital management platform. Since then, SEDIPUALB@ has expanded well beyond its original scope. Today, more than 300 public entities—including municipalities, consortia, and universities across seven autonomous regions—use the system. It supports over a million citizens and thousands of concurrent users daily. Governance is collaborative, with technical, legal, and administrative bodies advising on improvements, while costs are distributed among participants according to usage. This model ensures both sustainability and transparency, turning a local project into a national benchmark for digital public administration.

title: AI for Species Protection - Detection of Illegal Online Wildlife Trade
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: AI Lab at the German Environment Agency (UBA) and Federal Nature Conservation Agency
source_description: Germany’s Federal Agency for Nature Conservation, together with the AI Lab at the German Environment Agency, developed an AI-driven tool to detect illegal online trading of protected species, one of the fastest-growing environmental crimes worldwide. The system combines AI-powered image classification, rule-based text analysis, and tailored web scraping to scan thousands of online listings daily, identifying species even when disguised or misspelled. During a six-month pilot, the tool flagged over 50,000 protected animals from more than 1,250 CITES-listed species, transforming an unmanageable manual task into a scalable, data-driven process. It frees public servants from repetitive screening, allowing them to focus on high-risk cases, improving efficiency, and strengthening enforcement. Built entirely in-house with open-source technologies, the system ensures digital sovereignty, sustainability, and compliance with European interoperability standards. It has already inspired international interest, including from the Czech CITES authority, and provides a transferable model for EU-wide biodiversity protection.

title: Impulsa Autónomo: Intelligent Platform to Personalise Grants and Subsidies for the Self-Employed in Galicia through AI
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Impulsa Autónomo was developed by the Xunta de Galicia to simplify how self-employed professionals identify and access grants, subsidies and support measures. The administrative problem is that funding opportunities are often dispersed across different portals, calls and institutional sources, making it difficult for autónomos to understand which schemes are relevant to their activity, situation and eligibility profile. The platform consolidates this information into a single intelligent portal and widget, reducing fragmentation and improving the user journey. Its implementation uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation–based generative AI, connected to official databases, to provide personalised recommendations rather than static lists of subsidies. The system combines official information retrieval, conversational guidance, personalised publication of subsidies, automatic alerts, BI dashboards, satisfaction monitoring and two-way feedback channels. Early results indicate reductions in search time of more than 60% and over 100 hours of integrated specialised advisory services. The expected impact is faster access to relevant support, lower administrative costs through automated responses, more transparent communication of available aid, and stronger interaction between the administration and self-employed workers. Its design also supports interoperability and regulatory alignment, making it a potentially replicable model for digital public services. The Xunta’s official Oficina Virtual do Autónomo is currently online and provides information on support and grants for self-employment.

title: AI-Driven Market Surveillance to Safeguard Consumers in the Digital Single Market
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Launched in 2022 by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers (DG JUST), this project delivers an EU-wide platform that enables systematic surveillance of online marketplaces across all EU and EEA languages. By simulating human interaction to overcome obstacles like pop-ups, captchas, and hidden content, it ensures access to data that traditional crawlers cannot reach. The platform records dangerous products taken offline, fostering transparency, cross-border cooperation, and a shared view of enforcement progress. With the integration of large language models, the system significantly improves the precision of product identification, reducing false positives and enabling inspectors to focus on genuine risks. This shift accelerates enforcement cycles, supports Member States in handling the growing influx of imported parcels, and enhances consumer protection across the Single Market. Aligned with European interoperability principles and EU product-safety legislation, the platform connects seamlessly with the Safety Gate Rapid Alert System. It provides authorities with a cost-effective, centralised, and secure service that strengthens regulatory enforcement while generating valuable insights for future EU policy-making.

title: The Responsive PIAO: An AI-Enabled Model for Proactive and Continuous Skill Development
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Launched by LepidaSCpA in collaboration with the Italian public administration, the project introduces a strategic, data-driven approach to staff training, aligning professional development directly with the organisational objectives set out in the Piano integrato di attività e organizzazione (PIAO). Using an iterative Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle, it optimises training investment by mapping identified needs to existing courses on national platforms, ensuring both efficiency and value for money. Generative AI models, employed under human supervision, supported the design and analysis of tools such as the “interests and perceived gaps questionnaire”, which improved communication between management and employees and fostered organisational trust. The pilot phase recorded high levels of user satisfaction, validating the methodology’s potential to shift training strategies from intuition to evidence-based planning. Fully aligned with the European Interoperability Framework, the project demonstrates legal, organisational, semantic, and technical interoperability. It enhances transparency by creating a structured channel for employee feedback and by making its standardised training course index publicly available, offering a replicable model for other administrations.

title: GREEN-LOG Last-Mile Digital Control Tower: An AI-Driven Platform for Real-Time Optimisation and Sustainable Urban Logistics
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The GREEN-LOG Last-Mile Digital Control Tower (DCT), developed as part of the EU co-funded GREEN-LOG project, addresses the growing challenges of urban last-mile logistics driven by e-commerce expansion. The platform provides real-time monitoring of delivery assets, near real-time forecasting of transport demand and traffic conditions, and advanced data-driven analytics to enhance operational coordination among logistics service providers, city authorities, and other stakeholders. Leveraging AI-powered predictive models, dynamic multi-modal routing, and Logistics-as-a-Service (LaaS) Marketplace metrics, the system optimises fleet utilisation, reduces carbon emissions, and minimises urban congestion while improving delivery efficiency and reliability. Demonstrations across European cities, including Athens, Barcelona, and Flemish urban areas, have shown reductions in kilometres driven (-35%), travel time (-26%), and the number of stops (-12%), delivering both environmental and economic benefits. The DCT’s flexible, modular architecture enables deployment across diverse urban contexts, supports cross-modal routing, and integrates policy constraints and incentives set by local authorities. Its design aligns with the European Interoperability Framework, ensuring legal, semantic, organisational, and technical interoperability, GDPR compliance, and secure, transparent data sharing. Stakeholder engagement and continuous co-creation have driven usability and adoption, with user satisfaction reaching 90% in early 2026, demonstrating the platform’s effectiveness in supporting sustainable and efficient urban logistics.

title: Decision Support System Supporting Intelligent Real-time Resource Allocation of Response Teams (RART) for wildfire suppression
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Region of Central Greece (Perifereia Stereas Elladas), Greece
source_description: The RART tool, developed under the SILVANUS GreenDeal project by NETCOMPANY, is a Decision Support System designed to assist fire commanders in optimising wildfire response. By dynamically allocating available firefighting resources, including aerial and ground units, based on fire spread projections, population density, and resource availability, the system enhances situational awareness and enables more effective, timely interventions, reducing the impact on citizens, property, and the environment. The tool integrates open-source population data, AI-driven fire forecasting, and a multi-objective optimisation algorithm to guide resource deployment under complex, time-sensitive conditions. Field tests in October 2024 by the Region of Sterea Ellada, Greece, and simulations in France demonstrated high user satisfaction (>90%) and confirmed the system’s effectiveness in supporting decision-making under real-life constraints.

title: AI-Driven Early Warning and Decision Support for Fraud Prevention in Quality-Labelled Food Supply Chains
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Bavarian State Office for Health and Food Safety (Bayerisches Landesamt für Gesundheit und Lebensmittelsicherheit – LGL)
source_description: The ALLIANCE EWDSS, developed by Netcompany S.A. as part of the EU-funded ALLIANCE project, is an AI-powered system designed to detect and mitigate food fraud across complex supply chains. Focusing on sectors such as Feta Cheese, Organic Pasta, Organic Honey, and Fava Beans, the solution combines Artificial Intelligence, fuzzy logic, operations research, and multi-criteria decision analysis to provide early risk detection, transparent risk scoring, and actionable decision support for farmers, auditors, and regulators. The system employs domain-specific monitoring—including real-time pH and temperature data for feta cheese, anomaly detection for honey, and machine learning models for fava beans—to proactively identify potential fraud before it enters production. Developed through a co-creation approach, it ensures usability, transparency, and stakeholder engagement, enabling evidence-based decision-making, consistent risk management, and compliance with food safety and certification standards. By integrating human-in-the-loop decision support and standardised data models, ALLIANCE EWDSS fosters collaboration, accountability, and trust across the food supply chain, representing a significant advancement over conventional single-method detection systems.

title: AI-Driven Harmonisation of Albanian Legislation with the EU Aquis
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: National Agency of Information Society, under the Prime Minister’s authority
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The AI-assisted platform, developed by Microsoft in partnership with the Albanian Government, accelerates the transposition of EU legislation into Albanian law, enhancing both administrative efficiency (G2G) and public service quality (G2C, G2B). By combining AI-powered translation (ChatGPT-4 architecture) with automated compliance table generation, the system reduces manual effort, improves accuracy, and tracks thousands of EU measures and national acts requiring alignment. Implemented within the existing PIEA (European Integration and Membership Platform), the solution supports Albanian institutions without restructuring, providing real-time access to CELEX documents and ensuring full interoperability across legal, organisational, semantic, and technical levels. Phase 2 introduces AI-based legal analysis to detect overlaps and contradictions, helping Albania stay on track to meet its EU integration objectives by 2030.

title: Archimede (Antifrode) - Evolution of Anti-Fraud Systems and Continuous Internal Auditing
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL)
source_description: Archimede is an AI-driven solution developed by INAIL to detect and anticipate errors, evasions, and fraud (EEF), supporting effective risk prevention policies and highlighting process anomalies. During testing, the system demonstrated high accuracy: in six central audits, 100% of flagged cases were confirmed as anomalous, with 44% showing non-compliance in case handling. By integrating with INAIL’s auditing systems and the CRIBIS business information database, Archimede enables the identification of mismanagement and process irregularities, forming a core component of ongoing monitoring and auditing strategies. Built as a versatile, open-source on-premise solution, it ensures secure handling of confidential data and is fully adapted to INAIL’s organisational and analytical context, providing a competitive technological advantage.

title: The Pre-University Management Information System (SMIP/PUMIS)
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: National Agency for Information Society (NAIS) – in cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Sports.
source_description: The Smart Management Information Platform (SMIP) was introduced to modernise Albania’s education governance and overcome the inefficiencies of manual, paper-based processes, fragmented communication, and limited digital access. As a unified platform, SMIP brings together education, health, and administration in a way not previously available in the country. It currently integrates more than 407,000 students, 35,000 teachers, and 800,000 parents, providing real-time academic updates for families, digital reporting tools for teachers, and centralised dashboards for education authorities. The platform also supports wider public services, such as issuing over 10,000 digital vaccine cards via the national e-Albania portal, and promoting digital literacy, with more than 74,000 students trained in ICT skills through SmartLabs. By interoperating with national systems like e-Albania, the e-Vaccine system, and the NAIS Government Data Centre, SMIP improves efficiency, reduces bureaucracy, and strengthens transparency in education management. Aligned with the country’s Digital Agenda 2022–2026 and designed in line with EIF interoperability principles, SMIP enables evidence-based policy-making, enhances parental engagement, and lays the foundation for future regional cooperation, including cross-border diploma recognition.

title: Cruscotto infortuni - Cognitive Systems for Road Accidents
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL)
source_description: The Road Accident Analysis Dashboard, developed by INAIL, strengthens workplace safety policies by providing structured data and AI-driven insights into incidents that significantly contribute to annual injury statistics. Designed for the Central Health Supervisory Authority, the tool enables the identification of trends, risk factors, and intervention areas, supporting more targeted prevention strategies. Based on Oracle Analytics Server, Cloudera, and IBM Watson, the platform integrates institutional records with predictive analytics to improve data accuracy and uncover previously unclassified accidents. It currently covers incidents from 2018 onwards and will expand to a ten-year overview, with updates every six months. Early adoption shows strong user engagement, high satisfaction, and recognised added value, making it a reliable foundation for evidence-based decision-making and future predictive planning.

title: MyInail Chatbot - support tool for INAIL users
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL)
source_description: The MyInail Chatbot provides users with guided, conversational support across INAIL’s wide range of services, from healthcare and financial benefits to prevention and training. Launched in June 2024, it improves accessibility to INAIL’s knowledge base while directing users to the most appropriate support channels when needed. Integrated into both the INAIL web portal and mobile app, the chatbot reduces contact centre calls, ensures secure and privacy-compliant interactions, and is continuously updated through user feedback. Early adoption shows strong satisfaction and no reported service complaints, confirming its role as a reliable first-level assistance and knowledge management tool.

title: AI-powered Linguistic Mediator: A Phygital Solution for Inclusive and Accessible Public Services at INAIL
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL)
source_description: To respond to the needs of an increasingly diverse workforce—20% of insured workers in Italy are foreign-born—INAIL has developed the Linguistic Mediator, an AI-powered tool that provides real-time voice and text interpretation at service counters. Integrated into INAIL’s “phygital” service model, it helps front-office staff, social workers, and doctors communicate effectively with non-Italian-speaking users, improving access to services while streamlining internal processes. Early pilots in territorial offices have shown strong results, with translation accuracy around 92% and clear efficiency gains for staff. Built on Microsoft Azure AI Services, the solution is modular, secure, and interoperable, with future extensions planned for document translation and Italian Sign Language (LIS).

title: JuntaGPT: the internal GenAI based assistant for civil servants within the biggest regional administration in Europe.
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: In June 2025, the Andalusian Regional Government launched JuntaGPT, an on-premises generative AI assistant for its internal personnel — over 240,000 civil servants — to help with document drafting, normative queries, summarising, email writing, and other administrative text work. Developed by the regional digital agency (ADA) and deployed on the Hércules supercomputer at CICA, the system is designed to ensure digital sovereignty, data protection, and that all information remains securely within the Junta’s environment. It allows users to upload documents, ask questions naturally, chain conversational queries, and access pre-loaded information by domain without always having to upload files. Early stages of deployment are underway; the tool is already partly active and intended to improve productivity, efficiency, and internal service quality by streamlining the drafting and information-retrieval tasks of public employees.

title: On Record, a tool to help engage youth and other stakeholders in current decision-making processes.
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Agency for State Technological Reform Agency (ARTE), Portuguese Institute for Sport and Youth (IPDJ) and the Cascais Municipality
source_description: Portugal launched the “On Record” platform to address the democratic challenge of politically disengaged youth, despite their digital savviness. Developed by LabX/ARTE with support from the Portuguese Institute for Sport and Youth (IPDJ) and the Cascais Municipality, the project is part of the EU-funded initiative Improving Civic Participation through Emerging Technologies. On Record is a modular, AI-enabled deliberation and engagement platform embedded in Participa.gov, designed specifically to amplify youth voices (ages 14–30) in policymaking. It combines structured dialogue environments, gamified learning tools, AI-powered transcription and summarisation, and user tracking to ensure continuity across participation cycles. Pilots (2025) have shown its capacity to lower barriers to participation, foster inclusive debate, and enhance transparency by linking proposals to policy follow-up. With interoperability built into its architecture, GDPR compliance, and integration with national digital identity tools, the solution is both scalable within Portugal and transferable across Europe. By co-designing with youth and institutions, Portugal is creating a sustainable digital public good that strengthens trust, accountability, and democratic engagement, while setting the foundations for broader adoption beyond youth participation.

title: KIEZ - an Agentic AI Assistant for Development Cooperation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
source_description: KIEZ is an AI-powered assistant developed by the Datalab of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) to support public servants in processing large volumes of text and improving decision-making in the domain of economic cooperation. Built as a trustworthy chat interface, KIEZ integrates agentic tools, domain-specific prompt templates, document uploads, controlled internet search, and internal databases, while balancing usability with strict privacy, security, and vendor-independence measures. The platform enables tasks such as document summarisation, translation, and refinement, and operates on a cloud-native, GDPR-compliant infrastructure that supports multiple AI models, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). KIEZ has already demonstrated strong impact, with 44% of surveyed staff rating it “important” or “very important” to their work and 51% reporting improvements in efficiency and communication. With over 1.6 million tokens processed daily, KIEZ exemplifies a scalable, secure, and interoperable AI solution for modernising public administration workflows, funded by NextGenerationEU.

title: Alhambra and Generalife Digital Twin Living Lab: Technology to Preserve Beauty.
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Alhambra Living Lab is an initiative led by the Andalusian Digital Agency (ADA) to develop a comprehensive digital twin of the Alhambra and Generalife palaces in Granada. Announced by Antonio Sanz, Regional Minister for the Presidency, Interior, Social Dialogue, and Administrative Simplification, and supported by Patricia del Pozo, Regional Minister for Culture and Sport, and Marifrán Carazo, Mayor of Granada, the project seeks to transform how visitors experience the Nasrid complex while improving its conservation, accessibility, and sustainability. Funded with over €3.2 million (€3,226,546) through the Spain Living Lab initiative within the Territorial Networks of Technological Specialisation (RETECH) programme, the Alhambra Living Lab will run until June 2026. The project integrates advanced technologies, including 3D modeling, IoT sensors, AI, mixed reality, and blockchain, to create a virtual replica of the monuments. This digital twin will allow the testing of innovative solutions to manage visitor flows, monitor environmental and structural conditions, enhance cultural engagement, and support sustainable heritage preservation. The first use cases are expected to launch in the first quarter of 2025, providing actionable insights for both site management and visitors. By combining state-of-the-art digital technologies with real-world heritage conservation, the Alhambra Living Lab represents one of Europe’s most forward-thinking cultural digital twin projects, offering a model for balancing tourism, sustainability, and citizen engagement.

title: ParticipApp - more inclusive, transparent, and effective citizen participation in government decision-making
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service
source_description: ParticipApp is a national digital platform designed to make citizen participation in government decision-making more inclusive, transparent, and effective. The platform allows contributions in all co-official languages of Spain, and supports multiple input types, including text, voice, and images of handwritten notes. Using AI-powered tools, ParticipApp clusters and summarizes contributions thematically, helping participants and policymakers make sense of large volumes of input. The platform also provides AI-assisted drafting, enabling users to refine proposals while retaining full control over their content. Highly supported ideas can then be routed to a voting phase and formally considered in policy processes. For administrators, ParticipApp offers comprehensive dashboards to monitor participation, track emerging trends, moderate contributions, and measure engagement and impact. Built on open-source frameworks like Decidim and Consul and hosted on GDPR-compliant EU infrastructure, the platform is modular, scalable, and interoperable with existing digital public services. ParticipApp lowers barriers to participation, particularly for marginalised groups or those with limited digital literacy, and ensures transparency by providing visible summaries of contributions and clear feedback on how ideas are integrated into decision-making. By combining AI with human oversight, the platform strengthens public trust, enhances the quality and legitimacy of consultations, and establishes a sustainable digital public infrastructure for participatory governance, with potential for adoption across other European countries.

title: Integration of an Innovative Product – AI Technology – into Public Procurement Object Price Analysis and Forecasting, and Centralized Public Procurement Savings Identification Procedures
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Public Institution CPO LT (Viešoji įstaiga CPO LT)
source_description: The Republic of Lithuania is pioneering the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into centralised public procurement to improve efficiency, transparency, and cost-effectiveness. Led by CPO LT, the national Central Purchasing Body, this project uses a generative AI solution — including large language models (LLMs) and advanced analytics — to analyse procurement prices, forecast costs, and calculate actual savings. In 2024, CPO LT managed €1.245 billion in procurements, representing around 15% of Lithuania’s total public procurement.The AI tool enables real-time market price analysis, identifies overpriced offers, predicts procurement values with high accuracy, and optimises supplier selection. These capabilities result in lower prices, reduced resource requirements for contracting authorities, increased supplier competition, and greater trust in procurement processes. The project complies with EU interoperability and procurement regulations, aligns with the European AI Act, and integrates open data sources such as CPO LT’s catalogue and kainos24.lt. Developed by NFQ Technologies, it is the first AI-based public procurement solution in Lithuania and represents a scalable model for other EU Member States. The pilot version is currently undergoing testing, with full deployment expected in December 2025, marking a significant step towards more transparent and efficient public procurement in the country.

title: Once-Only Common Services: Portugal uses cloud native, cloud agnostic building blocks to make accessing the Single Market simple and easier for EU citizens and businesses
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Portugal is making it easier for citizens to live, study, work, or retire in other EU countries through the Once-Only Technical System (OOTS), an EU-wide framework that reduces the administrative burden of cross-border procedures. With OOTS, citizens and businesses only need to submit required documents (“evidences”) once, as these can be securely exchanged between public authorities across Member States, including permits, certificates, diplomas, or licenses. In December 2023, Portugal went live with the OOTS Common Services, which enable interoperability between procedure portals across the EU, covering around 80,000 national competent authorities. The system reuses existing technical components like eID and eDelivery, and is developed as open-source, ensuring scalable, secure, and GDPR-compliant operations. OOTS simplifies life events such as registering a vehicle abroad, studying, or running a business, while improving administrative efficiency, trust in shared data, and transparency. Early studies suggest that SMEs and self-employed workers could save up to 50% of costs and time when completing cross-border procedures. Students applying to study abroad can also save days or weeks in administrative processes. Portugal is now progressing to level 5 on the OOTS Acceleratormeter, aiming for the first live transactions in collaboration with the Directorate-General for Higher Education. Through OOTS, Portugal contributes to a seamless EU digital single market, enabling faster, more transparent, and citizen-centric public services across Europe.

title: (AILUME) - Artificial Intelligence-Based Application for the Early Detection of Forest Fire Outbreaks
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Agency for Technological Modernization of Galicia (AMTEGA) – Xunta de Galicia
source_description: AILUME is an artificial intelligence system developed to strengthen Galicia’s response to one of its greatest environmental threats: forest fires. The region’s vast forest coverage, rural depopulation, and increasing climate change impacts make early detection essential. AILUME addresses this by continuously analysing video streams from the Xunta de Galicia’s forest surveillance camera network, strategically placed across the territory. Using advanced deep learning models, optimised YOLO detectors, and vision-language reasoning, the system identifies smoke, filters false alarms, and provides explainable alerts to operators at the Central Coordination Center for Forest Fire Defense. The platform combines state-of-the-art AI with robust software architecture: a Django-based modular backend, Apache Kafka for distributed real-time processing, PyAV/OpenCV for video capture, and PostgreSQL for structured data management. It includes a human-in-the-loop feedback system, ensuring that operator validation contributes to continuous learning and higher detection accuracy. Designed for resilience and scalability, the solution can handle dozens of concurrent video streams with sub-second data latency, operating 24/7 under real production conditions. Pilot testing launched in August 2025 has confirmed its effectiveness: 86.1% detection success in real-world cases, precision of 98.2%, recall of 99.9%, and detection lead times averaging 18 minutes earlier than official notification channels. The system has already proven especially valuable in depopulated rural areas where traditional surveillance is limited, outperforming commercial alternatives in both accuracy and speed.

title: NORMA - virtual assistant for the analysis of legislative production
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Polytechnic University of Milan and the Einaudi Institute for Economics and Finance
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
