title: AI Mobility Challenge - DataTalks
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Cities increasingly collect mobility, parking, weather and infrastructure data, but much of this information remains difficult for residents and visitors to use in everyday decisions. DataTalks, presented by NinjaLabo during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this problem by creating a natural-language interface to urban data. The operational problem is that users may need to combine several sources of information before making a simple mobility choice: whether there is parking available, whether weather conditions make walking or cycling practical, or whether a trip can be planned more efficiently. DataTalks connects to different data interfaces and allows users to ask ordinary-language questions such as whether there is space in a specific parking garage and whether they need an umbrella outside. At a conceptual level, the service acts as a conversational data broker: it translates a user’s practical question into queries against parking, weather and potentially other urban datasets, then returns an integrated answer. The expected impact is easier access to city data, reduced unnecessary driving, smarter journey planning and better use of existing infrastructure. The case is significant because it demonstrates how AI can make open or municipal data more actionable for non-technical users. Rather than presenting a dashboard that requires interpretation, the tool provides answers in a form closer to how people make daily travel decisions. It remains a challenge-stage solution rather than a confirmed deployed municipal service, but it illustrates a promising direction for AI-enabled citizen mobility support.

title: AI Mobility Challenge - CamTalks
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Smart-city cameras can support traffic and public-space management, but they also raise privacy concerns if raw images are transmitted, stored or analysed centrally. CamTalks, presented by NinjaLabo during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this tension by using edge computing to analyse camera feeds locally. The operational problem is that city authorities may want information such as how many people are present in a scene, whether a space is crowded, or whether mobility conditions are changing, but they do not necessarily need to retain identifiable images. CamTalks processes video data on site rather than sending raw footage to the cloud, allowing users to ask simple questions such as “how many people are in the picture?” and receive an answer based on local AI analysis. At a conceptual level, the system turns camera feeds into metadata while reducing exposure of personal data. This is important because urban AI systems must balance situational awareness with citizens’ rights to privacy and proportionality. The expected impact is improved real-time understanding of urban movement, better support for transport or event management, and reduced data-protection risks compared with centralised video analytics. The case is relevant because it shows a privacy-preserving design principle for AI-enabled cities: computation can be moved to the edge, and only necessary outputs can be shared. It should be treated as a challenge-stage or potential pilot solution, since the available source describes it as one of several ideas being refined within Espoo’s AI Mobility Challenge.

title: AI Mobility Challenge - 0Flow
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Urban freight and service logistics generate emissions when vehicles travel with unused capacity, poorly coordinated routes or unnecessary trips. 0Flow, presented by Finnish Logistics Group during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this problem by using AI and data to improve utilisation of transport capacity. The operational problem is that many freight trips are not fully loaded or are planned without a complete view of available capacity, demand and routing possibilities. This creates avoidable traffic, emissions and operating costs. 0Flow proposes to optimise freight loads and route planning so that vehicles make better use of available space and reduce underutilised movements. At a conceptual level, the system treats urban logistics as an optimisation problem: available vehicles, parcels, destinations, time windows and route constraints can be analysed together to identify more efficient combinations. AI can support matching demand with capacity, grouping deliveries, reducing empty or partially empty trips and improving operational planning. The expected impact is lower transport-related emissions, fewer unnecessary kilometres, improved logistics efficiency and better use of existing vehicle fleets. The case is relevant because city climate strategies often focus on passenger mobility, while freight and service traffic also contribute materially to emissions and congestion. 0Flow shows how AI can support the less visible logistics layer of urban mobility. However, it should be framed as a challenge-stage solution under development, not as an already implemented citywide freight-optimisation platform.

title: AI Mobility Challenge - Traffic Info
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Mobility information is only useful if people can access it quickly, understand it and apply it to their journey decisions. In multilingual urban environments, standard traffic bulletins or map-based alerts may not be equally accessible to all residents, commuters or visitors. Traffic Info, presented by Cadweiser during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this issue by using AI to generate traffic updates and announcements in natural language, both written and spoken. The operational problem is that traffic data may exist in structured systems, but users need understandable messages in the language and format most convenient to them. Traffic Info proposes a multilingual AI layer that can transform transport information into accessible announcements, improving communication about disruptions, congestion, route changes or travel conditions. At a conceptual level, the system connects mobility data with language generation: raw traffic information is translated into user-facing communication that can be delivered through speech or text. The expected impact is better access to real-time mobility information, improved inclusion for residents and visitors with different language backgrounds, smoother journey planning and potentially more efficient traffic flow as users adjust behaviour based on clearer information. The case is significant because it focuses on communication as a mobility intervention. Better transport systems do not only require sensors and infrastructure; they also require people to receive the right information in a usable form. Like the other Espoo challenge entries, Traffic Info should be classified as a solution in development or pilot preparation rather than a confirmed deployed municipal service.

title: AI Mobility Challenge - Dynamik Allocator
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Mobile workers such as service technicians, inspectors, maintenance staff and field personnel often travel between multiple tasks during the day, and inefficient scheduling can create unnecessary driving, fuel use, emissions and lost working time. Dynamik Allocator, developed by Paavo Kytölä and Anita Kuitunen, addresses this problem by using AI to optimise daily routes and task allocation for mobile workers. The operational problem is that manual scheduling may not fully account for geography, time windows, task duration, staff availability and route efficiency. Even small inefficiencies repeated across many workers and days can produce significant emissions and costs. Dynamik Allocator proposes to arrange job sequences and schedules more intelligently, minimising redundant travel while preserving operational requirements. At a conceptual level, the tool treats field-service work as a routing and allocation optimisation challenge: AI can analyse tasks, locations and constraints to recommend sequences that reduce unnecessary kilometres. The expected impact is lower work-related travel emissions, reduced fuel consumption, time savings for organisations and more predictable field operations. The case is relevant because it connects climate objectives with internal organisational logistics, showing that emission reductions can come not only from major infrastructure projects but also from smarter allocation of everyday work. In a municipal context, such tools could support maintenance crews, social-service visits, inspection units or other teams that move across the city. The available source describes the solution within Espoo’s AI Mobility Challenge, so it should be framed as challenge-stage development or potential pilot rather than an implemented municipal routing system.

title: Processing of personal data, AI translation service on the Hello Espoo website
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Espoo’s AI translation service on the Hello Espoo website improves multilingual access to municipal information by providing content in audio and text formats across 13 languages. The initiative addresses an important inclusion challenge in local government: residents with different language backgrounds may struggle to access information about public services, integration support and municipal opportunities if content is available only in Finnish and Swedish or if translation is not provided in accessible formats. The AI-powered service combines text translation and voice functions to make Hello Espoo content easier to use for a wider audience. It is tested from September 2025 to August 2026, with the City of Espoo responsible for the Finnish and Swedish source content and Voice Intuitive responsible for the translated text and voice functions. At operational level, the service enables multilingual communication directly on the city website, helping users listen to or read translated content according to their needs. Usage data, such as use of text and audio functions, pages visited and time of use, support testing, development and user-experience improvement, while data-protection arrangements limit identifiability and keep processing within the EU/EEA. Feedback from users further supports accessibility improvements. The expected impact is easier access to public information, stronger integration support, better inclusion of multilingual residents and improved evidence for future AI translation services in municipal communication. The initiative is particularly relevant because it combines AI-enabled language accessibility with explicit privacy governance in a live public-service environment.

title: Pioneering Europe’s Future of Autonomous Urban Mobility
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Turin and the Piedmont Region are positioning the city as a European laboratory for autonomous urban mobility, combining the region’s automotive heritage, research capacity and urban infrastructure with AI-enabled transport experimentation. The initiative responds to the challenge of moving autonomous-driving technologies from controlled environments into real public-service mobility settings. Turin’s candidacy aims to secure a formal role within the European network of pilot cities for autonomous driving, with the ambition of testing driverless public mobility services such as taxis or shuttles on public roads. The city’s ecosystem provides strong enabling conditions, including the Politecnico di Torino, an established automotive supply chain, existing innovation infrastructure and previous experimentation around the university campus area. AI models are expected to support real-world testing by monitoring vehicle flows and helping analyse traffic conditions during trials. At operational level, the initiative would allow public authorities, researchers and industry actors to test autonomous vehicles in an urban environment where safety, service quality and interaction with ordinary traffic can be assessed under realistic conditions. The expected impact is stronger European leadership in autonomous mobility, attraction of investment, development of local expertise and creation of a model for AI-supported public transport innovation. The initiative also connects transport innovation with broader regional industrial policy, using Turin’s automotive strengths to support the transition towards software-defined, AI-enabled and service-oriented mobility.

title: Piedmont harnesses AI to bring healthcare to every corner
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Piedmont’s AI-healthcare initiative focuses on using artificial intelligence, diagnostics and telemedicine to improve healthcare access across a region where more than 40% of the territory is mountainous. The operational challenge is territorial inequality in access to care: residents in peripheral or mountain areas may need to travel long distances for diagnostic examinations or specialist medical consultations, creating delays and barriers to timely treatment. The initiative proposes an extended system of telemedicine cabins where patients can undergo examinations with the support of a trained health or social-care operator while a doctor connects remotely from a hospital. Artificial intelligence is positioned as a support layer for diagnostics, organisational efficiency and telemedicine workflows, helping clinicians interpret information, monitor patients and manage remote-service delivery more effectively. At operational level, the system decentralises access to diagnostic services by bringing examination capacity closer to residents while keeping specialist medical expertise connected through video and digital tools. This helps shift healthcare from a hospital-centred model towards more distributed territorial care. The expected impact is improved healthcare coverage for remote communities, faster access to diagnostic support, reduced travel burden for patients, more efficient use of medical resources and stronger resilience of the regional health system. The initiative is particularly relevant because it links AI not only to clinical innovation, but also to equity of access and territorial cohesion, using telemedicine to make the right to health more practical in peripheral areas.

title: ChatPat - Virtual assistant
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Citizens, businesses and professionals often need to identify the correct public service, understand eligibility requirements and access online forms without knowing the internal administrative terminology used by public bodies. ChatPaT addresses this problem by providing a virtual assistant for the public services of the Autonomous Province of Trento. The operational objective is to reduce search time and make provincial services easier to find, understand and use. The assistant allows users to ask questions in natural language and receive immediate answers based on official information from the Province’s Service Catalogue, including direct links to detailed pages and online forms. It supports Italian, English, German, French, Spanish and Portuguese, and is available every day at any time. At a conceptual level, ChatPaT uses retrieval-augmented generation to connect colloquial user questions with the formal taxonomy of administrative services. The technical architecture is based on Microsoft Azure, including Azure AI Search, Azure Document Intelligence, Azure Functions and Azure AI Foundry, with production infrastructure hosted on an ACN-qualified cloud environment. The service includes privacy safeguards: conversations are anonymised, personal data are not intentionally requested or stored, and any personal data provided accidentally are removed before saving the conversation. The expected impact is improved access to digital public services, reduced burden on information offices, better multilingual support and continuous refinement through anonymised feedback and usage metrics. The case is significant because it combines generative AI, official-source retrieval, privacy-by-design and public-service usability in a controlled provincial-government setting.

title: EDF Leverages AI to Predict Grid Stress During Heatwaves
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Electricity systems face increasing stress during extreme heat, when cooling demand rises, grid components operate under thermal constraints and localised overloads may develop quickly. The EDF use case described in the available secondary source concerns an AI system intended to predict grid stress during heatwaves and help operators prepare corrective actions before outages occur. The operational problem is that conventional monitoring can be reactive: operators may detect stress once transformers, substations or local networks are already close to operational limits. The reported system combines weather forecasts, consumption patterns, transformer loads and local events to model stress on high-voltage and regional grids, using transformer-based forecasting and graph neural networks. At a conceptual level, the model treats the electricity grid as a spatial and temporal system: network components influence one another, while weather and demand conditions evolve over time. Forecasts can then be presented through GIS-enhanced dashboards, allowing operators to identify vulnerable areas and consider mitigation measures such as demand shedding, battery dispatch or industrial load adjustment. The expected impact would be faster response, reduced outages, better voltage stability and more targeted protection of ageing grid assets during heatwaves. However, the evidence for this specific deployment is weak. The main source is DigitalDefynd, and I did not find an EDF source confirming the reported Rhône-Alpes results, the exact modelling architecture or the stated impact figures. EDF does publicly describe AI as a major part of its R&D strategy, but not this specific heatwave-stress system in the sources found.

title: Paris Hospitals Use AI for ICU Bed Allocation and Mortality Prediction
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Intensive-care coordination becomes especially difficult when hospitals face sudden surges in critically ill patients, as happened during the COVID-19 crisis. The Paris hospitals use case concerns the reported use of AI to support ICU bed planning, patient transfer decisions and mortality-risk prediction across Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris. The operational problem is that ICU capacity depends on rapidly changing factors: bed availability, ventilator use, staff capacity, laboratory results, patient comorbidities, ambulance flows and local disease pressure. If these data are outdated or fragmented, hospitals may lose valuable time when deciding where a patient should be treated. The reported system uses federated learning so that predictive models can be trained across hospitals without centralising sensitive patient data. LSTM-based forecasting models are described as predicting ICU occupancy from clinical and operational indicators, while a triage module ranks patients according to survival probability and expected resource need. At a conceptual level, the system combines capacity forecasting, mortality-risk modelling and operational coordination, allowing emergency departments, ambulance dispatch and hospital managers to align transfers more effectively. The expected impact is faster ICU transfers, better use of beds, staff and ventilators, more accurate planning during surges and clearer information for families. However, this case should be handled cautiously: the available source is a secondary article, and I did not find an official AP-HP source confirming the exact metrics or system architecture. title: AI to notify the police about suspicious persons
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Regional security authorities in wartime or high-risk contexts need to monitor strategic infrastructure, transport entry points and public spaces in order to detect unusual behaviour and respond quickly to potential threats. The Zakarpattia use case concerns the reported deployment of an AI-supported monitoring system connected to video cameras across the region. The operational problem is that human operators cannot continuously review all video streams in real time, especially where checkpoints, infrastructure sites and transport hubs generate large volumes of footage. The system described by the head of the Zakarpattia regional military administration connects regional cameras to an AI system that monitors and analyses the situation across the oblast. When the system detects suspicious presence near strategic infrastructure or identifies a person who is not recognised in the system, it alerts law-enforcement authorities for human follow-up. According to the source, all people entering the region through checkpoints undergo monitoring, cameras capture faces and vehicle numbers, and unrecognised individuals are then approached by police. At a conceptual level, the system acts as an automated surveillance and alerting layer, prioritising potential risks for human assessment rather than replacing police judgement. The expected impact is faster notification of suspicious activity, improved protection of strategic sites and stronger situational awareness for regional security authorities. The case is sensitive because it involves biometric or near-biometric monitoring, public surveillance and possible police questioning or detention; any such system requires strong legal safeguards, proportionality, oversight and protection against false positives. (unian.ua

title: Gismap AI model for land cover analysis
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal planning, biodiversity policy, climate adaptation and environmental reporting require accurate and up-to-date information on land cover, but producing this information manually can be time-consuming and inconsistent. The Gismap use case in Ballerup Municipality applies an AI model to generate land-cover data and combine it with environmental and spatial datasets. The operational problem is that municipalities need to understand how areas are distributed between buildings, roads, vegetation, water, bare ground and other land-cover categories, but traditional mapping may depend on periodic surveys or manual GIS updates. Gismap supports this work by using AI-based classification, editing tools and integration with public geospatial sources. The solution draws on publicly available datasets from Danish authorities, including the Danish Climate Data Agency, GeoDanmark, the Danish Environmental Portal and the Ministry of Environment. At a conceptual level, the model converts aerial, map and environmental data into structured land-cover layers that can support analysis across multiple municipal functions. These outputs can be used for biodiversity registration, operational optimisation, ESG reporting, strategic planning and spatial planning. The expected impact is faster production of land-cover information, better evidence for green-space management, improved environmental reporting and more efficient use of GIS capacity. The case is relevant because it shows how AI can strengthen ordinary planning and environmental administration by converting existing public data into decision-ready spatial information. It should be seen as a municipal geospatial-AI support tool rather than an autonomous planning decision system.

title: Implementation of AI in the knowledge database in Topdesk
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal employees need fast access to internal guidance on IT, accounting, procurement and support processes, but knowledge is often spread across previous tickets, helpdesk articles and staff experience. Randers Municipality’s Ebbot use case integrates an AI chatbot into TOPdesk, the municipality’s IT service-management system, to improve internal support. The operational problem is that employees often submit recurring questions to support teams, while the relevant answer may already exist in a knowledge article or previous case. This creates avoidable workload for support staff and delays for the employee waiting for help. Ebbot acts as a conversational layer over the TOPdesk knowledge base: employees can ask questions in ordinary language, and the chatbot searches previous support cases and knowledge articles to produce a relevant answer. When the system cannot find a suitable response, it helps the user create a support ticket, preserving the escalation route to human support. At a conceptual level, the solution combines chatbot interaction, retrieval from structured knowledge articles and case-history reuse. The expected impact is faster first-line support, more consistent answers, reduced repetitive workload and improved use of existing organisational knowledge. The case is relevant because it applies AI to internal municipal productivity rather than citizen-facing services. By supporting staff with routine administrative and technical questions, the municipality can improve operational continuity and allow specialist support teams to focus on more complex or exceptional issues.

title: Roboref - Generative AI in the Randers Municipality
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Meeting documentation is a persistent administrative burden in public organisations, particularly where staff must record decisions, action points and discussion summaries while also participating actively in the meeting itself. Roboref addresses this problem by using speech-to-text and generative AI to record, transcribe and draft meeting summaries. In Randers Municipality, the tool is being tested by a selected group of employees for internal meetings. The operational problem is that manual note-taking can be time-consuming, uneven in quality and potentially distracting for employees who need to listen, contribute and capture key points at the same time. Roboref automates the first draft of meeting documentation by recording the meeting, converting speech into text and generating structured summaries or notes. At a conceptual level, the tool acts as an AI notetaker: it does not replace human validation, but produces a draft that can be reviewed, corrected and finalised by staff. The expected impact is time savings, more consistent meeting records, better objectivity in documentation and improved ability for employees to focus on the substance of meetings rather than on note-taking. The case is relevant because it represents one of the most common practical uses of generative AI in public administration: reducing documentation work without transferring decision-making authority to the system. It also requires clear governance on consent, recording, data protection and the handling of confidential meeting content. RoboRef is described elsewhere as a collaboration involving more than 20 municipalities, organisations, ATP and Droids Agency. (offentlig-ai.dk

title: Copilot in the Randers Municipality
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal employees increasingly use generative AI to draft text, summarise information, prepare communications and support routine productivity tasks. The Randers Municipality Copilot use case concerns staff access to Microsoft Copilot in Edge as a general-purpose assistant for everyday work. The operational problem is that employees often need to produce first drafts, simplify complex text, summarise documents or prepare meeting-related material, but these tasks consume time that could otherwise be spent on service delivery, case handling or professional assessment. Copilot in Edge provides a browser-based generative AI interface that can help employees generate text, rephrase content, summarise information and structure ideas. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as a productivity assistant rather than a decision system: the employee remains responsible for checking outputs, correcting inaccuracies and ensuring that final content is appropriate to the administrative context. This is especially important in public administration, where errors, confidentiality issues or unclear provenance can affect citizens and legal obligations. The expected impact is faster drafting, reduced administrative friction and improved individual productivity. However, the source link provided in your table appears to point to the Dutch Municipality of Arnhem’s Microsoft 365 Copilot register entry, not Randers Municipality. It is therefore useful for explaining general public-sector Copilot governance, including human oversight and data risks, but it does not directly verify the Randers deployment. The Randers-specific description should rely on the Danish AI-landkort entry rather than the Dutch algorithm register.

title: OS2ai - Open-source AI solution in Danish municipalities
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Danish municipalities are exploring generative AI, but many want solutions that preserve public ownership, reduce dependency on large proprietary providers and allow shared development across authorities. OS2ai addresses this need by providing an open-source AI platform for the public sector, built around common governance, shared costs and stronger ownership control. Randers Municipality participates in this wider public-sector AI community. The operational problem is that individual municipalities may not have the resources to build secure, reusable AI infrastructure alone, while proprietary tools can raise concerns about data control, vendor lock-in and long-term costs. OS2ai offers a shared platform that can be used for both everyday AI support and more specialised municipal applications. At a conceptual level, OS2ai is an enabling layer: it makes it easier for municipalities to integrate AI into workflows, develop assistants, automate tasks and reuse components developed by other public authorities. The platform builds on work initiated by Aarhus Municipality and is further developed through the OS2 community, which has long focused on shared open-source public-sector software. The expected impact is faster AI adoption, lower duplicated development costs, greater transparency, improved public control over data and models, and more scalable experimentation across municipalities and regions. The case is relevant because it treats AI infrastructure as a shared public-good approach rather than a set of isolated local procurements. This is particularly important where municipalities face similar tasks and can benefit from common technical foundations.

title: RandersGPT
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipalities using generative AI need to balance productivity benefits with data protection, information security and responsible use. RandersGPT is an internal GPT environment for Randers Municipality, based on OpenAI through Azure and accessed through the municipality’s AI portal. The operational problem is that employees may otherwise turn to public tools such as ChatGPT or browser-based assistants, which can create uncertainty about where data are processed, what information may be entered and whether outputs are appropriate for municipal tasks. RandersGPT provides a more controlled internal alternative for administrative support. It is designed to assist employees with tasks such as drafting, summarising, structuring text, preparing material and navigating towards more specialised assistants available in the AI portal. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as a secure municipal front door to generative AI: employees can use a general assistant while being directed to domain-specific agents where more tailored support is available. The expected impact is safer and more consistent AI use, reduced reliance on uncontrolled external tools, improved productivity and better organisational oversight of generative-AI adoption. The case is relevant because it reflects a maturing stage in public-sector AI use. Instead of simply allowing or banning external AI tools, the municipality creates its own managed environment with clearer data-processing responsibilities, documentation and governance. Randers Municipality’s own privacy notice states that the AI portal is used to provide general chat and access to specialists, supporting task performance, quality assurance and documentation.

title: Fasit Dialogstøtte – AI Assistant for Conversation Notes
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Caseworkers in employment and social-service settings must listen carefully to citizens while also documenting conversations accurately for case files. This creates a practical tension: manual note-taking can reduce presence in the conversation, while incomplete documentation can weaken case quality and increase the risk of mistakes. Fasit Dialogstøtte addresses this problem by integrating an AI assistant into the Schultz Fasit case-management environment. The operational objective is to support caseworkers by automatically transcribing conversations with citizens and generating draft summaries, minutes or journal notes. At a conceptual level, the assistant acts as a documentation support tool rather than a case-decision system. It captures the spoken conversation, converts it to text and prepares a draft that the caseworker can review, correct and approve before it becomes part of the case record. This allows the professional to remain responsible for the final documentation while reducing the repetitive burden of manual note-taking. The expected impact is more focused citizen dialogue, more consistent records, reduced administrative workload and stronger documentation quality. The system may also support accuracy because key points from the conversation can be captured systematically rather than reconstructed from memory after the meeting. The case is relevant because it shows how AI can support front-line welfare administration in a relatively bounded way: it improves the production of case documentation while leaving professional judgement, case assessment and legal responsibility with the human caseworker.

title: Pluto – Road Analysis and Maintenance
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Municipal road maintenance requires up-to-date information on potholes, surface wear, cracking and other defects, but manual inspections can be slow, expensive and unevenly prioritised. Pluto Technologies’ solution addresses this problem by using AI, smartphones and GPS to monitor road conditions and support more targeted maintenance planning. In Hvidovre Municipality, the tool is used through devices installed on municipal vehicles, such as refuse trucks, which already travel regularly across the road network. The operational problem is that municipalities often lack a continuous, objective and scalable picture of road condition. By collecting data from vehicles that are already operating, the system can reduce the need for dedicated inspection rounds and transform routine municipal driving into a source of infrastructure intelligence. The AI model detects damage and wear on road surfaces, while the results are visualised on a digital map for planners and maintenance teams. At a conceptual level, Pluto creates a data-driven road-management loop: sensor and image data are collected, AI identifies defects, maps show where action is needed, and maintenance resources can then be prioritised according to actual condition. The expected impact is faster detection of damage, better prioritisation of repairs, more preventive maintenance, lower costs and potentially longer road lifespan. The case is relevant because it applies AI to a very concrete municipal asset-management task, making infrastructure maintenance more proactive and evidence-based. Pluto describes its product as AI-powered software for detecting damage, planning repairs and managing road maintenance

title: InDialog Voicebot – Internal AI Support for ESDH and Topdesk
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Hvidovre Municipality’s InDialog Voicebot supports municipal employees by making internal guidance easier to access through voice-based interaction. Public administrations rely on many internal systems, including electronic document and case-management systems and service-management platforms such as TOPdesk. Employees often need quick answers on how to use these systems correctly, but finding the relevant instruction can require searching manuals, intranet pages or previous support material. The InDialog Voicebot addresses this problem by allowing staff to ask questions through voice commands and receive guidance rapidly. The solution is used internally to support navigation and guidance in the municipality’s ESDH system and TOPdesk. At operational level, the voicebot works as an internal first-line assistant: employees can obtain immediate answers or locate relevant instructions without interrupting their workflow or submitting routine support requests. This reduces the time spent searching for procedural guidance and allows support staff to focus on more complex issues that require human expertise. The expected impact is faster internal support, more efficient use of digital systems, reduced friction in administrative work and improved productivity for municipal employees. The voice interface is also relevant because it lowers the threshold for using internal knowledge tools, especially in situations where typing a search query or navigating a system manually is inconvenient. The initiative demonstrates how AI can be used inside local government to improve the everyday experience of staff working with digital administrative systems.

title: KAILA - AI tool for Danish legislation
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Municipal legal staff must interpret current legislation, prepare arguments, draft legal documents and ensure that advice is based on reliable and up-to-date sources. KAILA supports this work by providing an AI assistant grounded in Karnov’s legal content and, in the municipal case-management context, potentially combined with the municipality’s own uploaded documents. The operational problem is that legal professionals spend substantial time locating relevant provisions, guidance, case law and arguments before they can apply them to a concrete case. KAILA is designed to accelerate this research and drafting process while preserving source verification. It can help generate legal text, gather relevant sources and arguments, provide new perspectives and assist preparation for meetings or case discussions. At a conceptual level, the system works as a retrieval and drafting assistant for legal work: it uses AI to interpret the user’s question, search trusted legal materials and produce a response with references that the legal professional can verify. This is important because legal AI must not be treated as an uncheckable answer generator; the value lies in combining speed with transparent source grounding. The expected impact is faster legal research, more efficient preparation of legal documents, improved consistency in municipal legal work and reduced time spent on preliminary information gathering. The case is relevant because it applies generative AI to a high-accountability domain where human verification remains essential. KAILA should therefore be presented as decision support for legal professionals, not as an automated legal decision-maker. (karnovgroup.dk

title: AI-for-Søren: AI for work injuries
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Work-related injuries and eye injuries involve specific reporting obligations, rights, responsibilities and procedural steps that can be difficult for employees and managers to understand quickly. AI-for-Søren addresses this problem by providing an AI assistant that answers questions about municipal procedures for handling occupational injury cases. The operational problem is that different users need different kinds of guidance: an injured employee may need to know what to do immediately, a manager may need to understand reporting obligations, and HR or working-environment staff may need consistent procedural information. The assistant communicates the municipality’s procedures and links users to supplementary information from relevant Danish authorities and professional sources, including the Danish Working Environment Authority and the National Board of Industrial Injuries. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as a specialised knowledge assistant for a narrow administrative domain. It does not decide whether an injury is compensable or replace formal case handling; instead, it helps users find correct guidance and understand the steps involved. The expected impact is easier access to accurate information, fewer procedural mistakes, more consistent handling of work-injury cases and reduced workload for staff who otherwise answer recurring questions manually. The intended users include managers, working-environment representatives, injured employees, HR staff, MED organisation representatives and the municipality’s occupational-injury function. The case is relevant because it shows how a municipality can create a focused AI assistant for a specific internal governance and employee-support process, where a well-defined knowledge base can reduce uncertainty and improve procedural compliance.

title: A Sovereign AI Model: National LLM to Enter Beta in 2026
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Ukraine is developing its own sovereign large language model (LLM)—a national artificial intelligence system tailored to the Ukrainian language, culture and public-sector needs. The project has moved from concept to technical planning and is being built in partnership with Kyivstar, with the first beta version due in spring 2026. It uses Google’s open Gemma models as a base, which are being adapted and trained on extensive Ukrainian-language datasets drawn from government, academia, media and other sources. An independent expert panel is shaping quality, safety and linguistic benchmarks, while a legal framework for data use and intellectual-property compliance is under development. Once tested, the model will be made available to public institutions, researchers and developers, and is intended to bolster Ukraine’s digital sovereignty and reduce reliance on foreign AI technologies.

title: ELLI - Chatbot of the City of Linz
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The City of Linz provides an AI-powered chatbot service called “ELLI” (short for Elektronische Linzerin) to help citizens find information about municipal services quickly and easily. The chatbot supports multilingual interaction, is continuously updated with new content, and helps reduce routine inquiries to the City’s Teleservice Center by providing instant responses to common questions.

title: AI solution in Roskilde Municipality helps create minutes of consultation responses
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Roskilde Municipality uses generative AI to automatically create summaries of consultation responses from residents regarding planning decisions. When citizens submit feedback on municipal projects, employees manually had to summarize each response—a time-consuming and variable process. The AI solution uses Azure GPT to generate initial drafts of these summaries, which employees then review and refine to ensure accuracy. Testing shows the AI produces summaries of 75-80% quality initially, potentially saving up to one hour per consultation response. This allows staff to redirect time toward other citizen-facing tasks.

title: AI helps the Danish Digital Agency conduct analyses
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Since 2021, large Danish companies must address data ethics in their annual reports. The Digital Agency needed to analyze thousands of reports to strengthen national data ethics guidance. The sheer volume—3,673 reports totaling approximately 88,000 pages from 2022-2023—made manual analysis impractical. The agency developed a generative AI solution using ChatGPT API with a custom prompt containing 30 classification categories. This enables systematic analysis of data ethics policies across entire company populations rather than just samples, allowing faster, more comprehensive insights for policy development.

title: AI solution in ATP writes journal notes of conversations with citizens
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: ATP, Denmark's labor market fund, receives approximately 2.5 million citizen calls annually, each requiring documentation as journal notes. Results show the system generates draft notes in 5 seconds, with employees spending under 2 minutes correcting them in 70% of cases. This automation frees employees from time-consuming documentation tasks while maintaining consistent, high-quality records of citizen interactions.

title: Agrinio Environmental Digital Observatory: A Digital Twin Ecosystem for Sustainable and Data-Driven Governance
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The Agrinio Environmental Digital Observatory establishes a unified digital twin and governance ecosystem operating as a decision-support system for evidence-based, climate-resilient and participatory governance in the Municipality of Agrinio. It integrates environmental monitoring, spatial planning, municipal intelligence and citizen engagement into a single interoperable platform. The system combines real-time IoT sensor networks, Copernicus Earth Observation data, GIS analytics and open data services with participatory planning tools, enabling continuous monitoring of environmental conditions, land-use dynamics and urban development in near real time. It functions as a single source of truth for municipal territory, improving coordination, efficiency and cross-departmental decision-making. A KPI framework aligned with ISO 37120 supports performance monitoring of municipal services. Citizens access environmental and spatial data, strengthening transparency and participation. The solution is aligned with EIF,INSPIRE principles, ensuring interoperability, scalability and reuse across European public administrations.

title: Skrinja: AI-Enhanced Business Intelligence for Evidence-Based Decision-Making and Policymaking in Slovenia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: MINISTRY OF THE INTERIOR AND PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION
source_description: Skrinja is Slovenia’s national Business Intelligence (BI) and AI-enabled analytics platform, supporting evidence-based decision-making and policymaking across public administration. It provides strategic KPI dashboards, advanced analytics, standardised reports, real-time reporting, interactive visualisations and predictive analytics, transforming administrative data into actionable insights. Operating in a secure GDPR-compliant government environment since 2020, Skrinja integrates major national datasets, including the Common Agricultural Policy (covering over 80,000 farms), Administrative Procedures (more than 1 million cases annually), Market and Health Inspections, Public-Sector Salaries (over 180,000 employees and 2,000 budget users), Public Procurement, the Central Personnel Registry and Public Funding Programmes. In 2026, Skrinja Open was launched to provide citizens, businesses, researchers and journalists with direct access to public procurement analytics, strengthening transparency, accountability and data-driven governance.

title: Latvia enables legal recognition of Ukrainian trusted e-signatures
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development of the Republic of Latvia
source_description: Latvia introduced a legal and technical solution enabling Ukrainian electronic signatures to be recognised and verified in Latvia. The initiative builds on Ukraine’s recognition of EU electronic signatures since January 2023, and on the European Commission’s Trusted List of third countries, which together created the legal and technical foundation for the acceptance of Ukrainian electronic signatures within Latvia’s digital environment. It responds to the needs of Ukrainian citizens, residents, entrepreneurs and business representatives who interact with Latvian public institutions and service providers but may not have Latvian digital credentials. It also benefits Latvian citizens and businesses cooperating with Ukrainian partners, by enabling legally valid remote transactions. By amending national legislation and integrating verification functionality into Latvia’s national e-signature infrastructure, documents signed with Ukrainian electronic signatures issued by trusted Ukrainian service providers can now be accepted for legally binding digital interactions. The solution removes administrative barriers, supports remote access to services, and strengthens secure cross-border digital cooperation.

title: Matuok.lt: Open-Source Network Measurement and Data Platform for Public Internet Quality Monitoring
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: The Communications Regulatory Authority of the Republic of Lithuania
source_description: Matuok.lt is a public network measurement platform implemented and operated by the Communications Regulatory Authority of Lithuania (RRT), based on the open-source RTR-NetTest framework. It enables citizens and businesses to objectively assess the quality of their internet access services by measuring key parameters such as download/upload speed, latency, and additional quality indicators. The solution builds on an existing European open-source software and adapts it to national needs, providing detailed reports, historical data, and visualized statistics, including maps and open datasets. It empowers users to verify whether their service meets contractual conditions and supports complaint processes with evidence-based measurements. At the same time, aggregated data supports public authorities in monitoring national network performance, identifying coverage gaps, and informing infrastructure investment decisions. The platform is accessible via web and mobile applications, ensuring broad public access and usability.

title: Simple: A Semantic, Voice-Driven Procurement Intelligence and Training System for Auditing and Decision Support in Public Administration
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Simple is a semantic, graph-based procurement intelligence system developed within a university-led public sector innovation context and currently in pilot phase. It integrates European (TED) and national (KIMDIS) procurement data into a unified knowledge graph aligned with the eProcurement Ontology (ePO), enabling large-scale audit and analysis across contracting authorities, time periods and CPV categories. The system supports automated generation of structured audit reports and provides multi-layer diagnosis of procurement markets (macro–meso–micro) through explainable indicators, enhancing audit, policy analysis and decision-making. It also incorporates legal knowledge into a graph-based reasoning framework, enabling structured interpretation within the regulatory context. A voice-driven interface allows non-technical users to interact naturally, while a human-supervised self-correction mechanism ensures continuous refinement and transparency. The solution improves efficiency, compliance and data-driven policymaking in public procurement.

title: Servizz.gov – Reimagining Public Service Delivery Through AI-Powered Citizen Engagement
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Servizz.gov is Malta’s next-generation national public service platform, designed to transform how citizens discover, access and interact with government services. Unlike traditional government portals, Servizz.gov does not only present information. It actively guides citizens through their service journey by using personalisation, life-event information and intelligent recommendations to make public services easier to understand and access. The initiative demonstrates how artificial intelligence can be deployed responsibly within public administration to create measurable public value, while providing a model that can be replicated by other public administrations in Europe.

title: Madrid Smart Urban Spaces: Interoperable Edge Intelligence for Real-Time Urban Operations
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: Madrid's Smart Urban Spaces (EUI) are interoperable urban ecosystems that connect infrastructure, digital platforms and public services across Madrid's 21 districts. Built on open standards and a common architecture, each EUI integrates IoT devices, AI and real-time analytics through UrbanOS, Madrid's City Operating System, creating a shared data space for urban management. The platform enables automated and coordinated services, including adaptive street lighting, smart parking, environmental monitoring, waste management and EV charging optimization. Two EUIs are already operational: ValdemingÃ³mez and Mercamadrid, integrating energy, mobility and environmental solutions. Data is harmonized using FIWARE/NGSI-LD and European Smart Data Models, ensuring semantic interoperability across domains and vendors. Feeding Madrid's city-scale Digital Twin, the initiative supports evidence-based decisions while offering a scalable, vendor-neutral and replicable framework for cities across Europe.

title: Visor 2030: plataforma de codi obert que permet comprendre, monitoritzar i avaluar la realitat del territori des d'una perspectiva multidimensional vinculada als Objectius de Desenvolupament Sostenible.
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: El Visor 2030 és una plataforma de codi obert impulsat per la Diputació de Barcelona que integra dades socials, econòmiques i mediambientals dels 311 municipis de la província de Barcelona per comprendre, monitoritzar i avaluar el territori des d’una perspectiva multidimensional vinculada als Objectius de Desenvolupament Sostenible. La plataforma combina 76 indicadors alineats amb els ODS amb capes addicionals d’informació —pressupost municipal, plans estratègics, percepció ciutadana— per oferir una visió 360º que dona suport a la presa de decisions basada en evidències, la transparència i la rendició de comptes. title: LExIA - AI-assisted regulatory screening for early detection of competition restrictions.
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia (CNMC): Deputy Directorate for Economic Analysis (Advocacy Department). Technical support: Deputy Directorate for Information Systems and ICT (SSTIC).
source_description: LExIA (“Lectura Experta con IA”) is an AI-based internal solution developed by the CNMC to support early detection of public regulatory restrictions to competition in Spanish official gazettes. It addresses a high-volume, time-sensitive process: thousands of legal texts are published across multiple official sources and must be screened quickly when they may require competition advocacy or, ultimately, legal action. LExIA combines preliminary filters, key information extraction, preliminary assessment of restrictions, retrieval of CNMC precedents through Retrieval Augmented Generation –RAG–, legal analysis against related official sources, prioritisation and automatic generation of Word reports and e-mail alerts. The system runs on real regulatory publications and sends daily results and filtering statistics for expert review. It does not replace legal or economic judgement; it structures, documents and prioritises cases, enabling CNMC to identify cases to challenge in court and engage authorities to amend anti-competitive rules, and has already helped remove restrictive regulation.

title: AI Playbook
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: The AI Playbook developed by Digitaal Vlaanderen establishes a practical operating model for trustworthy, scalable and interoperable AI adoption across the public sector. It was created in response to growing challenges faced by public administrations in adopting AI in a strategic and responsible manner, including fragmented experimentation, rapidly evolving technologies and regulations, and varying levels of organisational readiness. The Playbook supports public administrations across the entire AI lifecycle: defining strategy and roadmaps, identifying and prioritising AI use cases, implementing governance aligned with the EU AI Act, strengthening organisational readiness and skills, and embedding AI architecture. The Playbook turns policy ambitions into concrete tools, checklists and reusable guidance, enabling administrations to move from fragmented experimentation to coordinated and interoperable AI adoption. It provides a common framework and shared language for AI adoption, helping organisations move from fragmented experimentation towards coordinated, interoperable and value-driven AI implementation. The Playbook supports organisations at different stages of AI maturity, from initial exploration to large-scale operational adoption.

title: Prozorro.Sale
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
source_description: Prozorro.Sale is Ukraine’s national digital public infrastructure for the transparent sale and lease of public assets and rights. It addresses fragmented procedures, limited competition, unequal access to information, and integrity risks in public asset management. The solution combines a state-administered electronic trading system with more than 40 private e-marketplaces operating under common rules and standards. It uses APIs, open data, public BI dashboards, cloud infrastructure, and transparency-by-design principles to ensure equal access, accountability, and public oversight. Prozorro.Sale enables fair competition and market-based price discovery. Since 2016, the system has conducted over 860k auctions, generated more than UAH 130 billion, and attracted over 149k participants. It improves administrative efficiency and provides a scalable model for digital governance.

title: Medical Drone Transport Corridor in Catalonia
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: The responsible public sector organisations for this case are the “Centre de Telecomunicacions i Tecnologies de la Informació” (CTTI), as the main ICT provider for the Generalitat de Catalunya, and the Departament de Salut,Fundation TIC Salut i Social
source_description: Rural and remote healthcare areas in Catalonia, particularly in the Pyrenees, face logistical challenges in the rapid transport of biological samples, blood products, medicines and medical equipment. The Medical Drone Transport Corridor in Catalonia, led by CTTI and the Department of Health, introduces a drone-based logistics service starting with the Lleida–Tremp corridor and Tremp-Sort corridor. It uses Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) to complement road transport with regular, on-demand and urgent aerial services between healthcare centres. The project combines certified drone operations, healthcare air corridors, vertiports, traceability and a digital platform for mission management. Building on two pilots in rural and urban areas, the solution has shown faster deliveries, lower emissions and better sample preservation, including up to 75% shorter delivery times, up to 98% lower emissions and a 50% reduction in sample hemolysis. It also provides a scalable model for future healthcare corridors.

title: BRISA: A Cross-Domain AI Foundation Model for Predictive Public Infrastructure Management
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
organization: The responsible public sector organisations for this is is the “Centre de Telecomunicacions i Tecnologies de la Informació” (CTTI) of the Generalitat de Catalunya.
source_description: BRISA is an interoperable Artificial Intelligence solution that helps public administrations move from reactive management to predictive decision-making in energy and environmental policies. Based on a proprietary time-series foundation model trained on more than 11 billion energy, climate, mobility, occupancy and environmental data points, BRISA forecasts demand, detects anomalies, simulates intervention scenarios and prioritises actions with explainable and auditable outputs. The solution has already been validated in energy-efficiency management through GovTech4All with the Generalitat de Catalunya, and in urban air-quality forecasting and policy simulation with Pamplona City Council. It is now being validated as a cross-domain predictive model for district heating and shore-side electricity demand for vessels through the awarded Horizon Europe COSMIC project, and for public-space management through the awarded DesafIA Madrid challenge.

title: Artificial intelligence-based legal search service integrated in the Hungarian Gazette and National Legislation Database
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.

source_description: The Gazette 2.0 project modernised IT systems supporting official gazette publication and integrated the National Legislation Database with an innovative AI platform accessible via jog.gov.hu, free of charge, implemented by co-financing of EU and hungarian Government. Key features include digital access to current gazette issues, AI-based legal search engine and smart summary of gazette content, interoperable and ELI-compatible integration of National Legislation Database, Gazette Portal, and Company Information Portal. The system improves user experience, legal awareness, supports informed decision-making, and serves both common citizens and legal professionals.

title: Transforming environmental assessment with AI for Denmark's state-designated energy parks
source_attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (2026), PSTW: Public Sector Tech Watch latest dataset of selected cases, doi:10.2905/JRC.J1MWC9R; September 2026 snapshot. Fields selected and normalized; no endorsement implied.
